entries.title: When Your Subscribers Actually Cancel Their Subscription (And What To Send)
entries.summary: I've audited a lot of 8-figure+ subscription brands this year, and right now it's basically the wild wild west lol.
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I've audited a lot of 8-figure+ subscription brands this year, and right now it's basically the wild wild west lol.

Specifically around customer churn…

Every brand does something different, but almost none of it is grounded in actual data.

That’s why today I’m walking through a quick break down of when subscribers actually cancel, and the emails you should be sending to make sure your subscribers actually stick around.

Let's get into it!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eaaa829e-67a9-4cf0-8be2-d298f14f143c/axoj6h.jpg?t=1785329622)

#### The Days-Until-Churn Chart

Before you create a single onboarding email, you need to know when your subscribers actually cancel.,,

We pulled this data through WellTV (our custom retention analytics platform exclusive to our clients) across all of our subscription brands, and the chart looked roughly the same across the board…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0b97d4b1-b1be-43ad-b4fa-df9225e47a46/Screenshot_2026-07-21_at_9.34.32_AM.png?t=1785327100)

What Days After Subscribing To Customers Churn

There are four spikes in every subscription brand's chart and each one tells you something specific about what your subscriber is doing at that exact moment.

**Day 0** is your first medium-sized cancellation spike (usually it’s a bit higher than the example image), and it comes from deal-seekers who signed up for the intro subscription offer but then cancelled almost immediately.

Most of these you can't save because they were never going to stick around in the first place, BUT the ones who genuinely signed up need something that makes them feel confident about their order…

Which is why the email firing (Your Order Confirmation) has to do the heavy lifting.

It’s one of the highest-open emails in your entire account and it fires the exact second your subscriber buys.

Rebuild it in Klaviyo with a warm welcome, subscription benefits, a dynamic order block, and some early 90-day timeline messaging to start setting expectations.

It’ll look much better than a basic Shopify receipt.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/faf9134e-0552-438f-98f2-27489fe40105/dense-conf.png?t=1785327362)

Optimized Order Confirmation

**Days 1-7** are the quietest window of churn your entire onboarding period.

The product hasn't been delivered yet, there's excitement in the air, and nobody is going to cancel a subscription for something they haven't even tried.

So use this time period to go hard on education because people won't cancel.

The second somebody gets the product, they're much more likely to cancel from an email, so I'd rather get all my onboarding education before delivery rather than after.

**Days 7-27** are where the biggest _prolonged cancellation period_ happens.

Now, the product has landed in the customer's hands and they're actively judging and deciding whether it's worth sticking with or not.

This is a very sensitive period where you want to back off with your messaging and trust that your onboarding emails before delivery and your product are good enough to get people through.

I recommend another tips email when the order's delivered, and then maybe one other email as a one-week or two-week check-in.

Other than that, send no other emails until the billing reminder and order confirmation emails…

**Days 27-30** is when the billing reminders and rebills go out, presenting the customer with the actual cost of the subscription and a clean path to cancel.

This is easily the biggest churn spike of the whole cycle…

On day 27, the billing reminder goes out telling people, "Hey, you're about to get rebuilt." This billing reminder email is incredibly important to optimize, or else people will just see that and cancel. We've seen updates and A/B tests we make to this email reduce day 27 churn by 30% to 50%

On day 30, the customers charged again, and they received that scary Shopify receipt email saying, "Thanks for your purchase. Here's how much you spent." That's the biggest churn spike. Most brands do nothing with this. Instead, I recommend turning off your Shopify transaction email and building a custom order that turns it into a fun thing talking about the great decision and benefits the customer is getting

It's incredibly important to optimize your messaging around these four spike periods.

It's also incredibly important to track this and know when and where people are churning so you can address it.

If you want to see this for your own brand, WellTV is our own analytics platform that tracks deeper subscription data (like the days-until-churn chart) for every brand we manage.

Book a call with us [here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=when-your-subscribers-actually-cancel-their-subscription-and-what-to-send) if you want an audit with it!

entries.title: Welcome Flow Non-Negotiables
entries.summary: I've audited hundreds of welcome flows this year, and after a while, you start to notice a pattern.
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I've audited hundreds of welcome flows this year, and after a while, you start to notice a pattern.

Your welcome flow is the first email sequence every new subscriber goes through.

It's where first impressions get made and first purchases happen, so it should be the most dialed-in flow in your entire account.

But for some brands, it's not…

That’s why today I'm walking through **7 non-negotiables to have in every welcome flow** so that you convert more first-time buyers, build stronger customer loyalty, and stop letting subscribers slip through the cracks.

Let's get into it.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/69ab5447-4dba-4527-aa2f-3b7ebc4c1ac0/axirs0.jpg?t=1785151498)

**1) Turn Off Double-Opt In**

Double opt-in is that confirmation email that goes out asking someone to click a link to confirm they actually want to subscribe.

Turn this bad boy off so that no one needs to jump through an extra hoop and they can smoothly start receiving your welcome sequence from the moment they sign up.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/dacbcc43-010b-4ef3-85bc-26ab408fd490/Screenshot_2026-07-27_at_3.58.34_AM.png?t=1785150680)

**2) First Email Fires Immediately**

We don't want the first welcome email going out any later than we absolutely have to, so no one minute or five minute or ten minute delay on this…

Set the very first email in your flow to fire **immediately upon signup.**

The second someone signs up is the exact moment they're most likely to open your email since they were just on your site and are still thinking about your brand.

So any kind of delay pushes that open into a moment where they're likely distracted, doing something else, or already past the impulse to check their inbox.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/384fb1d1-91f6-415d-8ada-85de3502601f/Screenshot_2026-07-27_at_4.14.21_AM_1.jpg?t=1785150956)

**3) Minimum of 3 Emails**

The biggest welcome flow mistake I see is brands running a 1-2 email welcome flow and calling it a day.

Which is a shame because your welcome flow is doing more work than any other flow in your account, and shortchanging it means you're leaving your highest-intent audience hanging.

The more touches a new subscriber gets, the more chances you have to catch them on the right day, in the right mood, with the right angle that finally lands and gets them to convert.

3 emails is the absolute bare minimum and for us our standard is 4-5!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d836ba2e-982c-4dcc-988f-376e440dd943/Screenshot_2026-07-27_at_4.18.09_AM.png?t=1785151113)

**4) Emails Spaced 1 Day Apart**

If you're an aggressive brand you can send 2 emails on day 1 (the welcome email at signup and a second one around 4 hours later) and widen the delay to 2 days at the tail end of longer flows.

But the general rule of thumb is to make sure your emails are spaced 1 day apart for the majority of the sequence.

**5) Welcome Discount In The Hero Sections**

Every single email in your welcome flow needs to have the welcome discount right in the hero section so that the moment a subscriber opens the email, they see the offer that's the primary reason they'll buy in the first place.

Welcome flows aren't like your regular campaign sends where you're doing brand education or building emotional connection.

They are conversion emails, and the offer needs to lead in each send so the subscriber never has to hunt for it.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c9bca00b-496f-4bb3-a013-46ce20a80189/Screenshot_2026-07-27_at_4.22.32_AM.png?t=1785151372)

**6) At Least One Text-Based Email**

Somewhere in your welcome flow, drop in a text-based email that comes across as a personal note from either the founder or someone on the support team.

Text-based emails crush because they feel like a real human just wrote you a message instead of a branded marketing send.

That human touch is often what gets a hesitant subscriber to finally convert.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/95bcf01d-7236-4ed6-9403-a5e1c3598d16/Screenshot-2025-05-13-at-7.21.39-AM.png?t=1785151393)

**7) Last Chance Urgency At The End**

The final email(s) in your welcome flow have to make the discount feel like it's actually going away.

Urgency is what closes the sales that the first 3-4 emails couldn't, because when a subscriber has ignored a few discount pitches already, the fear of losing the offer entirely is often the thing that pushes them to finally use their code.

You can frame the last email around _"your discount expires tonight"_ or _"final chance to redeem your code before it disappears"_.

Conversion rate on that email will spike compared to every other email in the flow.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6d374c9b-9135-4d0f-9cfd-1aa72279e0cd/Screenshot_2025-09-06_at_12.28.21_PM_1.jpg?t=1785151453)

And that's the full list!

Take 10 minutes this week to run through your own welcome flow against these. Anything that's missing is the first thing you should get dialed in.

And if you want my team to build your welcome flow for you, book a call with us [here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=welcome-flow-non-negotiables) »

entries.title: Learn From These 6 A/B Tests
entries.summary: We're 6 months into 2026, which means BFCM is officially around the corner.
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

We're 6 months into 2026, which means BFCM is officially around the corner.

Most brands start thinking about BFCM in October, which is roughly the marketing equivalent of studying for finals the night before…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6148d4a2-5ae2-414c-a18b-0dbd95f30806/axcndb.jpg?t=1784907153)

But by the time BFCM rolls around, you should already know what subject lines work for your list, what pop-up offers convert best, what welcome flow variation drives the highest AOV, and every other lever you can pull…

Which is why today I’m walking through 6 recent A/B tests learnings we've found that you can steal to lock in your Q4 game plan.

Let's get into it.

### Test 1: Scroll-To-Reveal Design vs Standard Layout

We tested a scroll-to-reveal design (where the product hides at the top and reveals as the customer scrolls) against our standard hero + product layout for a new product launch campaign.

See example below:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d678a737-5103-4b38-baa8-61ee942bf6e9/scrilklk_revrweak.png?t=1784896749)

_What A Scroll-To-Reveal Design Looks Like._

**Winner:** Scroll-to-reveal by a wide margin on revenue.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/09cd5fc9-71fd-4627-81f2-61755e6f5903/image__2___1_.png?t=1784902428)

For product launches or any promo where curiosity matters, the scroll-to-reveal design can be a fun thing to try and force engagement!

### Test 2: SMS With Image vs Without

We tested a new product drop SMS with an image attached against the same SMS without an image.

**Winner:** SMS with an image, by 4x on revenue.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8d734fee-6eb8-4ddf-b7b2-238ce65dc36c/Screenshot_2026-04-23_at_10.27.19_AM_1.jpg?t=1784902595)

For any high-intent SMS send (drop, promo, restock, etc), the image lets customers look at the product before they even click. If they like what they see, the click is basically a done deal.

### Test 3: "Your Order Is Ready To Be Shipped" vs Offer-First Subject Line

We tested a welcome email with a _"Your order is ready to be shipped"_ subject line and framing against a standard offer-first welcome email that leads with the discount.

**Winner:** Order-ready-to-ship framing, by a long shot.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/29a0298f-022a-4489-bc19-98359c7fa5c6/image__9___1_.png?t=1784846159)

Order Ready To Ship vs Offer-First

The framing of your subject line changes how the customer sees the entire email before they even open it. "Your order is ready to be shipped" frames it as an urgent action item the customer needs to take.

Much stronger than another discount they can circle back to later.

### Test 4: Welcome Email #1 Discount Placement

We tested where the discount code lives in the first welcome email. One variation had the code below the hero image (Variation A), and the other led with the code at the very top of the email (Variation B).

**Winner:** Code above the hero, with a higher click rate AND higher placed order rate.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c2cd9f42-9719-4466-b5a1-35374c4c3f5b/Screenshot_2026-03-11_at_8.40.12_AM_1__1_.jpg?t=1784903167)

As expected, putting the discount code and CTA button higher up in the email drives more clicks and more purchases. Customers don't want to scroll to find their offer, but want it front and center.

Put your discount code above your hero images!

### Test 5: Flat vs Mystery Discount In Abandoned Checkout

We tested _"Take 10% OFF your cart with code XXX"_ against _"You have a mystery discount in your cart with code XXX"_ in the abandoned checkout flow.

**Winner:** Mystery discount, with significantly higher engagement and orders.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/79e8ed36-1d7a-42b2-b964-b377f71612a9/Screenshot_2026-07-24_at_7.28.11_AM.png?t=1784903318)

Mystery codes are especially effective in abandoned cart and abandoned checkout flows.

Customers are already close to purchase, and the intrigue of _"what could the discount actually be?"_ is often enough to get them back to complete their order.

### Test 6: Pop-Up Image vs No Image

We tested including a product image in our desktop pop-up against a simpler form with no image.

**Winner:** No image, with a higher submission rate, more orders, and higher revenue.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d16e710d-09b6-48b4-b470-2ad8bd7eb4e4/Screenshot_2026-03-11_at_8.52.15_AM_1.jpg?t=1784904303)

For desktop pop-ups, less can actually be more. A cleaner form without an image gives the customer less to process, so their eye goes straight to the fields and the CTA button.

Faster read time = more submissions.

**And there you have it, 6 tests you can steal and run for yourself!**

These could be tests being ran on your account by our team… minimum 6-10 AB tests every month. Book a call [here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=learn-from-these-6-a-b-tests) »

entries.title: The Easiest Email Marketing Hack... Resend Your Past Winners!
entries.summary: The single easiest campaign win most brands are missing out on, is literally resending your campaigns that already crushed!
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Marketers love to say _"never send the same email twice."_

I disagree.

The single easiest campaign win most brands are missing out on, is literally **resending your campaigns that already crushed!**

Today, I'm going to walk you through why it works, when to do it, and how to run it without your list even noticing.

Let's get into it.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2e7691d1-d795-4d99-bc9d-6311037dff2a/ax69bx.jpg?t=1784718631)

### Repeating Your Winners

Before we break it down, here's a quick story time.

I was auditing a client brand recently that was somehow sending 30-40 campaigns a month. They were sending every day, sometimes twice a day…

So I pulled up the calendar and figured out what was going on…

I found that they were pulling 10 winning campaigns from months back, making zero changes, and dropping them into the calendar as fresh sends.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5c28ffaa-be84-41a5-8fd9-b822ffc02807/Screenshot_2026-06-02_at_12.29.37_PM.png?t=1784719200)

_All Resends Of Older Winning Campaigns._

The reason this actually works comes down to simple math on your list…

Say you send a campaign and it rips….

You probably had a 50% open rate on it, which means **half the people you sent it to never even saw it the first time.**

And **the ones who did open it are going to forget about it in a month…**

Add on top of that, **your list is constantly getting refreshed with new subscribers who have never seen that email before at all.**

If it was a winner once, it's going to be a winner again!

Nobody is going to care that you sent the same angle twice. Especially if it's a good email.

Which means you, as the brand, will get higher email volume (and more revenue), without doing any extra work.

### How To Do This For Yourself

Once you find a winning campaign in your account, here are a few ways to reuse it without your list catching on:

**1) Send The Same Email**

Literally change nothing if you want. I would recommend subject line change to be safe.

**2) Change the format.**

Take a graphic-heavy email and rewrite it as a plain text one from the founder, or vice versa. It’s the same message, but different look in the inbox.

**3) Adjust the copy / design slightly.**

Same angle, but in different words or different imagery! Rewrite the intro paragraph, swap the hero image, and keep the rest of the email 90% intact.

**5) Add the winning angle into your flows.**

If a testimonial email crushed as a campaign, add the testimonial email into your welcome flow, your abandonment flows, and your post-purchase flows so it runs on autopilot for every new subscriber.

Bottom line is, your best campaigns already exist…

Go mine your archive and think smarter, not harder folks!!

entries.title: Copy Maxxing Your Hero Sections
entries.summary: You ever wonder why some emails get tons of clicks but barely any sales?
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

You ever wonder why some emails get tons of clicks but barely any sales?

Most often this happens because you don’t give them enough _reason_ to buy.

Many brands hear “put a button in your hero section” and think that’s enough…

And while that gets clicks, it doesn't get sales because the customer hasn't been given a real reason to actually buy yet.

Today, I'm going to walk you through how to fix that so the clicks you get are actually high-intent ones.

Let's get into it.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b3027ab4-4108-43fd-b1b5-227b539ac0b0/ax0sui.jpg?t=1784551192)

### What Makes A Customer Actually Click AND Buy

For a customer to actually click a button in your email AND buy on your site, they need two things:

- A reason to click.

- A reason to click _with the_ _intent to buy_.

A CTA button on its own gets you clicks…

Nut a lot of those clicks come from customers who are just clicking to click. They haven't been given enough info to actually want to buy yet.

So they land on your site, look around for a few seconds, and bounce…

The fix is **copy maxxing** your hero section.

It just means giving the customer more real and valuable copy at the top of the email before the CTA.

Now, you’re giving them valuable reasons to click, showing off product benefits, and important context that makes them want to buy before they ever hit the button.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/22fe6745-ffd5-485d-9273-8da274eea3e3/1823-3.png?t=1784554511)

Copy Maxxed vs Not

A copy-maxxed hero may look like a lot of text at first, but if it's actually strong and compact, it gives the customer everything they need to know before hitting the button.

Which means the customers who DO click are way more likely to convert.

**When To Copy Maxx**

Copy-maxxed hero sections work great across almost every campaign and flow you send, but especially for:

**1) Educational campaigns**

The more you teach the customer inside the email, the higher the click-to-buy rate on your site.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2264ba5a-d358-45af-97d9-5b4b6be039ef/screencapture-mail-google-mail-u-1-2024-04-04-07_13_21-edit-1.png?t=1784551718)

**2) Post-purchase flows**

Customers are open to hearing more from you right after buying, so the hero is prime real estate for cross-sells and reviews.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f5771e33-26c0-46f3-9486-4e351d0d0e58/oyther-pro.jpg?t=1784551763)

**3) Winback flows**

The customer already knows the brand, so a copy-maxxed hero is your chance to remind them exactly why they should come back and buy again.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d3678e2e-61c5-45f6-a8bb-38bb2453b99b/Group_1000005058.jpg?t=1784551786)

And there you have it, copy maxxing in a nutshell. Try it out and A/B test it in your next big campaign 🧪.

entries.title: How To Use Zaymo For Building Interactive Emails
entries.summary: What if your customers could leave reviews, take upsells, and edit their subscriptions directly inside an email without ever needing to leave their inbox?
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

What if your customers could leave reviews, take upsells, and edit their subscriptions directly inside an email without ever needing to leave their inbox?

Well… now they can!!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5802dde0-b6f3-41ca-9960-cd063e9d40f2/awowtg.jpg?t=1784142820)

This is showing up a lot more among the biggest eight and nine-figure brands (especially in the subscription niche, though it applies to any brand running email).

Today, I'm going to walk you through what it does, where to use it, and the exact impact it's already having on our subscription brands.

Let's get into it.

### What This Tech Actually Is

You can now let customers take real actions (leaving reviews, taking upsells, editing subscriptions, answering surveys, etc) directly inside the email without ever going to your site.

Instead of the classic email → click → land on your site → complete action flow, everything happens in one click, right inside their inbox.

It’s the tech I've been waiting years to come out, and it's finally here!

#### The Best Use Cases Right Now

**1) Leaving reviews directly in email**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1e7e6603-59dd-4c8e-ade8-179b52b5e9d0/Screenshot_2026-07-15_at_11.34.21_AM.png?t=1784142191)

_Leaving A Review Directly In An Email_

Customers can leave a star rating and written review without ever leaving the email.

Because they don't have to go to your website to submit, you're going to get way more reviews across the board.

**2) Running surveys directly in email**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ed6f998f-5b6a-4c24-b52b-21fd84c8ef6e/Screenshot_2026-07-15_at_11.37.18_AM.png?t=1784142264)

_Asking Survey Questions Directly In An Email_

Same principle. Customers answer directly in their inbox, so you get way more feedback and way faster.

Which means the retention insights, product feedback, and customer research loops start moving much faster too.

**3) [Subscription Brands] One-click upsells directly in email**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6dade51a-8d4d-4892-9721-619c091ccd9a/Screenshot_2026-07-15_at_12.02.40_PM.png?t=1784142288)

_One-Click Upsell Directly In An Email_

Customers can add products to their next subscription order without ever going to the customer portal.

All they need to do is click once and their subscription is updated with the upsell!

**4) [Subscription Brands] Editing subscriptions directly in the billing reminder.**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9003dc99-8834-4722-825e-25edd17cf666/Screenshot_2026-07-15_at_11.44.11_AM.png?t=1784142320)

_Editing A Subscription Directly In A Billing Reminder_

This is the biggest use case for eight and nine-figure subscription brands (and even seven-figure ones).

**Subscribers can edit their subscription directly in the billing reminder email without ever landing in the customer portal.**

This matters because the customer portal is where your cancellations happen… So if your subscribers can make changes without ever visiting that page, they never see the cancel button and stay as a subscriber.

We actually implemented this for one of our subscription brands and it was one of the biggest reasons why we decreased their billing reminder cancellations by over 50%.

entries.title: Email Marketing Segmentation: Send To Your Whole List
entries.summary: One mistake I see a lot of brands make is only ever sending campaigns to their most engaged segment…
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

One mistake I see a lot of brands make is only ever sending campaigns to their most engaged segment…

This is honestly a reasonable move on paper, because sending to only your most engaged people protects deliverability and keeps your open rates high.

But by only sending to your engaged segment, you're missing out on a big chunk of subscribers who could still buy from you… and it's a lot of missed sales every single month.

Today I'm going to walk you through when to actually send to your whole email list, why it works, and the exact checklist to make sure each full-list send actually converts.

Let's get into it!

### The Segmentation Mistake Many Brands Make

Now, this goes against what I usually talk about, but I actually encourage you to send to your whole email list… sometimes.

Take a look at this screenshot below…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a11d2370-2598-4671-83be-7e926a5251b4/screenshot_2026-05-14_at_6.53.59___am_720.png?t=1784084517)

_Example Of A Brand Only Sending To Their Engaged List._

This is an example of what NOT to do.

Every single campaign only goes to the same engaged segment, while the rest of the list just sits there.

This can be fine for simplicity and deliverability… but I don’t recommend for most brands.

The thing is, you're paying for every profile on your list whether they open your emails or not.

If the rest of your list never sees another campaign from you, they're literally just costing you money for no reason.

So if your deliverability is in a healthy spot, sending to your whole list 1-2x a month (things like sales, big announcements, or major promo drops) is smart to do.

You get revenue from people you'd otherwise never touch, and Klaviyo picks up fresh engagement data that helps you re-segment down the road.

You’ll get a nice healthy extra bump in revenue as well.

One send here and there to your whole list will not destroy your deliverability.

Now, before you send to your whole list, there's something to keep in mind…

You're sending to people who haven't opened your emails in weeks or months. That means you get ONE shot to re-earn their attention.

I just recommend blasting to your whole list 1-2 times per month for a big campaign… something like a sale announcement or product release.

When you are sending it… make sure you have things dialed in…

#### The Full-Send Checklist

**1) Use your best-performing subject line format.**

The subject line has to be strong enough to pull an open from someone who hasn't opened in 60+ days. This is NOT the time to test a mid subject line or try a new angle.

Look at your top 10 highest open-rate subject lines from the past 3-6 months, find the pattern, and lean on it.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4899893b-7805-47c4-8070-21e113082434/Screenshot_2026-07-14_at_8.11.00_PM.png?t=1784085097)

_Subject Line Performance With Hiro Analytics._

**2) Send at your best-performing day and time.**

Send day/time matters way more on whole-list sends than engaged-only ones. Your engaged segment will open whenever, but your quieter subscribers only open if you catch them at the exact right moment.

Look at your top-performing sends and match your whole-list send to the same day/time.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b7e1cbcf-c46a-4d79-960d-9ffb7b676f72/Screenshot_2026-02-10_at_1.47.25_PM_1.jpg?t=1784085290)

_Send Day Report With Hiro Analytics._

**3) Use your best-performing creative format.**

If your list responds to bestseller highlights, run bestseller highlights. If they respond to FAQ-style teardowns, do that.

Don't pick a creative format because it feels fresh. Pick based on what your data says is actually converting.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8b97240c-ac40-4288-8b79-751dc985714b/Screenshot_2026-07-14_at_8.16.39_PM.png?t=1784085460)

_Campaign Creatives Tab With Hiro Analytics._

All of these can easily be pulled through_[Hiro Analytics](https://www.hiroanalytics.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=email-marketing-segmentation-send-to-your-whole-list)_… which is what we use for email analytics.

We run it for all of our brands, and it shows you trends that save you a ton of time vs going in and looking at Klaviyo campaign-by-campaign. Highly recommend checking it out.

Bottom line… full send to your whole list 1-2 times per month and you'll be shocked at the revenue sitting in that dormant part of your list!!

entries.title: How To Customize Your Welcome Flow By Quiz Answer
entries.summary: What if you could have your welcome flow speak EXACTLY to your customer’s main pain point they are looking to have solved?
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

What if you could have your welcome flow speak EXACTLY to your customer’s main pain point they are looking to have solved?

Well, you can.

And pretty easily too…

Almost every high-performing brand is running some version of a quiz pop-up these days, and for good reason!

It's one of the highest-converting pop-up format right now…

Not to mention, subscribers are basically telling you what to sell them.

But most brands collect all that data and then send every subscriber the same basic welcome flow, which makes zero sense when every subscriber literally told you exactly how to sell them.

Today, I'm going to walk you through how to turn those quiz answers into a customized welcome flow so that you can get an easy 15-25% lift in conversions.

Let’s get into it.

### How To Set This Up

**1) Build your quiz pop-up**

Quiz pop-ups ask a question first from a customer, such as "What problem are you trying to solve?" before asking for email.

This works great because it seems like a low barrier to entry, and we're not asking for email right off the bat, which is like asking someone to marry you on the first date.

You can build this in Klaviyo, but I recommend you use [Alia](https://www.aliapopups.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-customize-your-welcome-flow-by-quiz-answer) for it (killer pop-up form platform we use for most of our 100+ brands).

Whether you build it in Klaviyo or Alia, you can easily tag people with a profile property based on what pain point they clicked in the quiz.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/96b850d2-1aff-4f0d-bb58-f6d5d946399e/Screenshot_2026-07-13_at_9.22.31_AM.png?t=1783923760)

Quiz Pop-up Example Built On [Alia Pop-Ups](https://www.aliapopups.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-customize-your-welcome-flow-by-quiz-answer)

**2) Split welcome flow paths by their quiz answer**

When someone answers your quiz, all you have to do is split paths in your Klaviyo flow with a “conditional split” with each response.

Here’s how it should look…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f10248c3-d839-40da-9d49-413a808c4ab2/Screenshot_2026-07-13_at_9.32.16_AM.png?t=1783924393)

Splitting Welcome Flow By Profile Property From Quiz

**3) Customize the first 2-3 emails to speak directly to their answer.**

If someone told you their main problem is dry skin, the first email should be about dry skin.

If someone said their issue is post-workout recovery, the first email should be about recovery.

You'll be catering the content to what the subscriber actually cares about.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d16c5f85-509c-4ab5-b86b-5a0b7216bf61/07fccfa45f9041ad9fc44eda3c19defc5cb3b090f3c74dc1a53242a16fe005ec.png?t=1783919770)

_Example Email 1 Customized Based On Quiz Answer._

**4) Merge everyone back into the same emails after those 2-3 emails.**

Once you've hooked them with the personalized opener, the rest of the welcome flow can run as normal…

This will just help you with reducing workload so you don’t need full welcome flows by answer.

Personalization is the key in 2026.

We typically see a 15-25% lift in conversions from this. Nothing insane, but for a brand that's scaling hard, this can have a big impact!

Now go audit your welcome flow and start plugging in those quiz answers. It’s a very simple and easy win…

entries.title: When To Use Klaviyo Dynamic Product Sections
entries.summary: A question I often get is: "How do I feature the right products when I have multiple SKUs? How should my campaigns be different than stores with one product"
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

A question I often get is: _"How do I feature the right products when I have multiple SKUs? How should my campaigns be different than stores with one product"_

This is one of the trickiest problems in email marketing… and today I'm walking you through a Klaviyo feature that shows your customers the product they're most likely to buy every time.

It's called dynamic product sections, and it's a total game changer if your catalog is massive and you have no way to know which products each customer actually wants.

Let's break it down.

### Dynamic vs Static Product Sections

There are two ways to build a product section in your emails.

The first is a **static product section..**.

You pick the products yourself, design the section, and lock it in.

This is what it’s like when you design emails in Figma… you are choosing which products to feature and everybody is getting the same product.

The second, and less commonly used…

Is a **dynamic product section**.

Klaviyo picks what products to feature per person, and pulls in whatever they've recently viewed, added to cart, or are most likely to buy based on their behavior.

It’s way less pretty and on brand… but much more relevant to the customer and what they’re interested in.

We love using these product sections for brands with 10+ SKUs oftentimes instead of stores with just a few SKUs.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2eb2b406-e065-441e-a778-7bcc2aa2823b/Screenshot_2026-07-02_at_10.00.46_AM.png?t=1783487772)

_The Product Feed Klaviyo Pulls From (Based On Recent Views)._

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8cc12594-5a90-4f6c-a84b-4e417c264897/Screenshot_2026-04-16_at_7.40.08_AM.png?t=1783487692)

_What your product feed may look like_

But most brands default to static like it's the safer bet, when it's actually the one costing them money in some cases…

Say you're a fashion brand and you build your welcome flow with a static product section with products that are popular in January.

By summer, you've got outdated products being sent while customers are looking for what's actually in season.

That's exactly why dynamic sections fix this problem.

Instead of you picking, Klaviyo pulls in whatever your customer has been browsing OR what products are most popular in your store right now.

As a result, your flows stay relevant all year without you ever touching them and it’s much less work to maintain…

Take a look at this A/B test:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b9fb218b-5eb1-44ef-b48f-e84fed46a37b/Screenshot_2026-04-16_at_7.38.04_AM.png?t=1783488243)

_Dynamic vs Static Test_

You can see that dynamic nearly doubled in placed orders, and lifted CTR from 0.24% to 0.38% at the same time.

This is just one test, but these results held consistent across many emails.

**Test dynamic product sections on your flows / campaigns and see if they work for you!**

entries.title: A Sneaky Way To Get More Clicks From Every Email
entries.summary: The footer is the ONE section that stays exactly the same across…
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

When was the last time you thought about your email footer?

The footer is the ONE section that stays exactly the same across…

So if you optimize it once, it gets you clicks and $$$ on every campaign and flow going forward.

Today, I'm walking you through the exact footer structure we build that increases click rates 25%+.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d9d7a422-eaf8-45b5-a9ca-04350c801442/avxwx1.jpg?t=1783292139)

### Why The Footer Matters More Than You Think

The footer is one of the most-clicked sections in your entire email.

Customers who didn't connect with the products you featured in the regular email scroll to the bottom looking for another way in.

That means if the only thing waiting for them down there is legal text and an unsubscribe link, you just lost a warm customer…

Case in point: On a recent email we sent, the footer alone drove MORE clicks than the core email content itself:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/29bb4755-9a01-41dd-91d9-aaa2cad82d29/gikahdfxcaarfbu__2_.jpg?t=1783293977)

_Footer Links (766 clicks) Outperforming The Core Email Content (722 clicks)._

You're basically running a second store at the bottom of every email…

### Every High-ROI Footer Has These 3 Parts:

**1) Category Buttons**

This is a non-negotiable…

A simple grid of _"Shop Skincare / Shop Body / Shop Hair"_ or whatever the brand's main categories are.

The customer who doesn't want your featured product still wants something, so give them the option to find it!

You'll turn a lot of "scrolled past" moments into actual sales.

**2) Unique Selling Points**

This is your risk reversal and core selling points. Things like "_Free shipping over $50,_" "_90-day money-back guarantee,_" "_Made in USA,_" or "_Trusted by 100K+ customers._"

As a brand, you want the last thing they see to reinforce trust, not just the unsubscribe link.

**3) Social Proof**

The footer is the perfect place to show them you're the real deal before they close the email.

Rotate through star ratings ("★★★★★ 10,000+ reviews"), press logos, UGC photos , or trust badges like "Made in USA" or "60-Day Guarantee" to prove you've got the receipts.

And if you have room, throw in a "Tag us @brandname and we'll feature you on our story" or "Follow us for new drops and behind the scenes" to keep them in your world after they close the email.

It builds your social presence at zero cost plus the customers who actually engage with those CTAs tend to become your highest-LTV customers anyway.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a5ef0bdc-486c-4d24-b6c9-ae54aa9d6dcd/screenshot-2026-05-29-at-8.43.12-am-1.png?t=1783293930)

_Footer Examples We Build For Our Brands._

As a note, make sure to keep these light! You want a few clean rows, instead of a whole other email built on the bottom lol.

PS - I have 10+ footer templates in my private community as well as 250+ other email templates… [check it out here](https://www.skool.com/email-marketerz/about?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=a-sneaky-way-to-get-more-clicks-from-every-email).

entries.title: Simple Offer Mistake Most Brands Make
entries.summary: Most brands already offer some kind of discount on their site OR on a product at all times… which is fine and great.
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most brands already offer some kind of discount on their site OR on a product at all times… which is fine and great.

But then they slap ANOTHER discount in the pop-up form that sounds way worse than the one already sitting on their site…

Today, I'm walking you through how to frame your discounts so your pop-up leads with the strongest offer and you make the most profit!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b6380fa6-8161-4d87-9a5b-b3e317f8a860/avojcm.jpg?t=1782976679)

### The Offer Mistake

Let's look at this brand…

As a brand, their goal is to push people toward the 3-pack ($139.90) over the single pack ($54.95) because it is bettyer economics for them.

The 3-pack is advertised as 15% off, which if you translate the value it is **$25 OFF** in actual dollars.

**$25 OFF hits WAY harder than "15% off" in a shopper's brain.**

That’s the first point…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9296ef4f-dcef-4c05-84bc-929fd3e1cbfd/screenshot_2026-06-30_at_8.56.42___am.png?t=1782970453)

_Chronic Australia's 3-Pack Discount._

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/eb03ea98-c500-4e2e-9227-b11e6fe2025e/Screenshot_2026-07-01_at_10.33.21_PM.png?t=1782970488)

_Chronic Australia's Pop-Up Form._

The second point… is their pop-up form offer.

They are pushing a WORSE offer than what is on the site!

The email sign-up and pop-up push $10 OFF…

Why lead with a worse-sounding $10 off when they're already giving away $25 off on the core offer?

Do you think your pop-up form and welcome flow would get more leads and conversions if you led with here’s $25 OFF rather than $10 off?

The answer is yes and our data backs it up.

Here's how they should be framing this instead, and how you should think about your offers too:

**Option 1: Drop the pop-up discount completely.**

Save the margins and just highlight the core offer you have for your main product on the site!

Make the pop-up say _"You've Got $25 OFF!"_ and let the welcome flow drive people straight to the 3-pack page with discount already applied.

The added benefit to this is nobody's incentivized to grab the single pack because that discount only works on the 3-pack (which the brand wants people to buy)

It's a real margin saver when you're trying to push as many people toward the core offer without over-discounting.

To show you much offers can move the needle, take a look at this AB test we ran for a different brand by doing this same sort of offer test:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7817f9a7-a332-400d-8fc2-14b6e4965359/Screenshot_2026-05-25_at_10.29.11_AM.png?t=1782971113)

_$25 OFF brought In 10.7% placed order rate._

Just by switching the pop-up offer to $25 OFF, we saw placed order rate jump from 3.3% to 10.7%!

This kind of strategy is why we run most of our brands on [Alia](https://www.aliapopups.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=simple-offer-mistake-most-brands-make). It's the easiest way to whip up pop-ups and A/B test offers like this.

**Option 2: Keep $10 OFF… But Stack it to $35 OFF the 3-pack.**

$25 off the 3-pack + $10 pop-up discount = $35 OFF total.

The brand is already giving this away but they’re telling customers they only get $10 off.

You're already giving this away…the customer just doesn't perceive it that way.

Make the pop-up say _"You've Got $35 OFF!"_ and let the welcome flow break down the math for them.

Just make sure the discount only applies to the 3-pack, so single-pack buyers still pay full price and get pushed toward the core offer.

Either option lifts take rate, and pushes people toward the exact product you want them to buy.

Offer maxx your pop ups and welcome flows in 2026!!

**This is the biggest lever you can pull. You can see the offer test and impact it had on the brand above. We will manage all of this for you.** [**Click here to book a call.**](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=simple-offer-mistake-most-brands-make)

entries.title: Send This Email Before You Set Your Next Sale
entries.summary: Have you ever had a big sale or product release completely flop?
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Have you ever had a big sale or product release completely flop?

We all have.

Here’s one trick you can use to make sure it doesn’t happen again…

Today, I'm walking you through one email you can send before any big launch that solves this AND builds hype for the drop at the same time.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f8fe3239-58c7-4307-999d-8720fdf510d2/avknle.jpg?t=1782860638)

### The Deliverability Booster Teaser Email

A few days before your big sale or drop, send this simple teaser email.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d75ad656-a617-4f7d-b8d2-135178870688/screenshot_2026-06-17_at_10.50.25___am.png?t=1782861154)

_The Pre-Sale Teaser Email_

At first glance, it looks pretty basic, but the real magic is in the ask…

Because you're going to tell subscribers to do 4 specific things in exchange for "early access" or "first dibs":

- Move this email to your primary inbox

- Star it

- Reply with an emoji so we know you're in

- Click the link below

Every single one of these 4 actions is a top-tier engagement signal that tells Gmail _"these people LOVE this brand."_

So when your actual sale email sends a few days later to your full list, you’re pushed straight to the primary inbox.

As a note, you don't actually have to give anyone "first dibs" or even track who replied…

Anyone who engaged with the teaser is going to see the actual sale email in their main inbox anyway, so you’re getting two wins for the price of one.

**When To Send It**

Any time you're about to blast your wider list with something important (product launches, sales, restocks, etc.)… Send this 2-5 days before!

You'll find your deliverability holds up way better when launch day actually comes around.

Now go pull this off on your next promo and thank me later.

entries.title: When To Use MMS In Your SMS Marketing
entries.summary: Because if you're not, you're leaving easy revenue on the table…
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Are you using MMS in your SMS marketing?

Because if you're not, you're leaving easy revenue on the table…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d0cb9296-adc0-46b3-a978-10f58327da3f/avg6gj.jpg?t=1782741040)

MMS costs 3x more than regular SMS, and blasting them on every send will burn through your budget fast… But done right, it unlocks a whole new level of conversion.

Let's break it down.

**The Net Profit Math**

Here's a real AB test we ran for one of our clients recently.

Version A was a plain SMS. Version B was the same message with an MMS visual added.

The results:

- Revenue: Version B made 116% MORE revenue.

- AOV: Jumped from $64 to $86.

- Net Profit: Doubled from $309 to $658.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b5d67901-656b-40a2-b698-47df6208cff1/screenshot_2026-05-13_at_09.24.16_720.png?t=1782741382)

_MMS AB Test_

MMS costed 3x more per credit on this send. But the extra $24 in send cost printed an extra $349 in net profit!

If you're wondering when MMS is actually worth it, the general rule is the image has to move enough extra revenue to cover the cost AND still turn a profit.

If it can't do that, save the credits.

With that rule in mind, here are 4 sends where MMS consistently pays for itself.

**1. New Product Drops**

When you've got a new product to push, show it. People are way more likely to click through and buy something they can actually see.

Plus, customers want to see what they're buying before they commit.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/21f0ba52-6848-4d3c-a70a-5e306e267e67/screenshot_2026-06-26_at_10.26.43___am_360.png?t=1782741510)

_New Product Launch MMS_

**2. Educational Infographic**

Some things are faster to show than to explain.

A clean infographic gets the point across before they read a single word.

Use it for explaining how the product works, what's inside, or the kind of results people see. Anything where a paragraph of text would slow the message down.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/affffc8e-2ce9-432d-b885-6ba62887bb82/hlmenm_w0aagwg7_720.jpg?t=1782741871)

_Infographic MMS_

**3. The Meme**

Most brands are too scared to be funny over text, which is exactly why it stands out.

A meme that fits your brand doesn't read like marketing, so people keep your number around instead of opting out the second they get bored.

Mars Men runs these constantly and it's a big reason their SMS doesn't get ignored no matter how often they send.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1e42f5fd-5e59-421c-92ac-87b7f7f1e0f0/hlmemuwwkaa2chk_720.jpg?t=1782741983)

_Meme MMS_

**4. The Free Gift Reveal**

We tested this for one of our clients recently. Version A was a plain SMS mentioning the free gift they were offering with purchase, while version B was the same exact message with a visual of the gift added.

Version B brought in 4x more revenue, because the visual makes the offer feel real instead of just sounding good!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7bd11265-3dc8-45be-b946-92972915c8c1/screenshot_2026-06-26_at_10.16.23___am.png?t=1782742359)

_Free Gift With Purchase AB Test_

**The Final Takeaway**

Bottom line is the math has to work with MMS. If you're unsure what to send, these 4 use cases are a great place to start.

Every MMS in your calendar should be earning its place!

If you want my team to audit your SMS program and run it for you, book a call [here »](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=when-to-use-mms-in-your-sms-marketing)

entries.title: The Best Non-Discount Emails You Can Send
entries.summary: The default move when revenue dips is to send another sale… but it's the fastest way to demolish your margins and train your list to wait around for the next promo.
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most ecom brands lean WAY too hard on discounts.

The default move when revenue dips is to send another sale… but it's the fastest way to demolish your margins and train your list to wait around for the next promo.

Today I'm walking you through the 5 best non-discount emails you can send instead.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/fbd3b3bd-9ab1-4e8d-82ab-c2c5bcdf8d29/av9om0.jpg?t=1782491023)

Let's break it down.

**The Long Form Testimonial**

Nobody reads short, tiny testimonials.

But when a customer sees someone going through a real emotional transformation in your testimonial, they buy into it hard. They see themselves on the other side of the journey, and read every single word.

These crush as ad creative too, and they're insanely easy to make. Just let your customers do the selling for you!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9fd35343-bc28-4009-9581-197b3ed7096e/Review_Spotlight___The_Black_Stuff.jpg?t=1782488237)

_The Long-Form Testimonial Email._

**The Restock Email**

Something went out of stock and now it's back.

Even if customers didn't care about the product before, FOMO kicks in the second they see it restocked.

The best part is that you don't actually need a product to go out of stock to send this either…

**If you just got a fresh shipment in, or you just want to push a specific SKU, a simple** **_"Hey, this just got restocked!_****" angle is more than enough.**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/18639b49-5581-4254-82e3-dd33f98ce46e/Syrup_Back_in_stock__Smokeshow.jpg?t=1782488297)

_The Restock Email._

**The Founder OR Product Story**

People will always want to buy from people.

A plain-text email that looks like it's coming from a real human always stands out in an inbox full of branded marketing emails.

Tell a story, share the vision, and let the product mention come naturally at the end.

It hits hardest because it feels less like a sales pitch and more like an email from a friend.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/bfeca3c3-e0bb-463b-a65e-76124687fbca/screenshot_2026-06-26_at_5.45.25___pm_720.png?t=1782488336)

_The Founder Story Email._

**The Data-Backed Stat**

Numbers speak louder than words. Every single time.

_"61% of people are switching from alcohol to THC drinks"_ hits WAY harder than _"people are switching from alcohol."_

Doesn't matter if it's about how customers behave, the cost of skipping your product, or the science behind it… as long as the number is strong and relevant, build the email around that one stat.

Numbers do all the convincing for you.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9a08ed10-1c4e-42b9-b045-e9ead792c639/20_Early_Access_%2B_Retail_Reminder.jpg?t=1782488365)

_The Data-Backed Email._

**The Single-Question FAQ**

Most FAQ emails have 5-7 questions stacked on top of each other, but nobody is going to read all that.

Instead, build the entire email around just ONE question.

Whatever the biggest objection or hesitation people have about your product, have your founder answer it in depth, plain-text style, like they're talking directly to the customer.

No discount needed at the end!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d84b1d78-6011-4b32-84f2-ddfb5f7a7267/screenshot-2025-05-01-at-7.53.48-am__9__720.png?t=1782488396)

_The Single-Question FAQ Email._

Add these five to your campaign calendar this month and stop relying on discounts to keep your profit up!!

entries.title: The 2026 Email Flows Playbook
entries.summary: So today I'm handing you that entire playbook to digest in less than 5 minutes...
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I gave a keynote to 50+ ecom founders/marketers last month.

I shared the 2026 email flows playbook

So today I'm handing you that entire playbook to digest in less than 5 minutes...

In the exact order they need to be done…

Let’s go.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2a4ec0ec-7da4-4dfd-b1cc-e3c119e2db23/Screenshot_2026-06-24_at_9.37.36_AM.png?t=1782283045)

### The Pop-Up

Your pop-up is the single biggest lever you have.

Doubling your opt-in rate doubles the value of every single email you'll ever send.

That's why this is the first thing we fix on every audit.

Target 10%+ opt-in rate as the floor, NOT the ceiling. And always be testing the offer, timing, design, and copy.

Quiz pop-ups and gamified formats are absolutely ripping right now…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b2882ff8-1c7f-4a0f-860f-906677a98dc4/Frame_2__4_.jpg?t=1782247384)

_Mystery Discount Framing Outperforms Standard Pop-Ups 2-3x Every Time._

_[Alia](https://www.aliapopups.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-2026-email-flows-playbook)__is the easiest way to build these pop-ups. We run most of our brands on it and it always outperforms every other tool out there._

### The Pre-Purchase Flows

Our pre-purchase flows are our welcome flow, site abandon, browse abandon, cart abandon, and checkout abandon.

For your welcome flow, you have to be sending every single day.

Every day you wait, the lead gets colder.

A two-day delay between emails is money lost!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/02108f5d-def0-4377-ac33-7fb3950263df/Commerce_Roundtable.pptx.png?t=1782247585)

_Welcome Flow Mixed In With Value And Offer Reminder Emails_

Aim for 3-5 emails per flow, sent one per day. No skipping days, and no spacing them out across the week.

Hit on different educational points, include your discount in every email, and include at least one text based email in your welcome flow.

Same idea applies to your abandonment flows… but there's one extra layer that 90% of brands get wrong.

Two non-negotiable rules for every abandonment email:

- **Rule 1:** Dynamic product block at the top. The exact product they were looking at should be the first thing they see.

- **Rule 2:** Aggressive copy beats passive. _"you left something behind”_ is not strong enough!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5ea29bdb-9f07-44b2-8d1f-52b303c6a6b3/Screenshot-2026-05-07-at-7.40.25-AM.png?t=1782247679)

_Dynamic Product Block At The Top!_

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a3446a16-204d-4abd-bfc9-ac7e406f19ed/Screenshot-2026-03-11-at-2.00.52-PM.png?t=1782247669)

_Aggressive Copy Framing_

These two fixes alone usually lift abandonment revenue 20-30% on the audits we run.

### The Post-Purchase Flow

Pre-purchase gets you the first order. Post-purchase is where LTV is actually built.

This is a relationship flow first. The goal is to make customers feel great about the purchase they just made, educate them on the product, and only then nudge the reorder.

Here's the sequence we start with:

- **Immediately:** Founder thank-you email. Text-based, personal, with a soft P.S. cross-sell. Sets the tone for the entire post-purchase experience.

- **Days 2-6:** Product education. Show customers how to use the product properly so they get results faster. Faster usage = faster reorders.

- **Around day 10:** The cross-sell. Time it for when the product physically arrives at their doorstep and excitement is highest.

- **Days 21-28:** Founder check-in. Warm, personal, with a soft reorder nudge baked in. Underrated, especially for consumables.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/09f06201-ff9d-4585-9755-7b0f5f494209/Commerce_Roundtable.pptx-1.png?t=1782247911)

_Post Purchase Example Flow_

And if they go quiet for a while after that, the winback flow takes over.

### Winback Flow

This flow is meant for people who haven't thought in a while…

Lapsed customers need a real reason to come back.

We start the flow around 3x your average repeat purchase time, and test offers such as store credit, BOGO, bundles, and free gifts to find what hits.

Lapsed customers don't come back because you asked nicely lol…

They come back because of the right incentive.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b8803560-4429-4974-8806-bad924f90558/Screenshot-2026-03-11-at-12.52.52-PM.png?t=1782248420)

_Consistently Outperforms "We Miss You" Sends._

### What To Test

Once the foundation is dialed in, these are the highest-leverage tests across every flow, in order:

Offers first. Different discounts can DOUBLE conversion rates on the same flow.

Subject lines next. They reframe the email and impact revenue, not just opens.

Send timing. Time between emails, time until your first email, etc. These will vary account to account.

Email format. Mix graphic and text-based emails and test placement for each.

These points are the bare minimum for 2026.

Lock in your email systems… escape the Meta trap.

entries.title: How Most Brands Run Giveaways Wrong
entries.summary: Most brands look at the opt-in count, see thousands of new emails on the list, and assume the giveaway worked!
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I hate when brands run giveaways…

Most do it completely wrong and cause more harm than good.

Most brands look at the opt-in count, see thousands of new emails on the list, and assume the giveaway worked!

The problem is though that opt-ins are **NOT** buyers…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/3fb81f8d-d7d2-4949-8174-6070493976c9/auweof.jpg?t=1782114599)

You're growing the list while stalling your own revenue at the same time…

**The Giveaway Trap**

Giveaway opt-in subscribers consistently underperform every other lead source we see across our 200+ clients. They convert worse than people who came in through urgency, discounts, or even regular pop-up forms.

Because, say you're giving away a $2,000 chair, and someone opts in on June 5th hoping to win it…

They're not buying anything from you for at least a few weeks because they might win it for free!!

So why would they buy from you and pay full price right now?

So, you end up with a bigger list, lower deliverability, lower revenue per opt-in, and a 3-week stall on everyone who's actually real.

**The Post-Opt-In Flip**

Here's the move that fixes this.

The second someone opts in for your giveaway, try to upsell them…

Use something like this:

=====

_"We're expecting over 20,000 people to enter this giveaway. The odds of winning are extremely low._

_Because you opted in we want to give you $250 off, expires in 3 days. You'll still be entered into the giveaway._

_If you do happen to win, we'll refund you in full and ship the chair anyway."_

=====

Now look what just happened.

**You kept the giveaway hook intact, but now you handed them a real reason to buy NOW and not wait.**

You introduced urgency that runs on a tighter timeline than the giveaway itself. And you removed the risk of them missing out on the prize.

The conversion rate on this flow is significantly higher than letting them sit on the list for 3-4 weeks doing nothing.

Plus you still get the list growth, brand awareness, and viral upside of running a giveaway.

If you're running giveaways without an aggressive post-opt-in flow, you're leaving most of the revenue on the table and training your newest subscribers to wait.

_**Build the flow first. Then run the giveaway.**_

If your giveaways are growing your list without growing your revenue, our team builds these post-opt-in flows for our 100+ clients across email and SMS. We've done $250M in email sales across 300+ brands the past 2 years. [Book a call here »](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-most-brands-run-giveaways-wrong)

entries.title: How To Actually Use AI For Email Marketing
entries.summary: Today, I want to talk about how to actually use AI for email marketing the right way,
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Today, I want to talk about how to actually use AI for email marketing the right way,

Most brands are letting AI plan their entire campaign calendar in 2026…

The worst part is they're just prompting ChatGPT with _"make me a calendar,"_ taking whatever it spits out, and shipping 15 emails that all sound the same.

**And your email marketing results suck as a result…**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5dd0da76-1150-4b07-a01b-1f9adfb6fa86/aup5qw.jpg?t=1781845653)

Let’s break it down.

#### The 4 Part Calendar Strategy Process

Every monthly calendar planning session starts with four steps… in this order:

- Past winners

- Winning ad angles / landing page angles

- Competitor swipes

- AI ideation last.

Past winners are emails that already crushed in your account. All you need to do is resend them with some because if they worked once, they'll work again. This alone usually fills 3-5 spots in the calendar.

Winning ad angles come next. Take the top-converting angles from your paid acquisition and turn them into emails. Your ads team has already validated what messaging works on your audience, so use those too.

Then competitor swipes. Pull ideas from [milled.com](https://milled.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-actually-use-ai-for-email-marketing) and the brands you actually follow. You're looking for what's working in your category right now.

ONLY after all of that do you bring in AI. By the time it gets involved, your calendar already has its strongest ideas locked in. AI just fills the remaining gaps and suggests send dates.

Here's what the flywheel actually looks like:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a76901c2-eb3d-458e-af4f-ab9ea6b10f37/Screenshot_2026-06-18_at_10.40.40_PM.png?t=1781847692)

_How We Build Every Calendar At Well Copy._

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/494a2ad1-772a-496c-9927-b7b0ec4926a5/ChatGPT_Image_Jun_7__2026__09_13_53_PM_1.jpg?t=1781847720)

_How We Build Every Calendar At Well Copy._

#### The 5 Pillars

Now that you've got your inputs lined up, the next step is making sure every idea fits one of five content pillars: educational, social proof, community, product highlights, and sales.

A balanced calendar runs across all five every month so the list never feels like you're just hitting them with sales.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/16a830c4-b334-4da9-b968-ad543e60941a/image_4499.jpg?t=1781847124)

_The 5 Pillars Of A Balanced Email Calendar._

**The Prompt**

Once you've pulled your past winners, ad angles, and competitor swipes, drop them into ChatGPT or Claude with this:

_"Here are the angles I've already pulled from past winners, ads, and competitors. Help me round out the rest of the month across the 5 pillars, suggest dates, and flag gaps."_

You'll have a balanced 15-email calendar built around what's already proven to work for your brand.

**The Bigger System**

Aside from calendars, we also use AI for analysis, copy writing, and flow briefs.

Which is why I built two AI resources trained on everything we do across 100+ brands and $250M+ in email data at my agency:

**1. Email Marketing Brain (Free)**

This ChatGPT bot pumps out campaign calendars, email copy, flow strategies, and email audits, all trained on our frameworks. And it's free.

[Get the Custom GPT here »](https://www.wellcopy.net/gpt?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-actually-use-ai-for-email-marketing)

**2. MX Claude Skill File (In My Paid Community)**

This is the more advanced version. The output is on another level when it comes to writing copy, especially compared to the GPT. These are the actual skill and context files we use internally at our 100+ client agency. It forces you to give proper brand context before it writes anything and QAs against itself so nothing gets made up.

I dropped this in our Skool community a bit ago and the response has been insane:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e4ffc1b7-6828-4377-b469-4d383405f7fd/Max___June_Week_1___Infographic_6.jpg?t=1781847148)

If you want in, it lives inside the community alongside 30+ course modules, 250+ templates, and two live calls a week with me 😉

[Access the Claude Skill + community here »](https://www.skool.com/email-marketerz/about?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-actually-use-ai-for-email-marketing)

entries.title: The Easiest 10-Minute Pop-Up Fix Before Your Next Sale
entries.summary: If so, you should be updating your email pop-up and core email flows to go along with it!
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

You are going to be running a 4th of July Sale soon… right?

If so, you should be **updating your email pop-up and core email flows to go along with it!**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0acaa869-05a8-46b0-9a92-29ca94deffae/auj3cy.jpg?t=1781682229)

Lots of sales are about to hit this summer (Fourth of July, summer clearance, Labor Day, etc.), and most brands are about to let conversions and email sign-ups slip through the cracks because they forgot this one thing.

Takes 30 ~ish minutes to setup and is well worth it.

Let's break it down.

**The Pop-Up Mismatch**

Say you're running a 40% off Fourth of July sale and your site is pushing it everywhere.

But your pop-up form still says "10% off your first order."

Now you've got a problem.

A new visitor sees 40% off everywhere on your site... but then your pop-up offers them 10%??

That's confusing and frustrating, and you're capping new sign-ups at a worse offer than the one they could just grab on site anyway…

When a sale goes live, your pop-up needs to go with it.

**Your form should instead say “40% OFF 4th Of July Sale!” and ask for the email.**

- 40% sounds better than 10% OFF so your will get more sign-ups

- You aren’t giving an extra 10% off which is going to save your margins

- It is a more fluid customer experience

(Yes, the customer doesn’t need to opt-in to get the offer… but they don’t know that and they opt-in at a high rate!)

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/432b0d76-9769-4ca4-9f50-31e50f5864cc/Max___June_Week_3___Infographic_4.jpg?t=1781682309)

_Pop-ups built to match the actual sale (Black Friday + Mother's Day)._

The fix takes about 10 minutes:

**Step 1:** Swap the pop-up copy to match the sale. _"Get 40% off, 4th of July Exclusive."_

**Step 2:** Update the welcome flow the same way so the emails reinforce the offer the rest of the site is pushing.

Both are text-only changes… No design work needed.

Klaviyo also lets you schedule pop-ups and flows ahead of time, so you can set it up the week before and have it auto-switch the moment the sale launches.

And if you want to push it even further, scratch-off pop-ups work really well too.

The mystery of scratching to reveal the offer gets way more engagement than a typical static pop-up.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/3e84aeb9-4f9d-49fb-8a29-7f2dc2371c8d/Max___June_Week_3___Infographic_5.jpg?t=1781682361)

Scratch To Reveal Pop Up

[Alia](https://www.aliapopups.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-easiest-10-minute-pop-up-fix-before-your-next-sale) is the easiest way to build these pop-ups… and they have a ton of templates for seasonal forms you can use (like these two versions above).

We run most of our brands on Alia. It always outperforms all other options.

This is one of those small tweaks that costs you nothing and recovers revenue every single sale you run.

entries.title: How Mars Men Converts Cold Traffic With Email & SMS
entries.summary: Testosterone supplement brand that came out of nowhere and scaled to $100M faster than almost any brand in history…
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Mars Men has been on an absolute tear lately…

Testosterone supplement brand that came out of nowhere and **scaled to $100M faster than almost any brand in history…**

And the thing that’s actually doing a ton of the heavy lifting in their funnel is email and SMS.

It's some of the most aggressive I've seen done right.

Today, I want to walk through how they structure it because they're using the same strategies we use to get results for our clients.

**The Pop-Up**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/31e0c727-7c8a-4e94-a71d-ccd5f2f4c92a/Screenshot_2026-06-14_at_10.13.34_PM.png?t=1781503338)

_Micro-commit form featuring their 50% off offer_

The pop-up fires about two seconds after the website page loads and it's a simple micro-commitment form.

Do you want the offer, yes or no… only then after you get engagement, do you ask for email. (Recent AB test showed this form converted 56% better than gfoing straight to asking for email address).

95%+ of your customers will NOT buy when they go to your website for the first time…

Pop-ups allow you to capture 15-20%+ of these people as leads where you can convert them later on.

Very important.

Micro-commitments like this work really well right now.

(The offer being 50% off is very high… yes. But this is the same offer they already have on their website. So they aren’t giving any extra discount).

**Then, their email and SMS goes to work**

I got FIVE emails on the first day alone.

One that’s immediate, then two hours later, then a few more spaced through the rest of the day.

And they're running daily SMS right alongside all of it…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/87d0d388-2ebb-457d-a781-5fde735238b1/Screenshot_2026-04-16_at_9.02.14_AM_1.jpg?t=1781503515)

_5 emails in 24 hours!_

Most brands would be terrified to send this much.

But it works because every email does a different job. They're not blasting the same one 5 times with new subject lines.

Instead, they open with things like a founder story in plain text so it reads like a real person talking to you…

They mix in infographics, longer educational emails, and they even throw in memes on the SMS to keep it from feeling like a constant sales pitch.

The whole sequence is then closed out by leaning on their risk-free 90-day trial to knock out the last objection…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9aab66cc-e7c1-4055-b5d9-229d9a6397f2/Screenshot_2026-06-14_at_11.07.34_PM.png?t=1781503716)

_Mars Men Welcome Flow_

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7cdb7d0c-d263-4f7b-8ebb-0a3ec55e77f8/Screenshot_2026-06-14_at_11.07.58_PM.png?t=1781503727)

_Mars Men SMS Welcome Flow_

Why go this hard this fast? It's all about timing.

The moment someone opts in is the warmest they will ever be.

They just raised their hand, they're curious, and they're actively thinking about your product. Every single day after that they get colder, they forget about you, and the odds of them ever buying drop.

Most brands waste that window, but Mars hits you while you're hot, stack the value fast, and give you every reason to buy before a competitor can pull you away.

Try AB testing this cadence vs a less aggressive one!
