entries.title: How To Optimize Your Email Design Hero Sections To Demand Attention
entries.summary: You have about 1.5 seconds when someone opens your email before they decide to keep reading or swipe away.
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

You have about 1.5 seconds when someone opens your email before they decide to keep reading or swipe away.

That's why 75% of your design effort should go into the hero section alone.

It's the single most important real estate in any email you send.

Today, I'm breaking down what the best brands do differently with their hero sections…

### How To Make A Hero Section POP

But before we make it pop, **a couple of quick best practices to get the hero bones right:**

- Headline, supporting copy, button, and a strong graphic all above the fold

- A clear button up top so every reader can click without scrolling, easiest click-rate win there is

- Keep it skimmable, one job, hand them the click

Now here's the actual secret sauce…

**Making that hero POP** 💥

A flat headline, one font, one size, one color, centered, gets read as a wall of text and skimmed right past.

You want visual energy that grabs the eye and forces a read…

Here are the tactical things to do to make this happen:

- Use different text sizes and weights across different parts of the headline / body copy

- Use different fonts for your headline/body copy… a bold display font for the punchy word, a clean one for the rest

- Mix up layouts that aren’t just centered headline, body copy, button

- Add fun visual elements coming from the sides or the top

- Use a top call-out bar when relevant to put the offer, free shipping, or urgency right in their face the second they open

Here is an example of what this looks like in practice.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f97d6c7d-7aac-41de-94ab-269593bd2131/Screenshot-2026-05-29-at-7.24.45-AM__1_.png?t=1781084175)

Lame Hero vs Hero That POPS

You see the difference?

Same copy but just a couple quick changes that grab your attention!

Here are more examples and use cases:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/82c6cfa1-21b1-4de0-b168-3d8a2f67e13f/Screenshot-2026-05-29-at-7.27.44-AM__1_.png?t=1781084297)

Different Layout, Custom Fonts, And Visual Elements

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/240e03f5-a126-47f0-89b0-7500bfc1c09f/Screenshot-2026-05-29-at-7.33.24-AM.png?t=1781084236)

Adding Visual Elements To Hero To Add Some Life

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/fc982e33-3f98-4ff9-9850-2b76a7ff1292/Screenshot-2026-05-29-at-7.50.03-AM.png?t=1781084257)

Adding Callout Bars At The Top W/ Important Info

Mess around with it!

Go in order of this list and look at how you can transform your designs with a couple tweaks.

- Use different text sizes and weights across different parts of the headline / body copy

- Use different fonts for your headline/body copy… a bold display font for the punchy word, a clean one for the rest

- Mix up layouts that aren’t just centered headline, body copy, button

- Add fun visual elements coming from the sides or the top

- Use a top call-out bar to put the offer, free shipping, or urgency right in their face the second they open

And THAT is how you FORCE your readers to read your emails 😛

entries.title: The Best Ecom Subject Lines (Steal These)
entries.summary: I get asked about subject lines all the time… so I figured I'd just give you the list.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I get asked about **subject lines** all the time… so I figured I'd just give you the list.

These are the subject lines and preview text tricks that consistently outperform everything else across our 120+ brands.

It’s a good idea to steal them for yourself.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/74cb8689-a2a9-4c31-bc24-62354df69ef9/atsejq.jpg?t=1780894614)

## Subject Lines To Steal:

**“Your Order Is Ready To Ship** 📦”
For any cart or checkout abandonment email, this crushes. We've A/B tested this against "Forgetting something?" and "You left something behind" and it wins…Every. Single time.

**“Quick Question {first_name}**”
This just rips for opens... It makes it seem like it will be something quick. Make sure your actual headline inside is some sort of question so it delivers on the subject line.

**“Didn't Plan On This”**
Great for new product drops or a surprise sale.

**3 Reasons For [product/benefit]**
People love lists and numbers. Something about a number in the subject line just gets more opens.

**“Beware”**
Sounds weird but it works. Can be just the one word or a full sentence. The scare factor gets attention.

**“Your [Product] Is Here”**
Makes it feel like something is waiting for them personally…

**We Owe You [XYZ]** - If you're running a sale or something, frame it as "we owe you." People see that and think they need to open it.

**“You've Got [XYZ]”**
Using "you've got" instead of "get" feels like something has already been given to them. Psychologically way stronger.

**“3. 2. 1...”**
Great for any launch or sale. Numbers stand out in the inbox and the countdown creates urgency.

**“POV:”**
Works really well for younger audiences. You can keep at just POV or do something like “POV: Summer Is Here”

**“For the [Identity]”**
Frame it around who they are. "For the early risers." "For the gym at 5am crowd." Identity-based subject lines get opened.

## Preview Texts:

**Leave it completely empty**
Forces curiosity. In Klaviyo's text editor you can just check a box to leave it blank. Most people don't do this and it stands out.

**End it with "..."**
Creates an open loop. I've tested this and it consistently gets more opens than preview text that finishes the thought.

BTW… If you want to actually see which of these subject lines are performing best on your account, we use Hiro Analytics for this.

SO easy to track and see what subject lines work best and for which reason.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/280bb0da-0bc7-4f4d-9e01-46dc86a09505/Screenshot_2026-06-06_at_11.29.05_AM.png?t=1780774540)

_Subject Line Tab In Hiro Analytics_

It lets you pull up a single view with every subject line you've sent alongside the open rate, send time, and revenue.

Way easier than going through campaigns one by one, trying to piece it all together.

If you are serious about retention you should be using them.

_[Check them out here.](https://www.hiroanalytics.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-combine-plain-text-and-designed-emails-for-a-killer-email-marketing-program)_

entries.summary: You know that basic Shopify order confirmation email that every brand sends?
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

You know that basic Shopify order confirmation email that every brand sends?

The plain black and white one that looks like a receipt from 2012?

Yeah, most brands want to get rid of that... And they really should!

Because your order confirmation is the most opened email you will ever send…

Someone just gave you their money and you're hitting them with a plain-text scary receipt with zero branding and education.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/50bc15b0-58a1-461b-a88f-3a57ff8735d3/atecyg.jpg?t=1780461829)

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5035a14c-cf43-452a-b487-6766d51769da/edit-order-confirmation-on-shopify.webp?t=1780461241)

Regular Order Confirmation

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a16030f2-6e01-4e31-a3bd-f4d3ca215801/screencapture-mail-google-mail-u-1-2026-02-23-07_35_26-edit_1.png?t=1780461289)

Custom Order Confirmation

The best way to fix this is by building a custom order confirmation inside Klaviyo.

You can add your full branding, product education, benefits of what they just bought, and footer buttons that link back to your store…

That footer alone drives extra clicks and revenue from people who literally just purchased from you.

Now here's the catch 😅

You need Shopify Plus to do this.

Shopify Plus starts at $2K/month or 0.25% of monthly revenue once you pass $800K/month in sales, so this isn't for every brand.

But if you or your client is already on Plus, here's how to set it up:

1) Build your custom order confirmation email inside Klaviyo.

2) Design it with your branding, product education, benefits, footer links, etc.

3) Once it's live, contact Shopify support directly and ask them to turn off the default Shopify confirmation. Super easy to do. You can’t do it yourself so you have to go through them.

The difference is night and day, right?

If you're on Plus and still rocking the default receipt, this is your sign.

entries.title: How To Stand Out In Someone's Inbox
entries.summary: But can immediately make your emails stand out in someone's inbox.
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Today I'm sharing a quick trick that almost nobody does…

But can immediately make your emails stand out in someone's inbox.

**Changing your sender name based on the email!**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2feddd58-e551-43e7-bcd6-daf70f206409/Screenshot_2026-06-01_at_6.16.28_AM.png?t=1780308976)

Your sender name is your first subject line.

It's the first thing people see when they get a notification on their phone.

Most brands just set it to their brand name and never touch it again.

But a look at how this brand does it:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8db9f977-2e9e-475f-b22f-9660e2df2e37/Screenshot_2026-05-26_at_7.05.07_AM.png?t=1780308999)

Notice how the emails around a sale or about rewards has a different sender name…

It catches your eye immediately because it looks different from every other brand sitting in your inbox with the same static name.

**Here’s how you can do the same:**

- **[Brand] SALE** - for when you're running a sale. People see "SALE" in the sender name before they even open.

- **[Brand] REWARDS** - for when you're giving people store credit or gifts. Feels like a reward program, not a promo.

- **[Brand] EARLY ACCESS** - for early access on sales or restocks. Creates exclusivity right in the inbox.

- **[Brand] NEW** - for announcements or new product drops. Stands out from your regular sends.

- **Name | [Brand]** - for messages from a specific person. Founder emails, personal check-ins, anything that should feel 1-on-1.

- **[Brand] Customer Service** - for flow emails like abandonments. Frame it as "there was an issue with your order" instead of a sales email. People open customer service emails.

- **Your [Brand] Stylist** - personal vibe using "your" to get attention. If you sell clothing this could be an email about recommended products based on their purchase history.

Start switching it up based on the email type and watch what happens to your open rates!

Easy win you can set up today.

If you want a team running stuff like this across your entire email program, [book a call with us here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-stand-out-in-someone-s-inbox).

entries.title: Steal These Pop-Up Formats
entries.summary: Today I'm sharing a pop-up swipe file. These are some of the best pop-up forms we've seen across our brands and some of the top DTC brands right now.
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Today I'm sharing a pop-up swipe file. These are some of the best pop-up forms we've seen across our brands and some of the top DTC brands right now.

If you're still running a basic "enter your email for 10% off" pop-up, this should give you some ideas.

**Quiz-Style Pop-Ups**

Ask a question before you ask for the email. "What are you looking for?" or "What's your biggest concern?"

The customer answers, gets slightly more invested, and is way more likely to give their email after.

You also get zero-party data you can use to customize your welcome flow.

**This is the style we use on 75% of our clients and see the best results consistently.**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/90eef9fc-9fd4-46f5-891a-806aea2d68b7/Screenshot-2025-11-11-at-7.41.32-AM__8_.png?t=1780048613)

Quiz Style Pop-Up

**Plinko Pop-Up**

Gamified format where the customer drops a chip and "wins" their discount.

People engage more when they feel like there's some luck involved and they earn their discount.

We've been A/B testing this one a lot lately and it's been winning across the board.

It follows same principle on follow up steps… They get their reward THEN we ask for their email. And the person is too invested in their reward they don’t want to lose it, so they give their email.

Not a fit for every brand… but if you are down for it, it rips!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/846989ba-f23e-4f46-9d51-1b1198940be4/Screenshot_2026-05-29_at_7.51.35_AM.png?t=1780066311)

Plinko Pop-Up

**Scratch-To-Reveal**

Same idea as Plinko, but the customer scratches off a card to reveal their offer.

Creates that same feeling of earning the discount instead of just being handed one.

Scratch To Reveal Pop-Up

**Countdown Timer Addition**

Creates way more urgency and makes people act instead of closing it and coming back later.

Because most of the time when someone closes your pop-up… they're not coming back.

This gives them urgency to enter their email right now.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a6ee1387-4b49-4ede-abff-b4250548e9c6/Screenshot_2026-05-29_at_7.45.31_AM.png?t=1780065994)

entries.title: Quick Psychology Trick To Increase Your Conversions
entries.summary: Today, I'm sharing a quick psychology trick we use to make your emails convert better without touching your offer.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Maybe you have the right offer…

But you aren’t framing it the right way 👀

Today, I'm sharing a quick psychology trick we use to make your emails convert better without touching your offer.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7115f060-c327-4f7f-b374-e735ded90e53/aspkrm.jpg?t=1779758946)

There's a reason some emails convert and others don't… even when the offer is the same.

It usually comes down to how the email is framed instead what it's selling.

Here's the one we use the most.

**Reciprocity Framing**

We've found that emails with the wording "On Us" consistently outperform things like "Free Shipping On Your Order" or "Here's Your Discount."

"On Us" gives the impression that the brand is personally paying out of pocket for the customer.

It holds more weight because it feels like a favor instead of a promotion.

Not to mention it also triggers something in the customer's head where they feel like the brand went out of their way for them.

And when someone does you a favor you want to use it.

The offer doesn't change at all…only the way you talk about it.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4d607fb9-6d9f-4e51-a807-8b218b916a66/screencapture-milled-snif-co-order-today-for-free-3-day-shipping-ctjwTs7Kr5xD5iy-2026-02-24-07_52_29-edit_1.jpg?t=1779757789)

But reciprocity isn't the only one.

Here are three more psychologically quick wins you can use right now.

**Identity Labeling** - Frame your customer as the type of person who already uses your product. "For serious athletes" or "for people who actually care about what goes in their body." People self-select into identities and buying just confirms who they already think they are.

**Bandwagon** **Over Elitism -** “Join the top 15% of Americans who take ashwaghanda” signals that 85% of people DON’T take it. So the customer will ignore and think they’re fine. Instead make them feel behind, like “ashwaghanda is the fastest growing supplement in the men’s health space, up 300% in consumption”.

**Concrete Numbers** - Specific numbers always outperform vague claims because they feel like proof instead of marketing.

Start working these into your campaigns and flows. Small copy changes like these add up fast.

If you want a team writing emails with this kind of thinking behind every send, [book a call with us here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=quick-psychology-trick-to-increase-your-conversions).

entries.title: How To Get MORE Positive Reviews and LESS Negative Reviews
entries.summary: Today, I'm sharing a quick hack for getting more positive reviews from your customers…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Happy Memorial Day.

Today, I'm sharing a quick hack for getting more positive reviews from your customers…

And more importantly less negative reviews.

Most brands send a review request email after purchase that just says something like "how did you enjoy your order? Leave us a review" and links straight to the review page.

The problem is you're sending EVERYBODY to leave reviews...

Happy customers and unhappy ones.

And the unhappy ones are way more motivated to leave a review than the happy ones.

**But what if you could lead unhappy people to your support team and happy people to your reviews page to actually leave a review?**

Instead of linking straight to the review page, you can put your star rating directly in the email.

Something like "How was your experience? Rate us below" with clickable stars from 1 to 5.

- If someone clicks 1, 2, or 3 stars, you route them to customer support or a private feedback form.

- And if someone clicks 4 or 5 stars, you send them straight to your public review page. These are the people you actually want leaving reviews.

That way, low review folks never see the public review page.

You catch the issue, fix it, and save the relationship before they blast you publicly.

**The same email and audience… but you're filtering who actually makes it to the review page.**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7663a38a-2689-4ee0-9bb3-d251617a34d2/Screenshot_2026-05-25_at_9.28.41_AM.png?t=1779715706)

How to structure review request email links

Set this up once and it runs forever inside your review request flow.

entries.title: How To Improve Your Welcome Flow Performance With Little Effort
entries.summary: Your welcome flow has had the same 5 emails in it since the day you built it.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Your welcome flow has had the same 5 emails in it since the day you built it.

Meanwhile, you've got campaigns sitting in your send history that absolutely PRINTED.

Nobody does anything with them… they just sit there.

Here's what we do instead…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4868b744-9ac5-46fd-8473-18395edc0af5/asf0jh.jpg?t=1779398624)

Pull up your top-performing non-discount campaigns.

Find the ones that crushed (with non-buyers specifically).

Take the winners, slap your welcome discount at the top of the email, A/B test it against whatever's underperforming in your welcome flow.

The logic is simple.

The people sitting in your welcome flow are non-buyers.

If a campaign already crushed with your non-buyer segment that same email is probably going to crush in the welcome flow too.

The audience is the same and the angle already works.

You're just giving it a permanent home.

**A Real Example / Use Case**

Say for example this was a long-form testimonial campaign that absolutely ripped.

Take it, add the welcome discount as a bar at the top, and swap it in as email three of the welcome flow.

It probably would outperform the old email three immediately…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c9548d96-8f24-4ad5-813e-736b723f1929/Screenshot_2026-04-10_at_7.25.08_AM.png?t=1779397930)

This works for literally any flow too.

If a campaign crushed, find one where the angle fits and drop it in.

No need to write new emails from scratch every time you want to improve something.

Think smarter not harder folks!

**BTW - You aren’t able to track new vs returning customer revenue in Klaviyo**

We use Hiro Analytics for every client and look at this data which you can see below.

Highly recommend Hiro if you want to take performance to the next level.

[Check them out here](https://www.hiroanalytics.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-improve-your-welcome-flow-performance-with-little-effort)

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e01e0073-6b4f-43ed-8eb0-cd5cdabbc281/Screenshot_2026-05-22_at_7.24.21_AM.png?t=1779449099)

entries.title: How To Run Email Marketing Sales That Actually Make Money
entries.summary: Every brand runs the same 20% off, 72-hour flash sale, countdown timer, same everything. Your customers have seen it a hundred times and they're not falling for it anymore.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Your customers are getting bored of your sales.

Every brand runs the same 20% off, 72-hour flash sale, countdown timer, same everything. Your customers have seen it a hundred times and they're not falling for it anymore.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/bb744a54-5a6c-46ef-8c02-62be7cd27f31/arusvj.jpg?t=1778836882)

So we started adding twists to our sales…

Here are a few that are working right now.

- **Store Credit**

Give people “store credit” instead of a discount.

Economically and logistically, it's the same thing… a discount code.

But psychologically it hits different... it feels like money that's already theirs rather than a deal they have to think about.

Brez does this for almost every sale they run. Even their BOGO was framed as "place an order and we'll double it for free".

Same offer but different framing to help it stand out

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/df0bd5ad-1685-45da-bfb2-955f50db955e/Screenshot_2026-05-20_at_8.09.03_AM.png?t=1779278934)

**2. First 100 Sale Instead Of 72 Hours**

This one changed how I think about flash sales.

Instead of "72-hour flash sale" try "first 100 orders only."

When you say 72 hours, the customer thinks "I have time I’ll just buy later" and then forgets about it.

But when you say “first 100 only!”, they can't come back later. It's now or never for them.

Simple swap in the copy, but completely different conversion behavior.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/279a583f-74c9-4f31-81ad-03db1d8fe92d/Screenshot_2026-05-20_at_8.10.31_AM.png?t=1779279018)

**3. Order Lottery**

Not technically a discount… but it works better.

Would you rather have a measly 10% OFF or a chance at getting your order completely free?

This gamified approach gets people off the fence who were already thinking about buying but needed one more push.

Rips every single time we run it.

(Should be known that this is technically a form of gambling and sweepstakes so look into the legalities on your own).

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/01a33858-7b2d-4dca-b8ef-5251f614d3cc/Screenshot_2026-05-20_at_8.11.54_AM.png?t=1779279103)

**4. Mystery Discount**

Instead of telling them the discount upfront, make them click and add the code to checkout to reveal it.

Curiosity gets people to engage!

This works particularly well on abandonment flows when the offer is already in their cart and they just have to click.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b7295d2d-2d46-42a9-8203-6b92539640dc/HELP4ciWYAAsFUK.jpg?t=1779273614)

**5. The "U Up?" Sale**

This one's fun. Send an email at 9 or 10 PM with the subject line: **"u up?"**

The whole email is 25% off but it's only live until midnight.

For anyone who opens it the next morning... you email them with "you snooze you lose, but here's 15% off since you missed the party."

Late-night crowd gets the better deal for acting fast. Morning crowd still gets something so they don't feel completely left out. And the whole thing feels like a text from a friend instead of another promo email.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ecf67180-07fa-44bc-8416-ce4d93ac5d80/Mix_and_Match_Templates_Ads__5_.png?t=1779276066)

### Final Thoughts

Most of your calendar should still be non-discount content. But when you do run a sale, make it something people actually want to open. The offer usually isn't the problem… it’s just that you’re running boring shit!

If you want a team running creative campaigns like this for your brand, book a call with us here:, [book a call with us here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-run-email-marketing-sales-that-actually-make-money).

entries.title: The Cancel Flow That Saves Subscribers From Churning
entries.summary: We recently rebuilt a client's cancel flow from scratch and their save rate went from 3% to 10%.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most subscription brands have a cancel flow…

But very few have a good one.

We recently rebuilt a client's cancel flow from scratch and their save rate went from 3% to 10%.

That means for every 100 people who hit the cancel button, we're now saving 10 of them instead of 3. On a subscription brand doing any real volume... that's a lot of monthly revenue retained.

Here's how we did it 👇️

### The Default Cancel Experience

Most brands use the default cancel flow from their subscription platform.

The customer clicks cancel, sees 'are you sure?', clicks yes, and they're done. The whole thing takes 5 seconds and gives the customer zero reason to stay.

That's what this client had and it was saving 3% of people, basically letting everyone walk out the door!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/69eb5541-f1a0-4818-9dde-58ff0f394aba/Screenshot_2026-05-18_at_5.55.51_AM.png?t=1779109071)

### What We Built Instead

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ba2dd1cc-7999-4d01-81f0-911afa667a94/_fddf.webp?t=1779116811)

Cancel Flow Experience Example Inside Skio

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/40b9f2d1-69f3-4071-9823-095cc7db7da7/Screenshot_2026-05-18_at_5.51.49_AM.png?t=1779109117)

Instead of a simple "are you sure?" we built a splash page when somebody cancels that does three things:

→ Asks WHY they're canceling (too expensive, too much product, didn't like the taste, etc.)

→ Based on their answer, serves them a specific offer to stay (skip a month, swap products, get a discount on their next order)

→ Makes it feel like a conversation instead of a cancel button

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d5d2c3bc-db9d-4fb6-bb91-8f748090ef16/Screenshot_2026-05-13_at_10.34.06_pm.png?t=1779109502)

That’s 3% to 10%.

That's almost 4x more subscribers staying every single month. Over a year that compounds into serious revenue you would have just let walk out the door.

Mixed with other initiatives, you can see the impact in revenue we’ve been able to have here on returning customer revenue.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9e2c5fd4-1e85-49d3-9e50-d8ae25c69100/Screenshot_2026-05-18_at_6.09.03_AM.png?t=1779109765)

That spike in returning customer revenue lines up with when the new cancel flow went live.

We pull all of our subscription and retention data through Hiro Analytics across our 100+ clients.

If you do not use Hiro Analytics then you are missing out on some amazing insights.

_[Check them out here.](https://www.hiroanalytics.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-combine-plain-text-and-designed-emails-for-a-killer-email-marketing-program)_

**Why It Works**

The key is matching the save offer to the cancel reason.

Someone canceling because it's too expensive needs a completely different save offer than someone canceling because they have too much product piling up.

A discount fixes one… A frequency adjustment fixes the other.

If you're a subscription brand and you haven't rebuilt your cancel flow yet... do it. It's one of the easiest ways to save customers you were about to lose.

Want us to build this out for your brand? [Book a call with us here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-cancel-flow-that-saves-subscribers-from-churning).

entries.title: A Text Based Email Masterclass
entries.summary: That was the difference in a recent AB test of a graphic-based email vs a plain text-based email.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

$8,500 vs $13,200

That was the difference in a recent AB test of a graphic-based email vs a **plain text-based email.**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7d70687a-e978-414c-8c7d-d78cd1132878/Screenshot_2026-05-15_at_9.04.56_AM.png?t=1778850323)

Plain text-based emails include no images and they are formatted to show up in your inbox just like a friend sent you an email.

And that’s why they works so well.

Here are the 3 types of text-based emails you can run…

### 1) Short Form SMS-Style (Under 30 Words)

Literally just a couple sentences and a link.

I hate how well these work lol

These work because they feel like someone grabbed their phone and shot you a quick message.

Great for restocks, flash sales, and anything time-sensitive where brevity IS the urgency.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a0363091-5485-4607-8dd8-79befc885c76/Screenshot-2026-05-11-at-10.08.50-AM.png?t=1778837692)

### 2) Medium Form (Most Common)

This is your workhorse text-based format.

Structure is simple:

→ Intro... short personal opening. Set the tone like you're writing to someone you know.

→ Body... the main message. Pull in a story or share a specific insight. Keep it tight, every sentence earns its spot.

→ CTA... one clear call to action at the end. Don't scatter buttons throughout. One ask.

→ PS... always include a PS. More on this in a second.

Works well for founder messages, personal recommendations, story-driven product pitches...

Basically any email where you want it to feel more intimate than a designed email would.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0e0d67b0-7e09-4b03-8ea8-ee127361cf14/Screenshot-2025-05-01-at-7.53.48-AM__9_.png?t=1778837741)

### 3) Long Form (Classic Direct Response)

Most under-appreciated format out there. This is where real copywriting craft shows up.

You're telling a story, building tension, and writing each line so it pulls the reader into the next one.

The goal is once someone starts reading, they can't stop.

This format works for deeper brand storytelling, high-AOV products where you need to build the case, and any email where the story itself is the selling mechanism.

Hardest to write well... but when it hits, it outperforms everything.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6f7cb48f-2b3e-42a7-8808-7694a037f4a2/screencapture-mail-google-mail-u-1-2026-05-11-10_07_15-edit__1_.png?t=1778837888)

### Text Based Email Tips

**Formatting Rules For All**

- Bold your main points. The reader's eye needs anchors even in text-only emails.

- Short paragraphs. One to two sentences then a break. White space is what makes these feel easy to read instead of overwhelming.

- Use bullet points when listing anything. Don't bury three items in a run-on sentence.

- No large copy blocks. Same rule from graphic emails... if you have more than 2-3 lines without a break, split it up.

**Always include a PS.**

PS sections are statistically the most-read part of any email. People scroll to the bottom, see "PS" and read it even if they skimmed the entire body.

Use this to your advantage. Restate your CTA, add a final hook, or a piece of urgency. It's your second chance to convert someone who didn't engage with the main body.

(Notice how I do this in every newsletter I send)

**The magic button.**

Throw a little mystery button in your footer. Link it to your homepage or a product page. Doesn't matter where it goes.

The intrigue just gets people. I have terrible ADHD and I click it every single time. Hermozi does this in his newsletter too... always links a meme or image in his footer just to get clicks. It works.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/746d6b12-9865-4f26-88ec-0838f84d2da0/Screenshot-2026-01-23-at-7.07.12-AM-2.png?t=1778838180)

We run about 75% graphic and 25% text-based across our brands.

Text-based emails convert better on a per-send basis but they work best as a pattern interrupt... not as your whole calendar.

If you want a team writing emails like this for your brand, [book a call with us here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=a-text-based-email-masterclass).

inspiration.note: MARYJAE wrapped their whole email in a "conquer your to-do list" angle and broke their lineup by what customers actually need that day. Grouping products by moment (Focus, Quick-Hit, Uplifting, On-the-Go) instead of category makes it really easy for customers to pick the right fit.

entries.title: 13 Emails Worth Adding To Your Swipe File
entries.summary: Today, I'm breaking down three emails from my swipe file so you can steal them and apply them to your own brand.
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Today, I'm breaking down three emails from my swipe file so you can steal them and apply them to your own brand.

Been saving emails all week and finally went through the folder.

I'll show you what makes each one work and the exact play you can pull from it.

Let's get into it.

### 1) OVR Performance

**"Should You Buy OVR?" (Pre-purchase FAQ)**

**Email Design:**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/83eef7d3-8705-4278-a8f3-280383f43837/FAQs_1__2_.jpg?t=1778700514)

**Notes:**
FAQ-style email knocking out pre-purchase objections in one shot. Alternating Q&A blocks make it easy to scan and answers are broken out by product line. Run this format to anyone sitting on your list 3+ days without a purchase to clear the last objections holding them back.

### 2) HOPR

**“The Perfect Evening Ritual" / LinkedIn-style email**

**Email Design:**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/22acadc8-ae3b-4ad1-b87b-eaf37e68a33d/Frame_2147226200.jpg?t=1778700500)

**Notes:**
Creative email that turns a product lineup into a fully themed LinkedIn job listing. HOPR built every product as a job candidate with profiles, skills, mutual connections, and a "Hire the Whole Team" CTA tying the whole concept together. Steal this for product launches or bundle pushes when you want to be the email people stop and read instead of scrolling past.

### 3) XIDAX

**"The Community Has Spoken" (Social proof / testimonials)**

**Email Design:**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b22e64cb-a42c-4eaa-b2d1-999d0a7cacd8/Social_Proof___Xidax.jpg?t=1778700453)

**Notes:**
Social proof email styled in a retro gaming OS aesthetic to feel native to its audience. Every testimonial gets a bold pull-quote headline before the full review, so readers can scan the wins in seconds. Take the pull-quote-headline for any testimonial email to make social proof actually readable instead of letting it become a wall of quotes.

### 4) Smokeshow

**"Stop Swiping... We Found Your Drink's Soulmate" (product matchmaker)**

**Email Design:**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8cb1eb9d-3118-4616-8164-2be8f53dfe93/Email.jpg?t=1778698699)

**Notes:**

entries.title: How To Get Claude Design To Actually Create Good Emails
entries.summary: Today, I'm talking about using Claude Design to create professional emails.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Today, I'm talking about using Claude Design to create professional emails.

Claude Design is the new AI design tool from Anthropic.

And if you've tried using it only for the output to look too generic or unusable... this is probably why.

I've been running all of our brands' emails through this system and it genuinely creates professional emails in about 10 minutes.

But only when you give it the right context.

There are only two things that make the difference between a garbage output and something you can actually send:

### 1) A Design System

A design system is your branding inside Claude Design. You create one per brand and Claude uses it for every email going forward.

Inside of Claude Design go to Design Systems → Create.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/13a9ec5c-0def-4441-bc83-82a61e2aecf9/Screenshot_2026-05-11_at_7.12.25_AM.png?t=1778497970)

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e83fa9c4-263f-4520-ab5a-306113947878/Screenshot_2026-05-11_at_7.14.22_AM.png?t=1778498048)

Then upload everything you have for your brand... company name and a blurb, your website URL, brand guidelines PDF, fonts, logos, lifestyle imagery, and product photos.

If you have a Figma file of the website, upload that too.

Claude can actually read Figma files and the output quality jumps when you give it one.

This takes about 5 minutes to set up and you only have to do it once per brand. After that, it's locked in.

Now, the design system will tell Claude what the brand looks like, but it doesn't tell Claude what a good email looks like.

That's where the second piece comes in.

### 2) An Email Rules File

It’s one thing to have branding down…

It’s another to have AI actually create email design that convert.

I created a text file with my specific rules for how to create a high-performing ecommerce email. I attach it to every single email I create in Claude Design.

It covers things like the exact structure every email should follow, where your offer should live (hint: above the fold, always), CTA sizing and placement, and a list of things to never do.

Exactly like how a good designer would.

You can grab my email rules file here: [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YElATXdNIxOUw5fhuwNo6mmbMKOZsk9O/view](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YElATXdNIxOUw5fhuwNo6mmbMKOZsk9O/view?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-get-claude-design-to-actually-create-good-emails)

Save it to your computer and attach it when you create an email. Takes only 2 seconds.

### The Final Product

With just a simple prompt like "create an educational email about our ingredients," Claude asks you the right questions first, follows a proven structure, nails the branding, and creates something you could actually send to a client.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1cea0c45-be8b-4bd9-9aa1-b91f863636bc/Background.png?t=1778498204)

The whole process from prompt to this email being finished took about 10-15 minutes.

A copywriter and designer building this from scratch would take at least 60 minutes.

This doesn't replace your designers and copywriters... it just lets them focus on the stuff AI still can't do.

You still need someone who knows what good looks like and can make the right calls on strategy.

If you want a team that does both, [book a call with us here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-get-claude-design-to-actually-create-good-emails).

entries.title: How To Read Customer Cohort Analysis Report In Shopify
entries.summary: Today, I’m talking about the best Shopify report you can pull…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Today, I’m talking about the best Shopify report you can pull…

And many brands/agencies have never actually looked at this.

It's called **Customer Cohort Analysis.**

As a brand owner or retention marketer, this is the #1 most important report that you should be able to read and understand.

All you do is go to Shopify → Reports → Search "Customer Cohort Analysis"

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4e74461e-4519-4afe-86df-76c4d5b881c6/Screenshot_2026-05-08_at_2.07.19_AM.png?t=1778232257)

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e3aa2bd8-0bb8-478a-a889-3f4f643f5ac8/xsample-report-b6b-w746-x1.webp.pagespeed.ic.X2pU5mmFk0.webp?t=1778235598)

Customer Cohort Report

### How To Read A Cohort Report

On the left side, you see different months of the year, and then in the next column you see customers. What that shows is how many new customers bought for the first time in that given month.

And then you have month 0, month 1, month 2, etc.

Those are showing the different months since the person bought. For example, November 2021’s Month 2 would be January 2022.

And then you have those percentages, which essentially tell you what percent of those customers who bought initially in that prior month came back and made another order.

If you look at February of 2022 in the above example, you can see 13% of people who bought in February bought again in month one, which would be March.

You can track ALL sorts of things here…

Here’s a practical example…

### Customer Cohort Use Case

For this brand, I switched the view to track LTV and filtered by first order type…

One-time buyers versus subscribers.

My goal was to see how much more valuable people who first placed an order on subscription are compared to people whose first orders were one time orders.

By month 6, one-time first orders average was ~$105 LTV…

By month 6, subscription first orders was $170 LTV…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e1c89e6f-b790-46db-a2d0-9801e86df150/Screenshot_2026-05-08_at_2.05.01_AM.png?t=1778232382)

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2c4ea476-0c7d-46cf-983b-d449bfedbd5f/Screenshot_2026-05-08_at_2.06.00_AM.png?t=1778232483)

**That's a 62% difference per customer. The only difference is what they bought first.**

This tells you exactly whether you should be pushing subscriptions harder on first-time buyers. For this client, the answer is obvious.

That one stat gives us the green light to restructure our entire funnel to be around subscription-first messaging, all because the data says that customer is worth almost double.

If you've never opened this dashboard, go do it right now. Takes 30 seconds and might change how you think about your entire funnel as well.

You can even split by product to see which SKUs create the most valuable customers over time.

Just a simple tip for ya!

If you want a team looking into this for you and managing your email/sms channels as well, [book a call with us here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-read-customer-cohort-analysis-report-in-shopify).

entries.title: The Pricing Reframe That Makes Any Offer Feel Like A No-Brainer
entries.summary: I was reviewing a win-back email for a consulting client last week and the whole thing was honestly solid.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Quick story and lesson from today…

I was reviewing a win-back email for a consulting client last week and the whole thing was honestly solid.

Good storytelling, showed off new features, had social proof, etc it checked every box.

But then I got to the offer:

**_"75% off your next 3 months. Just $24.25/mo instead of $97."_**

It’s a great deal…

But it’s a mouthful… a jumble of numbers… and it doesn’t look like as good of a deal as it is.

I then went on a bit of a rant on copywriting and buyer psychology…

It’s important to understand:

**The fact that you have a great deal doesn’t matter…**

**The perceived value of the deal from the customer is what matters.**

$24.25 a month makes your brain immediately run the math and compare the numbers to real-life items.

$24 is two bowls at Chipotle! I could get Spotify Premium instead! That’s 3 tins of Zyns that will cover me 2 weeks!

So we told them to change one line and this is how it turned out:

_“As a thank you, I made a personal coupon for 75% OFF your next three months. That is 81 cents a day for a tool helping creators land millions of views.”_

5 things at play here:

- Cut down on all the numbers (easier to comprehend)

- Made it a “personal” coupon code (higher perceived value than a code everyone gets”

- Boiled the number down to cost per day at 81 cents

- Removed the dollar signs ($) as people react harsher to it… it’s a scary symbol

- Added the core benefit directly after the offer

Nothing about the actual offer, price, or discount changed.

Only how we presented it.

This is one of those things that sounds so obvious but almost nobody does it...

If you’re selling a $90 supplement → Don't say $90… Say $1 a day for better sleep.

If you're running subscribe and save, don’t just say "save 15% on every order." Nobody knows what that means in real money.

Instead, say "subscribers saved an average of $214 last year."

Now it's not a percentage, it's a number they can actually feel.

So, the next time you're writing an offer for any email... flows, campaigns, whatever... have the daily cost somewhere in it.

And use some of the other tactics I mentioned above such as using personal wording, cutting down on numbers you show, and removing $ signs.

That one number does more selling than your entire email above it.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f08d2465-19d0-4fcf-8f13-bd7b47831e04/Screenshot_2026-04-29_at_10.44.33_AM.png?t=1778064763)

Someone who received this winback email we updated sent this back lol. It works!

### What type of content style do you prefer to receive on this newsletter?

- [Short, snappier newsletters (like this one) with one core lesson](https://www.inboxnewsletter.com/login)

- [Longer, tutorial based newsletters](https://www.inboxnewsletter.com/login)

[Login](https://www.inboxnewsletter.com/login) or [Subscribe](https://www.inboxnewsletter.com/subscribe) to participate in polls.

entries.title: What a $100k/Day Store's Email Setup Looks Like vs. a $5k/Day Store's
entries.summary: And every single time, the gap between them comes down to the same handful of decisions… most of which the smaller stores aren't even aware they're making.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I get to peek under the hood of a lot of email programs.

Some are doing $5k/day.

Some are doing $100k/day.

And every single time, the gap between them comes down to the same handful of decisions… most of which the smaller stores aren't even aware they're making.

If you're stuck somewhere between those two numbers, this issue is going to make it really obvious where you're leaving money on the floor.

Let's get into it.

### POP-UPS

**$5k/day store:**

- Set-it-and-forget-it pop-up form

- Basic 10% off, standard Klaviyo template

- No offer testing on acquisition

**$100k/day store:**

- Constantly testing pop-ups (offer, copy, image, time delay, form type)

- Frequently tests acquisition offers on ads AND in the pop-up

- Knows which offer wins on margin, not just on opt-in rate

- Uses advanced form setups and testing features on [Alia](https://www.aliapopups.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=what-a-100k-day-store-s-email-setup-looks-like-vs-a-5k-day-store-s)

**Why this matters:**

The offer is the #1 lever in your entire pop-up.

A 5% discount on a $500 AOV product is unappealing. A $25 off discount on the same product converts 2-3x higher even though the math is identical.

5k/day stores set things in forget and use the basic templates

The 100k a day stores know how big of a lever testing is in your pop-up forms. They invest time into testing, and they invest money into proper tools like [Alia](https://www.aliapopups.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=what-a-100k-day-store-s-email-setup-looks-like-vs-a-5k-day-store-s) (use them) to convert more website visitors into leads

### FLOWS

**$5k/day store:**

- Two emails in the welcome flow

- Two emails in each abandonment flow

- Hasn't touched their flows in over a year

- No buyer / non-buyer splits anywhere

**$100k/day store:**

- Every flow is 4+ emails long

- All abandonment flows have a buyer / non-buyer split at the top, with custom discount strategy for each path

- Custom post-purchase journeys based on what the customer bought

- Includes at least one text-based email per flow

**Why this matters:**

Two-email flows that are set and forget won’t cut it.

The $100k stores aren't doing anything fancy here. They're just running 4-5 emails per flow with the basics done right:

- Buyer/non-buyer splits so first time buyers and multi-time buyers get custom info

- Discount in the hero of every welcome email

- Dynamic product block at the top of every abandon email (not below a hero image)

- Updates and optimizations every month

### CAMPAIGNS

**$5k/day store:**

- Sends 2x per week

- Doesn't use SMS

- No A/B testing

**$100k/day store:**

- Sends 5-7 campaigns per week

- A/B tests in over 50% of emails (subject lines, hero images, offers)

- Strategically mixes in text-based emails alongside designed ones

- Avoids reusing the same basic 15% off… custom offers based on customer behavior

- Layers SMS on top for high-leverage moments

**Why this matters:**

The frequency thing trips people up the most.

Many 7-figure brand owners I talk to are scared to send more than 2x per week because they think they'll burn the list…

But here's what actually burns the list: your content isn’t good enough.

The $100k stores can send 5-7x per week because every email is doing different work. One day it's a story. One day it's a product launch. One day it's a text-based founder email. One day it's a churned customer offer that nobody else on the list sees.

Send more, make more money.

#### THE RECAP

The gap between $5k/day and $100k/day is a mindset problem.

The $5k store treats email like a chore… build it once, set it, send the occasional campaign.

The $100k store treats email like a core part of their business… because it is.

If you want to close that gap:

- **This week:** test a new pop-up offer. Pick one that isn't 10%/15% off.

- **This month:** extend every flow to 4+ emails and add a buyer/non-buyer split to every abandonment flow.

- **Ongoing:** push your campaign frequency to at least 4x per week and A/B test something on every send.

Just the basics, executed at a higher level.

entries.title: Why Your Ecommerce Acquisition Offer Is the Only Thing That Actually Drives Demand
entries.summary: I was listening to a podcast recently and the marketer being interviewed said something that reallllyyyyy hit hard.
entries.body:
Hey it's Max from The Inbox Newsletter…

I was listening to a podcast recently and the marketer being interviewed said something that reallllyyyyy hit hard.

She worked at a baby formula brand.

And for a brief window in time, she had the opposite problem most ecom brands dream about…

**Too much demand.**

Her competitors had shut down due to supply shortages across the industry. Parents were panicking and her store was one of the only ones still live…

And orders were flooding in faster than they could fulfill them.

She needed to slow down demand so they didn’t run out of stock and have supplier issues.

**She assumed it would be easy to turn off or slow down demand.**

She turned off her Meta ads, expecting that to slow things down.

But guess what?

Demand stayed the same.

Okay…

How else can she do to turn down demand?

She stopped sending email campaigns.

But still, demand stayed the same.

She killed all her email flows but STILL demand stayed the same.

Then, as a last resort…

**She turned off her acquisition offer.**

Her trial bundle discount. The front-door deal that got new customers in.

It was a trial order with a big discount, free gifts, and it was subscription based so when people bought it they would start getting the product monthly.

**And immediately… orders cut in half.**

That story should rewire how you think about your marketing stack.

You think that ads and emails and driving attention is what is converting customers.

But the biggest driver of conversion and demand is your acquisition offer.

This shows how impactful banger acquisition offers can be.

So what does a great acquisition offer actually look like in 2026?

[IM8](https://im8health.com/products/the-beckham-stack-pro?selling_plan=2948432039&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=why-your-ecommerce-acquisition-offer-is-the-only-thing-that-actually-drives-demand), [Gruns](https://gruns.co/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=why-your-ecommerce-acquisition-offer-is-the-only-thing-that-actually-drives-demand#offers), and [AG1](https://drinkag1.com/en-eu/campaign/immunity/gs2?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=why-your-ecommerce-acquisition-offer-is-the-only-thing-that-actually-drives-demand) follow the same playbook.

Massive discount, free gifts, subscription only offer.

Take a look at what they do and see how you can do it for yourself.

I pulled one offer this week that I've been sending to clients as inspiration.

Magic Mind… if you don't know them, they make mental performance shots.

They just ran something called the **Mental Performance Starter Set.**

Here's how it works:

→ $27 gets you 15 shots across their 3 most popular formulas (Original, MAXX, and Sleep)

→ That same $27 comes back to you as a credit toward a future subscription

→ You also get a free e-book from the founder

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/fb7bf5a2-8bf9-43ea-b15d-9bdfce6db6ef/Screenshot_2026-05-01_at_9.59.48_AM.png?t=1777630668)

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/47e03aaf-b528-41b5-8c7b-66c130445dca/Screenshot_2026-05-01_at_10.00.02_AM.png?t=1777630673)

So effectively… if you like the product and subscribe, the starter set costs you nothing.

$0 net.

The genius here is the architecture**.**

They removed the risk of trying something new _and_ created a natural conversion bridge into their highest-LTV product (subscription)…

All in one low $27 transaction.

New customer acquisition + subscription trial + retention mechanism baked into a single offer.

That's how you build an offer in 2026.

Not "20% off your first order."

The brands winning are the ones engineering the customer journey inside the offer itself.

**Quick Recap:**

→ The offer is the #1 driver of demand… not your ads, not your flows, not your subject lines

→ Most brands are underinvesting in offer testing and over-investing in channel optimization

→ Magic Mind's Starter Set is a masterclass: low risk entry + built-in subscription bridge + full credit = zero net cost if they convert

→ If you're not testing at least 2-3 different acquisition offers right now, you're leaving serious money on the table

If you want help strategizing this, [book a call with us here.](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=why-your-ecommerce-acquisition-offer-is-the-only-thing-that-actually-drives-demand)

entries.title: How To Improve Your Cart Abandon Flow With One Trick
entries.summary: I'm going to share one of the dumbest, easiest A/B tests I've ever run on a cart abandon flow…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I'm going to share one of the dumbest, easiest A/B tests I've ever run on a cart abandon flow…

And it doubled the click rate.

Same discount, same products, same flow… one simple change on the offer.

Here's the setup…

Most brands run their cart abandon email like this: "Hey, here's 10% off your cart, come finish checking out."

It's fine, it works, it's not broken… but it's also lame.

The reader sees the number, decides in half a second whether 10% is worth their time, and either clicks or doesn't.

**You're letting them make the buying decision before they've even opened the cart again.**

Here's the fix…

Don't tell them the discount, tell them there IS one.

"We dropped a mystery discount in your cart, click to reveal it."

The discount underneath can be the exact same 10% you were already running…\

Nothing about the actual offer changes, the only thing that changes is whether the number is visible upfront or not.

And the results are kind of stupid…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/934d6798-bc29-4506-a381-20694b7341c9/Screenshot_2026-04-29_at_10.52.17_AM.png?t=1777456329)

→ Click rate jumped from 3.2% to 6.7% (a clean 2x)

→ Placed order rate went from 2.4% to 3.5% (a ~46% lift)

→ Same discount, same products, same audience

Why this works so well…

When the discount is visible, the reader's brain immediately runs the calculation: _is 10% off this $80 cart worth re-engaging with?_ Half the time the answer is no, and they don't click.

When the discount is hidden, there's no calculation to run… there's just a question. _What did they give me?_ And the only way to find out is to click.

The friction to find out is one tap, the perceived upside is unknown but probably good… so people click way more.

The "mystery offer" framing on a cart abandon email also lands harder than on a cold winback or browse email, because the reader already wants the product.

Try it out, I’ve yet to see it perform worse!

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/69f87364-713c-4bde-9a67-2f7e748f93c7/Screenshot_2026-04-29_at_10.54.11_AM.png?t=1777456445)

entries.title: Stop Trying to Write Original Emails - Steal From These Brands Instead
entries.summary: They're staring at a blank email calendar… trying to write something original… something clever… something nobody's done before.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most ecom founders I talk to are stuck on the same thing.

They're staring at a blank email calendar… trying to write something _original_… something _clever_… something nobody's done before.

Why?

You don't need to be original… You need to be effective.

The brands doing $10M+ in email revenue aren't sitting in a room trying to invent new email formats from scratch.

They're running emails and angles that have been tested, refined, and proven across hundreds of sends.

Your job isn't to reinvent the wheel and come up with the most unique campaigns possible.

Your job is to steal proven structures, swipe the angle, and adapt it to your brand.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c6d5fe9f-b99a-48ee-8e8b-9784a7cc96f1/Screenshot_2026-04-27_at_9.49.29_AM.png?t=1777279779)

Pick three brands from the list above that are closest to your category. Open Milled, search them, and read their last 30 days of campaigns.

Go through every email and write in a Google doc what angles and email ideas could work for your brand.

Screenshot those emails, give it to Claude, and tell it to rewrite that email for your brand.

entries.title: 5 SMS Marketing Myths Costing You Money
entries.summary: I've been preaching SMS best practices for years... some of which I'm now walking back.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I've been preaching SMS best practices for years... some of which I'm now walking back.

If you've read my SMS playbook, you've seen me tell you to avoid MMS, cap sends at 1-2 per week, and keep segmentation simple.

Most of that still holds... but after running SMS for 8-figure brands through another full year, a few of those "rules" don't survive contact with the data anymore.

So today I'm dismantling 5 pieces of SMS advice the industry (including past-me) still repeats.

Let's get into it...

**1) "Images are too expensive to send"**

This is the one I've changed my mind on the hardest.

The old math: MMS (texts with images) costs 2-3x more than SMS, so stick to plain text for better ROI. I still stand by that for most of your sends.

But here's what I was missing...

A $1K SMS send making $10K looks "better" ROI wise than a $3K MMS send making $20K on a spreadsheet.

One is 10x ROI. The other is 6.6x ROI.

But the MMS send put an extra $7K of net profit in your pocket… assuming simple COGS numbers.

Mix MMS into your highest-intent sends (product launches, BFCM, back-in-stock for top sellers) and measure the delta in profit, not return on spend.

**2) "Segmentation needs to be complicated"**

It doesn't. You need one segment. Unengaged.

Unengaged = received 20+ SMS, zero clicks, no site activity.

Full-list blast for your biggest messages (launches, sales, BFCM).

Exclude this unengaged segment on every other send.

That's it. That's the whole strategy.

**3) "Don't send SMS too often"**

The blanket rule of 1-2 sends per week is still generally right... for your main campaign calendar.

But your welcome flow is a different animal, and this is where most brands leave money on the table.

Someone who just opted in 20 minutes ago is at peak buying intent.

Daily SMS (even multiple per day_ during the welcome flow window is fine (assuming your opt-in disclosure and frequency language support it... check your compliance copy before you flip this on).

After the welcome flow ends, drop back to 2 per week for most brands.

The welcome window is your highest-intent moment you'll ever get with a subscriber… I’m now warmer on being aggressive here.

**4) "You need an extra discount to get phone numbers"**

The playbook I see very often: 10% off for email, bump to 15% for SMS opt-in.

I've tested this across dozens of brands. That extra 5% does almost nothing for conversion rate on the SMS step.

What actually works is changing the framing.

Instead of "get 15% off when you give us your number"... try "enter your phone number to activate your discount."

Same discount and list growth but you keep the extra 5 points of margin on every first order from those subscribers.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b87f3c5b-1812-42c1-90dc-08dd33806f11/Screenshot_2026-04-24_at_10.08.18_AM.png?t=1777021725)

Take A Look At The Wording Here… ACTIVATE your discount.

This pop-up form is built on Alia… best pop-up platform and a no-brainer for any brand. [Check them out and get a free trial.](https://www.aliapopups.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=5-sms-marketing-myths-costing-you-money)

That’s what I’ve got for today.

Every brand should have SMS setup… stop procrastinating it. Get it live!

entries.title: Claude Design Just Dropped... and it Broke the Internet
entries.summary: People were posting prototypes, landing pages, and full app mockups.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

AI email design may be here…

Claude Design dropped on Friday and it broke the internet.

People were posting prototypes, landing pages, and full app mockups.

Figma's stock dropped 7% in hours. Needless to say, it was chaos.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c4e20d94-9ead-42b8-9cff-bdb8f9644da5/HGHuN6aaYAA2Xki.jpeg?t=1776642560)

Figma’s stock price after Claude Design Dropped.

I wanted to see what it could do for email…

So I tested it over the weekend.

The results we got were insane.

### Step 1: Feed It Your Branding, Or Past Emails

I uploaded a Figma file with a brand’s past emails we had been working on.

Claude Design read all of it and locked in the brand identity before I even wrote a prompt.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2fabc3ad-e7af-4673-bc0a-5ac5aec6b327/Screen_Shot_2026-04-19_at_4.21.36_PM.png?t=1776640902)

Brand design system generated by Claude Design

### Step 2: Prompt it like you're briefing a designer

This is the most important part.

If you type "make me a promotional email" you'll get something generic.

You have to be specific.

Tell it the product, the angle, the layout, the tone.

Brief it the same way you'd brief a real designer.

It produced these three emails, all of which were on-brand and almost ready to ship:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/faf6fb46-054f-4141-8de9-0921e5e83ad7/18619.png?t=1776642389)

Emails produced by Claude Design.

### Step 3: Export and drop it into your ESP

You can export as HTML, PDF, or send it straight to Canva where it becomes fully editable.

Pull it into Klaviyo, add in your links, and you're live.

**The catch**

Usage limits are rough right now.

People are reporting they hit the cap within 20 minutes or just a few prompts. So you're not going to sit down and crank out a full month of emails in one session.

At least, not yet.

But even with the limits, think about what this means for the brands that tell us "we can't send more than 4 emails a month because we don't have the design bandwidth."

That excuse just got a lot harder to justify.

**How To Use:** If you are on Claude’s pro plan, simply go to [https://claude.ai/design](https://claude.ai/design?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=claude-design-just-dropped-and-it-broke-the-internet) and you can use it!

[Here’s a video of me explaining this a bit more.](https://www.instagram.com/p/DXSsRFxCQ0G/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=claude-design-just-dropped-and-it-broke-the-internet)

Keep following along, as I will have a ton more updates soon!

entries.title: The Funnel Gruns Used To Help Them Sell For $1.2B
entries.summary: Grüns(https://gruns.co/?amp%3Butmmedium=referral&amp%3Butmcampaign=the-funnel-gruns-used-to-help-them-sell-for-1-2b) just got acquired by Unilever for $1.2 billion.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

[Grüns](https://gruns.co/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-funnel-gruns-used-to-help-them-sell-for-1-2b) just got acquired by Unilever for $1.2 billion.

The gummy vitamin brand went from launch to acquisition in under 3 years... INSANE.

They have over 1 million customers and ship 10 million+ gummies per day.

And they did it largely through DTC and email.

I want to walk through 3 specific emails from their welcome flow because they're using the same strategies we use to get results for email clients.

### Email 1: Lead with the offer, then educate

Important to note about this flow… is their offer is 52% OFF, but that is the same offer available on their website to anyone (even if they don’t opt in to the email list.

Seeing brands do this a lot more… avoiding adding an extra discount and using the same offer as the website for the pop-up and welcome flow.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7a764915-488b-40a4-9c0a-62da317f39b7/email_1.png?t=1776406463)

_Grüns welcome email 1_

First thing you see when you open this email is the discount.

“GET OVER HALF OFF” is an enticing offer for someone who’s never tried the brand before.

That matters because I see brands all the time that include the welcome discount way too low in the email.

Treat the hero sections as the place to deliver the value, then educate below.

The structure is: convert the ready buyers first, then educate the ones who need more before they pull the trigger.

### Email 2: Same offer, different angle

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/dae5fbdb-61d6-4845-bf46-e0565ddbff0a/screencapture-mail-google-mail-u-2-2025-07-14-11_10_52-edit.png?t=1776406647)

_Grüns welcome email 3_

At this point, we’re 3 emails in and if someone hasn’t bought yet, they need a different angle.

This email effectively covers 2 angles:

- Grüns serves as your delicious multi-vitamin powerhouse

- Relieve constipation and bloating while traveling

The first gets to the core value prop of Grüns. Wellness that’s convenient and delicious.

The second hits a real, specific, slightly uncomfortable problem that their audience actually deals with.

And then they drop a customer testimonial from Matthew: "After a week of taking Grüns, I poop regularly now."

A real person with a genuine, casual review that makes you go "okay maybe I should try this." Social proof works best when it sounds like something a friend would text you.

### Email 3: Close the loop with urgency

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/342531de-303f-469a-a18d-b96c45bb4047/screencapture-mail-google-mail-u-2-2025-07-14-11_11_37-edit.png?t=1776406996)

_Grüns final welcome email 5._

This is the final email in the welcome flow.

At this point they've educated you and they've shown social proof. Now they create urgency.

**"Offer valid today only on your first purchase."**

Three separate CTA buttons throughout the email so you never have to scroll far to convert.

And an ingredient grid showing the full breadth of what's in the gummy (21 vitamins, mushrooms, adaptogens, prebiotics) for anyone who still needs the logical justification to buy.

It works because emails 1 and 2 already did the heavy lifting. All they have to do is tell you it’s your last chance and let the customer decide.

### The Takeaway:

Your welcome flow shouldn't repeat the same pitch 3 times with different subject lines.

Each email should move the customer forward.

Grüns does this perfectly: offer first, education and social proof second, urgency third.

By the time that "today only" email hits, the subscriber already has every reason to buy. The deadline just gives them a reason to buy now.

[If you want more info, here’s a 30+ page guide on how to nail your welcome flow »](https://gamma.app/docs/cvqck3qt1mg7hrh?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-funnel-gruns-used-to-help-them-sell-for-1-2b)

entries.title: Using Gamified Pop-Ups To Grow Your List
entries.summary: If you've been running the same boring "10% off" pop-up form, you're getting ignored.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you've been running the same boring "10% off" pop-up form, you're getting ignored.

“But Max, I thought you said popups are one of the highest leverage things you can do to make sure you're converting more website traffic.”

They are, but the problem is so many brands run generic popup forms with no personality.

There are so many different (and better) options out there.

Today, we’re talking about gambling…

**_Disclaimer: I know this type of form setup isn’t for every brand. This isn’t necessary to do, but it works well for the brands that do it._**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/20bff398-451b-4741-bbea-a35e424ac330/Your_paragraph_text__4_.png?t=1776240819)

Here are a few gamified pop-ups we’ve been A/B testing across client accounts lately:

### The Plinko Machine

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0dcfb96d-6f84-4b98-9875-f14b81bcacd9/IMG_5996.jpg?t=1776239268)

True Classic uses a plinko board for up to 20% store credit back.

A ball drops through a maze of pins and ricochets toward a prize slot at the bottom.

The psychology here is suspense. The outcome feels random, but visitors dropped the ball themselves, so they're invested in where it lands.

That active involvement makes the discount feel _earned,_ not like it was random chance.

This is an easy way to stand out… as you don’t see this sort of form often.

### Scratch Off Prize

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/dd37a282-6427-4ac8-99c8-fc79e36abf05/IMG_6001.jpg?t=1776239384)

_Grazly running a mystery discount scratch card._

This one's different because the interaction is tactile.

Instead of watching a ball drop, you’re actively revealing the discount.

The act of scratching makes them feel like they almost won. And almost winning is somehow more motivating than not playing at all.

Additionally, by making it this far, you’ve triggered commitment bias, so people are more likely to continue to the next step of the pop up.

### Spin to Win

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/77e037e2-b75a-4d6d-9b4a-dd79ae7b1f36/image_88.png?t=1776239613)

Javvy runs a spin-to-win which offers multiple prize tiers, including up to 38% off.

This is the most well-known of the three.

Showing multiple prizes makes people inclined to try for the best one. It’s a form of gamification. You don’t know what you’re going to land on and that unpredictability is what makes you want to spin.

There's also a few seconds of genuine suspense during the spin itself.

All three of these work because they are _different._

Different works in 2026 with all the AI slop and generic setups people use.

If you want to run any of these formats without building them from scratch, [Alia](https://www.aliapopups.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=using-gamified-pop-ups-to-grow-your-list) has all three and is my recommended platform for pop-ups (even if you don’t use one of these forms).

Have fun growing your list!
