entries.title: How to Crush Holiday Sales with SMS Without Blowing Your Budget
entries.summary: SMS is like email on steroids during Q4. But if you don’t do it right, your sms bill is going to be crazy high.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

SMS is like email on steroids during Q4. But if you don’t do it right, your sms bill is going to be crazy high.

Here’s how to send more texts, make more sales, and keep your margins healthy this holiday season.

**Key Takeaways:**

- SMS has a 98% open rate and is your direct line to customers this holiday season.

- Send a minimum of 2 texts per week during Q4 but do it smart to control costs.

- Use segmentation and timing to minimize waste and maximize ROI.

- Reserve high-cost sends for your warmest segments and key sales moments.

- Set up automated SMS flows to make sales in your sleep.

## Why SMS Is a Holiday Weapon You Can’t Ignore

SMS has a 98% open rate. That’s not a typo.

Your audience is checking their phones 100+ times a day and the text message app is one of their most used apps (in the US)

But with great power, comes great carrier fees…

If you want to send 2+ messages per week this holiday season (and you should), you need to be strategic or you’ll burn more on sms marketing than you’ll make.

### Smart SMS Sending Schedule for Q4

Here’s a baseline cadence to aim for:

**Minimum:** 2 SMS sends per week

**Ideal Days (e.g. BFCM + Christmas):** 1-2 sms per day

Yes, 1-2 per day during big days like Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

People are getting messages from every brand ever… you need to be at the top of their notifications if you want to be the first to get to their wallet.

**Who do you send to?**

I’m on the side of sending to your whole list… if people are ever going to buy from you, it’s going to be in this gifting period.

My piece of advice is try not to get too cute on segmentation. Send to your whole list besides maybe hyper-unengaged folk.

### Cost-Saving Tactics to Protect Margins

Sending more texts = higher costs. Here’s how to protect your budget while scaling:

**1. Use SMS for Clicks, Not Stories**
Keep SMS short and CTA-driven. Save storytelling and longer copy for emails. One idea, one link. Only a couple of sentences. The longer your sms are the more they are going to cost.

**2. Stack SMS With Email**
Example: Email promo in the AM, SMS “final hours” in the PM. This prevents overlap and lowers the frequency needed to convert.

**3. Automate the Basics**
Set up key flows now so you’re not scrambling mid-season:

- Welcome series

- Abandonment flows

- Post-purchase upsell

**4. Skip SMS for Low-Intent Campaigns**
If the goal is education, branding, or just “getting on their radar”, don’t waste a text. Save SMS for conversion plays.

### What to Text (Without Sounding Desperate)

Your texts should punch, not pitch. Here are a few plug-and-play styles:

**Scarcity Alert:**
“Only 18 sets left — our Holiday Bundle is almost gone! Grab yours before it’s too late: [link]”

**Last Chance:**
“Final hours to save 25%! Sale ends at midnight. This is your sign. [link]”

**VIP Only:**
“You’re on the list. VIPs get 24-hour early access to our Holiday Sale. Shop now: [link]”

**Free Gift Teaser:**
“FREE gift with every $75 order — just for this weekend (text list exclusive). Use code SMS: [link]”

Want more info?

Here’s a 41 page guide on everything you need to know about scaling your sms marketing: _**[SMS Marketing Free Guide »](https://gamma.app/docs/The-Blueprint-to-Scaling-Your-SMS-Marketing-Channel-to-100kmo-8c3x1ijuckhynud?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-crush-holiday-sales-with-sms-without-blowing-your-budget)**_

entries.title: The Anatomy of a High-Converting Email (And How to Design One Fast)
entries.summary: Most brands obsess over how their emails look… and then wonder why nobody clicks them.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most brands obsess over how their emails _look_… and then wonder why nobody clicks them.

After generating $150M in email revenue, I can tell you: performance beats pretty 100% of the time.

Here’s how to design an email that actually sells.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Good email design at it’s core is about guiding the customer to click.

- The three parts of a high-converting email are: copywriting, structure, and graphics.

- Most brands overcomplicate design and lose revenue as a result.

- You can literally recreate winning emails using ChatGPT and Figma.

- Image-only emails _do_ work

### Copy Comes First

Before you start designing anything, you need solid copy.

But not just any copy of course…

You need **skimmable**, **benefit-driven**, and **action-oriented** copy.

The 2025 inbox is ruthless. Customers don’t read, they skim. Your email needs to feel fluid so it’s easy to scroll.

Here’s what great copy looks like:

- Headline that calls out the pain or benefit

- Subhead with 1 sentence of punchy info

- Short sections of body copy (1 sentence max)

- Repeated CTAs throughout

- Social proof or product highlights

Tip: Use ChatGPT to reverse engineer great emails. Copy + paste a brand’s email → ask GPT to generate a reusable template → input your brand → profit.

### Structure Is Very Important

Even if your copy slaps, bad structure kills performance.

You need to **guide the reader’s eye** down the page.

Here’s the structure we use for 7–9 figure brands:

- **Hero section**: logo, headline, subheadline, and CTA button _above the fold_

- **Bridge section**: justify the hook with some quick info (think icons, not paragraphs)

- **Infographic/product highlight**: keep it visual, not text-heavy

- **Final CTA**: always give them a clickable next step

- **Footer**: secondary links and brand elements

Repeat your CTA buttons after _every_ section. If a customer scrolls and is ready to buy, don’t make them hunt for the button.

This example has everything we need with great copy and structure:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/bbc80a05-f9b3-47c9-8f82-9c066dcb7dfd/screencapture-milled-bitetoothpastebits-com-were-picky-about-ingredients-FJ5h2S3xds-SR1nI-2025-10-29-06_17_29-edit.png?t=1761743872)

All Sections Needed Here

### Design Should Elevate, Not Distract

Your design should support the copy and guide the scroll… not overwhelm the reader.

I HATE all the crazy flashy emails… these are blinding and distracting.

Keep it simple and use strong CRO tactics like button placement and button size.

Here’s what works:

- Big, tappable buttons

- Consistent color use and contrast

- Clean sections that flow into each other

- Smart use of infographics and visual proof

- Subtle details: gradients, shadows, spacing

Make SURE to include infographics… avoid blocks of copy. Turn blocks of copy into graphcis whenever and wherever you can.

Take inspiration from emails by [**Bite**](https://milled.com/bitetoothpastebits.com?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-anatomy-of-a-high-converting-email-and-how-to-design-one-fast) or [**Grüns**](https://milled.com/gruns.co?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-anatomy-of-a-high-converting-email-and-how-to-design-one-fast)… simple, punchy, beautifully structured.

### Want to See This in Action?

Words are great. But if you want to **watch me design a 9-figure email live**, you’ve got to check out the full video.

I walk you through:

- The full design process inside **Figma**

- How to write emails that convert without guessing

- The _exact_ structure and layout top brands use

- And how to upload & send image-based emails in your sending platform

entries.title: Black Friday / Cyber Monday Strategy That Sells
entries.summary: If your entire BFCM strategy is just one “20% off everything” code… you’re doing it wrong.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If your entire BFCM strategy is just one “20% off everything” code… you’re doing it wrong.

Because Black Friday isn’t a day anymore… it’s a season.

And if you’re not running multiple offers across multiple weeks, you’re losing engagement, conversions, and repeat revenue.

**Key Takeaways**

- A single Black Friday discount leaves money and engagement on the table.

- Launch your first offer 1–2 weeks before BFCM with Early Access.

- Use distinct offers for Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and Holiday Gifting.

- Multiple offers = multiple urgency peaks and more reasons to buy.

- This approach drives more revenue, more opens, and more repeat purchases.

Every year, it’s the same playbook:

Launch a sitewide discount on Black Friday… keep it running through Cyber Monday… then wonder why sales start flatlining halfway through the week.

The truth is, **one offer isn’t enough anymore.**

Consumer attention is fractured. Inboxes are flooded. And “20% off everything” just doesn’t cut it for 10 straight days when there are thousands of brands fighting for the same people.

If you want to maximize revenue and engagement this season, you need to think bigger and smarter.

That starts with structuring BFCM like a true campaign with _phased offers_ that build momentum and give your list fresh reasons to buy at every step.

## The Phased Offer Structure

The top brands are structuring BFCM like a 3-4 week campaign, not a weekend blitz.

Use this timeline as an example of how you can time your different offers

#### Early Access (Nov 13–24)

- Use a similar to Black Friday offer but less

- Positioned as exclusive and early access

- Push on the benefits of being early, guaranteed shipping, and guaranteed stock

#### Black Friday (Nov 26–30)

- Main offer, your best and most sitewide deal

- Simple, clear, and easy to understand

- Should feel like the core event

#### Cyber Monday/Week (Dec 1-3)

- Change the angle or add a twist (free gift, new product drop, extra % off)

- Re-engages people who ignored or missed Black Friday

- Focus on gifting for the holidays

- Giving Tuesday is on December 2nd as well

#### Gift-Giving Campaign Offers (Dec 5–14)

- Pivot messaging to gifting and bundles

- Focus on AOV boosts and upsells

#### Last-Chance Holiday Gifting (Dec 15–21)

- Final shipping cutoffs = urgency drivers

- Offer can stay the same, the urgency at the shipping cutoffs are the new driver

- December 15th cutoff for standard shipping

- December 19th for priority shipping

- December 21st for express shipping

### Why This Works: The Compounding Effects of Multi-Offer BFCM

Running different offers for each phase is more leverage.

Here’s what it unlocks:

✅ **Keeps your list engaged longer**
Each new offer gives people a reason to open, click, and buy again.

✅ **Creates multiple urgency peaks**
No more one-and-done. You get 3–4 urgency-driven send moments.

✅ **Reactivates buyers who didn’t convert**
Black Friday missed? Cyber Monday or Gifting gives them another shot.

✅ **Drives more repeat purchases**
Each offer introduces a new reason to come back and buy again.

✅ **Appeals to different buying styles**
% OFF, bundles, gifts—different offers speak to different shoppers.

✅ **Lets you test messaging and angles**
Get data on what actually works: tiered offers? Bundles? Scarcity-based?

✅ **Builds energy around your brand**
You’re not another brand screaming “25% off” for 15 straight days. You’ve got motion, momentum, and a real strategy.

**Your BFCM success depends on your strategy.**

This is just a base guideline and is not a plug and play for all brands.

Clothing brands will be different from supplement brands.

Supplement brands will be different from home goods brands.

Etc etc

Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you ever find yourself wondering how the biggest DTC brands structure their funnels from top to bottom, this email’s for you.

I’ve personally dissected hundreds of ecommerce funnels, and these 6 brands are doing things right.

I dropped links to full funnel files + video breakdowns so you can plug and play inspiration for your own email flows, popups, and customer journeys.

## Links To Breakdowns 👇

#### Snow Whitening - $200M Brand

SNOW offers LED‑whitening kits, whitening serums, strips, toothpaste and booster powders aimed at the at‑home smile‑enhancement market. They position themselves as the internet’s #1 teeth‑whitening brand

- [Link To Funnel File »](https://www.figma.com/board/o5RsJIsIbvXf9qDSWDd7U2/Snow-Funnel?node-id=0-1&t=G7WfvtdAkWl8K3tV-1&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=6-killer-funnel-breakdowns-from-brands-doing-8-9-figures)

- [Link To Video Explanation »](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DP3-xYxEQOa/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=6-killer-funnel-breakdowns-from-brands-doing-8-9-figures)

entries.summary: We used to lose 100+ hours each month to a mindless, but necessary, task.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

We used to lose 100+ hours each month to a mindless, but necessary, task.

Today I want to share a tool that was used to cut the time in half.

I gatekept this tool forever… but they deserve the shoutout.

(Email marketing analytics platform for both agencies and brands)

As your agency starts to scale, you quickly realize not everything is about getting more clients.

Being able to scale to 100+ active clients while maintaining 95% retention comes down to **efficiency and time management.**

We’ve invested A LOT of time and effort into making our team members more efficient so they can focus on high-leverage things like strategy and client relationship management.

One example is with client reporting and data analysis.

After doing some surveys, we found that **our Account Managers were spending hours on hours just** _**pulling data**_ **for monthly reports.**

Literally downloading screenshots from Klaviyo, digging for flow numbers, campaign performance, popup metrics, switching between 3–4 tabs, then pasting everything into Google Slides to make it look client-presentable.

It came out to roughly 2 hours per client per month.

Which didn’t sound too bad until we did the math…

Each AM manages ~6 accounts and we have 14 AMs.

**That’s roughly 168 hours per month across the company spent just compiling data… not analyzing it, not strategizing off of it, literally just compiling it.**

The end result was decent, but not incredible…

Too many screenshots. Formatting slightly different person to person. It was a pain to update SOPs so nothing changed, etc etc

Now, our team generates full monthly or quarterly client reports literally in one click.

Account Managers can just look at the data, analyze it, and make their strategic recommendations.

It cut our reporting time by at least 50%. And more importantly, **it freed up dozens of hours every month for our AMs to focus on actual strategy, communication, and client relationships.**

entries.title: The $200M Ecom Funnel You Can Steal
entries.summary: This bootstrapped brand does $200M+ a year with this acquisition funnel.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

This bootstrapped brand does $200M+ a year with this acquisition funnel.

Most brands won’t do this because it’s “too aggressive.”

But hey… it works!

**Key Takeaways:**

- Snow uses irresistible offers to turn traffic into conversions

- Every landing page has a strong pop-up form system that captures both email and SMS.

- Daily emails and texts post-opt-in convert cheaper than any ad ever could.

- Upsells and sneaky offers at checkout to help with AOV

You’ve probably seen _Snow Whitening_ on TikTok or Instagram.

Bootstrapped brand. Clean aesthetic. $200M+ in annual revenue.

But their secret sauce isn’t just a good-looking product. It’s their funnel.

And it’s _dialed._

From the first ad to the final checkout bump—and everything in between—Snow has one of the cleanest, highest-converting ecommerce funnels I’ve ever broken down.

Let’s go step-by-step so you can steal what’s working and leave the fluff behind.

## 1. Ads: Driving Traffic with Intent

The funnel begins with a relentless top-of-funnel strategy:

- **Influencers & Celebs:** They use public figures (big and small) to give social proof and instant trust.

- **TikTok & UGC Ads:** Raw, real, and unpolished videos that carry the education

- **Static + Offer-Based Creatives:** They run countless statics showcasing specific deals (not just product benefits).

- **Always-On Offers:** You’re never just “learning”, you’re always being sold something.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e02805a1-3796-4a0b-bbef-0c32d0957446/Screenshot_2025-10-20_at_5.57.53_AM.png?t=1760965076)

### 2. Product Pages: Where the Banger Offers Live

Snow doesn’t waste too much time educating. They sell HARD.

Every product page is built around a **high-converting offer** and that’s why it works.

Here’s what you’ll find:

- **Freebies with Subscriptions:** Their whitening kit offers a **free month** of product when you subscribe. That’s front and center.

- **Pre-Selected Subscription:** The recurring option is auto-checked—so users have to _opt out_ of more revenue.

- **Urgency and Value Stacking:** They mix in bundles, discounts, and high-perceived-value offers like “Free Gift When You Spend $XX.”

- **Visuals That Sell:** Clear benefits. Before/afters. Celeb UGC. All reinforcing why _now_ is the time to buy.

Their goal isn’t to explain why the product works. It’s to give you **zero excuses** not to buy it right now.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8e7f445e-d9fc-4841-accc-aba35ccc0e37/image.png?t=1760965233)

PDP Example

### 3. Cart & Checkout Pages: Print More Per Purchase

Most brands settle once the cart is full, but not this one:

- **Upsells in the Cart:** Add-ons and bundles are presented without friction.

- **Free Gift Progress Bar:** Incentivizes larger orders.

- **“Snow Order Protection” Auto-Checked At Checkout:** $7.50 added to AOV with zero fulfillment cost.

- **Clean, Conversion-Focused Checkout:** Trust-building and urgency.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0c2aaf68-4f53-47b8-babc-91998f124c8b/image.png?t=1760965350)

Cart Page

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2a67f155-108f-46d8-ba1e-f278223ee85e/image.png?t=1760965356)

Checkout Page

### 4. Email/SMS Sign-Up Forms: Max Conversion Capture

The pop-up form to get your email / sms phone number is the key. They clearly have hyper-optimized this to grow their list with the most efficiency possible.

- **Step 1 Question:** Starts with an engaging micro-conversion (e.g., “What’s your biggest goal?”)

- **Step 2: Email + SMS Capture:** Splits email and phone number across two screens (boosts total opt-ins).

- **CTA Language:** “Activate your discount” works better than “Sign up.”

- **Design:** Mobile-first, frictionless, and value-packed.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a6212c4f-8a9d-4b9a-8514-824d49b7c574/Screenshot_2025-10-20_at_6.03.25_AM.png?t=1760965407)

Sign-Up Flow

### 5. Email & SMS Welcome Flow: The Profit Printer

Once someone signs up, the brand goes full throttle:

- **10-Day Follow-Up:** 1 email + 1 SMS **every single day**.

- **Discount-Driven + Visual:** They lean into urgency, graphics, and bold claims.

- **Daily Value Drops:** Every message has a CTA and a reason to buy _right now_.

- **Social Proof:** Tons of before and afters, testimonials, and results stack like crazy.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1af304ba-8875-4f54-ab8b-db8d50658875/Screenshot_2025-10-20_at_6.04.56_AM.png?t=1760965498)

Welcome Sequency (just the first part)

I mapped this full funnel out for you right [here](https://www.figma.com/board/o5RsJIsIbvXf9qDSWDd7U2/Snow-Funnel?node-id=1-242&t=7qfoILjSezCFAd8k-1&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=the-200m-ecom-funnel-you-can-steal).

Has all of the assets and whatnot, enjoy!

This funnel isn’t complicated.

But it is one of the cleanest examples of what works in 2025.

Here’s the playbook:

- Load your product pages with banger offers

- Get aggressive with your email/SMS welcome flow

- Optimize your cart and checkout pages for AOV bumps

- And stop being afraid to follow up daily

If you want help with this, book a call with us [here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-200m-ecom-funnel-you-can-steal).

entries.title: The Simple Email Flow Strategy That’ll Print You More Money This Black Friday
entries.summary: If you like money and you're running Black Friday Cyber Monday (BFCM) promos, this might be the highest ROI thing you do this year.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you like money and you're running Black Friday Cyber Monday (BFCM) promos, this might be the highest ROI thing you do this year.

A few small flow updates could be the difference between an okay sale and a record-breaking month.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Don’t use your default pop-up and flows during BFCM, create seasonal-specific versions.

- Reminder to run a 45-day phased BFCM offer schedule, not just one big weekend sale.

- Set up five essential BFCM specific flows: Welcome, Site Abandon, Browse Abandon, Cart & Checkout Abandon, and Post-Purchase.

- Use short flows, fast time delays, and lots of urgency.

- Optimize for conversion, not clutter—make your offers the focal point.

## Why BFCM Flows Matter More Than You Think

Every ecommerce brand gets flooded with site traffic during BFCM, but most are letting a chunk of that traffic walk away without converting.

Why? They don’t update or optimize their pop-ups or flows for the BFCM window.

This is your biggest opportunity of the year.

You need to make sure you have pop-up forms specific to the offer and flows with more urgency.

You need to build custom flows that speak to the moment, highlight the offer, and move fast. Y

our evergreen 10% off pop-up and standard welcome flow won’t cut it here.

### Custom Pop-Up Forms = Explosive List Growth

Update your pop-up forms for each BFCM phase.

You're about to get more site traffic than any other time of year… this is your **biggest opportunity to grow your email and SMS list.**

Your pop-up should clearly feature your BFCM offer and ask for the user's email and phone number.

Obviously… they don’t need to opt in to get the deal but many will and you will grow your list.

Also, they will convert at a higher rate cause now you can hit them with daily email reminders and urgency + they can now receive abandonment flows.

Use a slightly pop-up for Early Access, Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and Gifting.

We’ve seen 32% opt-in rates with this.

That’s **17,000+ new subscribers** in just 7 days. It prints.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/422d16b5-e9da-4aa4-9aae-d8b0f463663e/Screenshot_2025-10-17_at_6.49.04_AM.png?t=1760705345)

17k New Subs in 7 Days

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0f0a633b-dd61-425c-a954-150d06ea5e59/Screenshot_2025-10-17_at_6.49.17_AM.png?t=1760705365)

Example Form

### 5 Custom BFCM Flows You Need to Build (Or Update)

During BFCM, you can't just use the same flows you have year round…

We need to update our flows to highlight our special offers, be quicker, and have more urgency for maximum conversions.

**Welcome Flow:** When someone opts into our pop-up we want to highlight the offer and give some brand info

**Site Abandon Flow:** If someone browsed the site, we want to reel them back by mentioning the abandonment and highlight the offer / urgency

**Browse Abandon Flow:** If someone views a product and leaves, we want to send two quick emails showing exactly what they left behind with some objection handling and highlighting the offer.

**Cart / Checkout Abandon Flows:** For efficiency you can use the same emails for these flows by showing what the person left behind, highlighting the offer, and using extreme urgency.

**Post-Purchase Flow:** When someone buys, we want to send an immediate text-based thank you message from the founder while also pushing them to place another order to get ahead of gifting (you'd be surprised how many people buy from this).

Each of these flows should be **short**, **urgent**, and laser-focused on the BFCM offer.

**Short Flows, Fast Time Delays, High Urgency**

We really don't need to have flows with 3+ emails in them for BFCM.

Why? Because you should be sending 1-3 emails every day over the BFCM period… no need for extra flow emails.

**Key Features of BFCM Flows:**

- 1-2 emails in length

- Short time delays (wait 30 minutes before first email and only hours in between emails)

- Creatives outline the specific offer and have a lot of urgency

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4037015f-3381-43b1-82aa-7fe1d3d88c67/Screenshot-2025-07-31-at-2.11.47-PM.png?t=1760705467)

Example BFCM Flow Strategy

I posted this YouTube video the other day going over this in-depth.

It includes examples for each email and flow.

Check it out!

We’ve done this for 7-9 figure brands generating over $150M in revenue.

entries.title: 5 Emails That You Should Be Repeating to Your List
entries.summary: Let’s talk about 5 emails you should be repeating constantly.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s talk about 5 emails you should be repeating constantly.

**Key Takeaways:**

- People need repetition… or else they will forget

- Use new content formats to keep repeated emails fresh and engaging.

- Testimonials build trust, which you can cash in on now or later

- Brand mission emails differentiate you and emotionally connect with buyers.

- Repeating FAQs, bestsellers, and feature/benefit emails eliminates objections and boosts conversions.

**Repeating Yourself Isn’t Lazy.**

We’re all living in the age of amnesia.

People consume content, swipe away, and forget it 3 seconds later.

If you’re not consistently reminding your list _who you are_ and _why you exist_ — you’ll get forgotten.

So no, repeating yourself isn’t annoying. It’s essential.

Especially when you know **how to do it right.**

Let’s break down the 5 emails you _should_ be repeating and how to keep them fresh 👇

### 1. Testimonial Emails

Social proof sells every time.

People want validation before they commit, and showcasing real results from real customers gives it to them.

Not only this, but even if people don’t buy now… sending testimonial emails will build up trust which you can cash in on later → Priming customers to buy.

**Repeat 1-2x per month.**

Switch up your testimonials angle:

- One email = ease of product use testimonials

- Next email = product love testimonials

- After that = testimonials from parents talking about their kids using the product

- Etc

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d31103f7-cfae-4763-97e3-d9347e93772a/G3Qa7FYXoAEN0lp.jpeg?t=1760533515)

Testimonial Email

### 2. Brand Mission Email

People don’t want to buy from corporations, they want to buy from people.

And in today’s ecom world where every product is commoditized, your mission an story is all you got. Your brand’s mission is what makes people _choose you_.'

**Repeat bi-monthly**

Don’t just copy and paste the same email though.

Mix up the format:

- A raw text email from the founder

- A behind-the-scenes studio story

- A video of your mission in action

- Screenshots of impact / donations / milestones

Consistency here = memorability.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8a0eaf8a-3456-42fd-b6f0-7f7a54e0e181/G3Qa78UXAAEZrBW.png?t=1760533504)

Brand Mission Email

### 3. FAQs Email

People are silently unclear. And unclear people don’t buy.

Answering common objections removes friction and builds trust.

**Repeat every month.**

Try focusing each email on a theme:

- Product FAQs

- Shipping & returns

- Subscription info

- Ingredients / sourcing / sizing

Pro tip: Use GIFs or infographics to break it up visually.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/249bb28a-2461-4bda-9b1c-64701c8d2d12/G3Qa8bgXAAA4Rou.jpeg?t=1760533550)

Answering an FAQ Email

### 4. Bestsellers Email

People want what’s popular.

Even if they already bought it, reminding them sparks FOMO, gifting ideas, or reorders.

**Repeat monthly.**

But each time, switch up the **why**:

- “Why everyone’s obsessed with [Product Name]”

- “How to get the most out of your [Product Name]”

- “Our most gifted item this year”

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/94427760-4bd9-46f4-b339-49000dbb2bee/screencapture-milled-beistravel-proof-you-can-have-it-all-YSaUPoprOH5abVDA-2025-10-15-06_08_14-edit.png?t=1760533714)

Bestseller Mixed With Testimonial Email

### 5. One Feature / Benefit Email

This is where you drive home differentiation and product purchases.

Most brands shout “features.” The smart ones translate them into “benefits.”

💡 **Repeat 2-4x per month.**

Take one feature, explain it clearly.

Then turn it into a benefit.

Boom. That’s two emails from one idea.

Example:
**Feature:** Waterproof zippers
**Benefit:** Your stuff stays bone dry in the worst downpour

And yes, use different formats for each:

- Text-based breakdown

- Comparison graphic

- Demo video

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5f54278b-62c9-459d-8df1-15c3e3be8e0f/G3Qa9pBWgAEmld8.jpeg?t=1760533766)

One Feature / Benefit Email

Repetition = revenue.

But boring repetition = unsubscribes.

The key is to change the _format_, not the _message_.

Stay top of mind to stay relevant and let your emails will do the heavy lifting.

Let’s get those 5 emails in rotation.

entries.title: 4 Quick Email Marketing Hacks That Are Crushing Right Now
entries.summary: Here are 4 fast and proven hacks we’re using right now that are getting big wins for our clients that we manage email marketing for.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Here are 4 fast and proven hacks we’re using right now that are getting big wins for our clients that we manage email marketing for.

Steal them, test them, and make more cash.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Mystery discounts in checkout abandonment flows spike re-engagement.

- Moving the pop-up “X” below the CTA boosts form conversions.

- Email polls skyrocket clicks _and_ segment your list on autopilot.

- Highlighting real studies in campaigns builds massive credibility.

## Hack #1: Mystery Discount in Checkout Abandonment

Want to revive the hottest leads on your list?

Try this: send a mystery discount to anyone who ditches at checkout.

The easiest way to get them back to checkout is to give them a mystery in their checkout for them to find.

They’ve already shown intent… a mystery element gets them curious, re-clicking, and buying.

Here’s how Dr. Squatch did it: Hey, we noticed you left something behind… We’ve got a mystery surprise for you 👀

It doesn’t need to be huge. Just enough to create a sense of “what’s waiting for me?”

This works insanely well to spike engagement rates and pull people _back_ to checkout.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ed21e7e9-5277-40e8-8f72-d592a4bee174/screencapture-milled-dr-squatch-curious-about-your-secret-discount-MfElw5n22pmttRsr-2025-10-09-06_28_29-edit__1_.png?t=1760101749)

Mystery Discount At Checkout

## Hack #2: Move the “X” on Your Pop-Up Form

This one is stupid simple but it works every time we test it.

Move the “X” (close button) _from the top corner to under the CTA button_.

Why?

Because most shoppers are conditioned to instantly smash that top corner of a pop-up without reading a single word.

When the “X” is at the bottom, it forces people to _read the offer first_. And when they read, they convert.

This single tweak has improved pop-up conversion by up to **2x+** in some brands we work with (look at the example below)

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c9e0a183-baac-429f-9297-95fc9c5d0abe/image__40___1_.png?t=1760101883)

Bottom One Showing No X In Corner

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/5273dfa5-9269-4552-8321-b7dc92a1c49e/Screenshot_2025-10-02_at_5.15.09_AM.png?t=1760101886)

Example

## Hack #3: Use Polls in Campaign Emails

Email polls are a secret weapon for CTR.

It could be something simple like, “Are floral scents manly”

What Dr. Squatch did this brilliantly:

They tracked click data inside Klaviyo…
→ If someone clicked “yes”, they were redirected to floral scent PDPs.
→ If “no”, they saw bestsellers without any flowers.

And then segmented their list based on what link they clicked and marked them as interested or uninterested in floral scents

It’s a _brilliant_ way to drive clicks, segment passively, and increase conversions all at once.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e33605a1-ae65-4a26-9432-e33b530590b2/screencapture-milled-dr-squatch-are-flowers-manly-wFtHcO8-9SfyutIm-2025-09-15-06_27_51-edit__1_.png?t=1760102014)

Poll Email Example

## Hack #4: Drop Scientific Studies in Your Emails

Trust = conversions.

One of the fastest ways to build that trust is to reference real, legit studies in your campaigns.

Example: “Did you know X ingredient is proven to reduce skin inflammation by 36% according to a 2022 clinical study?”

Then tie it directly back to your product.

Don’t make the mistake of using fluffy, generic copy. Show proof. Back it up. And your emails will hit harder.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1fea57e0-6ea9-4bbc-9cc4-abef85dd80d4/screencapture-milled-bitetoothpastebits-com-does-nano-hydroxyapatite-actually-work-wVasOeDIE3Req34b-2025-09-16-07_00_33-edit__1_.png?t=1760102065)

entries.title: How We Added $200K/Month With 3 Simple Email Marketing Moves
entries.summary: Everyone loves a flashy number… but hates the steps that actually get you there.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Everyone loves a flashy number… but hates the steps that actually get you there.

In just 60 days, we added over **$200,000/month** in total revenue for a client.

Taking email from just 12% of their total revenue to 44%.

These are the same 3 foundational moves we use every single time.

Let’s break them down.

### Key Takeaways:

- You’re three initiatives away from scaling to $200K+ per month in email revenue.

- Optimized pop-ups can 3x your list growth without increasing ad spend.

- Flow automations don’t need to be complex, just executed well.

- Non-discount campaigns with clear angles can drive consistent revenue.

- Most brands miss out because they don’t execute the basics at a high level

## The Situation

This brand was being ran by a busy founder scrambling to do emails.

Often times, emails being skipped because they just had too much shit on their plate.

Very impressive what they were able to do with just themself.

But it was time to get email off their plate and handled by experts.

In just 60 days, this brand went from **$70K/month in email revenue** (12% of store revenue) to over **$347K/month** (44% of store revenue)… a **$277K/month increase** from email alone.

We did it with just three core initiatives whcih I’ll be breaking down below.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9c78591c-22a2-45e7-8a2a-db0282745445/Screenshot_2025-10-08_at_6.21.57_AM.png?t=1759929720)

Before + After Revenue (email rev on right)

# The Initiatives Executed

#### 1. Explode List Growth With Better Pop-Ups (3x More Emails Without More Traffic)

Most brands treat pop-ups as an afterthought.

Set up your form and you’re good to go! Sike.

We tripled list growth for this brand by swapping their generic pop-up for an interactive survey-style form.

**The Results:**

- Before: 16.8K subscribers over 3 months →

- After: 50K subscribers in the same period

- **21%** of total website traffic converted into emails vs the industry average of 2-4%

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8cf90ed4-518e-4bfd-bfdd-dbcd0593a0f9/Screenshot_2025-10-08_at_6.24.09_AM.png?t=1759929852)

**Why It Works:**

- **Commitment bias:** Once a user answers a question, they’re more likely to keep going.

- **Customization bias:** Personalization boosts perceived value.

- **Novelty bias:** It feels new—so it grabs attention.

**Execution Tip:** Use a platform like Klaviyo or AliaLearn. Start with one multiple-choice question before asking for the email. It lowers resistance and boosts opt-ins.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6472f688-cebc-4490-8354-b6a1d0fb04d8/Screenshot_2025-10-08_at_6.25.13_AM.png?t=1759929915)

Example Quiz Based Form

#### 2. Build (or Fix) Your Flows to Capture Buying Intent

Pop-ups are the top of the funnel.

Flows are the high-converting bridge to sales.

Flows are the automated emails that will fire based on a customer’s action.

We rebuilt the flows from scratch without anything too complex or crazy... Just 9 key flows and 30-40 total emails.

**Before:** $129K in 3 months

**After:** $539K in the next 3 months

That’s 4.17x revenue just by properly setting up automations with our advanced strategies that most brands forget.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/bc5f59e9-2779-4a7e-8366-f82a9d4d20da/Screenshot_2025-10-08_at_6.29.33_AM.png?t=1759930177)

**The Flows We Built:**

Flow Name

Flow Trigger

Flow Purpose

Number of Emails

Welcome Flow

When someone joins the email list

Give the customer their discount and educate on the brand to guide into a purchase.

5

Site Abandon Flow

When someone is active on the website but doesn't view any products

Get the customer back on the site to browse products

2

Browse Abandon Flow

When someone views a product

Get a customer to convert on their browse item

4

Cart Abandon Flow

When someone adds to cart but doesn't buy

Recover the lost sale

4

Checkout Abandon Flow

When someone goes to checkout but doesn't buy

Recover the lost sale

4

Post-Purchase Flow

When someone places an order

Get upsells, affirm purchase, and build community

3

Winback Flow

When someone bought 90 days ago but hasn't bought since

Get past customers to purchase again

4

Sunset Flow

When someone has been inactive on the email list for 180 days

Re-engage inactive profiles and suppress inactive profiles

2

**High-Leverage Advice:**

- Most stores only have a checkout abandon flow (not cart abandon).

- Most only send 1-2 emails (you need 3-5).

- Add urgency, clear CTAs, and don’t be afraid to sell hard.

#### 3. Send 3–4 Campaigns Per Week (Without Burning Out Your List)

No, one email per week is _not_ enough.

We increased campaign volume to 3-4x/week and it added **$90K** in revenue alone in the 3-month window.

Here’s how we pulled it off without a single discount email (except one the brand insisted on):

**Strategy:**

- Enemy-based marketing (us vs them comparisons)

- Text-based messages from the founder (adds a personal touch)

- Educational & benefit-driven content

- Mix of graphic + plain text formats

**Examples That Crushed:**

- “What’s hiding in your xyz?” → exposed competitor ingredients

- “Microplastics? No thanks.” → subtle sustainability flex

- “Your gut’s on the line.” → social proof meets value prop

These converted like crazy

_without_ hurting margins.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/50267c31-2c58-448e-97f2-1c023942ba32/Screenshot_2025-10-08_at_6.31.25_AM.png?t=1759930289)

### Final Thought

I made a video going over this all in-depth [here](https://youtu.be/BRMWWOLxS0I?si=RXfSP-2pjuMgOb6N&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-we-added-200k-month-with-3-simple-email-marketing-moves).

That’s it. No gimmicks, no AI-driven segmentation, no hyper segmented funnels.

Just high-leverage basics executed better than 99% of brands out there:

- Get more emails with a better pop-up.

- Convert with flows that don’t suck.

- Scale campaigns using proven frameworks.

Want us to do this for your brand?

We have 2 onboarding slots remaining before Black Friday / Cyber Monday.

Book a call with us **[here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-we-added-200k-month-with-3-simple-email-marketing-moves)** and we’ll show you exactly how to make email your most profitable channel and break your Q4 records.

Let’s make email your most profitable channel.

entries.title: How HexClad Built a $500M Funnel
entries.summary: They do this with one of the most commoditized products… cooking pans.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

HexClad is doing $500 million in annual revenue.

They do this with one of the most commoditized products… cooking pans.

Here’s the exact funnel strategy they use and how you can rip their best ideas for your own brand.

**Key Takeaways:**

- HexClad runs over 700 ad creatives driving traffic into segmented landing pages.

- Their pop-up uses a micro-commit strategy that boosts opt-ins without upfront email asks.

- They offer discounts _only_ on second purchases to maximize LTV and profit.

- HexClad’s funnel leans heavily on conversational SMS + email with layered personalization.

- Their end-of-sale pop-ups are smart, timely, and optimized for list growth—not just sales.

## 1. 700+ Ads → 3 Core Entry Points

HexClad currently runs **790 active Meta ads**, which is insane.

Lots of testing and high frequency.

They all funnel traffic through 3 main pages:

- **Top of Funnel → Education-Based Listicles**: Why Chefs Swear By This Pan" style landing pages listing out why to use Hexclad. This is for education and TOF people who don’t know about the product yet. Example [here](https://hexclad.com/pages/listicle-one?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-hexclad-built-a-500m-funnel).

- **Middle of Funnel → PDP Direct Hits**: For retargeting and middle of funnel traffic. Driving people in the consideration page just to their product pages where they can learn more or buy on the spot.

- **Bottom of Funnel → Seasonal Sale Pages**: Like their current “End of Summer” promo page to get people who need soem urgency and a discount to purchase.

### 2. Converting Traffic To Email Subscribers

On every page off of their site viewers they fire an email sign- up form immediately.

They know that email is much cheaper to get someone to convert than just blasting ads.

It’s a Micro-Commitment style pop-up… meaning it gets you to opt-in to a question BEFORE asking for your email.

First, it asks a fun question over an image of the pan (“Want $75 off your next purchase?”), _then_ it asks for email… and _then_ SMS.

This taps into behavioral psychology: the second “yes” (entering your email) is easier after the first.

Something creative is that their offer is **for the second purchase**, not the first

Meaning:

- No margin gets eaten upfront

- They incentivize repeat orders

- And LTV shoots up as people want to claim that discount

I’ve never tried this… but it is interesting for sure.

BONUS: They also will update their pop-ups for sales they have going on… like the summer sale example below. Great way to get more email sign-ups in periods you may be driving a lot more site traffic.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6c483e1d-093a-4f77-aa6d-b39e0c046b66/Screenshot_2025-10-06_at_5.37.54_AM.png?t=1759754279)

Evergreen Pop-Up

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/dabd275d-07ce-4155-ab5f-88e6c64bc4f6/Screenshot_2025-10-06_at_5.39.19_AM.png?t=1759754362)

Sale Pop-Up

### 3. Welcome Flow That Educates and Converts

After opt-in, HexClad’s welcome email series over 2 months hits:

- Email 1: Clear offer + visual brand intro

- Email 2: Infographic on product benefits

- Email 3+: Social proof (with Gordon Ramsay), educational content, product recommendations

- SMS: Conversational messages from “Jesse” guide shoppers through what to buy via quiz-like prompts.

Each email is layered with product CTAs, category links, and gentle urgency around their second-purchase offer.

You can look at the whole sequence here, I laid it all out for you: [Welcome Series »](https://www.figma.com/design/NRx0UHPjWmr5NEIS9i3qND/Hexclad-Sequence?node-id=0-1&t=zJunfahXC4ncZcXA-1&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-hexclad-built-a-500m-funnel)

**The Bottom Line**

This funnel hits all the bases.

Tons of traffic → Strong pop-up form for email capture → Banger educational welcome email / sms series to get the conversion.

This is what has allowed them to scale to this point.

If you want a similar system set up for your brand on the email / sms front, book a call with us [here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-hexclad-built-a-500m-funnel) (we’ve done $150M in ecom sales).

entries.title: I Spoke On Stage At One of The Biggest Ecom Events Of The Year Yesterday
entries.summary: But what’s even wilder is realizing I wasn’t just there to learn from him — I was there to add value too.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Yesterday, I shared a stage with Taylor Holiday.

One of the biggest names in ecom.

But what’s even wilder is realizing I wasn’t just there to learn from him — I was there to add value too.

Here’s some of the questions I was asked and the answers I shared (and what I didn’t say out loud but wish I did):

### 1. Thoughts on Hiring Outside The US?

The question came up: _"Do you hire international or U.S.?"_

Hiring both in the US vs internationally both have their merits.

But let’s be real: most brands say they want a U.S. agency... until they see the $10k/month minimum price tag.

If brands want a US based agency they better be ready to pay US based prices!

Our agency hires global talent and I _love_ it.

For the work ethic, the culture, the hunger.

International talent often has something to prove and it shows. Our 95% client retention speaks for

This also allows us to be able to charge 50% lower than US-only based agencies, which many brands love.

The same or better quality of work, but a lower price. It’s why clients love us.

That being said, if U.S. only is your hill to die on, just understand it’s gonna cost you 2–3x. Choose your hill wisely.

### 2. Thoughts On Adding Services to Your Agency?

Every agency bro wants to upsell.

“Add CRO! Add Meta! Add UGC!”

I get it. Sounds good in theory. And it has a place.

But here’s the thing... We already have _waitlists_ for email and SMS.

That’s not an accident, it’s because we stay in our lane.

We are relentlessly focused on being the premier retention agency in the space.

Could we slap on some extra services and make a quick buck? Probably.

But it would dilute our product. And I’m not about to build a leaky bucket.

Will I expand eventually?

Sure, but only when I find the right partner who can do it better than I can.

Until then: email and SMS only. That’s the game.

### 3. Reporting: The Balance of Templates and “Oh Sh*t” Moments

Reporting came up.

My take is that consistency is non-negotiable.

But flexibility is what makes you world-class.

Here’s how we do it:

- **Weekly updates every Tuesday**

- **Monthly + Quarterly slide decks with takeaways**

- **Random ad-hoc reports** when something big happens (like a surprise product drop or unexpected data shift)

Templates keep us on track.

But it’s the ad-hoc stuff that makes clients feel like we’re in their business.

Both matter. Don’t just rely on one.

### 4. Where My Time Goes (and Why I Guard It Like a Pitbull)

This one was important: _“How do you spend your time as you grow?”_

My answer: The highest leverage thing I can do for Well Copy is make content and close deals. Period.

Every morning I block 4 hours for:

- Writing content

- Doing audits for brands in our pipeline

- Supporting the sales team

After that, it’s training the team, business development, and handling whatever fire pops up.

Be relentless with your time and make sure you have time set aside every day to push the business forward.

If you don’t set time aside, you’ll just be catching up with fires all day.

Sitting on that stage was amazing. But what felt even better than the honor… Was realizing I had real value to give back.

I’m not building a _big_ agency… I’m building a _great_ one. One that’s proud to sit next to Taylor and not just nod along.

We’ll work directly with you to build your full email engine from scratch… flows, campaigns, segmentation, calendar, everything.

entries.summary: And every time, we use the same foundational system to turn email into a predictable profit machine.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I've worked with over 200 brands doing $1M to $100M+ a year.

And every time, we use the same foundational system to turn email into a predictable profit machine.

This is the exact blueprint I’d use if I had to start from scratch and scale my store revenue on autopilot.

## 60 Second Roadmap To Scale Your Email Marketing To 50% of Your Store Revenue

Follow these steps exactly, in this order, to build your email engine.

Using email as your conversion engine will allow you to be more profitable and build a passionate community at the same time.

Let’s get into it.

#### Step 1: List Growth Optimization

If you're not converting 10%+ of your traffic into leads, you're burning money.

Start with your pop-up form. Test the offer. Test the design. Test the timing.

This will allow you to get more leads and return on your ads to be able to convert them with email, which costs pennies to send.

Optimize until you're consistently converting 10% of site traffic into email subs.

No, 4% is not "good enough." You're leaving revenue on the table.

#### Step 2: Build Out Your Core Flows (This Is Your Foundation)

You only need 7 flows to print money on autopilot:

- Welcome Flow (4 emails)

- Site Abandon (2 emails)

- Browse Abandon (4 emails)

- Cart Abandon (4 emails)

- Checkout Abandon (4 emails)

- Post Purchase (4 emails)

- Winback (4 emails)

Each of these flows should have roughly 4 emails minimum per flow.

Structure them around where the customer is in the journey.

Use urgency, education, and objections-handling to convert.

Don’t overthink, just set them up and iterate later.

#### Step 3: Send 3-4 Campaigns Every Week

Your campaigns are the retention engine and your path to consistent sales.

Use basic segmentation of anybody who has opened an email in the last 120 days

Run non-discount emails on:

- Testimonials

- Product education

- Brand stories

- Myths vs facts

- FAQ highlights

- Zero-discount offers

Every month, **look back at what worked and double down on the winners with altered angles.**

This is how you scale _without_ annoying your list or killing margins.

#### Step 4: Run Monthly Offers the Smart Way

One sale per month at most. That’s it.

It’s important to run offers to keep your list subscribed. People will stay subscribed if you’re always giving them reasons to stay subscribed.

But we don’t want to use the same offer every time…

Make it strategic. Use slightly different offers every time like:

- Bundles

- BOGO

- Percent off

- Dollar off

- Free gifts

Send 3-5 emails for each sale. Build hype, drop the offer, then close with urgency.

#### Step 5: Review, Iterate, Scale

At the end of every month, audit the whole account.

Block off 2-3 hours of your time to just click around your account and see what you can find.

- What angles in campaigns worked?

- What campaigns that worked can we adapt and turn into flow emails?

- What sale offers worked?

- Where are people falling off?

- What segments are converting the best?

- What A/B tests can we run this month?

Use this intel to rinse and repeat.

This system alone can drive 30–50% of total revenue when dialed.

[Watch this video of me going through all of this »](https://youtu.be/VySMspI613w?si=gWQBJ6KHk4U2uQji&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=the-150m-email-marketing-system-you-can-copy-today)

entries.title: The $50K/Month Mistake You Might Be Making
entries.summary: In fact, I put $50,000/month back into a brand’s pocket with one simple tweak that was hiding in plain sight.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Marketing isn’t that complicated.

In fact, I put $50,000/month back into a brand’s pocket with _one simple tweak_ that was hiding in plain sight.

Their current email agency didn’t spot this, but I did.

Here’s what happened and how you can do the same.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Most subscription brands obsess over acquisition but ignore retention.

- Email campaigns often remind customers to cancel, unintentionally.

- Segmentation is everything, stop emailing current subscribers like they're cold leads.

- One tweak dropped cancellations by 51% and saved $50K/month.

- Simple, expert eyes can spot hidden revenue leaks instantly (which is why you should get expert opinions often!)

## The Subscription Business Trap

Subscription-based ecom brands usually live and die by how many people they can get to sign up each month.

And while acquisition is important, most completely overlook a more important stat: **retention.**

I was auditing a client’s Klaviyo campaigns for their subscription product. On the surface, things looked great… thousands of dollars in new subscription revenue rolling in every week.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/20b6a0f6-5939-4203-bde5-d131b6d64b91/Screenshot_2025-09-17_at_8.02.35_AM.png?t=1758110668)

$13,300/mo In New Subscriptions Started

But then I looked deeper...

### The Ugly Truth Behind the Numbers

Here’s what we saw:

- Subscription Starts: $2K, $3K, $5K, all looking solid.

- BUT Subscription _Cancellations_? $6K, $14K, even $16K from singular emails

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/9cbce163-a8e4-448e-a103-59f490e50be3/Screenshot_2025-09-17_at_8.03.39_AM.png?t=1758110731)

$62,400/mo in Subscriptions Cancelled

Just these 6 campaigns resulted in:

- +$13,300/mo in new monthly subscriptions

- -$62,400/mo in cancelled monthly subscriptions

**That’s a net negative of $49,100/mo from just 6 campaigns** 🤯

**When we zoomed out, they had started $33,000 in new subscriptions across the last 30 days... but lost $129,000 from cancellations that same month.**

They weren’t just leaking money. They were setting it on fire.

Yikes…

So, they started working with us to fix this (we’ve had some great results).

Here’s what we did.

### The “Why am I subscribed to this?” Problem

What was causing the drop-off? So many damn cancellations.

Well, they were blasting their 2-3 email campaigns per week _everyone_ including active subscribers.

They were good emails… educational and value-driven.

You would assume active subscribers on the product would want education and nurturing to stay subscribed.

But that’s just not what happens with subscription products…

Every time a subscriber opened an email, they were reminded they were still subscribed to the product.

And a good chunk of them went, “Oh yeah, I meant to cancel this,” ... and they did.

Every time you remind a subscriber you exist, you run the risk of them being like “eh I’ll cancel this I don’t want to pay another $75”.

But what if you never messaged them? And had them just receive your product?

You see it with app subscriptions…

Sometimes I’ll check my bank subscriptions and see I’ve been getting charged $29.99 once a month for 6 months for an app I haven’t checked once in that time period lol.

That same logic should apply to your brand.

The less you can message someone and remind them “HEY YOU ARE PAYING US MONEY HAHA THANK YOU” the better.

### The $50K/mo Fix: Segmentation

Here’s all we did:

✅ We excluded active subscribers from their general email campaigns.
✅ That’s it.

No crazy flows (we did at that shortly after). No complicated logic. Just common-sense segmentation.

Since implementing the change, among other things, email cancellations dropped by 51%.

That’s over $50,000/month in saved recurring revenue.

We added more advanced strategies to get new subs and more strategies for keeping subs…

The results have been sweet.

- 76% INCREASE in Subscriptions Started (+$48k/mo)

entries.title: How We Drive $500K/Month With Email & SMS (80% of Store Revenue)
entries.summary: And we drive $500,000 per month through email & sms for them.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

This is a clothing / fashion client of ours.

And we drive $500,000 _per month_ through email & sms for them.

And here’s the wildest part…

**Email and SMS accounts for 80% of the total store revenue was from email and SMS alone.**

Let’s walk through the exact setup and learnings you can swipe and deploy into your own brand.

**Key Takeaways:**

- High-converting pop-up forms are the foundation of scalable email/SMS revenue.

- Automated flows drive $250K+/mo with a simple but strategic setup.

- Campaigns, done right, add another $200K+ with a mix of graphic + text based formats.

- SMS should be short, punchy, and reserved for the biggest moments.

- Don’t overcomplicate… test, tweak, and scale what works.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/63e73a3b-2cf3-447b-86b1-7e8417389cdb/Screenshot_2025-09-15_at_7.02.35_AM.png?t=1757934161)

Email & SMS Over 30 Day Period

## 🧲 Sign-Up Forms: The Foundation of $500K/Month

Most visitors won’t buy on their first visit to your site.

So if you’re not capturing them with a great pop-up, you’re just leaking revenue.

We don’t run boring “10% OFF” pop-ups.

We use **survey-style forms** that ask a question and personalize the experience. Why? Because:

- **Low friction** (easy entry… we aren’t diving into asking for their email right away)

- **Customization bias** (feels personal)

- **Commitment bias** (once they start, they finish)

- **Novelty** (people actually engage)

Through meticulous A/B testing, we took their conversion rate from **4% → 16.9% of website visitors converting to email subscribers.**

**The result?**

- 16.9% conversion rate (up from 4%)

- 17k–30k new email subs/month

- $200K–$300K/mo in revenue just from focusing on converting new leads.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6fc17e16-59fa-4091-8acf-e1f7132eb7f4/Screen-Shot-2025-05-09-at-15.36.31.png?t=1757933775)

Acquisition and Pop-Up Results

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7bd1c372-b646-4f41-b529-9cebdbed1fdb/Screenshot-2024-04-22-at-2.32.16-PM__5_.png?t=1757933823)

Quiz-Based Pop-Up Example

### ⚙️ Automated Flows: $250K+/mo on Autopilot

Flows are the unsung heroes of email/SMS.

Most brands don’t set these up correctly or don’t

consistently optimize them.

Here’s the breakdown:

**Flow Name**

**Flow Trigger**

**Flow Purpose**

**Number of Emails**

Welcome Flow

When someone joins the email list

Give the customer their discount and educate on the brand to guide into a purchase.

8

Site Abandon Flow

When someone is active on the website but doesn't view any products

Get the customer back on the site to browse products

3

Browse Abandon Flow

When someone views a product

Get a customer to convert on their browse item

5

Espresso Shot Flow

When someone clicks an email but doesn't buy

Add an extra nudge and discount for an impulse purchase

2

Cart Abandon Flow

When someone adds to cart but doesn't buy

Recover the lost sale

5

Checkout Abandon Flow

When someone goes to checkout but doesn't buy

Recover the lost sale

7

Post-Purchase Flow

When someone places an order

Get upsells, affirm purchase, and build community

2

Winback Flow

When someone bought 90 days ago but hasn't bought since

Get past customers to purchase again

4

Sunset Flow

When someone has been inactive on the email list for 180 days

Re-engage inactive profiles and suppress inactive profiles

2

Through email these bring in **~$100K/mo** (16% of revenue)

Our SMS flows we have set up are similar to the above but very optimized andconverting **~ $150k/mo contributing to 24% of total store revenue.**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b5544bec-4434-429b-91c1-6bd8f4947cc6/Screenshot-2025-05-22-at-7.04.52-AM.png?t=1757933874)

SMS Flow Results

### 📩 Campaigns: $200K+/mo Extra

Email campaigns are how we scale retention and get repeat purchases.

We send **15–18 per month** (4 emails per week), mixing:

- Graphic-based (branded, visually rich)

- Text-based (founder voice, punchy copy)

**We lean heavily on non-discount content:**

- Reviews + UGC

- Product benefits

- Brand story

- Entertaining takes (not just selling)

**Campaign revenue:**

- Email: ~$100K/mo (16%)

- SMS: ~$100K/mo (16%)

**For SMS campaigns, we keep it simple:**

- <250 characters

- No MMS (saves $$$)

- Always include a strong CTA (e.g. "Shop Now")

**Here’s Exactly How The Email/SMS Revenue Shakes Out**

entries.title: How to Write Non-Discount Emails That Make You $$$
entries.summary: If you want to build a real brand with healthy margins, you need to master the art of selling without selling.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

“10% OFF!” isn't a strategy.

If you want to build a real brand with healthy margins, you need to master the art of selling without selling.

And that starts with non-discount emails that actually win.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Stop relying on discounts, use your brand's real edge to convert.

- Your Unique Selling Propositions _are_ the offer…

- Compare yourself to competitors _visually_ for max skim-ability.

- Use bold infographics, simple layouts, and punchy copy to hook.

- Confused customers don’t buy, keep emails stupid simple.

### Stop Copy-Pasting Competitor Discounts

Most brands survive on sales and discounts are their only lever.

It’s the Great Ecom Disaster of 2025.

But here’s the reality: if you always need to discount to drive sales… You don’t have a brand.

Real brands can make sales without discounts. Purely just educating on their products and how they are different.

**Let’s walk through this below example we made for a client 👇**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0f540f4a-4b2e-4ddb-813d-fa3635eefcf6/Frame_924.png?t=1757658962)

Client Non-Discount Email Example

### Find Your Unique Selling Propositions, And Double Down On It

Here’s what you need to do instead of slamming discounts.

**Identify what makes your product irreplaceable.**
Not “high quality.” Not “affordable.” Go specific. Go deep. Go where your competitors don’t.

In the example attached, we went after the USP of “**Ingredients You Can Actually Pronounce**” hitting on our natural ingredients.

This is perfect. It’s punchy, catchy, and leverages us vs our competitors.

### Make It So Easy a Goldfish Could Convert

Don’t get cute with complexity…

Make your emails and sales assets as simple as possible.

The modern customer is Tik Tok brain-fried and they need info delivered on a silver platter.

Let’s look at the above example ☝️

**Strong Hero Section:**
Cool hero asking the customer a question to get them engaged and thinking. Then showing the ingredients in the background in competitor soaps that just look like chemicals.

**Quick Body Copy and CTA:**
Just two sentences explaining how we’re different from competitors… then a massive CTA.

**Educational Infographic and CTA:** People loveeee infographics. They are easy to skim and better than blocks of copy. Explain our product and how we’re different and end with a clear CTA.

**Footer w/ Category Buttons:** Finish with a footer that allows customers to browse by individual categories if they choose to.

[**Here’s the email design if you want to save it »**](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1rXEmdyD8TyT17EsIBG8SzkPUOGZI2Vsg/view?usp=sharing&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-to-write-non-discount-emails-that-make-you)

### Final Word

You don’t need to run another “15% OFF ends tonight!”

You need to _communicate value like a real brand._

entries.title: The Most Underrated Email Flow: The Site Abandon Flow
entries.summary: What happens when a shopper hits your homepage and then just... vanishes?
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

What happens when a shopper hits your homepage and then just... vanishes?

They didn’t view a product. Didn’t add to cart. Just bounced.

That's where the Site Abandon Flow comes in. A silent nudge to bring them back without feeling salesy.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Most brands don’t hvae this high leverage flow installed

- The Site Abandon Flow is the _first re-engagement layer_ for lost visitors, don’t skip it.

- Email 1 should focus on product discovery and light support.

- Email 2 should feel like a personal check-in, not a sales blast.

- Prioritize clickable, scannable layouts with buttons above the fold.

### The Site Abandon Flow: Your Lightest, Most Overlooked Win

Most flows target deeper funnel activity (like checkout or cart abandonment), but the Site Abandon Flow is your chance to recapture top-of-funnel interest.

I audit 5-10 brands per week and about 90% of them do not have this flow involved.

Getting this set up and optimized is a low-hanging fruit for many ecom brands.

Let’s break it down:

### ✅ Email 1: Bring Them Back to Browse

**Goal:** Give them a reason to click again. Show off your bestsellers. Offer help.

**Key Elements:**

- **Encourage Browsing:** “Still exploring? Here's what others are loving.”

- **Show Products:** Highlight 2–4 bestsellers with **individual CTA buttons** under each.

- **Offer Support:** Light, friendly tone: “Have questions? Hit reply—we’ve got your back.”

- **Design Tip:** Add a main CTA button above the fold (“Continue Browsing” or “Shop Now”).

- **Bonus:** Include category buttons in the footer to help them browse more specifically.

**Subject Line Options:**

- “We saw you seeing us…”

- “Find what you’re looking for?”

- “There’s more where that came from 👀”

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/dfdd8c27-50b6-4fc0-aee6-e4f293851c03/Did-you-find-what-you-were-looking-for_-Customer-support-details__1_.png?t=1757324281)

Site Abandon Email #1 Example

### ✅ Email 2: Personal Reminder From Someone On The Team

**Goal:** Feel personal. Show what makes the brand different. Nudge gently.

**Key Elements:**

- **Personal Check-In:** “Hey—it’s [Founder Name]. Just checking in. Still looking for something?”

- **Brand Uniqueness:** Include a quick 1-liner about your brand's unique edge.

- **Navigation Tip:** Add one clear CTA to your homepage or categories.

- **Format Tip:** Keep it short and text-based. Looks like it came from a real person.

- **Sender Tip:** Change sender name to [Founder’s First Name] from [Brand] for added trust.

**Subject Line Options:**

- “Find everything okay?”

- “Here to help out”

- “Just checking in 👋”

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/431343e2-ade4-4923-aea9-2b1eeee6bf7a/screencapture-mail-google-mail-u-0-2025-03-26-06_42_47-edit__1_.png?t=1757324340)

Site Abandon Email #2 Example

### Final Thought

The Site Abandon Flow is your low-effort, high-leverage chance to re-engage soft interest.

You’re not selling hard, you’re just guiding.

When done right, these two emails quietly fill your funnel back up with warm, interested traffic.

Most brands skip this. You shouldn’t!

If you want a team on top of these flows and optimizations, book a call with us [here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-most-underrated-email-flow-the-site-abandon-flow).

entries.title: Steal This Email. Make More Money.
entries.summary: Then, Corbin (a made-up person) from Brez shows up with a plain-text email that feels like a friend messaging you.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most brands are screaming for attention in the inbox.

Loud colors, image-heavy design, “FINAL CHANCE” sales.

Then, Corbin (a made-up person) from Brez shows up with a plain-text email that feels like a friend messaging you.

Guess who wins the open and click?

**Key Takeaways:**

- Personal message-based marketing makes your brand feel more human and trustworthy.

- Using a “fake” persona like Corbin adds relatability without compromising authenticity.

- Plain text emails cut through noisy inboxes and boost engagement.

- These emails don’t scream “sell”, they build relationships and drive conversions.

- You can easily replicate this format with the template below

### Why Personal, Text-Based Emails Hit Different

This email from “Corbin at Brez” is a perfect example of how to humanize your brand with minimal effort.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/3ff2286c-b6cf-43ba-9005-4d853cf4abea/Screenshot_2025-09-05_at_9.33.52_AM.png?t=1757057843)

Here’s what makes it so effective:

- **It’s text-only.** No images. No flashy buttons. It feels like a real person mesaging you.

- **It’s written like a 1:1 message.** Short, direct, and personal.

- **It’s “from” a person.** Even though Corbin likely isn’t real, he feels real enough to connect with.

- **It tells a story.** Not a brand story, but a little “here’s what’s going on behind the scenes” moment.

- **It soft-sells.** Their is barely even a CTA… just links to the product that people will naturally want to click.

This kind of email _feels_ like it was written just for you…

Which makes people actually want to read it.

### Human ≠ Salesy

One of the biggest mistakes brands make is thinking every email has to sell something.

That mindset turns emails into ads… and customers become defensive.

But when you approach email like a conversation, not a conversion, you build trust. And trust is what gets people to buy _again and again_.

This Corbin email didn’t even have a discount. Just a heads-up on their brand story and common misconceptions behind their products.

No pressure. No urgency. Just a light nudge.

And that’s why it works.

These emails also stand out more than designed emails, by doing less.

Because it looks like a personal email, it bypasses mental sales resistance.

It’s not: “Oh great, another offer.”
It’s: “Huh, what’s this person saying?”

Inbox providers also love text-based emails.

They often land better in the primary inbox vs. promotions tab.

#### Here’s How You Can Replicate This Format

Want to swipe the Corbin email? Here’s a simple plug-and-play framework:

**Subject Line**: Make it personal or casual (e.g. “just got this in” or “quick update for you”)
**Sender Name**: Use a name + brand (e.g. “Corbin at Brez”)
**Email Body:**

**Intro**
Hey [First Name or general casual greeting],

I've been thinking about how people talk about [brand/product], and I realized… we might not be telling the full story.

When people hear "[common product category term]," they probably expect [insert outdated or incorrect assumption].

But that's never been what we're about. Sure, [acknowledge known attribute or ingredient], but that's just one piece of the puzzle.

From day one, we’ve been building something different. Not [industry stereotype], but [true purpose/feeling].

Whether it’s [benefit 1], [benefit 2], or [benefit 3]—the goal has always been the experience, not the hype.

That’s why we obsess over [ingredient, process, design detail].

It’s why we [something unique you do].

And it’s why [another thing that separates you from the pack].

People don’t say “[old perception].”

They say things like “[real customer quote #1]” or “[quote #2].”

That’s exactly what we’re building here.

So no—we're not just [label]. We're [higher purpose].

nd if you’ve been with us, you get it. If you’re new—welcome. You'll understand after your first [product experience].

Much love,
[Founder’s First Name] from [Brand Name]
[CTA Button – “Try It Now” or “Shop Now”]

P.S. Got thoughts on this? Hit reply, I actually read these.

Use this… it works!

And if you want me to personally audit your email account and give you 3 quick wins that will make you an extra $5k tomorrow… book a call [here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=steal-this-email-make-more-money).

entries.title: Why You Shouldn’t Just Do a Black Friday Sale
entries.summary: If your entire BFCM strategy is just one “20% off everything” code… you’re doing it wrong.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If your entire BFCM strategy is just one “20% off everything” code… you’re doing it wrong.

Because Black Friday isn’t a day anymore… it’s a season.

And if you’re not running multiple offers across multiple weeks, you’re losing engagement, conversions, and repeat revenue.

**Key Takeaways**

- A single Black Friday discount leaves money and engagement on the table.

- Launch your first offer 1–2 weeks before BFCM with Early Access.

- Use distinct offers for Black Friday, Cyber Monday, and Holiday Gifting.

- Multiple offers = multiple urgency peaks and more reasons to buy.

- This approach drives more revenue, more opens, and more repeat purchases.

Every year, it’s the same playbook:

Launch a sitewide discount on Black Friday… keep it running through Cyber Monday… then wonder why sales start flatlining halfway through the week.

The truth is, **one offer isn’t enough anymore.**

Consumer attention is fractured. Inboxes are flooded. And “20% off everything” just doesn’t cut it for 10 straight days when there are thousands of brands fighting for the same people.

If you want to maximize revenue and engagement this season, you need to think bigger and smarter.

That starts with structuring BFCM like a true campaign with _phased offers_ that build momentum and give your list fresh reasons to buy at every step.

## The Phased Offer Structure

The top brands are structuring BFCM like a 3-4 week campaign, not a weekend blitz.

Use this timeline as an example of how you can time your different offers

#### Early Access (Nov 13–24)

- Use a similar to Black Friday offer but less

- Positioned as exclusive and early access

- Push on the benefits of being early, guaranteed shipping, and guaranteed stock

#### Black Friday (Nov 26–30)

- Main offer, your best and most sitewide deal

- Simple, clear, and easy to understand

- Should feel like the core event

#### Cyber Monday/Week (Dec 1-3)

- Change the angle or add a twist (free gift, new product drop, extra % off)

- Re-engages people who ignored or missed Black Friday

- Focus on gifting for the holidays

- Giving Tuesday is on December 2nd as well

#### Gift-Giving Campaign Offers (Dec 5–14)

- Pivot messaging to gifting and bundles

- Focus on AOV boosts and upsells

#### Last-Chance Holiday Gifting (Dec 15–21)

- Final shipping cutoffs = urgency drivers

- Offer can stay the same, the urgency at the shipping cutoffs are the new driver

- December 15th cutoff for standard shipping

- December 19th for priority shipping

- December 21st for express shipping

### Why This Works: The Compounding Effects of Multi-Offer BFCM

Running different offers for each phase is more leverage.

Here’s what it unlocks:

✅ **Keeps your list engaged longer**
Each new offer gives people a reason to open, click, and buy again.

✅ **Creates multiple urgency peaks**
No more one-and-done. You get 3–4 urgency-driven send moments.

✅ **Reactivates buyers who didn’t convert**
Black Friday missed? Cyber Monday or Gifting gives them another shot.

✅ **Drives more repeat purchases**
Each offer introduces a new reason to come back and buy again.

✅ **Appeals to different buying styles**
% OFF, bundles, gifts—different offers speak to different shoppers.

✅ **Lets you test messaging and angles**
Get data on what actually works: tiered offers? Bundles? Scarcity-based?

✅ **Builds energy around your brand**
You’re not another brand screaming “25% off” for 15 straight days. You’ve got motion, momentum, and a real strategy.

**Your BFCM success depends on your strategy.**

This is just a base guideline and is not a plug and play for all brands.

Clothing brands will be different from supplement brands.

Supplement brands will be different from home goods brands.

Etc etc
