entries.title: How This Supplement Brand Scaled to $100M in 3 Years (Faster Than Athletic Greens)
entries.summary: Here's a peek inside their ultra-optimized funnel and how you can steal their playbook.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Athletic Greens took over a decade to hit $100M/year.

This direct competitor did it in _under three years_.

Here's a peek inside their ultra-optimized funnel and how you can steal their playbook.

**Key Takeaways:**

- The brand uses a high-converting quiz-style pop-up to drive list growth and get the most out of their ads

- Their strong welcome offer (52% OFF) is heavily integrated into both email and SMS funnels for maximum conversion.

- They aggressively follow up with 2+ emails and 1 SMS per day during a 4-day purchase window.

- Every email is optimized for clarity, urgency, and product education with a consistent CTA.

- SMS texts include infographics and direct comparisons to competitors to build trust and urgency.

## The Brand

The brand we’re talking about today is **[Grüns](https://gruns.co/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)**.

They sell a daily gummy which is supposed to be a replacement for Athletic Greens’ powder.

They grew from NOTHING to over $100M/yr in under 3 years by using this funnel I’m exposing to you today.

**[Here’s a video of me going over the funnel in depth »](https://www.loom.com/share/65b0455637584a36a98096ccfeb7aa32?sid=a90567f6-4e3e-4dde-bfea-ede2455cf846&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)**

**[Here’s a board going over all of the parts of their funnel »](https://www.figma.com/design/aKCbCQJVoYpuQDCI6ossFU/Gruns-Funnel?node-id=0-1&t=nYV2uVWBubhVyOGA-1&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)**

(This newsletter is summarizing the above resources)

### Funnel Step 1: Get Traffic (Meta Ads)

Gruns isn’t dabbling in ads.

They’re flooding Meta with over **1,200 currently live ads**…

From UGC testimonials to quick-hit static creatives.

They mostly rely on UGC style videos which typically convert the best. The problem is these ads are expensive and tough to organize.

They also use a ton of static ads which are cheap to test and easy to scale with AI.

Each ad is hyper-specific, driving traffic to its own **dedicated landing page or listicle** based on the user’s interest: gut health, weight loss, fiber, etc.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/57c4076f-7997-4a1f-86c9-464ca98a19ea/Screenshot_2025-07-14_at_5.28.14_PM.png?t=1752506898)

You Can View Their Live Ads Here: [https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?active_status=active&ad_type=all&country=ALL&is_targeted_country=false&media_type=all&search_type=page&view_all_page_id=107585658730958](https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?active_status=active&ad_type=all&country=ALL&is_targeted_country=false&media_type=all&search_type=page&view_all_page_id=107585658730958&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)

### Step 2: Targeted Listicles & Landing Pages

Groons doesn’t send traffic to a generic homepage...

They route their ad traffic to **custom-built landers focusing on singular benefits of their product to give a customized customer journey**:

- [First purchase educational landing page](https://gruns.co/pages/first-order?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens) (main lander)

- [Weight loss-focused listicle](https://gruns.co/pages/6-reasons-why-weight-loss-journey-listicle?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)

- [Nutrition / gut health listicle](https://gruns.co/pages/nutrition-support?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)

- [Protein based listicle](https://gruns.co/pages/protein?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)

- [Fiber based listicle](https://gruns.co/pages/fiber?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)

- [Kid-focused educational landing page](https://gruns.co/pages/first-order-gruns-kids-daily?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)

This lets them match ad messaging with on-page content, a conversion-rate multiplier most brands ignore.

But their landers don’t stop there…

### Step 3: The High-Converting Email/SMS Pop-Up Form

The pop-up form is their key to becoming profitable.

On each page, they have an email/sms pop-up form to get the most info out of their traffic possible.

Website conversion rates can be as low as 1-2%.

Whereas **pop-up form conversion rates can be as high as 20%.**

They understand not everybody will buy on the spot and need education over time to eventually purchase (this is where they recuperate all of their ad spend)

They use a VERY **strong offer of 52% OFF** (which is already available across their site).

They fire the form roughly 4-6 seconds upon page load. They don’t fire instantly to avoid people bouncing, but don’t wait too long so they can get as much traffic as possible.

They use a question-based form, which works SUPER well in 2025/2026. It feels custom to the user and low barrier to entry (they don’t know they have to enter their email right off the bat.)

They will then tag each user who answers to understand and personalize messaging down the line on what the customer is looking for.

They separate email / sms in different steps which helps conversion rates as well.

It’s clear they put A LOT of effort into this form and their email / sms strategies.

This thing is a **masterclass in opt-in psychology** which allows them to get more out of their ad-spend.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/37f5ec4d-2fe2-45eb-a84f-b7871dd0a2c1/Screenshot_2025-07-14_at_5.33.22_PM.png?t=1752507217)

Pop-Up Form Steps

### Step 4: The 4-Day Conversion Blitz

Upon someone entering their email / sms in the pop-up form, Gruns goes crazy with sending.

They send 1-2 educational messages every day across both channels.

Why so aggressive?

When someone first enters their information this is the HOTTEST THEY WILL EVER BE.

They would rather OVERSEND and convert as many people as possible in this high-conversion window... rather than risk sending too little, the customer loses interest, and goes with a competitor.

All emails are high converting:

- MASSIVE buttons

- Buttons at the top of every email

- Buttons throughout the email

- Strong educational graphics

- Reminding of 52% OFF offer every email

SMS in the welcome flow are long, educational, and contain infographics.

They target AG1 users and clearly explain why they are the better option.

Every message they send has some kind of offer... (don’t be afraid to discount and remind of your offers!).

**Email Welcome Flow (1-2 Emails Daily for 4+ days):**

- Each email is clear, design-heavy, and button-loaded.

- Every email mentions the 52% offer **at the top**.

- They use infographics, product education, and social proof (in every send).

- Buttons at the top, middle, and bottom ensure click coverage.

**SMS Welcome Flow (Also Daily):**

- Day 1 = offer + contact card humor

- Day 2-5 = product education, us vs them comparisons, testimonials

- Heavy on infographics early, then shift to plain text (to save SMS costs)

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/30688b6c-77cc-4b95-8d57-7c988c068a95/Screenshot_2025-07-14_at_5.35.05_PM.png?t=1752507315)

View All Emails and SMS Here: [https://www.figma.com/design/aKCbCQJVoYpuQDCI6ossFU/Gruns-Funnel?node-id=0-1&t=nYV2uVWBubhVyOGA-1](https://www.figma.com/design/aKCbCQJVoYpuQDCI6ossFU/Gruns-Funnel?node-id=0-1&t=nYV2uVWBubhVyOGA-1&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)

### Step 5: Daily Campaigns & Long-Term Retention

Once you're in the funnel, you're in. They keep up the engagement:

- **Daily or every-other-day campaigns**

- Offer always front and center

- Minimalist SMS with no images to save costs

- Subscription-only deals (smart move — gets recurring revenue)

They send A LOT of emails lol.

### Why This All Works

Most brands bleed money because they chase cold traffic and hope it converts.

Gruns built a system that _warms, nurtures, and closes_ at scale:

- **High-volume traffic** from Meta ads ensures they’re always top of funnel.

- **Tailored landing pages** match ad intent — increasing time on site and lowering bounce.

- **Multi-step pop-ups** multiply opt-ins, turning bouncers into subscribers.

- **Aggressive, value-packed email & SMS flows** convert leads during their hottest window.

- **Consistent daily follow-ups** keep the brand top of mind while reinforcing benefits and urgency.

It’s not just about more traffic. It’s about _capturing more of the traffic you already pay for_ — and squeezing every dollar out of it.

That’s how you grow faster, profit more, and outpace giants.

[Watch me break down this whole funnel on video »](https://www.loom.com/share/65b0455637584a36a98096ccfeb7aa32?sid=181f7843-9d1d-4190-a6b2-ecd4719a5e72&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)

[Take this file for free which breaks down every part of their funnel »](https://www.figma.com/design/aKCbCQJVoYpuQDCI6ossFU/Gruns-Funnel?node-id=0-1&t=nYV2uVWBubhVyOGA-1&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-this-supplement-brand-scaled-to-100m-in-3-years-faster-than-athletic-greens)

If you run a 7-9 figure ecommerce brand and want an email / sms system as bulletproof as theirs… book a free email strategy consultation, _**[book a call here »](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=newsletter&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-boost-your-email-open-rates-in-60-days-without-burning-your-list&amp%3B_bhlid=57320e9fad662a45511f0b06bd801981c99fd4a8)**_

entries.title: The Right (and Profitable) Way to Discount Your Ecommerce Brand
entries.summary: I will start this by saying you can function without discounts, but it is a lot harder and you must have an amazing product
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

[I will start this by saying you can function without discounts, but it is a lot harder and you must have an amazing product]

Let’s talk about the controversial (but critical) strategy almost every ecommerce brand needs to embrace from day one: discounting.

I know… “Discounts ruin brand value.”

But that’s BS, as long as you know how to do it right.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Discounting is essential, but only when it's strategic.

- Your acquisition offer is the most important lever in your funnel.

- Copying generic offers like “10% off” isn’t going to cut it.

- Test offers with real data using email pop-ups and profile properties.

## Yes, You _Should_ Discount Your Brand (Strategically)

Too many brands treat discounting like it’s a sin. But guess what?

- AG1 gives $20 off _+_ free travel packs + 2 FREE gifts if you buy from them…

- Dr. Squatch gives 20% off the first order

- Vuori, who NEVER runs site-wide sales, offers 20% off the first order.

Why? Because acquisition offers _work_.

They get people in the door.

Discounts aren’t about slashing your margins…

They’re about unlocking new doors for potential customers who otherwisr wouldn’t have been interested.

But these brands didn’t just slap on a random discount and call it good…

They’ve tested, iterated, and dialed it in based on the numbers.

**Your welcome offer is the #1 lever in your ecommerce funnel.**

Period.

### The _Wrong_ Way to Offer Discounts

Here’s what you don’t want to do:
📉 Throw up a 10% off pop-up and call it a day.
📉 Leave that same offer live for 2 years with zero testing.
📉 Blast the same code across every channel.

That’s not strategy and every day you keep running that offer you could be leaving money on the table.

You need to test what acquisition offer works best.

If you can find one that converts even 10% better… that’s a 10% decrease in your Cost Per Acquisition.

### The _Right_ Way to Create a Winning Acquisition Offer

Here's how to get real data on what works best, fast, and stop guessing:

- **Create 2 email pop-up variations** (in Klaviyo or your tool of choice): One offering one offer (Ex. “$10 off”)

- One offering a different offer (Ex. “10% off”)

- **Add a pop-up A/B test** showing half of your traffic the $10 OFF form and half of your traffic the 10% OFF form.

- **Add a profile property** to each pop-up when a customer opts in. $10 OFF form submitters get tagged with Offer = $10

- 10% OFF form submitters get tagged with Offer = $10

- **Split your Email Welcome Flow** based on that property. Show each subscriber their corresponding offer in the first email.

- Let the flows do the work.

- **Wait 2-3 weeks** and look at the data. Who converted more?

- Who spent more?

- Who stayed longer?

- **Repeat**

That’s how you build a brand that grows with profit baked in.

### Bonus: Offer Ideas That Work

Here are some of my personal go-to offer strategies:

🧴 **Supplements?** Bundle discounts that push subscriptions.
👕 **Apparel?** Dollar vs percent off, test both. You can also do free socks or blank tees with your first order.
🧪 **Beauty / CPG?** Free gift with purchase or kit bundles.

I have seen the most success with offering free gifts with purchase, but it has to be a good gift.

Find a product you have high margins on and offer ir for free with purchase.

**Final Word**

The brands winning today aren’t the ones who avoid promotions.

They’re the ones who test, optimize, and execute their promotions like scientists.

Use the pop-up + property split test and thank me later.

PS - **[this quick video](https://www.instagram.com/p/DLkOYzkuo-S/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-right-and-profitable-way-to-discount-your-ecommerce-brand)** shows you exactly how to do this in Klaviyo.

entries.title: Is Email Marketing Dead? Let’s Set the Record Straight
entries.summary: Usually after they check their inbox, see 47 promotional emails from brands they don’t remember signing up for, and think, “This doesn’t work anymore.”
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Every few months someone declares email marketing dead.

Usually after they check their inbox, see 47 promotional emails from brands they don’t remember signing up for, and think, “This doesn’t work anymore.”

But let’s be real... is email actually dying? Or are lazy strategies just dying off?

### 📊 Email Usage & Marketing Stats: The State of the Inbox

- **Nearly everyone uses email daily**: In the U.S., about 89–96% of adults across age groups (15‑64+) use email daily… many up to 20 times a day; 58% start their morning with email

- **Volume overload**: Globally, some 376–380 billion emails are sent daily in 2025—about 9.7 billion per day in the U.S. alone [demandsage.co](https://demandsage.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=is-email-marketing-dead-let-s-set-the-record-straight)

- **Mobile dominance**: Between 59–67% of Millennials and Gen Z check email primarily on smartphones

- **Influence on purchases**: 59–60% of consumers report being influenced by marketing emails to make a purchase .

These numbers tell one clear story: **email is still deeply embedded in daily life.**

And highly effective for brands.

### 📉 The Case for Email Marketing Dying

Let’s play devil’s advocate.

**1. Consumer Fatigue**
People are overwhelmed. Between newsletters, flash sale blasts, and “we miss you” emails, inboxes are a mess. Many consumers are tuning out, unsubscribing, or ghosting brands altogether.

**2. Rising Privacy & Deliverability Challenges**
Apple Mail Privacy Protection, Gmail’s ever-evolving spam filters, and engagement-based sorting mean just hitting “send” doesn’t guarantee visibility anymore. If your emails aren’t personalized, valuable, and optimized, they’re not landing or not being opened.

**3. SMS and Newer Channels**
SMS open rates are sitting around 98%. With channels like SMS, push notifications, and even DMs offering direct, high-engagement access, it’s easy to assume email is the past.

**4. Saturation & Declining ROI for Some**
For brands that batch-and-blast outdated templates to cold lists? Yeah, email _is_ dead for them. They’re seeing diminishing returns because they haven’t adapted.

### 💡 The Case for Email Marketing Being More Alive Than Ever

**1. 40%+ of Store Revenue Can Come From Email**
Our agency has scaled brands to 40–50% of total revenue from email alone. Not with outdated strategies but with flows, segmentation, and on-brand campaigns that nurture and convert.

**2. Owned Media = Power & Profit**
Email isn’t controlled by Meta, TikTok, or some other algorithm. It’s your list. Your audience. Your data. And with rising CAC, owning your traffic is more valuable than ever.

**3. Deliverability Is a Skill, Not a Gamble**
Spam filters are tougher, but brands that follow warm-up protocols, segment, and send high-quality content are thriving. Bad practices are dying. Email isn’t.

**4. Email Powers Cross-Channel Success**
Want your SMS to pop off? Email primes the list. Want retargeting to convert better? Email warms them up. It’s not either/or… it’s both.

**5. The Numbers Don’t Lie**
We’ve scaled fresh Klaviyo accounts to $31k/mo in 47 days. We’ve helped brands double list growth and revenue with optimized pop-up forms. These results don’t come from a dead channel.

### 🔚 Final Thoughts

Email marketing isn’t dying.

What’s dying is **lazy execution**: batch‑and‑blast. Ignoring list health. No testing.

But when you build a strong strategy of flows, segmentation, testing, and personalization… email becomes your most predictable, profitable, and powerful channel.

These stats show it's still stellar in usage, reach, ROI, and influence. Don’t fall for the hype.

Email isn’t dead. But your old approach? That might be.

entries.title: Complete Ecommerce Email Marketing Flows Tutorial
entries.summary: This completely AUTOMATED email flow setup brought in $471,000 in 30 days for one brand.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

This completely AUTOMATED email flow setup brought in $471,000 in 30 days for one brand.

If you're not running this exact structure or close to it, you're likely leaving six figures on the table every month.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ba3443c8-ed9f-439d-b4c9-1562192b3c7b/Screenshot_2025-07-07_at_7.22.54_PM.png?t=1751908979)

## The Full Breakdown: Email Flows That Actually Work

Email flows are automated sequences triggered by customer behavior.

Once they're built correctly, they’ll operate 24/7 without any manual effort.

But the majority of ecommerce brands either set up too few flows, set them up incorrectly, or let them go stale.

This system is designed to fix that.

## Section 1: Pre-Purchase Flows

Pre-purchase flows are the highest leverage. They trigger before a customer places an order and guide them to convert.

#### 1. Welcome Flow (4-5 Emails Minimum)

Triggered when someone signs up through a pop-up.
Each email should push toward a first purchase while building trust.

**Structure:**

- **Email 1:** Deliver discount, show best sellers

- **Email 2:** Brand story / mission

- **Email 3:** Unique selling points

- **Email 4:** Social proof

- **Email 5:** Final reminder with urgency

Every email should restate the discount and contain a CTA.

Use a mix of graphic and text-based formats to maximize deliverability and engagement.

#### 2. Site Abandonment

Triggered when someone visits the homepage or a non-product page and leaves.
Goal: Get them to view a product.

Send 1-2 emails showing best sellers or common product FAQs. Keep messaging simple and value-focused.

#### 3. Browse Abandonment

Triggered when someone views a product page and leaves without adding to cart.

**Structure:**

- **Email 1:** “Did you see this?” – reminder + product info

- **Email 2:** Add testimonials or reviews

- **Email 3:** Final reminder with urgency. Optional discount.

#### 4. Cart Abandonment

Triggered when someone adds to cart but does not reach checkout.

This flow is often missing because brands confuse it with checkout abandonment. Make sure the trigger is “Added to Cart,” not “Checkout Started.”

**Structure:**

- **Email 1:** Cart reminder with product details

- **Email 2:** Objection handling (shipping info, guarantees)

- **Email 3:** Introduce discount

- **Email 4:** Final CTA with stronger urgency

#### 5. Checkout Abandonment

Triggered when someone enters checkout but doesn’t complete purchase.
Structure can mirror cart abandonment but should reference the checkout experience (shipping, payment, etc.).

**Optional Split:**
Use conditional logic to segment first-time visitors. For new customers, restate the welcome discount in each email. For returning customers, skip the offer or save it for the last email.

## Section 2: Post-Purchase Flows

These flows focus on retention, increasing LTV, and improving the customer experience.

#### 1. Post-Purchase Thank You

Triggered immediately after purchase.

- Send a text-based thank-you from the founder.

- Include a “P.S.” with a link to shop again.

- Optional: cross-sell or invite to follow on social media.

This removes buyer's remorse and encourages a second purchase early.

#### 2. Replenishment Flow

Triggered based on estimated product usage.
Example: If one unit typically lasts 30 days, trigger the reminder around day 28-32.

- **Email 1:** “Running low?” – offer easy reorder

- **Email 2:** Cross-sell other products (wait 7-10 days after)

Use Klaviyo’s conditional splits to adjust timing based on product quantity or SKU.

#### 3. Winback Flow

Triggered when a customer hasn’t purchased in 90-180 days.

- **Email 1:** “We miss you” – feature best sellers or new arrivals

- **Email 2:** Discount offer

- **Email 3:** Final CTA with urgency

Target only those who haven’t converted via campaigns or flows during that period.

#### 4. Sunset Flow

Triggered when a subscriber hasn’t opened or clicked any emails for 90+ days.

- **Email 1:** “Still want emails from us?”

- If unopened, automatically suppress from sending.

This keeps your Klaviyo bill down and protects sender reputation.

### Final Notes on Optimization

- Test discount types: % vs. $ off vs. “mystery offer”

- Use pop-up forms to increase flow entry (aim for 8-10% CTR)

- Mix HTML design with 1-2 plain text emails per flow

- Personalize by using conditional splits (e.g., has purchased before)

- Set up a consistent A/B testing schedule across all flows

If you don’t have these built out, you’re leaving money on the table. Set them up properly once, keep them optimized, and let them run in the background while you focus on acquisition.

If you want more explanation, watch this video of mine where I go into depth on all of these flows.

_[**Video Tutorial »**](https://youtu.be/ymEpDZd_C2U?si=HTn4WjpdkHaD90KY&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=complete-ecommerce-email-marketing-flows-tutorial)_

Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

You know you're doing something right when someone calls your results fake.

## Wait… You Thought We Were Lying?

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/63262f4e-0c35-455e-9aad-ee4730c90d87/Screenshot_2025-07-04_at_1.09.26_PM.png?t=1751627379)

My Original Post

Someone Calling Cap On Our Results

So someone saw our post saying we do 80% of store revenue from email + SMS, and dropped a quick "cap" under it.

Cap = lie.
Lie = we’re full of it.
And that = my favorite kind of compliment.

Because if your numbers are _so good_ people don’t believe them… you’re probably doing something right.

### Breaking Down the "Unbelievable"

Here’s what the results really are:

- **Email Revenue YTD**: $1.28M

- **SMS Revenue YTD**: $1.67M

- **Total from Email + SMS**: $2.95M

- **Total Store Revenue**: $3.67M

- **Percent Of Toal From Email / SMS:** 80.37%

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8f9dee6e-31ac-4368-91a0-61ec0cda88dd/Screenshot_2025-07-04_at_1.24.51_PM.png?t=1751628334)

Email Results Year To Date

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b6238f45-46ef-4318-a276-7a7c86bb1834/Screenshot_2025-07-04_at_1.24.59_PM.png?t=1751628338)

SMS Results Year To Date

Yep. That's **80.38%** attributed to retention channels.

And no.

We’re not using some janky custom attribution hack.

This is straight from Klaviyo and Attentive's standard settings, which 95% of brands use.

Now I want to be fully transparent…

I’ll be the first to say that standard attribution settings are generous.

If we tightened the attribution windows to something like 12-hour clicks, of course the number would drop.

But this is the same setup most brands roll with and what this brand wanted us to stick to.

This is a VERY unique situation and these results are NOT normal.

AND we are achieving results after working with this brand for over 1 year… we don’t accomplish these sorts of results in just a couple months.

Here’s some info on the brand:

- Clothing brand

- They run plenty of drops, restocks, and limited edition content

- We push everybody into the email and sms list to stay updated with the high-demand drops

- The brand crushes it on their end with content and makes our lives easy on the email / sms front

Also… we’re crushing it for them 😉

And the reason we crush?

- Because our pop-ups convert at nearly 17% of new site visitors to email subscribers

- Because we’ve built and refined flows that bring in real revenue month after month

- Because we send clean campaigns that mix in design + text-based emails

- Because we’ve been doing this and optimizing with them for over a year

### I Would NEVER Lie About Our Results

I literally show everything in this breakdown doc.

Every flow. Every campaign. All the numbers.

That’s the opposite of cap.

That’s just what happens when you treat email and SMS like the core of your business and not just a little side channel for holiday promos.

entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you think emailing your list 2-3 times a week is “too much”...

Then you might want to look at what the fastest-growing brands in ecommerce are doing.

Spoiler: they’re doing more (and for good reason)

### The Top Brands Do It… You Should Too

Dr. Squatch. Vuori. Ridge. Brez. The list goes on.

These brands aren’t sending 1 email a week and hoping for the best.

**They’re hitting their list** _**4+ times per week**_ **and seeing massive returns.**

They aren’t doing this by accident.

They all do it because it WORKS and you NEED to send at a higher frequency if you want to maximize your backend store revenue.

These brands understand all the benefits of frequent sending.

So if your brand is stuck thinking once a week is “safe,”

Realize the biggest players are building their empires by doing the opposite.

### Increased Frequency = Staying Top of Mind

Every day your customer _doesn’t_ hear from you… they’re hearing from someone else.

People don’t sit around thinking about your brand.

You need to _remind_ them that you exist. Frequently.

More emails means more impressions.
More impressions means more trust.
More trust means less chance they wander off to a competitor.

Stay present or lose attention. It’s that simple.

### You Will Make More Money. Period.

You’re sitting on a goldmine.

You’ve already done the hard work of getting people on your list.

Now all you have to do is send to them, frequently, and the revenue will follow.

More campaigns = more clicks = more sales.

We’ve seen it across 100+ brands.

If you're not emailing often, you’re not just missing revenue… you're burning it.

### It’s Crucial for Deliverability

Inbox providers reward _consistency_.

If you send sporadically, your engagement dips.
And when engagement dips, your sender reputation tanks.
Which lands you in spam or promotions.

But when you send often and get good opens and clicks you train Gmail to trust you.

The result is primary inbox placement, higher open rates, and more sales.

### You're Not Annoying (As Long As Your Content’s Good)

Sure, bad emails are annoying. But great emails? People actually look forward to them believe it or not.

If you nail:

- your topics (relevant + timely)

- your copy (clear + persuasive)

- your design (clean + on-brand)

…then you can send as often as you want.

Instead of unsubscribes, you’ll get people scrolling through their email inbox like they do their social media.

### Example of Increased Campaign Sends Resulting In More Sales

Here’s proof…

For this brand we ramped up their email campaign content from 1x per week to 4x per week and just look at the massice impact on revenue from both campaigns and also flows.

The more you send campaigns… the more people will also enter your email flows and begin to convert.

It’s a full flywheel.

The craziest part?

**All engagement metrics improved… bounce rate, spam rate, and unsubscribe rate DESPITE sending more.**

This is what great content ideas, design, and copy can do for you when you increase frequency.

entries.title: Advanced Strategies for Scaling Your Email List Growth
entries.summary: They slap on a generic “10% OFF” form, call it a day, and assume that’s all they can get from their website traffic.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most ecommerce brands sleep on pop-ups.

They slap on a generic “10% OFF” form, call it a day, and assume that’s all they can get from their website traffic.

Big mistake.

Last month alone, one platform helped brands generate **$150M in sales** and collect **8 million emails** just through better pop-up strategy.

I sat down with Sean, the founder of [**Alia**](https://www.alialearn.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=advanced-strategies-for-scaling-your-email-list-growth), a tool that does nothing but build and optimize high-converting pop-ups for ecommerce brands. In our conversation, he broke down exactly what’s working right now and why most brands are leaving huge money on the table.

Here are some of the key takeaways from the conversation:

### Most Pop-Ups Underperform Badly

Default forms on platforms like Klaviyo or Shopify usually convert around **3%** of website traffic into email subscribers. **That means 97% of your hard-earned traffic is bouncing without a trace.**

But with just a few smart tweaks, you can get those forms converting at **9% or more**.

That’s 3x the subscribers, and 3x the long-term revenue—, rom the same traffic you’re already paying for.

### The Psychology of Micro-Commitments

Asking a **question before you ask for the email** is shown makes a massive difference.

Something simple like “What are you shopping for today?” or “Who are you buying for?” creates a moment of interaction that increases opt-in rate significantly.

Only after someone answers the question do you ask for their email.

Here’s why it works:

- **Commitment bias**: Once someone answers a question, they’re more likely to keep going.

- **Personalization effect**: It feels more relevant to them.

- **Curiosity**: It stands out from the boring “Get 10% off” pop-ups everyone else uses.

In tests, forms with a micro-commitment step regularly see **40–50% interaction rates** on the first step alone.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4044e9fa-1c2c-4e78-ad25-6743eb21605d/Screenshot-2024-04-22-at-2.32.16-PM__2_.png?t=1750841580)

Step 1

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0c23037f-e870-4c07-86fb-3e98bd87210a/Screenshot-2024-04-22-at-2.32.24-PM__2_.png?t=1750841588)

Step 2

### Smarter Offers (That Don’t Kill Your Margins)

Sean broke down some simple rules around offer structure:

- If you’re offering less than 15% off, frame it as a mystery discount. It tends to outperform showing the number.

- If your AOV is over $100, use dollar-off instead of percent-off.

- If you don’t want to discount at all, try positioning early access, bundles, or free shipping thresholds as the incentive.

They’ve seen opt-in rates as high as 16% using nothing but well-framed, non-discounted offers.

### Personalization Wins

The top-performing brands use pop-ups that:

- Change visuals based on gender selection

- Send users to **specific product pages** based on what they’re shopping for

- Dynamically update messaging based on source (e.g., UTM links from affiliates)

### Pop-Ups Don’t Hurt Conversion. They Boost It.

A lot of brands worry that pop-ups will annoy customers or hurt their site conversion rates.

Reality? **Hostage Tape** (an Alia client) ran a test and found that adding a pop-up **increased their sitewide CVR by 15%**.

Even customers who close it right away are more likely to buy just knowing a discount exists somewhere on the site helps them feel more in control of the purchase.

### MUCH MUCH MORE

These are just a few of the key insights from my conversation with Shaan.

Watch the full convo here: _**[https://youtu.be/pZBZxxFlSuc?si=gEYNgiDTKUa1GkPV](https://youtu.be/pZBZxxFlSuc?si=gEYNgiDTKUa1GkPV&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=advanced-strategies-for-scaling-your-email-list-growth)**_

entries.title: The Highest Leverage A/B Test You're Not Running (But Should Be)
entries.summary: Let me show you how one tiny change pulled in 4x more revenue...
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let me show you how one tiny change pulled in 4x more revenue...

...without changing a single line of copy.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Send time is one of the easiest A/B tests to run, but most brands skip it.

- Different audiences open and buy at different times of day.

- Testing send time can 4x your email revenue (without changing a single word).

- Lunch time and early AM tend to be top performers, but always test it.

### This Test Took 10 Seconds, And Made $6,000 More

Most A/B tests take effort.

Different copy. New subject lines. Rewriting CTAs. Designing variants.

But the highest leverage test? It’s dead simple: **change the send time.**

We ran a test for a Father’s Day campaign.

Same list. Same email. Same subject line. Same preview text.

The only difference?

**Variation A** was sent at 9:00 AM.
**Variation B** was sent at 3:00 PM.

Here’s what happened:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e801a1e5-5c27-43ef-bd87-3126315a25f4/Screenshot_2025-06-23_at_12.39.00_PM.png?t=1750678777)

Test Results

9:00 AM

$8,364.96

50.54%

3:00 PM

$2,062.99

Same email. **4x the revenue.**

All because of when we hit send.

### Why Send Time Works

Every audience has a rhythm.

Busy moms, 9-to-5ers, gym bros, night owls…

They all check email at _different times._

Most brands just default to 10am or 6pm and pray.

But there’s zero downside to testing your timing and huge upside if you hit the sweet spot.

### General Rules of Thumb for Send Time

Here’s what we’ve seen work across dozens of ecommerce brands:

- **Earlier = More Open Time** Emails sent earlier in the day have more time to be seen. The later you send, the more likely someone will fall asleep on not check their emails from the day before.

- **But Not Too Early** If you send at 6:00 AM, you’re fighting for attention in a crowded inbox while your customer is brushing their teeth and rushing to work.

- **Sweet Spot = 10:00 AM–2:00 PM** This window hits right as people are settling into their day or taking a lunch break, AKA scrolling their phones. It’s early enough to get seen, but not so early that you get buried.

- **Evening Sends (5:00–7:00 PM)** These can work well when you want quick, impulse-driven actions (like a flash sale or 24-hour drop). Just know these sends have a shorter shelf life, most of your opens will happen in the first hour or two.

Like anything in email, these aren’t hard rules. They’re starting points. Your audience is unique, so always back this up with real tests.

### Big News Coming Soon 😉

If you’re an ecommerce brand who doesn’t have the budget for our full service but want professional level partners running your emails, you’re going to like the news I share shortly.

Be on the lookout.

entries.title: How We Made MrBeast’s Chocolate Bar Feel Like a New Product (Without Actually Launching One)
entries.summary: Most brands treat non-sale emails like filler content that isn’t meant to make sales…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most brands treat non-sale emails like filler content that isn’t meant to make sales…

Drop that mindset.

I’m going to show you how we flipped that on its head by turning a simple peanut butter bar into a launch-worthy event.

All while staying 100% on-brand for one of the most followed people on the internet: MrBeast.

Let’s break down exactly how we did it 👇

(Mr. Beast isn’t a real client lol just made this email as a mock-up)

**Key Takeaways:**

- Use novelty psychology to breathe new life into existing SKUs.

- Ethical storytelling drives feel-good conversions.

- Design matters… playfulness + brand identity = trust + clicks.

- Use bridge sections to blend brand values into non-discount emails.

- Treat every campaign like a micro product launch.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/1bbfb6f1-a5b6-4d31-a22e-f58e085c4dc8/Feastables.png?t=1750416217)

Final Email Design

## The Strategy: Make Something Old Feel New

With non-discount emails, we need to find a way to tickle someone’s buying part of their brand.

Even if you have a past product that you want to make an email about, we can give that existing product new life.

For this email example, we leaned into _novelty psychology_: subtly framing the Peanut Butter Bar as something totally fresh.

Here’s how:

- **Voice-first headline**: “Peanut Butter That Slaps.” Pure MrBeast energy.

- **Set the stage**: “You’ve had chocolate. You’ve had peanut butter. But never like this.”

- **Lean on contrast**: “This isn’t your average gas station candy.”

Takeaway for your brand: Reframe familiarity. Newness isn’t just about product… it's about _presentation_.

### Emotional Leverage: Brand Mission As Selling Point

The “Taking Down Big Chocolate” bridge section brought the _why_ behind the product to the forefront.

This is another psychological trigger, making the customer pick a side when we are clearly the right side. This is called _enemy marketing._

We stacked:

- Rainforest Alliance certified cacao

- Regenerative agriculture

- Sustainable packaging

- Fair pay + ethical sourcing

This turns a chocolate bar into a vote against Big Chocolate and your purchase into a small rebellion.

Killer ridge sections are essential for non-discount campaigns. They let you educate _and_ convert.

### The Design: Playful, Depth-Driven, On-Brand

We matched Feastables' brand DNA down to the pixel:

- Blue-striped backgrounds, orange PB pops, clouds, and candy rainbows

- Layered hero section with 3D graphics + CTA early and often

- Infographic-style bridge section for easy digestibility

All images were sliced JPGs, compressed for load speed, and clickable to specific PDPs.

### Final Thoughts: A “Mini Launch” Mindset

This wasn’t a product drop but it _felt_ like one.

We treated it like a launch, designed it like a statement, and backed it with brand values and social proof.

Next time you’re “just sending an email,” ask: How can I make this feel like a launch?

If you want to watch me actually write and design this email in full, I posted a YouTube video yesterday going through it all.

entries.title: How to F*ck Up Your Cart Abandon Flow (And What to Do Instead)
entries.summary: If your cart abandon flow has one or two emails and a discount in email #1… you’re burning money.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If your cart abandon flow has one or two emails and a discount in email #1… you’re burning money.

This is one of the easiest flows to fix… and yet, most stores f*ck it up completely.

Let’s fix it!

### Key Takeaways:

- One or two emails won't cut it, aim for 4-5 well-timed touchpoints.

- Keep copy short, visuals strong, and your CTA above the fold.

- Don’t give away margin too early, save discounts for later in the flow.

- Use dynamic cart blocks to remind customers exactly what they wanted.

### 1. You’re Stopping at 1-2 Emails

A single reminder is not enough.

Abandonment flows are high-intent, high-leverage sequences.

Your customer got all the way to the cart, don’t ghost them after one nudge.

**What to do instead:**
Aim for 4-5 emails over 3-5 days. Start soft, build urgency, and hold off on discounts until the end of the flow.

### 2. Your Copy is Too Damn Long

No one abandoned the cart hoping for a novel.

The goal here isn’t storytelling, it’s reminding and re-selling.

**What to do instead:**
Snappy copy. Bullet points. “Hey, you left this.” Done. Customers should know exactly what to do within 2 seconds of opening the email.

### 3. Your CTA Button Is in No-Man’s Land

If I have to scroll to find your “Complete My Order” button, your flow already failed.

**What to do instead:**
Put your main button above the fold. Every. Single. Time. Then repeat it further down if needed.

### 4. No Dynamic Cart Block = No Context

A static email with “You left something behind” doesn’t cut it.

Your customer needs to see _exactly_ what they left.

**What to do instead:**
Use Klaviyo’s dynamic product block to auto-load the cart content. This gives visual context and reactivates interest.

### 5. You’re Giving Discounts Too Early

Offering a 10-15% discount in email #1 might convert a few people… but you’re slicing your margins before they’re even necessary.

**What to do instead:**
Reserve discounts for the final email or two. Try converting full-price first, then sweeten the deal if needed.

This document goes over ALL of the core abandonment flows you need with winning strategies we use for our 8-9 figure accounts.

entries.title: Stop Over-Segmenting. Start Sending More Emails.
entries.summary: Let’s kill the sacred cow of ecommerce email marketing real quick.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s kill the sacred cow of ecommerce email marketing real quick.

Stop obsessing over segmentation.

No, you don’t need 87 micro-lists based on who clicked a green sock ad in Q4 of 2022. That level of complexity is slowing you down—and more importantly, it’s costing you revenue.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Hyper-segmentation leads to complexity, confusion, and lower revenue.

- A single, well-engaged list consistently emailed will outperform micro-segments.

- Prioritize reach and frequency over extreme granularity.

- Keep it simple: what’s easy to manage is easier to scale.

### The Segmentation Trap

We all love a good segment. It feels smart. It feels advanced. It feels like you’re tailoring a white-glove experience for your customers.

But what starts as a clever strategy often turns into a bloated mess of lists that confuse your team and throttle your sending volume.

I’ve seen this time and time again: brands with dozens of segments, yet barely emailing anyone because they’re “trying to protect deliverability” or “don’t want to annoy subscribers.”

Here’s the truth…

**You're not annoying people if you send good emails.**

### Reach and Frequency > Granularity

Instead of slicing your audience into tiny segments, focus on sending more often to your engaged list:

- Anyone who’s opened, clicked, or visited your site in the last 30 to 90 days.

That’s your money list.

Send to them **3–4 times per week.** Minimum.

Yes, even if it feels scary. Because _sending more to engaged people makes you more money_.

This group already knows you. Likes you. Trusts you enough to open and click.

They don’t need hyper-personalized messages…

Just value, consistency, and reminders that you’re still the best option in the game.

### What Happens When You Simplify

A few things happen when you ditch the over-segmentation:

- **You send more.** (Because it’s easier to hit send on one clean segment.)

- **You make more.** (More reach = more eyeballs = more clicks = more conversions.)

- **You sleep better.** (No more 17-flow logic trees just to send a Tuesday email.)

You also build stronger deliverability.

Why? Because inbox providers love consistent engagement. And that happens when you email more of the right people more often.

### Keep It Simple. Scale It Big.

Want to make your life easier?

Here’s your base segmentation stack:

- **14-day engaged**

- **30-day engaged**

- **60-day engaged**

- **90-day engaged**

Start with the 14-day segment and scale up once you’re consistently seeing 40–50% open rates. No need to complicate it.

The brands that win aren’t the ones with the most segments. They’re the ones in the inbox the most, with the strongest brand presence and consistent deliverability.

Let the segmentation nerds fight over clickers vs. converters.

You’ll be over here printing money with your 90-day engaged list.

See you in the inbox 🫡

entries.title: What I've Learned After Sending 1 Billion Marketing Emails
entries.summary: After sending over 1 billion emails (yes, really), I've found there are only a handful of needle-movers that actually make a difference.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

After sending over 1 billion emails (yes, really), I've found there are only a handful of needle-movers that actually make a difference.

And if you dial these in, you're not far from doubling your sales… fast.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Repeating the same email designs will kill engagement—newness wins.

- Without consistent list growth, even perfect emails won’t convert.

- Plain-text emails can quietly become your best revenue drivers.

- Automation should start simple and strategic

- Frequency and strong pop-up forms are the fastest paths to more sales.

### 1. Customers Crave Newness

If you’ve been sending the same layout every week...stop.

Engagement nosedives when your emails feel copy-pasted. Your list needs dopamine.

Try new content formats… stories, myths, sneak peeks, quizzes. Switch up your email structure weekly.

And please do not use the same design templates every week… customers need new to keep opening and keep them on their toes.

👉 **Try this**: Alternate between short and snappy emails, story-driven emails, flashy graphics, and plain text-based emails.

### 2. No List, No Results

You can write the most beautiful, high-converting emails on the planet but if no one’s on your list, it doesn’t matter.

The silent killer of most email programs is lack of list growth.

You’re relying on traffic that doesn’t exist.

👉 **What to do**: Push paid traffic, partner with influencers, run organic content. But above all… optimize your website pop-up form (more on this later).

### 3. Use Text-Based Emails Strategically

Sometimes the prettiest emails underperform.

Plain-text, personal emails from the founder or team can feel more authentic and often drive more clicks and revenue.

👉 **Best use**: Drop 1 every 5 emails. Especially great in your flows as well… Welcome, Winback, and Abandonment flows.

### 4. Keep Automations Simple (At First)

Complex trees and endless splits might feel advanced but they’re overkill early on.

80% of your automation revenue comes from the first 2–3 emails in your flows.

👉 **Start here**: Nail your Welcome, Browse, Cart, Checkout, and Post-Purchase flows with 2–3 high-performing emails each. Then after you can add the advanced follow up emails.

### 5. Stop Over-Segmenting

You don’t need a segment for every birthday, shoe size, and eye color.

Micromanaging segmentation kills reach and momentum.

👉 **Focus instead**: Just send to your 30/60/90-day engaged segments frequently. Frequency > personalization in most cases.

### 6. Your Pop-Up = Your Revenue Engine

Most stores convert <3% of site traffic to email. You need to hit 8-10%+.

An optimized pop-up is the easiest way to 3x your email revenue.

👉 **Steps to audit**: Improve your offer, test multiple formats, fix timing, and tighten copy.

### 7. Frequency is King

If you’re only sending one email a week...you’re leaving cash on the table.

3–4x per week is the sweet spot for most brands. Not just for more touches but because consistency breeds trust.

👉 **Pro tip**: Rotate in content that entertains. Email isn’t just for promos, it’s for building a brand.

I dropped a YouTube video yesterday breaking all of these points in depth and showing you exactly how to execute on all of them.

entries.title: The ChatGPT Trick to Instantly Find the Perfect Testimonial for Your Email
entries.summary: You know testimonials work for getting conversions. But you’re probably picking the wrong ones. Or worse… just grabbing the shortest ones that look good on a banner.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s not waste time.

You know testimonials work for getting conversions. But you’re probably picking the wrong ones. Or worse… just grabbing the shortest ones that look good on a banner.

Stop. You’re missing out on a lot of money. Here’s a ChatGPT trick that’ll change how you build testimonial-driven emails.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Long testimonials outperform short ones in most ecommerce emails.

- The best testimonials directly address a pain point your customer is feeling.

- You can use ChatGPT to find high-performing testimonials hidden on your site.

- All you need is your website URL and a specific pain point to target.

### Why Testimonials Matter More Than Ever

With customer trust at an all-time low, real voices drive conversions.

But it’s not just about slapping a 5-star review in an email and calling it a day. The best-performing emails use testimonials that directly squash an objection.

Price, quality, shipping time. Whatever’s in the customer’s head, overcome it with proof it worked for others before they bounce.

### Longer = Better

Short reviews like “Love it!” or “Great product!” don’t convert.

You want paragraphs. Real stories. Reviews that sound like something your best friend would text you at 11 p.m. after finally trying that product you told them about.

These testimonials do heavy lifting and they tell the reader “Hey, I had the same hesitation, and this solved it.”

### How to Find the Right Testimonials (Without Losing Your Mind)

Most brands dig through review apps or product pages manually which takes forever.

Here’s how to cheat:

- Go to ChatGPT.

- Paste this prompt: _“Go to [insert your website URL]. Find 3 long customer testimonials that address [insert specific pain point, e.g., 'why someone might hesitate to pay a premium price']. Return the full quotes.”_

- Boom. You get gold in seconds.

You can get even more specific:

- “Find testimonials from first-time buyers.”

- “Find testimonials that mention customer service.”

- “Find testimonials that mention results within 7 days.”

Next time you're building a campaign and need proof… don’t just guess.

Use ChatGPT, drop in the right quote, and let your past customers sell for you.

entries.title: How AG1 Is Able To Sell Green Powder for $90/mo
entries.summary: Their 8-part email welcome flow is one of the cleanest, most strategic I’ve ever broken down.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most welcome emails fumble the bag in the first 5 seconds.

Athletic Greens (AG1) doesn’t.

Their 8-part email welcome flow is one of the cleanest, most strategic I’ve ever broken down.

There’s no hard sells… just pure psychology-driven sequencing.

Here’s exactly how they pull it off and how you can do the same.

**Key Takeaways:**

- AG1’s 8-part welcome series focuses on building trust, not chasing the sale.

- Each email strategically handles a key objection: from “What is this?” to “Is this worth it?”

- The flow uses data, storytelling, and reframing to guide the reader toward a purchase.

- High-performing flows prioritize sequence strategy just as much as copy and design.

Here’s a link to the drive with every email in their welcome flow: _**[AG1 Welcome Flow »](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1d3FrBh5ACIiyHE_PWYyJ_qggePniR7Cc/view?usp=sharing&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-ag1-is-able-to-sell-green-powder-for-90-mo)**_

### Email 1: The Perfect Welcome 👋

AG1 opens strong by delivering the offer + showing what’s inside the Welcome Kit.

By visually showing everything inside, the customer can see the value they are getting.

✅ Clean design
✅ Strong CTA
✅ High perceived value
✅ Quick brand intro
✅ Visual trust

It’s all about getting the click. If they don't buy now, that's fine... we will be overcoming objections throughout this flow.

### Email 2: Breaking Down the Logic 🧠

AG1 stacks the value by showing how one scoop replaces your entire cabinet.

Logically, they are showing how it makes sense to use their product because it simplifies your routine.

💊 Comparison chart = instant clarity
📉 $3/day vs. buying 7+ other supplements
🎯 Focus shifts from story → logic

This is where they close the "but is it worth it?" gap.

### Email 3: Simplify > Complicate 💯

AG1 doubles down on the simplicity angle (which is probably their strongest angle, considering how hard they hit on it).

Essentially they are pushing for you're not just buying a greens powder, you're ditching the pill drawer.

📦 Simple visual shows AG1 replacing 6+ supplements
🧠 75 ingredients = maximum coverage, minimal effort
🧘‍♂️ Copy emphasizes simplicity and ease

Important to note they’re not pushing “buy now.” They’re planting the seed: “Wouldn’t it be easier if it was all in one scoop?”

NOTICE - how simple this email is!!

### Email 4: Eliminate Uncertainty ⏱️

AG1 tackles the silent objection: “How soon will I feel a difference?”

This email maps out the first 90 days of using AG1 day by day, week by week.

✅ Day 1: Gut support
✅ Week 2: More energy
✅ Month 1–3: Clearer skin, better mood, real transformation

This is future pacing, giving hesitant buyers clarity on what to expect and when.

It also subtly gets people to COMMIT to use the product for 3 months... increasing their customer LTV.

### Email 5: Replace Doubt with Data 📊

This email removes alllllll the uncertainty on if this product works.

This works ESPECIALLY well since their customers are usually busy professionals you value the numbersa nd science.

🧪 97% felt more energy in 30 days
☕ 91% drank less coffee by month 2
🥱 97% had fewer cravings by month 3

Real data!

If you have a product in the health niche... FIND DATA LIKE THIS.

### Email 6: Tackle the Price Objection 💸

Okay this person should know the product works by now...

So AG1 comes right at the “it’s too expensive” barrier.

They don’t justify it emotionally, they frame it rationally.

People don't buy expensive products like this emotionally... they need to logically justify it.

🧮 Less than $3/day
📉 Cheaper than your coffee
🧠 Replaces 6+ supplements
💚 One scoop = total body support

It’s a value reframe: not “Is this worth $90/month?”

But → “What am I already spending more on for less?”

### Email 7: Ingredient Value Proposition 🥬

To really show the value behind the product, AG1 breaks down their extensive ingredient list showing they truly have an all in one product.

🧪 75 high-quality ingredients
🌿 Each one with a purpose

They’re justifying their ingredients and proving how all of their choices are made with purpose.

This email says: "You're not paying for fluff. You're paying for function."

### Email 8: Close with Cost Clarity 💵

AG1 wraps the flow with a value-driven mic drop.

Instead of discounts, they compare costs:

💊 $3.39 = multiple supplements
☕ $4.99 = your morning coffee
🍽️ $14 = eating out
⚡ $4.49 = energy drinks
💚 < $3 = AG1

They’re reframing the price as a smart trade-off.

Plus: vegan, gluten-free, sugar-free... to overcome dietary restriction objections.

This is the final nudge: premium nutrition without premium markup.

**Final Thoughts:**

This welcome flow doesn’t beg for the sale.

It earns the sale by stacking trust, educating strategically, and handling objections before they arise.

If your welcome flow isn’t converting, it’s probably trying to close before you’ve opened the conversation.

Steal AG1’s sequencing strategy and watch your conversion rate climb.

entries.title: Your Marketing Success Relies on Newness
entries.summary: - Switch up structure, length, and design often to keep performance high.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If your emails all look the same, people stop opening.

Same angles. Same layout. Same flow. Same dead engagement…

**Key Takeaways:**

- Repeating the same email layout kills engagement.

- Your list needs fresh content angles to keep opening.

- Switch up structure, length, and design often to keep performance high.

### Stop Sending Boring Emails

You know the formula: Headline. Product photo. CTA. Repeat.

At first it works. **Then it plateaus.**

Eventually, people ignore it completely.

### New Angles = Better Performance

KEEP YOUR LIST GUESSING.

You can’t send the same content angles.

A lot of brands want to do a weekly content calednar where every Monday is a product highlight, every Wednesday is a recipe, etc.

But I have seen engagement plateau.

Customers need NEW.

Mix up your angles…

- **Customer story** – Show real results.

- **Myth-buster** – Challenge assumptions.

- **Sneak peek** – Build hype for what’s coming.

- **Quick tip** – Teach something simple.

- **Founder note** – Add a personal touch.

Don’t say the same thing every week. Show it in new ways.

### Change the Format Too!

Even if your message changes, the layout matters.

Mix it up:

- Text-only emails that feel personal

- Short punchy emails with one-line copy

- Visual-heavy emails with GIFs or memes

- Long-form breakdowns once in a while

When the structure shifts, people pay attention.

It should be a game when someone opens an email from you…

You want them to think, “**ooo what’s it going to be this time?”**

### Your Design Shouldn't Be Predictable

If every email looks identical, your subscribers will tune it out.

Try:

- Swapping the CTA position

- Leading with a testimonial or bold headline

- Using different layouts (2-column, image-heavy, minimal)

- Highlighting urgency visually with countdowns or timers

Keep it fresh, even if the offer stays the same.

### Wrap Up

If your email calendar feels like copy-paste…

Your list knows it. And they’re tuning out.

Change the angle. Change the format. Change the design.
Because new = attention.
And attention = sales.

entries.title: The Perfect Email Welcome Flow for Ecommerce Brands
entries.summary: You’re already paying $30, $50, maybe even $100+ to get someone to your site. So what happens when they bounce without buying?
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

You’re already paying $30, $50, maybe even $100+ to get someone to your site. So what happens when they bounce without buying?

You just burned cash. Unless…

You’ve got a badass welcome flow that’s set up to catch, connect, and convert.

**Key Takeaways:**

- You’re spending money to drive traffic, make sure you’re capturing and converting it immediately with your welcome flow

- A strong pop-up + welcome flow combo can drastically reduce your CAC and increase LTV.

- Without this setup, you miss the trust window and future sales are gone forever.

- The brands winning in 2025 and beyond are building strong BRANDS… which starts with the email welcome flow

## 🧠 Why Your Welcome Flow Is the Cost Per Acquisition Fix

In today’s ecommerce market:

- Ad costs are at all-time highs.

- Conversion rates are shrinking.

- Over 1,000 Shopify stores launch every single day.

You can’t lower your CPMs, but you can increase how much every click is worth.

That starts with owning the attention you paid for.

Pop-up → Welcome Flow → Long-term customer. Simple.

### 💡 Strategic Framework: How to Convert More (Without Paying More)

**The Winning Formula:**

- Capture the email (via high-converting pop-up)

- Build trust fast (via welcome flow)

- Convert now, or later, without spending another dollar

Miss this window, and that customer is gone forever.

### 🧱 Non-Negotiables for Every Welcome Flow

- Disable double opt-in (email that makes someone confirm subscription after signing up)

- Trigger the first email immediately after signup

- Minimum of 3 emails (ideally 4–6), spaced 1–2 days apart

- Mention the discount in every email

- Include at least one plain-text and one urgency-based “last chance” email

### 🧩 The Welcome Flow Structure

**1. Email #1 – Immediate Send**

- **Hero:** Deliver the discount + strong CTA

- **Bridge:** Brief brand intro

- **Product:** Showcase bestsellers or categories

**2. Filler Emails (1–5)**
Each email builds trust and primes future purchases. It will be different for each brand… just use common sense on what education your customer needs.

Some Ideas:

- One Benefit

- One Feature

- FAQ

- “What’s Inside”

- How It’s Made / How to Use

- Testimonials

- Us vs. Them

- Founder’s Note

- Brand Values

- Tips & Tricks

- UGC / Staff Picks

**3. Last Chance Email**

- Create urgency (e.g., “Discount expires tonight”)

- Showcase what they’ll miss (bestsellers, bundles)

**4. Text-Based Email from Founder/Support**

- Personal, plain-text format

- “Hey—just checking in. Discount’s still active if you need it.”

- Invite replies to build real connection

### 🔁 Optimization Tips

Test:

- % off vs $ off

- Text-based vs graphic

- 1 vs 2-day delays

- Subject lines / preview text

- Linking to specific products vs general collections

And when you find a campaign email that crushes…

Turn it into a welcome email. Just add the discount.

I just made a banger 30 minute YouTube video going over all this: [https://youtu.be/dmNShBjMXA4](https://youtu.be/dmNShBjMXA4?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-perfect-email-welcome-flow-for-ecommerce-brands)

entries.title: 3 Modern Email Strategies That’ll Leave Your Competitors in the Dust
entries.summary: If you’re still sending the same strategies of last year in 2025, you're leaving money on the table.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you’re still sending the same strategies of last year in 2025, you're leaving money on the table.

The landscape has changed and smart brands are adapting fast.

Let’s get into what’s working _right now_.

## 1. Plain Text > Pretty Designs in Key Parts of Automations

Most brands over-design many of their automated emails. Looks good, performs mid.

Plain-text emails written like a founder message outperform every time in key flows.

They're direct, personal, and actually get read.

**Execution:**

- Welcome Flow: Email 3 should be a plain-text message that crushes objections.

- Browse Abandon: One-liner from the founder with a product link.

- Cart Abandon: Soft-check-in message with social proof, sent like it’s from a real person.

These outperform design-heavy templates in conversions—especially at the decision point.

Example:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/69d0d69e-a967-4c30-b82a-5f64136498c8/Screenshot-2025-05-01-at-7.53.48-AM.png?t=1748525366)

Text Based Automated Email

### 2. Redesign Pop-Ups to Trigger Micro-Commitments or Quizzes

Pop-ups with 10% off asking straight for the email don’t cut it anymore.

The customer is bored of that and they need more interaction.

Multi-step pop-ups with a micro-commitment crush them.

Here’s how to structure it:

- Step 1: Ask a low-friction question.

- Step 2: Then ask for email/phone.

- Optional: Tailor follow-ups based on answers.

This approach introduces commitment bias. Once someone clicks step one, they’re more likely to finish. Conversion rates double.

Old format: 4–6% submission
New format: 11–12.5% submission

Simple “Yes/No” pop-ups also outperform direct form requests.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/6a3b2e34-984d-4e98-8c31-1106b1fd19fd/Screenshot-2024-04-22-at-2.32.16-PM__1_.png?t=1748525447)

Step 1 Example

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a9f9ce8a-3abf-4cb9-b51e-d377170ad758/Screenshot-2024-04-22-at-2.32.24-PM__1_.png?t=1748525463)

Step 2 Example

### 3. Run 3 Non-Discount Campaigns Weekly

Campaigns need consistency. Most brands either don’t send enough or only send sales.

3x/week, send short-form value-based emails. No discounts. No fluff. One point per email.

Email types that work:

- Single benefit

- Product feature

- FAQ

- How to use

- Us vs. Them

- Myths vs. Facts

- Testimonials

- Customer results

Each email builds familiarity and familiarity builds trust and trust drives sales.

It may seem like a lot to send this many emails but trust me… it’s not.

Top brands like Dr. Squatch, Alo, Lulu Lemon, etc all send 7 emails per week.

Look at the engagement we receive below on one of our brands we send 3-4x per week for…

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/08eb6684-bff0-4f5b-b411-0b8e467fb023/Screenshot_2025-05-29_at_6.32.49_AM.png?t=1748525576)

Results Sending 3x-4x Per Week

Most of the market still operates on outdated tactics. These three things done consistently will generate more cash, more trust, and more leverage:

- Text-based founder-style emails in key flows.

- Micro-commitment pop-ups.

- Value-first campaign cadence at 3x/week.

Watch me explain these tactics in depth: _**[https://youtu.be/9_C3AW41T8k?si=ZjtnLKwilNsjVPLY](https://youtu.be/9_C3AW41T8k?si=ZjtnLKwilNsjVPLY&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=3-modern-email-strategies-that-ll-leave-your-competitors-in-the-dust)**_

entries.title: Why Reinventing the Wheel is Overrated
entries.summary: - The simplest path to success is choosing a proven market with clear demand.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s kill a popular myth.

You don’t need to be original to be successful.

You just need to be better than the guy next to you.

**Key Takeaways:**

- The simplest path to success is choosing a proven market with clear demand.

- “Saturation” is a green light, not a red flag. It means people want what’s being sold.

- Originality isn’t required to win… execution is.

- Outperforming others in a common niche often leads to more sustainable growth than launching a “new thing.”

### Stop Chasing "Blue Ocean" Myths

Every entrepreneur has flirted with the idea of “blue ocean” strategy.

You want to invent something no one's ever seen. Launch the next Uber for X.

However… 99% of the time, this path ends in a graveyard of "great ideas" that nobody wanted.

The world doesn’t have a good idea shortage… **it has an execution shortage.**

### Saturation = Validation

If you see 1,000 people doing the same thing… email marketing, fitness coaching, coffee brands… don’t run.

That’s your sign it works.

There’s proven demand. There’s existing buyer psychology. There are playbooks, case studies, best practices you can follow.

This is the good stuff.

Saturation isn’t not an enemy, it’s a shortcut!!

### The Simpler Path to Success

Every basic business or service you can think of: plumbing, copywriting, lawn care, email marketing, already has a roadmap.

You don’t need to guess to start and grow.

You just have to out-execute the others in the market using the knowledge and roadmaps which are already out there on the internet.

Want to be an email marketer? Good.

The systems are built. The clients are already shopping.

You don’t need to convince them they need email. You just need to show why they should choose you over the next guy.

### Why This Works Better

When you choose a high-demand niche, here’s what happens:

- **You speed up learning.** There are mentors, guides, and success stories to model.

- **You reduce risk.** You’re selling into a proven market.

- **You get better faster.** Competition forces you to up your game

Compare that to inventing a niche… where you have to educate your audience, validate your offer, and build trust from scratch. It’s exhausting and often unprofitable.

### What “Being Better” Actually Means

You don’t need to be a genius.

You just need to:

- Be easier to work with

- Communicate better

- Deliver higher quality work

- Be more responsive

- Make your clients' lives easier

Simple things that _most people skip_.

And yet, these are the levers that separate a freelancer from a six-figure operator.

I’ve been able to go from nothing… to passing the mentors I looked up to over the past 3 years.

Not because I’ve discovered this crazy new AI technology or whatever…

Just because I’ve been better. Better at email marketing, better at finding clients, and better at finding talent.

If you are a 7-9 figure ecom brand and you want more “better” in your life… book a call to work with the top email team in the game right now _**[here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=why-reinventing-the-wheel-is-overrated)**_.

entries.title: How to Create High-Converting Testimonial Emails
entries.summary: Many brands think dropping a few “nice product” reviews into an email = instant sales.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Testimonial emails can CRUSH for you or completely flop.

Many brands think dropping a few “nice product” reviews into an email = instant sales.

Wrong.

If your review email reads like an Amazon listing… you’re losing money.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Testimonial emails are _not_ the place to be boring.

- Use 1-2 _story-driven_ reviews that clearly highlight a transformation.

- Keep your email copy minimal and easy to read—don’t overwhelm.

- Choose reviews that overcome specific objections.

## Why Testimonial Emails Work (When Done Right)

**92% of ecommerce consumers read online reviews and testimonials when considering a purchase.**

**72% of customers trust a business more after reading a positive review.**

**Customers who interact with a positive review are 58% more likely to convert.**

But that doesn’t mean _any_ reviews will work.

It has to tell a story. It has to feel real. And it has to convert.

The best reviews don’t say “great product.”

They say: “I tried X, nothing worked, and then I found YOU.”

That’s a customer journey and that’s what sells.

### 1. Choose Testimonials That Sell

Your testimonial should show a clear “before and after.”

Look for reviews that show:

- Pain points the product solved

- Specific outcomes the customer experienced

- Personality or relatability (humor, emotion, etc.)

Bad: “Love this product, fast shipping.”

Better: “I struggled for months with back pain. One week with your posture corrector and I slept through the night.”

### 2. Only Feature 1-3 Reviews

More ≠ better.

If you throw 4-5 reviews in an email, none of them get read.

Focus on ONE powerful review. Two maybe and three max.

Give it space, highlight key lines, and direct the customer toward the buy.

### 3. Short. Simple. Clickable.

Your testimonial email is a teaser, not a landing page.

- Use a strong headline or quote to lead

- Use minimal design. Think image + review + CTA

- Always end with a direct CTA: “See why 4,000+ customers made the switch →”

### 4. Make It About the Customer, Not the Product

The review shouldn’t just say _what_ the product does.

It should show the impact it had on someone’s life.

Every review you pick should remove a fear, doubt, or objection.

### Strong Example

Great testimonial attacking pain points of customers…

Only one review so the customer will actually read it…

Bolded main points in the testominal…

Promoting the product subtly…

Short and sweet!

entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I’m extremely lazy.

I don’t like thinking and trying to come up with the next billion dollar idea.

So… I am relentless with stealing ideas and strategies from other brands.

Why try reinventing the wheel when you can piggyback on what’s already working?

**These seven brands have some of the best email strategies in the game right now** and you’d be crazy not to borrow a few plays from their book.

### 1. Seed – Infographic Education That Sticks

Every Seed email teaches you something… fast. They mix short, clean infographics with bite-sized insights that actually make you _want_ to open the next one.

**Steal This:** Add quick educational visuals to your emails that make readers smarter in 15 seconds or less.

View their email strategy: [https://milled.com/seed](https://milled.com/seed?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=7-ecommerce-brands-you-should-be-stealing-email-ideas-from)

### 2. Dr. Squatch – Dopamine Copywriting

They send ~5 emails per week and still stay fresh because their copy is pure dopamine. Fun, engaging, and always on-brand. Pair that with playful graphics and you’ve got an inbox experience people _want_.

**Steal This:** Write your copy like it’s entertaining content, not a sales pitch.

View their email strategy: [https://milled.com/dr-squatch](https://milled.com/dr-squatch?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=7-ecommerce-brands-you-should-be-stealing-email-ideas-from)

### 3. Brez – Simplicity Meets Founder-Led Voice

Brez’s emails are minimal in design but huge in impact especially their founder-style text emails. These feel personal and high-converting.

**Steal This:** Add plain text-style founder message into your flow and see how it performs.

View their email strategy: [https://milled.com/drinkbrez.com](https://milled.com/drinkbrez.com?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=7-ecommerce-brands-you-should-be-stealing-email-ideas-from)

### 4. Bite – No Discounts, All Value

Bite’s vintage ad aesthetic is refreshing, and they avoid the lazy discount crutch. Their emails sell with story, clarity, and brand authority.

**Steal This:** Run a campaign with zero promos—just a bold POV and a strong CTA.

View their email strategy: [https://milled.com/bitetoothpastebits.com](https://milled.com/bitetoothpastebits.com?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=7-ecommerce-brands-you-should-be-stealing-email-ideas-from)

### 5. Casely – Seasonal Strategy That Sells

This phone case brand knows how to ride the calendar. They send 4x a week and as a “fashion brand” they know that they have to promote different content for the seasons. They do this to perfection.

**Steal This:** Play into the seasons in your calendars and copy / design. Encourage people to buy based on the seasons shifting.

View their email strategy: [https://milled.com/getcasely.com](https://milled.com/getcasely.com?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=7-ecommerce-brands-you-should-be-stealing-email-ideas-from)

### 6. Beis – Minimalism That Converts

Beis doesn’t overcomplicate things. Clean layouts, product-forward focus, and strategic spacing make their emails feel premium and easy to shop.

**Steal This:** Strip your next campaign down to the essentials—1 product, 1 hook, 1 clear CTA.

View their email strategy: [https://milled.com/beistravel](https://milled.com/beistravel?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=7-ecommerce-brands-you-should-be-stealing-email-ideas-from)

### 7. Munk Pack – Clean and Clear CTAs

Their emails aren’t flashy, but they’re effective. Munk Pack keeps designs tidy and puts a bold CTA button right at the top, every time.

**Steal This:** Place your primary CTA _above the fold_ in every campaign. It works.

View their email strategy: [https://milled.com/munk-pack](https://milled.com/munk-pack?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=7-ecommerce-brands-you-should-be-stealing-email-ideas-from)

Don’t copy everything of course, but take the angles that fit your style and start testing.

What brand emails are _you_ stealing from?
