entries.title: Why You're Losing Sales By Not Repeating Yourself Enough
entries.summary: If you think you're annoying your list by repeating yourself, you're probably not saying it enough.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you think you're annoying your list by repeating yourself, you're probably not saying it enough.

People don’t remember what they’re told once.

They remember what they’re told constantly with clarity and conviction.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Repetition is essential. If you're tired of saying it, your customers are just starting to hear it

- You can’t over-communicate your value; only under-communicate.

- Repackage your messages with new angles and designs.

## Humans Forget Fast. That’s the Problem.

Your customer isn’t walking around memorizing your value propositions.

They’re juggling 37 other brands, 5 streaming apps, and whatever the algorithm spat out that day.

Your product might be incredible. Your emails might be stunning. Your offer might slap.
But if someone only hears it once?

It’s gone.

So what’s the solution?

**Drill it in their head. Over and over. And over again.**

### Repetition = Conversion

Sales is about repetition. Not creativity.

Not cleverness. Not “fresh content.”

The best brands win because they don’t try to reinvent the wheel every email. They just keep turning the same wheel faster and better than everyone else.

Think about Apple. You already know what you’re getting:

- It just works.

- Sleek design.

- Ecosystem heaven.

You’ve heard it a million times. And you’re still buying.

### Change the Wrapping, Not the Gift

Here's the play: keep the core message the same. Repackage the delivery.

Design the benefit into a new email format.

One day it's a clean infographic.
Next day it's a raw founder text.
Then it's a social proof story.
Then it’s a side-by-side competitor breakdown.
Then it’s a meme.

But the message is always clear: this is what we offer, this is why it matters, and this is why you should buy.

### You’re Not Repeating Yourself Enough

Feeling like you're saying the same thing too much? Good.

That's when it's starting to land.

The average person sees your brand maybe 1/100th as much as you think they do.
You live it. They don't.

So if it takes 7 touches to convert, and you're only saying the important stuff once… you're leaking revenue.

### Bottom Line

Simplicity scales. Repetition converts.

Drill your 3-5 core benefits like you’re teaching multiplication tables.
You’re not a broken record. You’re a consistent one.

And consistent brands win.

entries.title: How We Scaled Our Agency by Building Pods (And Why It’s the Most Efficient System We’ve Used)
entries.summary: If I had to start Well Copy from scratch today, I'd build it exactly the same way—pod by pod. Here's the exact team structure we use to deliver top-tier results to 60+ ecom brands without chaos, delays, or burnout.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If I had to start Well Copy from scratch today, I'd build it exactly the same way—pod by pod. Here's the exact team structure we use to deliver top-tier results to 60+ ecom brands without chaos, delays, or burnout.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Each pod is a self-sufficient unit managing 5–8 client accounts with precision and speed.

- Senior Account Managers oversee multiple pods to maintain strategy, standards, and scale.

- The Account Manager is the “mini-CEO” of each pod, owning outcomes, direction, and deadlines.

- Specialized roles like the Copywriter, Designer, and Klaviyo Technician allow for world-class execution at scale.

- This structure prevents bottlenecks, increases output, and keeps clients happywithout burnout.

### Why Structure Matters

When you're managing dozens of eCommerce clients—each needing multiple campaigns, flows, optimizations, and tests every single week—the old "everyone-does-everything" model falls apart. Fast.

We used to work that way. And it broke.

Deadlines slipped, quality suffered, and scaling became a nightmare.

So we rebuilt from the ground up with an efficient Pod Model.

### The Pod Breakdown

Each pod manages **5 to 8 clients** and is structured for speed, ownership, and specialization.

**1. Account Manager (AM) – The Pod CEO**
This person is the driver. They are responsible for everything related to the clients in their pod.

They lead the execution, ensure deadlines are met, manage the internal team, and act as the main point of contact for the client.

Their job: Get shit done. No excuses.

**2. Copywriter – The Brand Voice Expert**
Creates all emails, flows, and pop-up copy. They’re trained to write like the client brand not just like us.

They work closely with the AM to ideate angles, test messaging, and match tone. No generic stuff!

**3. Designer – The Visual Creator**
Designs emails that get clicks.
They turn copy into branded email graphics, and that is ALL they do. Just what they’re best at.

Every campaign and flow design is optimized for mobile and conversions.

**4. Klaviyo Technician – The Operator**
They’re the behind-the-scenes builder.

Flows, campaign sends, integrations, conditional splits, etc.

They make sure everything goes live without errors and with perfect timing.

### Senior Account Manager (SAM) – The Strategist & Quality Control

Each SAM oversees **3–4 pods**.

This is a strategic position.

They ensure consistent client strategy, prevent quality dips, and mentor AMs.

They also act as the safety net, stepping in when needed for complex issues or escalations.

Senior AMs are also super important in client relationships. Clients need to have senior person that they feel comfortable reaching out to for any issues or concerns. Are Senior AMs are trained in making sure they know when to reach out to clients if they could be feeling a bit on edge.

### Why This Works

This model prevents burnout by having everybody just focus on what they like and are good at, boosts output, and keeps clients insanely happy.

Every role knows their lane.

Communication flows through one AM, so clients aren’t juggling a 5-person thread.

And as we scale, we just spin up another pod.

How do we spin up another pod? Always being hiring. We have a huge pipeline of talent waiting to rock and roll. We just have to reach out, training them on our systems, and they are good to go.

### Final Thoughts

It took some trial and error, but this structure gives us leverage and lets us scale without sacrificing quality or results.

There are many ways to make this work, this is just what has worked for us.

entries.title: The 3 Design Principles That Turn Emails Into Cash Machines
entries.summary: Just because your emails look good doesn’t mean they’re converting.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

The 3 Design Principles That Turn Emails Into Cash Machines

Most people confuse “beautiful” with “profitable.”

Just because your emails _look_ good doesn’t mean they’re converting.

Let’s fix that.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Great design doesn’t just look good, it drives clicks.

- Ease of click and skimmability is everything — if it takes longer than 5 seconds to understand your email, you’ve lost.

- Infographics outperform blocks of copy every time.

## How to Create Email Designs That Actually Convert

Design is not just decoration. It’s persuasion.

And when it comes to ecommerce emails, every pixel should have one job: **Drive action.**

The goal isn’t to win a design award.

The goal is to make your reader stop scrolling, pay attention, and _click_.

So before you obsess over colors and fonts, make sure your design nails these **3 high-converting principles:**

### 1. Ease of Click

We live in the scroll era. People are flying through their inbox like zombies on autopilot.

You’ve got 2 seconds to grab their finger and guide it to a click.

Here’s how:

- Place a CTA button **above the fold** — don’t make them search.

- Use **large, tappable buttons** (especially on mobile).

- Write **clear, benefit-driven CTAs** like “Get My 10% Off” or “See What’s New.”

This isn’t about being polite. It’s about being _easy_. If your reader has to think… you’ve already lost.

### 2. Skimmability

Let’s be honest: Nobody is reading your email like a novel. They’re skimming.

3-5 seconds. That’s all you get.

So make it count:

- Use **bold headlines** and **short blurbs**.

- Avoid giant paragraphs that make your reader's eyes glaze over.

- Design your emails in Figma and keep your visual hierarchy tight.

You can reference the email comparisons in the “minimal copy” slide from our design swipe file — one bloated with text vs. one that’s clean and punchy.

TL;DR: The less you say, the more they absorb.

### 3. Infographics > Paragraphs

Infographics are your cheat code.

If you’re still stacking blocks of copy and praying someone reads… stop.

Start using:

- **Checklists** that spell out value

- **Icons** that communicate fast

- **Comparison graphics** that show “you vs. them”

These visuals reduce cognitive load and increase clarity. They’re also way more engaging than a wall of text.

Design tip: If your email doesn’t make sense in 3 seconds, it’s too complicated.

### Tying It All Together

This email is a great example of all 3 principles.

Ease of Click: There is a button above the fold and large buttons throughout the email that are clear to see.

Skimmability: There’s minimal copy, just short blurbs and clear hierarchy making the email easy to briefly look at and understand.

Infographics: The table in the middle is a perfect infographic. Short, punchy, value packed, and easy to read!

entries.title: Klaviyo's New Billing Settings
entries.summary: And if you’re not paying attention, you could see a huge jump in your invoice without sending a single extra email.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Klaviyo recently made a major change to how they bill users.

And if you’re not paying attention, you could see a huge jump in your invoice without sending a single extra email.

Let’s break down what’s happening and exactly what to do about it.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Klaviyo now charges for _all_ active profiles in your account, not just those you email.

- Unsuppressing a profile locks it in for 90 days. You can’t suppress it again during that time.

- Plan upgrades happen automatically if your active profile count exceeds your plan.

- Downgrades are manual unless you enable the new auto-downgrade setting.

### 1. You Now Pay for _All_ Active Profiles

**Before:** You only paid for profiles you emailed on a given month.

**Now:** You’re charged for every active profile in your account, whether they’re emailed or not.

If you’ve got 88,000 active profiles and only email 40,000 of them, you're still paying for all 88,000.

**What to do:** Start suppressing unengaged users aggressively before each billing cycle.

### 2. The 90-Day Suppression Lock

Once you unsuppress a profile, you can’t suppress them again for 90 days (meaning you have to pay for them for 3 billing periods).

This affects brands who bring old subscribers back for short-term promos or sales. If you re-engage them, you’re now stuck paying for them for three months.

**What to do:** Be _extremely_ selective when unsuppressing users—especially right before Black Friday or major campaigns.

### 3. Automatic Upgrades Without Warning

If your active profile count exceeds your plan limit, Klaviyo will bump you up to the next plan tier automatically. There’s no opt-out.

Your list can grow just a bit and trigger a major increase.

**What to do:** Monitor your active list count closely, especially if you’re in growth season or running lead gen promos.

### 4. Optional Auto-Downgrade

There is now an auto-downgrade feature, but it’s off by default.

You get to choose if you want auto-upgrade or auto-downgrade as a feature, but you can’t have both.

If your active profile count drops, you’ll only get moved to a lower plan if you turn this setting on yourself.

**What to do:** Go into your billing settings and enable auto-downgrade if you choose to do so. My team and I downgrade our clients plans every month anyways, so we are keeping auto upgrade on.

### Action Plan: Cut Your Costs Before They Spiral

Here’s how to keep your Klaviyo bill in check:

#### Suppress Profiles Before Your Billing Date

You don’t get charged for suppressed profiles. Find your billing date and set a calendar reminder to clean house every month.

#### Suppress These Segments Monthly:

- **Never Engaged:** Received 10+ emails, never opened, clicked, or ordered

- **Bounce Risks:** Hard bounces or marked you as spam

- **Long-Term Inactive:** No email or site activity in 72 weeks And exclude Apple Privacy opens

These segments are just burning your cash by sitting active in your account!

entries.title: How I Built a 7-Figure Email Marketing Agency While Still in School
entries.summary: I just took my college graduation pictures yesterday (I graduate college in 3 weeks).
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

A bit of a different newsletter today.

I just took my college graduation pictures yesterday (I graduate college in 3 weeks).

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/41f9fcc9-6c1c-4bcd-a563-7e6befedfc9e/A165B08C-B3D2-407B-9705-A4C47765C4D9_1_105_c.jpeg?t=1746450843)

Picture from my iPhone

So I’ve been reflecting and wanted to share some of the wins I’ve had in business over the last couple years.

**I want to talk about How I Built a 7-Figure Email Marketing Agency While Still in School**

Balancing 6 college classes, friend drama, finals, and a team of 50+ employees is not for the faint of heart.

I started Well Copy as a side hustle in a dorm room — and now it’s a 7-figure agency generating over $100M in client revenue.

**Here are 7 of the biggest lessons that helped me grow my agency** **_while still being a full-time student_****:**

**1. Win the first 3 hours of your day.**
Nothing moves the business forward more than protecting my mornings. Before I check Slack, email, or respond to anyone, I spend the first three hours doing high-leverage work. UNDISTRACTED. For me, that’s usually content or strategy that brings in new clients. Most people waste their best mental energy reacting to noise — and that kills momentum. I guard that time like my business depends on it. Because it does.

**2. Block your calendar or fall behind.**
You can’t do real work in scattered one-hour gaps between calls. You can’t switch between tasks every 30 minutes and expect to move the needle. I learned to stack my meetings back-to-back and leave large blocks of uninterrupted time for deep work. This changed everything. We all have the same 24 hours in the day… You don’t need more hours, you need fewer interruptions.

**3. Trust your team, or you’ll always be stuck.**
The moment I started trusting my team, things started running without me. When you let go, people step up. They take ownership, make better decisions, and you stop being the bottleneck. Could I do 10% of what someone else does “better” in my eyes? Sure. But that mindset will keep you small forever. Empowering your team is what actually scales a business.

**4. In email marketing, focus on the big levers.**
Most brands overcomplicate email. We don’t. We focus on pop-ups, core flows, and sending 2–4 campaigns per week. That’s it. If you can do those three things well, consistently, you’ll outperform 95% of ecommerce brands. Forget the fluff — master the fundamentals. This has allowed us to stay focused while also generating killer results for our clients.

**5. Always be hiring.**
Even when we’re “not hiring,” I’m hiring. There’s always room for A-players. Some of our best team members came from random DMs or referrals we didn’t plan for. When someone exceptional comes along, we find a way to bring them in. Talent creates opportunity.

**6. Always be laughing**
We run a tight ship, but we laugh a lot. Our Slack is full of memes, inside jokes, and friendly roasting. That energy makes work fun — and when people enjoy working together, they do better work. The culture we’ve built is one of the things I’m most proud of. We get results, but we also genuinely enjoy the ride. A lot of our team members come from other agencies and they say working there vs here is night and day. At other agencies, they show up to their computer, grind all day, and barely crack a smile. With us, it’s the opposite.

**7. Stay humble.**
It’s easy to let success go to your head, especially when you’re doing something somewhat unique while a lot of people around you are still trying to figure out what they want to do with their future. I’ve had to remind myself constantly: in the grand scheme, I’m still a nobody. There’s always someone better, smarter, further along. I try to find those people, spend time with them, and let their presence remind me how far I have to go. That humility keeps me sharp and always pushing rather than getting comfortable.

There’s more I’ve learned, but these are the lessons that changed how I operate — and helped me build something real while still (sometimes) showing up to college classes.

Hope you had fun reading that.

Cheers,

Max

entries.title: The Anatomy of a Winning Non-Discount Email
entries.summary: Most emails try to do too much. And when everything is important… nothing is.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most emails try to do too much. And when everything is important… nothing is.

If you want customers to convert _without offering a discount_, here’s the exact anatomy of the non-discount emails generating $1M+ for top ecommerce brands.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Great emails focus on _one_ clear benefit to avoid confusing the reader.

- Strong design makes action easy — your CTA should appear _before_ the scroll.

- Visuals win over text: use infographics to convert interest into clicks.

- Every scroll should feel seamless, leading naturally to the next section.

- Multiple CTAs reinforce your message without feeling pushy.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4a41c667-5c3b-457a-8b37-f021aa923eb5/Non-Discount.jpg?t=1746017721)

## 1. One Email = One Benefit

Your reader is scanning, not studying. Don’t give them a full pitch deck.

Instead, each email should hammer _one key benefit or feature_ — and nothing more.

No info-dumps. Just one focused message that resonates.

Examples:

- “The cleanest protein on the market — with zero bloating.”

- “Designed to reduce breakouts in 14 days (and it works).”

- “Why our 5-second setup saves 10 minutes every morning.”

Pick one idea. Build everything else around it.

### 2. Hero Section That Stops The Scroll

This is where 90% of your attention should go.

Your hero image and headline should instantly answer: **“What’s in it for me?”**

Make it bold, emotional, and obvious.

Avoid generic headlines like “New Drop” or “Our Latest Collection.”

Instead try:
**“Hydrated Skin, All Day — Without the Grease”**
**“Tired of Back Pain? This Might Be Why…”**

### 3. CTA Above the Fold

If someone doesn’t scroll, can they _still_ click?

Your first CTA button needs to appear within the first screen of the email.

Large, clear, and impossible to miss.

This gives your most eager readers a direct action path _now_.

### 4. Clean Transitions Between Sections

Once you hook them, don’t lose them.

Break your email into clean, digestible sections.

Use simple headers to bridge your story:

- “Here’s how it works…”

- “Why customers are switching”

- “You might be skeptical — that’s fair”

This creates flow and keeps them scrolling effortlessly.

### 5. Use Infographics Instead of Long Copy

You’re not writing a blog post. You’re guiding a buying decision.

Take that dense paragraph explaining your tech… and turn it into an image.
Visual hierarchy matters. Infographics allow readers to absorb info quickly and remember it.

Bonus: They work extremely well on mobile.

### 6. Repeat CTAs Without Being Pushy

Repetition = retention.

Place **multiple large CTAs** throughout the email:

- One above the fold

- One after a key testimonial or benefit

- One near the product section

Make it easy for the reader to click _when they’re ready._

### 7. Finish With a Clear Product Section + CTA

You’ve built the case. Now close the loop.

End with a bold, simplified product display:

- Product name

- Image

- Price (optional)

- Final CTA

Make this section clean and confidence-building.
No clutter. No noise. Just the product and the button.

I’m giving away free email account audits to e-commerce brands above $50k/mo. If you want to find out your opportunities with email marketing, book a call _**[here](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-anatomy-of-a-winning-non-discount-email)**_.

Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

## Everybody Overcomplicates Email Marketing

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e783b026-562e-4b3a-ad5e-c9b964123f87/56amfo.jpg?t=1745846450)

This meme I made is the perfect embodiment of the state of email marketing.

Of all the accounts I review, the one thing that stands out from the winners is that they are **sending more emails.**

The truth is… your email content can be mediocre, but if you have a strong frequency, you will make a lot of money from email.

I review 10+ 7-8 figure brands’ email accounts weekly.

It’s always the ones who are sending multiple emails a week already where I look at the account and I’m like, “Look, you have most of what’s going to be making you money. There are no large levers for us to come in and change your business. Sure, there are some small things. Incremental improvements we can make with strategy and design optimization, but nothing massive.”

And no, they aren’t doing any crazy segmentation or personalization or anything.

They just have an engaged segment of people they send to for EVERY campaign.

Literally. Same segment. Every send. And it works great.

The problem most people have is that **they think email marketing is this big crazy beast you have to tackle.**

They get overwhelmed with all of the noise with AI, hyper segmentation, having the craziest designs, etc.

And that overwhelm prevents them from doing the basics that drive all of the revenue.

By basics I mean:

- High converting pop-up form to grow your list

- Have all core email flows with multiple emails in each flow

- Send emails 3x per week

STOP being overwhelmed.

START focusing on the basics and the tasks that generate 80% of the results.

entries.title: 6 Email Marketing A/B Tests That’ll Instantly Make Your Emails Stronger
entries.summary: If you aren’t constantly testing, you’re leaving huge piles of cash on the table.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you aren’t constantly testing, you’re leaving huge piles of cash on the table.

Today I’m giving you 6 fast and easy A/B tests you can run that could instantly lift your open rates, click rates, and revenue.

Let’s get tactical👇

Key Takeaways

- Testing product prices in emails vs. hiding them can drastically change clicks and sales.

- Send time tests aren't just for fun

- Swapping between graphic, plain text, and "branded" plain text can expose hidden performance gains.

- Mystery discounts sometimes beat clear discounts by making people _curious_ enough to click.

- Lifestyle vs. product imagery triggers different buying emotions — test both.

- Long vs. short form emails reveal how impatient your customer really is.

## 1. Show Product Prices vs. Hide Them

One of the easiest things to test in your emails — _and one that can cause massive swings_ — is whether you display product prices or leave them off.

**Price shown:**

- Reduces "click curiosity" but increases "purchase intent."

- Great for lower-priced, impulse-driven products.

**Price hidden:**

- Boosts click-through rates because people _have_ to click to find out.

- Especially useful for higher AOV products where you want to sell through emotion first.

🔥 **Test It:**
Split your next few campaigns 50/50 — price shown vs. hidden — and measure CTR and sales.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2e2951b7-2062-430c-a7fc-7f35ddf1de10/image__1_.png?t=1745593265)

Crazy Example For a Client (prices shown won)

### 2. Send Time Testing

When you send your emails _matters_ way more than you think.

**Early AM (6–8 AM):**

- Great for "workday planners" who check email with coffee.

**Evening (4–7PM):**

- Perfect for impulse buys when customers are relaxed scrolling.

**Middle of the Day (11 AM–2 PM):**

- Casual lunch-break shoppers.

Every audience is different!

### 3. Graphic vs. Plain Text vs. Branded Plain Text

- **Full Graphic:** Looks gorgeous but sometimes screams "sales email."

- **Plain Text:** Feels personal and real, boosting trust + urgency.

- **Branded Plain Text:** Combo of logos, small branding, but otherwise very "text message" vibes.

🔥 **Test It:**
If your click-through rate is dipping, a simple text-based email might outperform your pretty graphic ones — especially for sale launches.

### 4. Clear Discount vs. Mystery Discount

- **Clear Discount:** “Get 20% off today!” — very straightforward and removes any confusion.

- **Mystery Discount:** “Use this code at checkout for a mystery gift” — taps into curiosity and urgency.

🔥 **Test It:**
Use a mystery discount when you want to increase clicks and browsing. Clear discounts can win when you're closing hard (like the final days of a sale).

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e9cb0116-c8a5-4602-a4fb-ed0987e6da76/Screen_Shot_2025-04-14_at_19.26.04__1_.png?t=1745593430)

Another A/B Test for Client Example Resulting in Higher Clciks and Placed Orders for The Mystery

### 5. Lifestyle Imagery vs. Product Imagery

- **Lifestyle Images:** Show the product _in use_ — taps into aspiration.

- **Product Images:** Straight-up "here’s what you get" — simple, no confusion.

🔥 **Test It:**
If your audience is very brand-driven or fashion-focused, lifestyle usually wins. If they are specs-and-price shoppers (like tech, supplements), product-only often outperforms.

### 6. Long Form vs. Short Form Emails

- **Long Form:** Detailed storytelling, FAQs, founder letters.

- **Short Form:** "Here’s the offer, here’s the link, let’s go."

🔥 **Test It:**
If your list skews younger or highly mobile, shorter will often convert better. Test a "long story" style email against a "few lines + CTA" version and watch how engagement changes.

### Final Tip:

**One test at a time.**
Don't change everything at once or you won't know what caused the change.

Pick 1-2 of these, set up your A/B splits, and optimize based on real data... not gut feelings.

If you want a team proactively testing your emails (10 A/B tests per month) book a call to learn more about our done for you email service [_**HERE »**_](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=newsletter&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-boost-your-email-open-rates-in-60-days-without-burning-your-list&amp%3B_bhlid=57320e9fad662a45511f0b06bd801981c99fd4a8)

entries.title: You’re Leaking $$$ Without These 4 Core Abandonment Flows
entries.summary: If you don’t have these four email flows live, you’re losing money daily. And not just a little. Potentially thousands each month.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you don’t have these four email flows live, you’re losing money daily. And not just a little. Potentially thousands each month.

Most ecom brands are flying half-blind with broken setups and missing opportunities. Let's fix that.

- There are four critical abandonment flows you need: Site, Browse, Cart, and Checkout.

- Each flow should include 3–4 emails to maximize revenue recovery.

- Use dynamic blocks, emotional text-based emails, and delayed discounts strategically.

- AB testing your flows is a must. Timing, subject lines, and format can significantly impact results.

## Why 4 Abandonment Flows Matter

70% of carts in ecommerce are abandoned. Now imagine that's just **one** of the four abandonment types. You also have visitors who:

- Land on your site but bounce (Site Abandonment),

- View a product and leave (Browse Abandonment),

- Add to cart but don’t check out (Cart Abandonment),

- Or start checkout and vanish (Checkout Abandonment).

Each step needs a dedicated recovery system. Set these up in Klaviyo and watch your lost revenue return.

#### Step-By-Step Setup: What You Need

**Metrics in Klaviyo You Must Track:**

- **Active On Site** → Site Abandonment

- **Viewed Product** → Browse Abandonment

- **Added to Cart** → Cart Abandonment

- **Checkout Started** → Checkout Abandonment

Make sure these are firing properly in your Klaviyo metrics. If not, reach out to their support.

#### Cart & Checkout Abandon Flows

**Cart Abandon** is often overlooked. Most brands only run a Checkout flow. But cart abandoners are earlier in the funnel.

**Flow Strategy:**

- **Email 1 (30 min delay):** Show exactly what was left. Use a dynamic block, keep it simple.

- **Email 2 (1 day later):** Personal, text-based email from the founder/team. Emotional tone + social proof.

- **Email 3:** Open with a discount. Include FAQs and testimonials.

- **Email 4:** Final reminder, urgent tone, text-based with support offer.

The same flow structure works for **Checkout Abandon**. You could have the same emails if you want, but I recommend changing them a little bit. Just make sure the trigger is different.

#### Browse Abandon Flow

These users showed interest but didn’t convert. They might need different products or more education.

**Flow Structure:**

- **Email 1 (1 hour later):** Show the product they viewed + other options.

- **Email 2:** Answer common objections and reinforce value.

- **Email 3:** Introduce a discount.

- **Email 4:** Text-based, brand-education, personal close.

#### Site Abandon Flow

These visitors didn’t even click on a product. Low intent? Maybe. But still worth a nudge.

**Flow Structure:**

- **Email 1 (4 hours later):** Encourage browsing, highlight bestsellers.

- **Email 2:** Text-based email from the founder/team. Educate on what makes your brand unique.

#### Bonus: AB Test Everything

Optimize over time with these top 5 tests:

- **Time Delays:** 10 min vs. 30 min vs. 2 hrs

- **Subject Lines + Preview Texts**

- **Text-Based vs. Graphic Emails**

- **Social Proof vs. Info Content**

entries.title: 5 Must-Do Email Marketing Shifts for 2025 (If You Don’t Want to Be Left Behind)
entries.summary: Email marketing has changed more in the past year than it did in the last five.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Email marketing has changed more in the past year than it did in the last five.

If you’re running the same plays you used in 2024, you’re falling behind.

Here’s what’s working _now_ in 2025 and what to shift ASAP.

Key Takeaways:

- Value-first content is now the cost of admission to stay in the inbox.

- Storytelling and personalization are outperforming transactional emails.

- Visuals and infographics are replacing long-winded paragraphs.

- Interactive, engaging pop-ups are the new list-building standard.

- Your email cadence needs to step up—3-4x per week is the new normal.

## 1. Lead With Value or Get Left on Read

In 2024, you could get away with sales-heavy content and shameless “pick me” emails. Not anymore.

Your list is smarter, pickier, and more ruthless with the unsubscribe button.

To keep their attention (and inbox real estate), you’ve got to _give_ before you ask.

Value can look like:

- Education around your niche

- Quick, actionable tips

- Freebies or bonus content

- Behind-the-scenes breakdowns

If your emails feel like a constant sales pitch, you’re getting ghosted.

### 2. Stop Being a Robot… Get Personal

We’re entering the “friend in your inbox” era.

People want real talk, real stories, and real people behind brands.

That means:

- Founders popping into the inbox with a personal message

- Sharing how a product was created

- Telling a relatable customer story

- Adding just a touch of imperfection and personality

Emails that read like a robot wrote them are toast. Realness wins.

### 3. Swap Paragraphs for Pictures

Your list is full of doom scrollers.

Long-form copy is failing unless you break it up with visuals.

What to do instead:

- Use infographics to explain concepts faster

- Drop in charts or product comparisons

- Make sure your emails are **scannable** and easy to digest

Design matters more than ever in 2025. Think in blocks, not essays.

### 4. Revamp Your Pop-Ups

That boring “10% off” pop-up is saturated and dead.

Interactive pop-ups are crushing 2025 because they _engage_ before they ask.

How to upgrade:

- Ask 1 fun or useful question before asking for someone’s email

- Gamify the experience with spin-to-win or quiz-style forms

This boosts opt-in rates and gives you better data from day one.

### 5. Send More

One or two emails a week makes you invisible.

Inbox volume is up, and attention spans are down.

To stay relevant, you need to show up more often _without annoying people_.

Sweet spot: 3-4 emails per week.

That’s how you:

- Stay top of mind

- Build trust faster

- Get more sales without leaning on discounts

As long as you’re providing value (see point #1), higher frequency isn’t spam.

entries.title: How to Use ChatGPT Image Generation to Create Email Marketing Designs
entries.summary: If you’re waiting on your designer to make hero section graphics — you’re wasting time.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you’re waiting on your designer to make hero section graphics — you’re wasting time.

Here’s how to make professional email designs and graphics in 3 minutes flat using ChatGPT.

**Key Takeaways:**

- You don’t need a designer to make great email graphics anymore.

- ChatGPT can write and generate product lifestyle images for you.

- All you need is a plain product photo.

## Step 1: Ask ChatGPT To Create You A Prompt

The quality of your output is determined by the quality of your input.

Good prompt → Good image generated

A lot of people don’t realize you can do this…

But you can ask ChatGPT to give you a prompt for creating a high quality image and it will come up with everything for you.

Simply attach your plain product photo and use this prompt template:

For this product and brand I want you to create me a prompt to then have you create a cool render to use in a welcome email.

Product and Brand: [insert website link]

The image should be 2x3 ratio. The product should be in the bottom 60% of the graphic so that I can include a headline and a button at the top of the email which I will add myself. The prompt should be detailed.

#### Example:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/59097483-68b7-40ae-bd7f-13a915e0bc2b/Screenshot_2025-04-16_at_5.27.17_AM.png?t=1744807116)

### Step 2: Generate the Image Off of That Prompt

Simply copy the prompt that ChatGPT gave you in step 1.

Paste it right back into ChatGPT.

It spits out a clean photo of your product — in context, in use, high quality.

You can go back and forth on any edits that you want.

Example result:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/33e982b2-5231-4745-afab-921e138a4be6/ChatGPT_Image_Apr_13__2025__12_28_56_PM.png?t=1744807227)

### Step 3: Add Your Headline & Button

Take that new image.

Drop it into Canva or Figma.

Add your:

- Headline

- Subheadline

- CTA button

And BOOM… you have a strong hero image for your email design.

Here’s my final example using the graphic for a welcome email:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f3b7e01a-daec-4de6-9057-47c7e0deed54/Frame_324535605.png?t=1744807284)

entries.title: Behind the Screens: How Hydro Flask, Vuori, and Huel Run Email Marketing
entries.summary: Let’s peel back the curtain and break down what email marketing actually looks like behind some of your favorite ecommerce brands…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Ever wonder what the big brands are doing in your inbox?

Let’s peel back the curtain and break down what email marketing _actually_ looks like behind some of your favorite ecommerce brands…

**Key Takeaways:**

- Each brand uses a welcome offer of XX% OFF to get email sign-ups

- Frequency and content style vary depending on brand positioning.

- Vuori leverages visual storytelling while Huel leans into education and trust.

- Sales are minimal for premium-positioned brands like Vuori, yet they still drive conversions.

- High-converting brands don’t overcomplicate, just execute consistently on value and visuals.

## 1. Hydro Flask – Product-Driven, Promo-Friendly

Hydro Flask runs a lean, evergreen strategy. They’re not the most frequent senders but every email has a clear job.

- **Signup Offer**: 15% off when you subscribe. Simple, direct, gives you a reason to get in their ecosystem.

- **Send Frequency**: 3x per week—often spaced out to avoid fatigue.

- **Content Strategy**: Most of their emails are built around seasonal themes (back to school, summer, winter sports).

- Emails highlight product use cases and benefits—hydration, outdoor durability, style.

- **Sales Cadence**: About one sale per month, often targeting a specific collection (e.g., tumblers, lids, or accessories).

**Key Insight**: They rarely offer sitewide sales… just collection specific sales. This keeps their margins high and allows them to not discount their brand.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/e26bbf99-e9e6-43bd-9501-7469343163e8/Screenshot_2025-04-09_at_7.05.44_AM.png?t=1744207552)

March Emails

## 2. Vuori – Visual Storytelling at Its Finest

Vuori plays in the high-end athleisure space and leans _heavily_ into aesthetics.

- **Signup Offer**: 20% off + plus gender selection required, to immediately personalize.

- **Send Frequency**: 5x-6x per week. Yup, you read that right.

- **Content Strategy**: Their emails are minimalist in copy but rich in visuals.

- Often use infographics and high-end photography to let the product speak.

- Emphasis on product drops over promotions.

- Weekly: 2 product launches + 3 value-driven / content or brand vibe emails.

- **Sales?** Basically none. They rarely discount outside of their welcome offer of 20% OFF

**Takeaway**: Vuori proves that you don’t need constant discounts to convert, you just need to look elite and stay top of mind with consistent emails.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/08c0ba1e-d0a0-490a-a0f7-e28ddfa2dfc2/Screenshot_2025-04-09_at_7.08.02_AM.png?t=1744207691)

March 5-27th Emails

### 3. Huel – The Education + Offer Combo

Huel finds a hybrid approach—educational, benefits-driven, and lightly promotional.

- **Signup Offer**: 15% off to join the list.

- **Send Frequency**: 3-4x per week.

- **Content Strategy**: 1x per week “digest” email—this is a recurring email giving value content: nutrition tips, customer stories, behind-the-scenes.

- 1-2x sales emails per month (modest offers, targeted at specific products).

- The rest of their calendar is focused on product benefits, lifestyle integration, and objection handling.

**Takeaway**: They use content to educate and build trust. Sales come secondary but they still run just enough to drive urgency.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/51f2554b-6b3b-4773-973a-ec3e3a6524ca/Screenshot_2025-04-09_at_7.08.42_AM.png?t=1744207731)

March Emails

**Closing Thoughts:**

If you run an ecommerce brand, there’s a lot to steal from these three:

- Offer something on signup. Not just for conversions right off the bat, but to be able to build a relationship to convert on down the line.

- You don’t need to send every day… just at least 3x per week. Whatever you do send, make it consistent.

- Sales aren’t required to make email work. Vuori proves this. Visuals + vibe = conversions.

- Use digest or educational formats (like Huel) to build long-term brand trust.

You don’t need to reinvent the wheel. Just know what lane you’re in and EXECUTE.

entries.title: How to Stay Out of The Spam Folder In 2025
entries.summary: You might be writing amazing emails. But if no one sees them, they won’t drive revenue.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

You might be writing amazing emails. But if no one sees them, they won’t drive revenue.

In 2025, spam filters have gotten savage and 75% of ecommerce brands are unknowingly stuck there. But fixing it isn’t rocket science. You just need to understand how your sender reputation really works.

Let’s break down exactly how to get out of the spam folder.

**Key Takeaways:**

- In 2025, inbox placement is tougher than ever, spam folder is default for most brands.

- Your domain's "credit score" dictates inbox placement, influenced by setup, volume, and engagement.

- Proper technical setup (like DMARC) takes 5 minutes and is critical for deliverability.

- Warming up your domain gradually and sending consistently keeps your email rep healthy.

- List hygiene and sending only to engaged subscribers is the fastest way to recover open rates.

## Step 1: Your Domain Has a Credit Score (And You Probably Don’t Know What It Is)

Inbox providers like Google and Yahoo assign a kind of “credit score” to your domain based on how people interact with your emails.

Open rates, clicks, replies = good credit score → inbox.

No engagement, high bounce/spam complaints = bad credit score → spam folder.

Use [GlockApps](https://glockapps.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-stay-out-of-the-spam-folder-in-2025) to check yours (not a sponsor I just like them). They’ll give you test email addresses, you send a campaign, and they’ll show you exactly where you’re landing (Inbox vs Promotions vs Spam).

**Goal:** You want 75%+ inbox placement.

### Step 2: Set Up Your Technicals (Takes 5 Minutes)

This is _non-negotiable._ Missing this = guaranteed spam.

Make sure the following records are correctly set up:

- SPF

- DKIM

- DMARC

If you're using Klaviyo, this is pretty painless and most of it is automated. You just need to manually add a DMARC record (Klaviyo has an article in this if you look it up).

Once it's done, it's done forever.

### Step 3: Warm Up Your Domain (Even If You’ve Been Sending for Years)

Think of warming up your domain like building trust with inbox providers. You wouldn’t apply for a $100k loan with zero credit history, right?

Same thing here.

If you’re switching domains or have low open rates, treat your list like it’s fresh:

**Example Warm-Up Cadence:**

- Start with 250 contacts.

- Then 250 → 500 → 1000 → 2000

- Send every other day.

- Monitor open rates and only scale when engagement stays strong.

Even with a massive list, you can get to full sends within 1 month.

### Step 4: Send Consistently (Or Pay the Price)

In 2025, going silent for weeks and blasting your full list out of nowhere is a _huge_ red flag.

Set a minimum cadence of 1 email per week, even if it’s just a simple text-based update. This keeps your domain “active” and builds positive sending history over time.

### Step 5: Engagement Is the Kingmaker

Open rates, clicks, and replies tell inbox providers, “Hey, people actually _want_ this.”

Shoot for:

- **50%+ open rates**

- **1%+ click rates**

- **

**Pro tip:** If you’re not hitting those numbers, STOP sending to everyone. Instead, build a 30-day engaged segment (people who opened/clicked in the last 30 days) and only send to them.

Once you’re consistently hitting 50%+ open rates, expand to 60, 90, 120-day segments.

### Bonus: Simple Emails = Higher Engagement

Fancy designs are cool. But inbox providers love engagement, not aesthetics.

Mix in text-based founder emails. Keep buttons clear. Add PS sections. Make it feel personal. It’s not just better for engagement, it builds trust and makes people want to open the next one.

entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

**I guess people actually do buy from emails?**

**I just pulled $200,000/mo out of thin air for this brand.**

**Here's the full, unfiltered breakdown👇**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a58e9423-8c95-4226-9311-1e2a31b290b4/Screenshot-2024-11-11-at-6.59.54-AM.png?t=1731680651)

Before

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c8f40c65-b014-4290-ac5a-5be6f3032bdb/Screenshot-2024-11-11-at-7.00.51-AM.png?t=1731680689)

After

## Context and Background

So this brand had heard around the block that you can make a lot of money with email…

Which for them was underperforming.

They were pulling $20k/mo from email -> 6.27% of total revenue.

No email campaigns.

Landing in the spam folder.

Very low list growth.

Almost no automations.

This got me excited 🤪

They worked with an agency and they struggled to get the right brand voice and design.

They were _very_ skeptical of working with us for this reason, thinking we wouldn’t get their styles down.

So I gave them a 30 day full money back guarantee (spolier alert - they didn’t use it)

We moved forward.

Got to work. And crushed.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/29d97a1f-80ca-4248-807c-3b5cc3b88475/GnnkqGEWUAAByiK.jpeg?t=1743770112)

## The Process For Scaling Their Brand

**Analyze (Days 1-7)**

- Full brand and marketing analyzation

- Thorough Klaviyo audit

- Building automated flow email lifecycle strategy with 40-60 emails

- Build a segmentation and deliverability plan

- Construct the campaign calendar equipped with 3-4 email campaigns per week

**Create (Days 7-45)**

- Building new subscriber acquisition systems and upgrading pop-up forms with initial A/B tests

- Creating all email flows with 40 emails across 8 different triggers

- Write, design. and implement emails following the deliverability protocol and campaign calendar from the Analyze Phase.

**Elevate (Days 45+)**

- Continued Execution with 3-4 email campaigns per week, new flow buildouts, and introducing strategic partners and softwares to add fuel to the email fire

- Ongoing optimization with a minimum of 3 A/B tests live per week across flows, pop-ups, and campaigns.

- Ongoing analyzation and reporting, with in-depth weekly breakdowns and monthly stat deep-dives using our custom-built Klaviyo API reporting software.

## 🔓 Major Unlock #1: List Growth

One of our first action items was to improve the pop-up forms which we're only converting 3.4% of website visitors into subscribers.

If we could improve this rate, we could skyrocket list growth as well as give weary site visitors information over email they need to convert.

Immediately we took this form from **3.4% on mobile to 6.8%**, resulting in a **double in welcome flow revenue to $26.8k.**

We continually are A/B testing our pop-up forms to try to optimize the amount of people joining our emails list.

We've added 39,000 net new engaged email list members.

It's important to note with our content we are keeping unsubscribes as low as possible to retain our list members that we worked so hard to get.

The numbers and boost in subscribers speak for themself.

entries.title: The Best Days and Times to Send Your Emails For Maximum Conversions
entries.summary: You’ve got the perfect subject line, clean design, killer copy.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

You’ve got the perfect subject line, clean design, killer copy.

So why are your emails still underperforming?

It could be because the _when_ is just as important as the _what_.

**Key Takeaways:**

- Midday (11am–2pm) tends to perform best for emails—people are more available and less distracted.

- Early morning inboxes are cluttered and make it harder for your email to stand out.

- Night emails can get high phone opens but low next-day action—bad for conversions.

- Day of the week doesn’t matter as much—test and learn what works for your audience.

- SMS performs best in the evening when people are relaxing and ready to take action fast.

## Why Midday Emails Win

There’s a reason the 11am–2pm window is the gold standard for email sends.

This is when people have settled into their day, cleared the morning rush, and are more likely to check in on their inbox, especially during lunch breaks.

You catch them when they’re not overwhelmed, not distracted, and still have time in the day to take action.

We’ve run enough sends across brands to see that mid-day tends to get the best engagement (and more importantly, conversions).

### The Problem with Morning Sends

Most people wake up to an avalanche of emails. If yours isn’t top 3 in their inbox, it’s probably getting archived or buried by 9am.

Even if open rates seem decent, morning sends often have lower click and conversion rates because people are in hustle mode with work, not shopping mode.

### Late Night Sends: Not Enough Time

At night, people are scrolling on their phones. Maybe, you’ll get opens. But what happens after that?

They read, they think “oh I’ll check this out later,” and then… they don’t. The next morning your email’s already old news, pushed down by 50 other unread messages.

So even if open rates spike, the follow-through usually doesn’t.

Also, if you send an email at 6pm you only have 3-4 hours for people to potentially open that email before going to bed (people rarely look at marketing emails the next day).

If you send at 12pm you have 9-10 hours for people to check their email and see your message.

### Day of the Week? Less Important Than You Think

We get asked this a lot: _What’s the best day to send?_

Truth is, it barely matters. Send Monday, Tuesday, or Friday. There’s no silver bullet.

What matters more is your consistency and testing.

You should be sending emails 3-4 times per week, and if you’re sending at that volume the exact says won’t matter all that much.

Every brand has different behavior patterns. Test different days and times, track your numbers, and double down on what works.

### What About SMS Timing?

Now, SMS is a different beast.

Unlike email, which people dip into throughout the day, SMS gets read immediately.

That makes evening the prime time.

People are home, relaxing, phone in hand. T

hat’s when you want to hit them with a quick, urgent text—especially for flash sales, last-chance reminders, or product drops.

Late afternoon to evening (5pm–8pm) is the SMS sweet spot.

You’ll catch them when they’re most likely to take action _now_.

### Final Thought

Timing won’t save a bad email lol

Focus on content first and making sure customers actually want to see your emails… only then can you worry about timing.

entries.title: ChatGPT 4o Just Changed Creative Production Forever
entries.summary: If you're spending time or money on ad creatives, you need to see this.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you're spending time or money on ad creatives, you need to see this.

ChatGPT’s latest update changes how fast we can produce, iterate, and scale content.

**Key Takeaways:**

- ChatGPT can now generate images with high accuracy and speed.

- You can use it to turn sketches, screenshots, or plain images into polished ad creatives.

- It’s not fully optimized for email marketing yet—but it’s close.

- This will save time, reduce creative costs, and compress production cycles.

### New ChatGPT Update

OpenAI released an image generation update inside ChatGPT.

You can now generate high-quality graphics by describing what you want or uploading a basic reference.

The outputs aren’t conceptual or abstract.

They’re actually good.

You get usable assets in under a minute.

This matters because creative development is a major bottleneck in ecommerce.

Now that bottleneck can be removed.

### Use Cases (with Examples)

There are three immediate use cases worth focusing on:

### A. Reproducing Winning Ad Creatives

You can upload a screenshot of an ad that’s working for another brand.

Ask ChatGPT to replicate the structure using your product and brand.

It returns a similar layout—same lighting, placement, and CTA design—customized to you.

This compresses what used to take hours into seconds.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/53ef7fb9-89fd-42a1-9494-f28bfc03e9ea/Screenshot_2025-03-31_at_6.11.57_AM.png?t=1743426724)

### B. Turning Sketches Into Graphics

You can draw a wireframe or sketch an idea manually or in Figma.

Upload that, and ChatGPT will output a fully designed image.

This removes the need for a designer in the early stages of creative production.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/fc78cdf1-6350-4ad1-a604-9b08d066d1d9/Screenshot_2025-03-31_at_6.09.47_AM.png?t=1743426597)

### C. Plain Photos Into Enhanced Imagery

Take a standard product photo or UGC image.

Feed it to ChatGPT with a simple prompt with basic directions to add life to it, a background, use case, etc

It will create you professional outputs that don’t look like AI.

This is a game changer for brands that are asset-rich but lack in-house editing resources.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/7eb60e92-d440-4c88-a57a-33cc70f5eda8/Screenshot_2025-03-31_at_6.10.49_AM.png?t=1743426693)

It’s not ready to replace your email designer.

entries.title: The Site Abandon Flow - Abandonment Email Flow That Recovers Lost Revenue
entries.summary: It’s literally a two-email sequence… and yet most don’t even have one.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let me hit you with a quick stat:

75% of brands I audit are missing a Site Abandon Flow.

It’s _literally_ a two-email sequence… and yet most don’t even have one.

This thing prints free money on autopilot, so let’s fix that today.

**Key Takeaways:**

- 75% of brands I audit are missing a Site Abandon Flow altogether.

- This flow fires when someone is active on your website but they don’t view any products

- The first email should be a reminder packed with products, sent 4 hours post-visit.

- The second is a plain-text, founder-led message to rebuild the relationship.

- Set it and forget it, this flow will quietly convert curious browsers into buyers.

### What Is a Site Abandon Flow (And Why You Need It)?

Most brands think abandonment email flows only start once someone adds to cart.

Wrong.

Site visitors are _already_ showing interest.

They clicked an ad. They typed in your URL. They poked around.

And then... they dipped.

The Site Abandon Flow is how you nudge those people back.

They’re low-hanging fruit. **You just need to remind them you exist.**

### Email 1: The “Product Buffet” Reminder

**Send time:** 4 hours after the site visit.
**Format:** Image-based, product-forward.
**Goal:** Get them back on the site browsing products.

What this email needs:

- A bold headline: “Still thinking about it?” or “Need help finding the right fit?”

- A hero section with your bestsellers.

- Clear CTAs driving back to category or product pages.

- Optional: a soft “Need help?” line offering support.

Don’t overcomplicate it.

Think of this email like your homepage in email form.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d5cd58f3-495f-46fe-8fcd-a1a0fd2cc0fd/Did_you_find_what_you_were_looking_for__%2B_Customer_support_details.png?t=1742998145)

Example Email #1

### Email 2: The Founder Follow-Up

**Send time:** 24 hours after the first email.
**Format:** Plain-text. Personal. No images.
**Goal:** Build trust. Make the brand feel human.

This email should come _from the founder_. Not “The [Brand Name] Team.”

Literally send it from the founder’s name and write it like you’re talking to one person.

What it needs:

- A warm intro (“Hey, it’s [Founder’s Name]—I saw you stopped by…”)

- A 2-3 sentence brand story or value prop (“We started this brand because…”)

- A friendly CTA (“If you need help picking something out, just hit reply”)

- A PS that recommends a favorite product or shares a customer review.

This isn’t about closing the sale immediately. It’s about re-opening the door.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d91dcdd4-7ca4-4dc6-ba1a-1267a6704dba/screencapture-mail-google-mail-u-0-2025-03-26-06_42_47-edit.png?t=1742998172)

Example Email #2

### Final Thoughts:

If you’re running a brand doing $50k/month+ and don’t have this in place, you’re leaking money.

Set up this 2-email Site Abandon Flow in Klaviyo today.

It’s quick. It’s low effort. And it’ll boost your bottom line more than you’d think.

entries.title: 100 Non-Discount Email Marketing Campaigns That Generate Actual Sales
entries.summary: Here are 100 non-discount email campaigns that you can send to your email list rather than just blasting a sale to them all.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

You might want to save this post today.

Here are 100 non-discount email campaigns that you can send to your email list rather than just blasting a sale to them all.

# 100 Non-Discount Email Campaign Ideas

## 🧠 Product-Focused (20)

- **One Feature** – Spotlight a standout ingredient or detail.

- **One Benefit** – Emphasize a powerful outcome of using your product.

- **What’s Inside** – Breakdown of what’s included in the box or bundle.

- **How It’s Made** – Share the materials, craftsmanship, or sourcing process.

- **How to Use It** – Instructions, tips, or best practices for success.

- **Why It Works** – The science or logic behind your product.

- **What Makes It Different** – Comparison to industry standards or common products.

- **What It Replaces** – Highlight what your product helps customers stop doing or using.

- **When to Use It** – Situational breakdowns: morning, night, gym, travel, etc.

- **Best Paired With** – Upsell with perfect pairings or complementary products.

- **Who It’s For** – Describe your ideal customer.

- **Who It’s Not For** – A contrarian approach to further qualify leads.

- **Product Spotlight** – Dedicate a whole email to one SKU.

- **Staff Favorite** – Feature an employee’s personal favorite and why.

- **Best-Seller Breakdown** – Deep dive on your top-selling product.

- **Travel-Friendly?** – Is it portable? TSA-approved? Tell them.

- **Child/Pet Safe?** – Answer common family-related product questions.

- **Limited Edition Look** – Highlight a time-sensitive or seasonal product.

- **Reorder Reminder** – Nudge to repurchase (especially consumables).

- **Zero Waste Use** – Share how to use _all_ of a product with no waste.

### 📚 Education & Comparison (20)

- **FAQ Roundup** – Answer top questions from support.

- **Myths vs Facts** – Bust industry misconceptions.

- **Us vs Them** – Brand comparison chart or list.

- **Why Cheaper Isn’t Better** – Quality over price argument.

- **Customer Misconceptions** – Clarify common misunderstandings.

- **How It’s Different Than It Looks** – Break assumptions.

- **You’ve Been Doing It Wrong** – A clever twist to educate.

- **Top 3 Mistakes** – Help customers avoid pitfalls in your niche.

- **Step-by-Step Guide** – Use, assemble, or apply.

- **Upgrade Your Routine** – Show how your product improves daily life.

- **Industry Secrets** – Share insider knowledge or sourcing practices.

- **The Dirty Truth** – Reveal what's wrong with other options.

- **Ingredient Highlight** – Focus on one specific ingredient or material.

- **Label Decoder** – Explain hard-to-understand product specs or certifications.

- **How to Read a Label** – Teach customers how to shop smarter.

- **Break the Rules** – Flip a standard belief in your category.

- **Expert Tip** – A niche trick from a pro or insider.

- **Better for You, Here’s Why** – Educate on long-term benefits.

- **3 Things You Didn’t Know** – Share surprising info about your product.

- **New Research Says...** – Cite studies relevant to your offering.

### 🧍‍♀️ Customer & Social Proof (20)

- **Testimonial Showcase** – Feature a customer quote and result.

- **Top Reviews** – A collage of happy customer feedback.

- **Before & After** – Visual or narrative transformation.

- **1 Customer Deep Dive** – Feature one customer story.

- **Video Review Spotlight** – Link to or embed UGC.

- **Celebrity/Influencer Endorsement** – Subtle flex without bragging.

- **Social Media Roundup** – Feature tagged posts from real users.

- **Fan of the Month** – Reward & showcase a loyal customer.

- **Customer Map** – Show where customers are located worldwide.

- **UGC Gallery** – Send an email just showing lifestyle content.

- **Your #1 Product – According to Reviews** – Backed by the data.

- **Product Rated 4.9 Stars – Here’s Why** – Social proof-driven explanation.

- **95% of Customers Say...** – Share stats from surveys or reviews.

- **Your Voice Matters** – Ask for reviews or feedback.

- **Thank You for 10,000 Customers** – Celebrate milestones.

- **How Customers Use It Differently** – Showcase unique use cases.

- **Customer Poll Results** – Turn survey data into an email.

- **What You Said vs What We Did** – Customer-driven updates or features.

- **Real People. Real Results.** – Compile mini testimonials with headshots.

- **“I Was Skeptical Until…”** – A compelling conversion story.

### 🔎 Brand & Community (20)

- **Note from the Founder** – Vision, gratitude, or a behind-the-scenes look.

- **Why We Exist** – Share your brand mission or problem you solve.

- **Meet the Team** – Spotlight team members with photos or fun facts.

- **Brand Timeline** – From launch to now.

- **Behind the Scenes** – Office, warehouse, or production shots.

- **Our Values** – Let people connect with your ethos.

- **Culture Corner** – What books, music, or vibes power your team.

- **Sustainable Practices** – Share your eco-commitments or efforts.

- **Impact Report** – Show how purchases support bigger causes.

- **What We Believe** – A manifesto-style email.

- **Founder's Favorites** – Product picks + personal story.

- **We’re Hiring** – Let your customers refer great people.

- **Charity Spotlight** – Promote who you support and why.

- **Team Favorites** – What your employees actually use.

- **From Our Family to Yours** – Humanize your brand with warmth.

- **Brand Anniversary** – Celebrate with reflection or a story.

- **Your Stories Inspire Us** – A thank you to the community.

- **BTS of a Product Launch** – Pull the curtain back.

- **Our Packaging Journey** – Sustainability or branding angle.

- **We’re Listening** – Invite feedback on your growth.

### 🎉 Creative & Fun (20)

- **Quiz Time!** – Personality quiz to match products.

- **This or That** – Poll your audience with 2 options.

- **Flashback Friday** – Old logo, product, or founder photo.

- **Trivia Time** – Fun facts about your industry or brand.

- **Sneak Peek** – A teaser of an upcoming product.

- **What’s Coming Next** – New products or updates.

- **Customer Challenge** – Encourage them to use the product daily, etc.

- **Your Daily Routine, Upgraded** – Fun checklist-style layout.

- **Style Guide / Lookbook** – Outfit or usage inspiration.

- **What's in Our Bag?** – Reveal your team’s favorite everyday items.

- **Treat Yourself** – Self-care focused without a discount.

- **Did You Know?** – Surprising trivia about your product or industry.

- **Pet Pics / Kid Pics** – Showcase customers’ pets/kids using your product.

- **Riddle or Puzzle** – Just for fun, tied back to your brand.

- **Weekly Roundup** – Recap blog posts, IG Reels, TikToks, etc.

- **Would You Rather** – Quick fun poll email.

- **You Voted – Here’s the Winner** – Share results of customer voting.

- **Behind the Name** – Explain product or brand name origin.

- **Design Process** – Share the early sketches or mockups.

- **Vision Board** – Show where your brand is headed in the future.

entries.title: April Fools’ Day: The Easiest Campaign You’ll Ever Run
entries.summary: April 1st is one of the best (and easiest) days to drive engagement and sales.
entries.body:
Hey, it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

April 1st is one of the best (and easiest) days to drive engagement and sales.

Most brands ignore it. The smart ones use it to boost clicks, get free virality, and even drive revenue.

### Why April Fools' Day Works for Ecom

- **People expect jokes** – Your audience is primed for fun.

- **Engagement skyrockets** – Even people who don’t normally engage will check it out.

- **You stand out** – While everyone else runs boring campaigns, you get to create a memorable brand moment.

Here are **5 April Fools’ Email Ideas** you can steal and run with.

### 1. “We’re Shutting Down. It’s Over.”

**Subject:** “This is it. We’re done.”

- Fake announcement that your store is closing.

- Let it sit for a few sentences.

- Then: "Just kidding. We’re actually running a 24-hour sale instead."

- Drop a discount code.

This works for one reason—people love drama. They’ll open just to see what’s going on. And once they’re in, you hit them with an offer.

Good April Fools joke.

### 2. “The Most Absurd Product Launch Ever”

**Subject:** “Introducing our most innovative product yet”

- Make up a ridiculous new product. A gold-plated version of your best-seller. A $10,000 subscription box. A product that literally doesn’t exist.

- Describe it like it’s real. Maybe even throw in fake testimonials.

- At the end: “Okay, this one isn’t real. But this deal is.”

- Link to an actual product with a limited-time discount.

Some brands do this as a joke and end up selling the product for real because people buy it as a gag.

### 3. “We’re Charging for Emails Now”

**Subject:** “New Policy: $5 Per Email Open”

- Say you’re switching to a paid subscription model for emails. Every time someone opens, they get billed.

- Let that sink in for a second.

- Then: "Kidding. But here’s something that actually is free—20% off your order today."

- Drop a discount code.

People will open out of sheer confusion. Some will laugh. Some will be annoyed. But all will see your offer.

### 4. “AI Has Taken Over Our Email Marketing”

**Subject:** “Meet our new marketer: AI-9000”

- Announce that you’ve fired your entire marketing team and replaced them with an **AI that makes all decisions** (including refunds).

- Describe how the bot is “learning” but has made a few mistakes—like **accidentally approving every refund request** or **randomly upgrading orders to VIP status for free.**

- At the end: "Alright, maybe we still need humans. But here’s something real—20% off today only."

- Call to action.

This one works because AI is a hot topic, and people already suspect companies are automating everything.

### 5. “The Most Shocking Announcement Yet”

**Subject:** “I can’t believe we’re doing this”

- Build suspense. Make them think something big is happening.

- Drag it out for a few lines.

- Then drop something completely absurd: “Our founder is quitting to become a full-time TikTok dancer” or “We’re replacing all our products with NFTs.”

- Then: "Okay, but here’s something real—[discount or new product drop]."

People love cliffhangers. The longer you keep them reading, the more likely they are to act.

### How to Make This Work for Your Brand

- Keep it simple. The goal is to grab attention and drive clicks. Don’t overthink it.

- Send early in the day. By noon, people are already getting tired of April Fools' jokes.

- Tie it to an offer. The joke gets them in. The discount gets them to buy.

April Fools’ is free money.

A well-executed campaign costs nothing and gets massive engagement. It’s pattern-breaking. It’s unexpected.

And most importantly, it’s **memorable**.

Pick an idea, tweak it for your brand, and send it out.

See what happens.

entries.title: Plain Text vs. Branded Text Emails: Which One Should You Use?
entries.summary: Let’s talk about a common debate in email marketing: Plain text emails vs. Branded text emails.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s talk about a common debate in email marketing: Plain text emails vs. Branded text emails.

Some brands swear by raw, plain text emails. Others can’t imagine sending something without at least a logo and a footer. So, which is better? And more importantly, when should you use each?

Let’s break it down.

#### Key Takeaways:

- **Plain text emails** feel personal and land in the inbox like a message from a friend—great for engagement and storytelling.

- **Branded text emails** maintain simplicity but add branding elements like logos, colors, and structured footers—ideal for credibility and navigation.

- **Plain text emails** typically outperform in open and reply rates due to their personal, no-frills nature.

- **Branded text emails** offer a balance between simplicity and branding, reinforcing brand recognition while keeping the email clean.

- **Use both strategically**—plain text for relationship-building and urgency, branded text for branding and click-through optimization.

### What is a Plain Text Email?

A **plain text email** is just that. pure text. No images, no fancy formatting, no brand logos. It looks like an email you’d send to a friend.

✅ **Pros:**

- Feels **personal and natural**—better for engagement.

- Often **performs better in inbox placement** (less likely to be flagged as promotional).

- Higher **open rates and reply rates**.

- Loads **faster** on all devices (no broken images or formatting issues).

❌ **Cons:**

- Can feel **too plain**—no visual branding or structured design.

- Harder to reinforce brand identity.

👉 **Best Use Cases:**

- Founder emails

- High-touch campaigns (e.g., follow-ups, special announcements)

- Cart abandonment emails (especially the last email in the sequence)

- Referral or partnership outreach

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0c1ed6db-3e9c-4f19-878e-07cfa1486e6a/unnamed__1_.png?t=1742218165)

Text Based Email Example

### What is a Branded Text-Based Email?

A **branded text email** is mostly text but includes key branding elements—like your logo, brand colors, and a footer with navigation links.

✅ **Pros:**

- **Maintains a personal feel** while still reinforcing brand identity.

- **Footer buttons can increase clicks** to key product categories.

- Creates **brand consistency** across all communication.

- **More structured** than plain text emails, making them easier to scan.

❌ **Cons:**

- Slightly **less personal** than raw plain text.

- Needs to be designed carefully, too many elements can reduce impact.

👉 **Best Use Cases:**

- Educational content (guides, blog posts, etc.)

- Sales emails (with category buttons for easy shopping)

- Post-purchase communication

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/72402e20-6d6f-4b7f-b23b-4eac3ce08583/d50c4617364f41e1adcc973f8a954e65ea8d38362ccc4dd3bf9ee0326b31e367.png?t=1742218033)

Branded Text Based Example

### Which One Should You Use?

It’s not an either-or decision. **The best strategy is to use both**, depending on your goal.

🔹 **If you’re trying to build trust and get replies → Plain text emails.**
🔹 **If you want to reinforce your brand and drive clicks → Branded text emails.**
🔹 **If you’re sending a multi-email sequence → Start with branded, follow up with plain text.**

**Example Strategy:**
🔥 First email: **Branded text-based** – introduce the message, include your logo, CTA buttons.
🔥 Follow-up email: **Plain text** – keep it direct, personal, and with a simple ask.

The magic comes in knowing when to use each.

### Final Thought: The Hybrid Approach

Want the best of both worlds? Try a **hybrid**:

- Use a branded header/footer for identity.

- Keep the email body in **plain text style** (no crazy formatting).

- Avoid too many images, one small logo won’t hurt deliverability.

This keeps the email looking **clean, personal, and effective** while still giving people an easy way to navigate back to your site.

Which type of email are you using the most? If you haven’t tested plain text vs. branded text, now’s the time.

entries.title: How to Use a “Mystery” Discount to Drive More Sales
entries.summary: Let’s talk about a fun take on a sale that we have implemented for a few of our partners with great success.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s talk about a fun take on a sale that we have implemented for a few of our partners with great success.

### Key Takeaways

- People love **curiosity**, they’ll add items to their cart just to see what discount they get.

- A **fake** mystery discount works just as well as a real one. The customer thinks it’s random, but it’s not.

- This tactic **increases conversion rates** by making checkout feel like a game.

- You control the margin. Offer 20% off (or whatever discount makes sense), but **frame it as luck-based**.

### Why a “Mystery” Discount Works

Consumers don’t need the best deal. They need a _reason_ to take action.

A static “20% off” offer is forgettable.

A mystery discount revealed at checkout? That gets people clicking.

Here’s the play:

- Offer **one** discount code (e.g., "LUCKY") for **20% off**.

- Tell customers the discount will be **randomly revealed** at checkout.

- They assume the outcome isn’t fixed. They add items to their cart, hoping for the biggest discount.

- At checkout, they see **20% off** and think they got lucky.

Same discount. Different framing. More conversions.

### How to Set It Up

**1. Create the Discount Code**

- Set up a single code like **"LUCKY"** for 20% off in Shopify or Klaviyo.

- Make it **sitewide** or apply it to specific products.

**2. Email + SMS Promotion**

- **Subject line examples:** “Feeling Lucky? Your Discount Will Be Revealed at Checkout”

- “Test Your Luck—Mystery Discount Inside”

- “Your Pot of Gold is Waiting. What Will You Get?”

- **Email body structure:** Explain that customers can “test their luck” and receive a **mystery discount** at checkout.

- Emphasize urgency. The offer is only available **for 24 hours**.

- Call to action: **“Add to Cart and Find Out Your Discount”**

**3. Add On-Site Reinforcement**

- **Homepage banner:** "Your Mystery Discount Awaits—Will You Get 20% Off?"

- **Checkout message:** "Congrats! You got 20% off with code LUCKY."

- **Cart abandonment email:** "You got lucky—your mystery discount is still waiting."

**4. Last-Chance Email**

- Sent **4-6 hours before the sale ends**.

- Subject lines: “Final Shot to Get Lucky”

- “Your Mystery Discount Disappears at Midnight”

- Remind them the deal is expiring and they won’t get another chance.

### Why This Works

This is **just a sales tactic**, but it works because it taps into psychology.

- **Curiosity** → Customers want to see their “random” discount.

- **Commitment Bias** → Once they add items to their cart, they’re more likely to check out.

- **Loss Aversion** → They don’t want to miss out on what _could_ be the best deal.

Most brands run **boring** sales. This gives customers a _reason_ to engage. More clicks, more carts, more sales.

## Example Email

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c4ba0776-3d87-4e14-ba6b-cb192b8b21da/Early_access_for_St._Patricks_Sale.jpg?t=1741974610)

(PS new YouTube video [here](https://youtu.be/tO_raTaO8d4?si=W_H0BwtZ6ILdC5t-&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-to-use-a-mystery-discount-to-drive-more-sales) - If I were to start doing email markeitng in 2025 this is what I’d do)

entries.title: The Espresso Shot Email Flow – A Quick Fix for Lost Sales
entries.summary: Quick newsletter today about an email flow you’ve probably never heard of that can make you quite a bit of cash…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Quick newsletter today about an email flow you’ve probably never heard of that can make you quite a bit of cash…

#### Key Takeaways:

- The Espresso Shot Flow targets people who click an email but don’t buy.

- It waits one hour, then sends a simple, text-based email from the founder.

- A short-term discount pushes them to take action now.

- Great for aggressive brands or those with impulse purchase products.

### The Problem

People click your email, check out your site, and leave without buying.

Most brands do nothing about it.

But there is something you can do to help recover these sales…

### The Solution

It’s called the **Espresso Shot Flow.**

Hit people who click your email but don’t purchase with a one-time offer while they’re the most interested they’ll ever be.

Here’s how it works:

- **Trigger:** Someone clicks an email but doesn’t buy (create a segment for anybody who clicks an email in the last 24 hours and trigger the flow off of someone entering this segment)

- **Wait:** One hour.

- **Send:** A short email offering a discount that expires soon.

### Email Template

**Subject:** Quick Question

Hey [First Name],

I saw you checked us out but didn’t finish your order. I get it—life gets busy, or maybe you weren’t sure if it was the right fit.

If price was the reason, here’s a [X]% off code: **ESPRESSO**. It’s good for the next **3 hours** only. After that, it’s gone.

If you have any questions, just reply to this email. Otherwise, you can grab it now before the deal expires.

[Your Name]
Founder, [Brand Name]

### Why It Works

- **Feels personal** (not a marketing email).

- **Short and direct** (no fluff, just the offer).

- **Creates urgency** (forces a decision).

### How to Improve It

- Test different discount amounts.

- Try different wait times (30 minutes vs. 1 hour).

- Add SMS if email alone doesn’t convert.

### Final Thought

Most brands let potential customers walk away without a fight. Don’t be that brand. Send this email. Get more sales. Simple.
