entries.title: Case Study: How We Took a Clothing Brand From $15k Email Revenue to $75K/Month in 60 Days
entries.summary: Today, I want to walk you through a real client case study. A clothing brand that came to us with almost no email marketing structure. No sign-up form, minimal flows, minimal campaigns.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Today, I want to walk you through a real client case study. A clothing brand that came to us with almost no email marketing structure. No sign-up form, minimal flows, minimal campaigns.

Fast forward 60 days, and email is now driving $75K/month for them.

Let’s break down exactly how we did it.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f7bbd4bc-af88-4502-bdca-095049baf9a1/Screenshot_2025-03-03_at_5.46.14_AM.png?t=1741009580)

## Starting Point: No Foundation, No Strategy

This client signed with us on **January 3rd** with:
❌ No sign-up form.
❌ Minimally structured campaigns or flows.
❌ No real email strategy (random blasts here and there).
❌ An Omnisend setup that wasn’t driving revenue $15k/mo

Essentially, email was an afterthought. And it was leaving tens of thousands on the table.

First step? Move them from Omnisend to Klaviyo and start fresh.

## Phase 1: Migration & Warm-Up

Since they were on Omnisend, we had to completely transition their email operations to Klaviyo (don’t overthink this, Klaviyo is the best so go get signed up with them)

This wasn’t as simple as flipping a switch. Klaviyo uses different IPs and sending domains, so if we just started blasting their full list, we’d tank deliverability and end up in spam.

Here’s what we did instead:

✅ Warm-up process – We started by sending low-volume emails to their most engaged subscribers.
✅ Gradual ramp-up – We slowly increased the volume over the next few weeks while monitoring engagement.
✅ Deliverability optimization – We ensured proper DKIM, SPF, and DMARC settings to establish domain reputation.

After 30 days, we were fully switched over and sending at full volume.

## Phase 2: Building a High-Converting List

### Sign-Up Form: From 0% to 7.3% Opt-In Rate

This brand had no sign-up form on their site. Meaning? They were losing every potential lead that hit their store.

We implemented:
✅ A high-converting pop-up with a strong incentive to capture emails.
✅ A 7.3% opt-in rate—which is above industry benchmarks.
✅ A structured Welcome Flow that immediately nurtured new subscribers into buyers.

Within 30 days, the brand had a grown list of thousands of new engaged potential customers.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/75b5c9c3-d955-4e2e-a83b-0d746557f92b/Screenshot_2025-03-03_at_5.54.00_AM.png?t=1741010047)

New Subscribers | Opt-In Rate | Revenue

## Phase 3: Automated Revenue Generation

At this point, we had clean data, a growing list, and a solid sending reputation. Now, it was time to make money.

### Email Flows: $45K in 30 Days

We built out the core automated flows that every brand needs:

🔥 **Welcome Flow** – Converts new subscribers into buyers immediately.
🔥 **Abandoned Cart & Checkout Flows** – Recovers lost sales on autopilot.
🔥 **Post-Purchase Flow** – Turns first-time buyers into repeat customers.
🔥 **Winback Flow** – Brings back lapsed customers with targeted messaging.
🔥 **Site Abandon Flow** – Engages visitors who left the site before clicking a product.
🔥 **Browse Abandon Flow** – Reminds shoppers about products they viewed but didn’t add to cart.
🔥 **Replenishment Reminder** – Nudges customers to restock products they’ve previously purchased.

These flows alone drove **$45,000 in revenue** last month… **all automated.**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/94432e0c-69a5-495a-8f43-b77be9366537/Screenshot_2025-03-03_at_5.58.57_AM.png?t=1741010344)

## Phase 4: Scaling Campaign Revenue

Beyond automation, we implemented a structured campaign strategy to keep revenue flowing consistently.

✅ 3-4 targeted emails per week (sales, product launches, brand storytelling).
✅ Segmentation to send the right messages to the right people.
✅ Consistent testing & optimization to improve performance.

This brought in an additional $30,000 in revenue last month.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/f942c5b9-1913-4cf5-8b08-060e442edf8a/Screenshot_2025-03-03_at_5.59.38_AM.png?t=1741010385)

## The Final Results: 60 Days Later

- $75K revenue from email in the last 30 days.

- $219K in total store revenue (up 88% from the previous period).

- 7.3% opt-in rate on the sign-up form (from 0%).

- Email is now a core revenue channel, not an afterthought.

## Key Takeaways: What You Can Learn from This

1️⃣ If you’re not leveraging email, you’re leaving money on the table.
2️⃣ A strong sign-up form is non-negotiable. You can’t monetize an email list you don’t have.
3️⃣ Flows do the heavy lifting. Over half of this brand’s email revenue came from automations.
4️⃣ Warm-up is essential. If you’re switching platforms, you need a structured approach to avoid deliverability issues.
5️⃣ Email is a compounding asset. This brand is just getting started, and email will only continue to scale.

entries.title: How to Handle Your Unengaged Email List
entries.summary: Here’s the truth: most of them aren’t coming back. And that’s okay. Let me explain.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I get this question all the time:

**“How do you re-engage inactive subscribers?”**

Here’s the truth: **most of them aren’t coming back.** And that’s okay. Let me explain.

### Subscriber Churn is Inevitable

No one stays interested forever.

It doesn’t matter how great your emails are, **some people will lose interest** and stop opening.

**This is why the real game isn’t about saving lost subscribers. It’s about constantly growing your list so you don’t feel the hit when some churn.**

Instead of stressing over re-engagement, put your energy into bringing in new subscribers. That’s where the ROI is.

### The Harsh Reality of Unengaged Profiles

If someone hasn’t opened an email in **90 to 180 days**, they’re pretty much gone.

Think about it—3 to 6 months of ignoring every email you send**.**

Let’s not sugarcoat it: Re-engaging past subscribers is HARD.

If I send to 50,000 unengaged profiles and manage to bring back only 10,000, that’s a win. But that still means 40,000 are dead weight.

And those 40,000? **They’re dragging your deliverability down.**

### How to Re-Engage Without Hurting Deliverability

I don’t waste time chasing people who don’t care anymore. But I do have a system for low-effort re-engagement that keeps things clean.

#### 1. Only Send to Your Engaged List (95% of the Time)

For most brands, I **only send to people who’ve opened in the last 120 days.**

If you’re outside of that window, you’re not getting emails. No point in tanking deliverability by blasting to people who don’t care.

#### 2. Send One “All List” Email Per Month

Once a month, I open up one send to the entire list, including unengaged profiles.

This is usually for a big sale, product launch, or restock.

Most won’t open. But some will. And that’s enough to re-engage without overcomplicating things.

#### 3. Set Up a Simple Sunset Flow

I also like to have a **one-email sunset flow** for inactive profiles.

Here’s how it works:

- Create a segment for people who’ve **opened at least one email before** but haven’t opened in **180+ days.**

- Send a **simple text-based email**: “Are you still interested?”

- Let them know you miss them but totally understand if they’re no longer interested. Invite them to unsubscribe.

This keeps your list **clean and engaged** without overcomplicating things.

## Send This Re-Engagement Email Today

### Who Should You Send This To?

✅ People who haven’t purchased yet but showed interest.
✅ Subscribers who haven’t engaged with your emails in a while.
✅ Anyone who needs a little extra nudge to take action.

### Why This Works

- **It’s personal** – A direct message from the founder builds trust.

- **It removes pressure** – There’s no hard sell, just an invitation.

- **It revives dormant interest** – A subtle reminder can bring people back.

**Sender Name:** Founder First Name | Brand Name
**Subject Line:** “Hey, quick thought…”

**Body:**

**Hi there,**

It’s [Founder Name], the founder of [Brand Name].

I wanted to personally reach out and say thanks for checking out [Brand Name].

A lot of people come across us because they’re looking for [specific problem your product solves]—and I totally get it. That’s why I started [Brand Name] in the first place. [Brief 1-2 sentence personal story about the brand’s origin or mission.]

If you’re on the fence, no pressure. I just want to share a little about why customers love us:

[Unique Selling Point #1][Unique Selling Point #2][Unique Selling Point #3]

And - I just reactivated your welcome discount for 10% OFF. Just use code **[Discount Code]** at checkout.

Whenever you’re ready, I’d love for you to give us a try. Here’s a link to check out our bestsellers: **[Shop Bestsellers »]**

Thanks for being here—it means a lot.

**[Founder Name]**

**P.S.** If you have any questions or want a recommendation, just hit reply. I actually read these myself.

### The Bottom Line

If you see thousands (or millions) of unengaged profiles in your list, don’t panic.

Just assume they’re gone. Your life will be a lot less stressful.

Spending energy trying to “revive” dead subscribers is a losing battle.

**Focus on list growth, not re-engagement.**

One of my clients has over 2 million unengaged subscribers we don’t send to.

Is it ideal? No. But churn is part of the game.

Grow your list. Send to your engaged audience. Keep it simple.

That’s how you win.

entries.title: You're Overthinking Your Email Marketing
entries.summary: Here’s something nobody tells you about email marketing: you’re overthinking it.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s talk about an interesting topic today…

## Your Customers Are Zombies

Here’s something nobody tells you about email marketing: **you’re overthinking it.**

Every time you sit down to write an email, you’re probably thinking…

- “What new angle should I take?”

- “How do I make this fresh?”

- “What if people recognize this from before?”

None of that matters.

Your audience isn’t keeping track of what you send. They’re on autopilot. They open their inbox, scroll through a flood of messages, and maybe, **maybe**, they stop on yours.

They aren’t studying your subject lines. They aren’t cataloging your messaging.

**And that’s exactly why you should be** **repeating yourself.**

## Repetition Wins. Here’s Why.

- **Your list is always changing.** You’re getting new subscribers every day. A portion of your list wasn’t even there when you sent that killer email three months ago. Why let your best content go to waste?

- **Your best emails will still work.** If an email drove sales, why would it stop working? Consumers don’t change that fast. Their problems don’t change. Their buying behavior doesn’t change. You don’t need to keep reinventing the wheel.

- **People need to hear things multiple times before they take action.** Marketing rule of thumb: people don’t act the first time they see something. Sometimes they need to see it three, five, or even ten times before they pull the trigger. You’re actually leaving money on the table by not repeating your message.

- **Your audience doesn’t remember your last email.** I promise you… nobody is scrolling back through their inbox thinking, “Didn’t they already say this?” They don’t remember. Even if they do, repetition **builds trust.**

- **Brand continuity is good for business.** The biggest brands repeat themselves constantly. Nike doesn’t change its messaging every week. They say the same thing over and over until it’s burned into your brain. You should be doing the same.

### How to Repeat Yourself EFFECTIVELY Without Looking Lazy

Reusing winning content doesn’t mean you have to copy-paste the same email over and over. Here’s how to do it the right way:

**1. Resend High-Performing Emails with a Slight Tweak.**
Change the subject line. Adjust the first sentence. Shift the offer slightly. Keep the core message intact.

**2. Repurpose Your Best Sections.**
If a specific call-to-action worked well, use it again. If a product description converted, don’t touch it. Copy, paste, send.

**3. Create “Variations” of Your Best Emails.**
If you sent an email about “The #1 Mistake People Make When Buying [Product]” and it crushed… guess what? You can send another one called “The Second Biggest Mistake People Make When Buying [Product].”

**4. Rotate Your Best Subject Lines.**
Have a subject line that got high open rates? Change a single word and use it again. Nobody will notice.

**5. Make Repetition Part of Your Strategy.**
The best marketers don’t come up with endless new ideas. They refine and repeat the ones that work. If an email made you money, **schedule it to send again in 90 days.**

### The Takeaway

Stop treating email like a creative writing exercise lol. It’s a sales channel. Your goal isn’t to impress people with originality all the time. It’s to drive revenue.

Winning emails keep winning. Use them.

Your list won’t notice. But your bank account will.

Make your life easier by repeating your winners.

entries.title: How To Improve Your Email Marketing Click Rates
entries.summary: They aren’t the most important KPI, but they are something that can make a difference.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Everybody obsesses about click rates.

They aren’t the most important KPI, but they are something that can make a difference.

Today I want to share the most impactful tips that will improve your click rates,

## Click Rates Don't Always Equal Cash

People love to brag about their email click rates. Like, congrats dude, your emails get clicks, but are you actually making money?

I will be brutally honest here… Click rates aren't as important as you think.

Everyone thinks having high click rates automatically means you're making bank.

Wrong. I have brands making tons of cash with click rates under 0.5%, and other brands come to me struggling with email results while having click rates over 2%.

Bottom line: **It doesn’t matter how many clicks you get if they don’t turn into sales.**

HOWEVER, clicks still help lol.

I just wanted to put that disclaimer that you don’t need to freak out above click rates if your revenue is looking good…

## Top Strategies to Improve Click Rates

### 1. Tighten Your Segments

Stop sending every email to every person on your list. That's how you annoy people. Instead, segment your email lists based on stuff like:

- How recently someone opened your emails

- Products they've checked out before

- People who've bought something versus those who haven't

The more specific your audience, the more likely they'll click and actually buy something.

(Hint: Just use a 60 day engaged list)

### 2. BIGGER, Clearer Buttons

Make your email buttons super obvious and easy to click.

I’m saying stupidly obvious and obnoxiously big.

Stop using fancy fonts and tiny buttons that blend into your design.

Think about your grandma, if she can’t immediately see your button, you're doing it wrong.

Make it stand out and say exactly what you want, like "Buy Now" or "Shop Here."

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/b6cdf7ef-e6a1-4863-a5e6-49a2b5e8b271/Screenshot_2025-02-24_at_6.00.20_AM.png?t=1740405628)

BIG Clear Button Above The Fold

### 3. Put Your Button Above The Fold

Don’t bury your most important button at the bottom of the email.

Most people won't scroll down to find it.

Put your main button at the top (above the fold, meaning visible without scrolling) so they see it immediately.

People are lazy, make it easy for them.

### 4. Every Product Needs Its Own Button

If you show multiple products in an email, don’t just give one general button.

Every product should have its own individual button linking directly to that product's page.

Why? Because if you make your customer click around your site trying to find something, they're probably just gonna give up.

Reduce friction for them and show them obviously that they can click a button and view your product.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/591c86b2-867c-4f2f-91d5-99e90f4dc6b3/Screenshot_2025-02-24_at_6.01.12_AM.png?t=1740405678)

Individual Product Buttons

### 5. Always End with a SHOP ALL Button

Not everyone knows exactly what they want when they open your email.

Always give them an option to check out everything you offer.

Add a general “SHOP ALL” button at the bottom of your emails as a safety net, so even if they don't want what you showed them, they'll still click around and buy something else.

### 6. Category Buttons in Your Footer

Put links to popular categories (like "Best Sellers," "New Arrivals," "Sales") in your email footer.

It’s a sneaky way to get more clicks and sales from people who aren’t interested in the main content of your email but might see something else they like.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/d13e03d4-1615-49ab-b5d5-e4b29a8caa4c/Screenshot_2025-02-24_at_6.04.25_AM.png?t=1740405874)

Footer Buttons

That’s it. Improve your click rates just like that.

If you follow all these best practices and still have low clicks, that’s out of your control.

Nail these, and then optimize your landing pages to improve conversions.

Here’s an email design tutorial if you want to learn more about email design: [Here](https://youtu.be/YzhXs9diyzU?si=0CbI4Sc8verQx8ci&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-to-improve-your-email-marketing-click-rates)

entries.title: How to Use Segmentation to Increase Sales Without Overcomplicating It
entries.summary: Most brands are sending emails to their entire list and wondering why their open rates are low and sales are flat. The brands making real money are segmenting.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most brands are sending emails to their entire list and wondering why their open rates are low and sales are flat. The brands making real money are segmenting.

Segmentation makes sure the right people see the right emails at the right time. But most people either don’t do it at all or they make it way too complicated.

Here’s how to do it right.

### What Segmentation Actually Is (And What It’s Not)

- **A list is static.** It’s just a collection of emails that never changes unless you manually add or remove people.

- **A segment is dynamic.** It updates automatically based on the rules you set.

This means you can create a segment of "people who opened an email in the last 30 days" and it will always stay updated as new people engage (or stop engaging).

### My Segmentation Strategy

Yes, you could segment your list by what color underwear they are wearing this morning and send them custom content based on that.

But that’s a lot of work. You’d have to make a ton of different email variations for minimal lift in revenue.

My default segmentation strategy is to just blast every email to your engaged list.

It saves you time, stress, and keeps your deliverability high.

Then, in your flows you can get more advanced and you can use segments and trigger certain emails based on people who enter certain segments.

In Summary: Don’t go crazy. Just send campaigns to your 90 day engaged list. If you want to get advanced, trigger automated emails to certain segments you set.

### The Only Types of Segments You Need

**Level 1: Basic (Everyone Needs These and They Are All You Really Need)**

- **Engaged vs. Unengaged** – Group people by those who have opened or clicked an email in the last 30, 60, or 90 days.

- **First-Time Buyers vs. Repeat Customers** – Treat new customers differently than your loyal buyers.

**Level 2: Intermediate (Can Be Useful in Flows)**

- **Cart Abandoners** – People who added to cart but didn’t buy.

- **VIP Customers** – Top 5-10% of customers based on purchase frequency or total spend.

- **Product Interest** – People who clicked on an email about a product but didn’t buy.

**Level 3: Advanced (Precision for Hyper Targeted Flows)**

- **Time-Based Segments** – Customers who bought multiple times but haven’t purchased in 6 months.

- **Specific Product Category Buyers** – People who only buy from a certain category (e.g., skincare vs. apparel).

- **Email Flow Engagement** – People who clicked an abandoned cart email but didn’t finish checkout.

That’s it. No need for 25+ different micro-segments.

### Real Segment Examples From Our Clients

**1. VIP Customers**
Criteria:

- Placed **3+ orders** in the last 12 months

- Spent over **$300 lifetime**

- Opened or clicked an email in the last **90 days**

How to use it:

- Give them early access to product drops.

- Send personal thank-you emails from the founder.

- Offer exclusive discounts, but not too often (keep it special).

**2. Cart Abandoners (High Intent Buyers)**
Criteria:

- Added to cart in the last **30 days**

- Did **not** complete checkout

- Opened an email in the last **90 days**

How to use it:

- Send an extra email to them with urgency or a flash sale

### What NOT to Do With Segmentation

- **Don’t overcomplicate it.** Trying to segment people by their favorite color or shoe size is a waste of time.

- **Don’t create segments that are too small.** A 500-person segment won’t make an impact. Focus on meaningful groups.

- **Don’t rely on segmentation alone.** Your emails still need to be good. No segment can save bad content.

### The Bottom Line

Segmentation works. It increases open rates, improves deliverability, and makes your email marketing more profitable.

But most people either don’t do it or they go too far.

Start simple. Use the high-impact segments above. Focus on **behavior that leads to purchases**, not vanity metrics.

Just fire up a 90 day engaged list and you're set!

If you want more info on segmentation [here’s a full guide](https://gamma.app/docs/Segmentation-101-kvmvgkb79i03tf4?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-use-segmentation-to-increase-sales-without-overcomplicating-it).

entries.title: Klaviyo's New Billing Changes – What You Need to Know & How to Save Money
entries.summary: Today, we need to talk about something that will impact every Klaviyo user starting TOMORROW February 18, 2025.
entries.body:
Hey, it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Today, we need to talk about something that will impact every Klaviyo user starting TOMORROW February 18, 2025.

Klaviyo just announced a major shift in how they bill users. And if you’re not careful, you could see your costs skyrocket.

But don’t worry, I’ll break it down for you and give you actionable steps to keep your costs low.

### 🚀 The Big Change: Billing Based on Active Profiles

#### Before:

You were only billed for the profiles you actively emailed. For example, if you had 88k active profiles but only emailed 40k, you’d only be charged for 40k.

#### Now:

You will be billed for ALL active profiles in your account, even if you never email them. That means if you have 88k active profiles, you're paying for all 88k.

👉 **Takeaway**: This change means your bill could increase significantly overnight if you’re not proactively managing your list.

### 🚨 90-Day Unsuppressed Profile Jail

Klaviyo is also introducing a strict suppression rule:

- Once you unsuppress a profile, you cannot suppress it again for 90 days.

- If you reactivate an old customer for a seasonal promo, you must keep them active for 3 months.

- This makes list cleaning and suppression strategy necessary

👉 Takeaway: Be very strategic when unsuppressing profiles, especially before big sales events becuase you won’t be able to suppress them for 90 days,

### ⚠️ Automatic Plan Upgrades (No Option to Decline)

- If your active profiles exceed your plan limit, Klaviyo will automatically upgrade your plan at the start of the billing cycle.

- No option to opt out.

👉 **Takeaway**: If your list unexpectedly grows, your bill could jump without warning. This makes list maintenance crucial.

### ✅ Auto-Downgrade Option (But You Have to Enable It)

- Klaviyo is introducing an auto-downgrade feature, but it’s not enabled by default.

- If your profile count drops below your plan’s threshold, you’ll only be downgraded if you turn this feature on.

👉 **Action Item**: Go to Billing Preferences and enable auto-downgrade ASAP to ensure you don’t overpay.

### 📉 First-Month Billing Increase Cap

- To soften the impact, Klaviyo is capping the first month’s upgrade increase at 25%.

- But if your profile count remains high, expect more upgrades in future months.

👉 **Takeaway**: This doesn’t mean your bill won’t go up—just that the increase is phased in. If your list is bloated, you need to act now.

## 🛠️ Action Steps to Save on Klaviyo Costs

To prevent unnecessary billing increases, follow these proven cost-saving strategies:

### 1️⃣ Enable Auto-Downgrade

- Head to Billing Preferences and turn on auto-downgrade so you move to a lower plan when eligible.

### 2️⃣ Schedule Recurring Profile Suppression

- You are NOT billed on suppressed profiles, so set up a routine suppression task before each billing cycle.

- Find your billing date in Klaviyo and clean up your list right before that date every month.

### 3️⃣ Suppress These Segments Every 30 Days

Use the following Klaviyo segments to clean your list before your billing cycle:

#### Never Active Profiles (These are dead weight)

- Person has received 20+ emails over all time

- Never opened an email

- Never clicked an email

- Never placed an order

- Can receive email marketing

#### Bounces to Suppress

- Person has bounced at least once over all time

- Bounce type = Hard Bounce

#### Marked as Spam

- Person has Marked Email as Spam at least once over all time

#### Long Term Inactive

- Person can receive email marketing

- Profile Created is at least 180 days old

- Has Received Email at least once in the last 72 weeks

- Has Opened Email zero times in the last 72 weeks _(Excludes Apple Privacy Opened emails)_

- Has Clicked Email zero times in the last 72 weeks

- Has Been Active on Site zero times in the last 72 weeks

- Has Viewed Product zero times in the last 72 weeks

- Has Started Checkout zero times in the last 72 weeks

- Has Placed Order zero times in the last 72 weeks

👉 Takeaway: Keeping your list lean and engaged is now more important than ever to avoid overpaying.

## Need help taking care of all this?

My completely done for you will fully manage your email marketing channel and take care of all list optimization needed.

Only for ecom brands above $50k/mo.

**[Book a call here »](https://calendly.com/maxwellcopy/discovery-meeting?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=klaviyo-s-new-billing-changes-what-you-need-to-know-how-to-save-money)**

entries.title: 6 Founder-Led Emails You Should Be Sending Right Now
entries.summary: Here’s 6 types of founder-led emails that actually work—with real examples you can copy.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most brands send generic, lifeless emails.

They get ignored.

Founder-led emails? Different story.

They feel personal. They stand out. They convert.

Here’s **6 types of founder-led emails** that actually work—with real examples you can copy.

## 1. The "Our Story" Email (_Example: Munk Pack_)

📌 **Best for:** Building brand trust, making people care

People don’t buy products. They buy into _people._ The story behind the brand matters.

Munk Pack’s email nails it:

- **Founder speaks directly** to the audience. Feels like a personal letter.

- **Tells a short, clear brand story.** No fluff. Just how and why they started.

- **Subtly ties it into the product.** No hard sell, just connection.

### How You Use This:

- Keep it **first-person** and direct (_“I started this brand because…”_).

- Be **short and to the point.** No one cares about your childhood dreams.

- End with a **soft CTA** (_Check us out. See what we’re about._)

👉 **Pro tip:** This works great as an early email in a welcome sequence.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/22422f78-ea69-45c2-b098-d15821181b26/screencapture-reallygoodemails-emails-a-note-from-our-founders-munk-pack-2025-02-14-12_09_59-edit.png?t=1739564179)

Example

## 2. The "Exclusive Offer & Info" Email (_Example: Brez_)

📌 **Best for:** Making people feel _special_ and driving action

Most brands send promo emails like:
👉 “Hey! Here’s a sale. Buy now!” (boring)

What Brez does:

- **Makes it feel exclusive.** _Not just a sale—this is something special._

- **Personalized from the founder.** Feels like a direct message.

- **Adds brand updates.** Not just pushing products, but keeping customers in the loop.

### How You Use This:

- Call it **"Founder’s Special"** instead of "Sale."

- Write it like you’re talking to a **VIP insider.**

- Stack value. Not just a discount—what else are they getting?

👉 **Pro tip:** Run these quarterly. Build hype before you launch them.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/630ee872-2fc3-4df1-9f93-d300da39658d/screencapture-milled-drinkbrez-com-sharing-the-love-big-news-inside-F4dXPPHNwg7mfV5i-2025-02-14-12_07_07-edit.png?t=1739564175)

Example

## 3. The "Holiday-Themed" Email (_Example: Wander & Ivy_)

📌 **Best for:** Tapping into emotions and seasonal buying patterns

Most holiday emails = generic discount spam.

What Wander & Ivy does:

- **Founder adds personal touch.** It’s not just “Valentine’s Day Sale” — it’s a _story._

- **Emotionally driven.** Connects product to a meaningful experience.

- **Tied to a specific moment.** Uses urgency without being pushy.

### How You Use This:

- Tie your product to **a feeling or tradition.**

- Speak **as the founder.** How does this holiday relate to _your_ brand?

- Don’t just push a sale. Create a **story worth reading.**

👉 **Pro tip:** Plan ahead so you’re not scrambling.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/121b56b9-9e1a-4f1e-98ca-388ce85fde5d/screencapture-milled-wanderandivy-com-valentine-from-dana-WrF8-SJw4LWJ15lE-2025-02-14-12_06_36-edit.png?t=1739564175)

Example

## 4. The "Tips & Giving Value" Email (_Example: JoyMode_)

📌 **Best for:** Positioning yourself as an expert & building trust

Most brands just sell. Big mistake. People don’t want _more products_—they want _better outcomes._

What JoyMode does:

- **Shares practical tips.** No selling—just useful, relevant advice.

- **Positions the brand as the expert.** Builds authority.

- **Naturally leads to the product.** The product is a tool, not the focus.

### How You Use This:

- Think: _What’s a problem my customer has? Solve it for them._

- Make it **simple, actionable, and quick to read.**

- Soft CTA: _“If you want an easier way to do this, check this out.”_

👉 **Pro tip:** The more **value you give for free, the easier the sale later.**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/311363d5-4c60-4fc5-8940-4d8222ae4409/screencapture-milled-usejoymode-com-a-valentines-she-wont-forget-F72mMwxvEMNUQl95-2025-02-14-12_07_34-edit.png?t=1739564175)

## 5. The "Item Abandonment" Email (_Example: Proof_)

📌 **Best for:** Recovering lost sales without being annoying

Most brands’ abandonment emails = “You left this in your cart.” (lame)

What Proof does:

- **Founder-led = more personal.** Not an automated bot—it’s _you_ following up.

- **Assumes good intent.** “Maybe you got distracted” → not pushy.

- **Adds an incentive, but only if necessary.** Don’t give away margin too soon.

### How You Use This:

- Keep it **casual and human.** _“Noticed you checked this out—any questions?”_

- Don’t assume they need a discount. Just **remind & reinforce value.**

- Only offer a **discount on the 2nd or 3rd follow-up.**

👉 **Pro tip:** Send this **within 1 hour after the abandonment.**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/76403c2d-0410-415e-bd70-686945ec0125/screencapture-mail-google-mail-u-0-2025-02-14-12_09_23-edit.png?t=1739564175)

Example

## 6. The "Welcome Email" (_Example: Cocunat_)

📌 **Best for:** First impressions & setting expectations

Most brands waste their welcome email. They either:

- Go straight into selling (_bad_), or

- Say something bland like “Thanks for subscribing!” (_also bad_).

What Cocunat does:

- **Introduces the brand like a real person.** Feels like a direct welcome.

- **Gives them a reason to care.** Why should they stick around?

- **Sets expectations.** “Here’s what you’ll get from us.”

### How You Use This:

- Open with **"Hey, I’m [founder’s name]. Here’s why I started this."**

- Make it **about them, not just you.** Why should they care?

- End with **a small CTA.** (Example: “Check out our bestsellers.”)

👉 **Pro tip:** Your **first email sets the tone.** Make it count.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/70dc5ea7-a8aa-42b8-868f-de6ddad7f006/image.jpg?t=1739564184)

Example

entries.title: Planning Email Marketing Calendars That Convert
entries.summary: The actual strategy and topics behind your emails are, in my opinion, more important than the actual emails themselves.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s start planning our email marketing for March!

## Campaign Calendar Planning

The actual strategy and topics behind your emails are, in my opinion, more important than the actual emails themselves.

A wise man once said, “you can’t polish a turd”…

Translation: You can’t make money on an email if it’s a topic your list doesn’t care about.

Spend time finding topics you know your list will find engaging!

Below I’m going to attach a **mock calendar I have created for Hydroflask for March** so you can see what kind of topics and strategies I run.

I always recommend 3-4 email campaigns per week focused on giving value and engagement to the email list.

Let me show you what I mean…

## March Email Marketing Calendar (4 Emails/Week + Spring Sale)

#### Week 1:

✅ **March 3 - "Hydration That Lasts All Day"**
📩 _Showcase TempShield® insulation with real-life scenarios (hiking, working, commuting)._

✅ **March 5 - "The Science Behind Hydro Flask"**
📩 _Educate customers on the technology that keeps drinks cold for 24 hours and hot for 12._

✅ **March 7 - "Meet Our Community: Real Hydro Flask Stories"**
📩 _Feature user-generated content and testimonials from adventurers & athletes._

✅ **March 9 - "Spring is Calling: Get Ready for Outdoor Adventures"**
📩 _Position Hydro Flask as the perfect companion for spring hikes, picnics, and workouts._

#### Week 2:

✅ **March 11 - "Sip Sustainably: Our Commitment to the Planet"**
📩 _Highlight the Parks for All initiative and eco-friendly aspects of Hydro Flask._

✅ **March 13 - "Your Perfect Adventure Companion"**
📩 _Help customers choose the right bottle size/style based on their lifestyle._

✅ **March 15 - "Behind the Bottle: How We Design for Durability"**
📩 _Showcase the craftsmanship and durability of Hydro Flask with a behind-the-scenes look._

✅ **March 17 - "Spring Sale is Coming... Get Ready!"**
📩 _Tease the upcoming sale and build excitement._

### 🌸 Spring Sale (March 18-22)

🎉 _5 Days Only: Exclusive Spring Sale on Hydro Flask!_
_Each email keeps urgency high while maintaining brand value._

✅ **March 18 - "Spring Sale Starts NOW: Upgrade Your Hydration"**

entries.title: The Biggest Lie in Email Marketing (That’s Costing You Sales)
entries.summary: They think they need long, detailed newsletters packed with graphics, storytelling, and intricate segmentation strategies.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most brands overcomplicate email marketing.

They think they need long, detailed newsletters packed with graphics, storytelling, and intricate segmentation strategies.

They believe email marketing is this grand strategy requiring 10 different audience segments, A/B tests for every subject line, and a fully optimized 500-word essay with a perfect CTA.

That’s complete nonsense.

The best email marketers do **the opposite**, and they make millions because of it.

Here’s what you should be doing instead.

### In this quick email I want to change some of your beliefs on “email marketing”

### Why Everyone Gets Email Marketing Wrong

Most people assume that a high-performing email must be **long**, **beautifully designed**, and **highly targeted**.

They think success comes from spending hours crafting a masterpiece.

They also think sending too many emails will "annoy" their list, so they hold back.

They send **once a week** at most.

And when they do send, the email is so cluttered with fluff that it buries the one thing that matters—**the CTA** (aka the reason someone should actually click and buy).

Here’s the reality:

- Your customers are **not** sitting around waiting to read your emails like a novel.

- They don’t need a dissertation on why your product is great.

- They are busy, distracted, and making fast decisions in their inbox.

If they open your email and can’t tell what it’s about within 3 seconds, they’re closing it.

So stop writing long emails.

### The Email Strategy That Actually Works

Want to know what the best brands do instead?

They send **3-4 times per week** (this is the optimized send frequency, every other day, nice and simple).

Want to know what the best brands do instead?

They send **3-4 times per week**.

They keep emails **under 100 words**.

They use **text-based or lightly designed emails**—because simple emails feel personal, like a message from a friend, not a faceless corporation.

And they focus on broad **engaged segmentation**—not hyper-segmenting their list into 20 tiny groups that require different messages.

### Why This Works (And Makes More Money)

📩 **Short emails get read.** Long emails get ignored.
📩 **More emails = more touchpoints.** Frequency builds trust (3-4 times per week)
📩 **Simple design removes friction.** The goal is to **sell**, not impress with fancy formatting.
📩 **Fewer moving parts = fewer mistakes.** The more complex your email strategy, the harder it is to optimize.

Would you rather send one email to 5,000 people, or three emails to 50,000 people? Most people overthink segmentation and **leave money on the table** by only sending emails to tiny slices of their list.

Instead, **send more emails, more often, to a larger audience.**

### What To Do Next (If You Want More Sales)

1️⃣ **Stop overthinking segmentation.** Send to your **engaged list** (90-day openers, for example).

2️⃣ **Write emails like a human.** Short. Direct. Conversational. No fluff.

3️⃣ **Send 3-4x per week.** You won’t annoy people as long as your content is clear and valuable.

4️⃣ **Keep it under 100 words.** If you can’t say it fast, you’re saying too much.

5️⃣ **One CTA per email.** Make it obvious what action they should take.

The best brands **make email simple**—and **they win because of it.**

If your current email marketing isn’t producing 30-40% of your revenue, it’s probably because you’re making it too complicated.

Fix it.

And watch your sales skyrocket.

entries.title: 5 Copywriting Tricks to Improve Email Marketing Conversions
entries.summary: You just need to use words that make people feel something.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Most people overcomplicate copy.

You don’t need fancy words. You don’t need to be a “writer.”

You just need to **use words that make people feel something**.

Here are **five simple phrases** that trigger action.

Use them in your emails, ads, and product pages. Watch your conversions go up.

### 1. “On Us” → Free Without Feeling Cheap

“Free” is a powerful word. But it can also feel **low value**.

Saying something is **“on us”** makes it feel like a **gift**, not a throwaway that is being sent to everybody.

🚫 **Before:** _“Get a free gift with purchase.”_
✅ **Better:** _“Your next order? The shipping is on us.”_

Same offer. Different perception. One makes you feel like you’re getting a deal. The other makes you feel **appreciated**.

📌 **Where to use it:**

- Free shipping offers

- Bonus gifts

- VIP perks

### 2. “Treat Yourself” → Removes Buyer Guilt

People feel guilty spending money, especially on things they **don’t “need.”**

So, remove the guilt.

“Treat yourself” **gives them permission** to buy without feeling bad.

🚫 **Bad:** _“Check out our luxury collection.”_
✅ **Better:** _“Go ahead, treat yourself.”_

When they see this, they think: _“Yeah, I do deserve this.”_ Boom. Sale.

📌 **Where to use it:**

- Luxury products

- Self-care brands

- Limited-time promos

### 3. “Less Than $1 a Day” → Turns Big Costs Into No-Brainers

$365 a year sounds like **a lot**.

But “less than $1 a day” sounds like **pocket change**.

People suck at understanding big numbers. But they **do** understand daily spending.

🚫 **Bad:** _“Our membership costs $365 per year.”_
✅ **Better:** _“For less than $1 a day, get unlimited access.”_

Now, instead of seeing a **big bill**, they compare it to **spare change**. That’s how you make expensive things feel cheap.

📌 **Where to use it:**

- Subscriptions

- Payment plans

- High-ticket items

### 4. “Cheaper Than Your Daily Coffee” → Uses Price Anchoring

Want to make your price feel **tiny**? Compare it to something they **already spend money on**.

People don’t think twice about a **$5 Starbucks** habit. Use that.

🚫 **Bad:** _“This costs $29.99 per month.”_
✅ **Better:** _“For less than your daily coffee, have better skin all month.”_

Now, instead of thinking, _“Can I afford this?”_, they think, _“I spend way more on dumb stuff.”_

📌 **Where to use it:**

- Monthly subscriptions

- Retargeting ads

- Any product under $50

### 5. “Invest in Yourself” → Turns Spending Into Growth

People don’t want to “spend” money. They want to **improve**.

That’s why **“invest in yourself”** is so powerful.

It reframes **spending** as something that gives them a return.

🚫 **Bad:** _“Buy this online course for $99.”_
✅ **Better:** _“Invest in yourself. Learn skills that pay for themselves.”_

Now, instead of thinking, _“Do I really need this?”_, they think, _“This will make me better.”_

📌 **Where to use it:**

- Education & coaching

- High-ticket products

- Fitness & self-improvement

These **five phrases** work because they make buying feel **easy, justified, and smart**.

Use them. Test them. Watch sales go up.

See you at the top.

entries.title: How to Make Your Emails Look Professional
entries.summary: There’s a hero image at the top, then a random-colored section, then another block of mismatched colors and images.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Today I have a quick email design tip to share with you.

## The Problem with Most Email Designs

Most brands treat email design like stacking LEGO blocks.

There’s a hero image at the top, then a random-colored section, then another block of mismatched colors and images.

It creates **visual friction**, disrupting the reader’s flow. Instead of immersing your audience in your brand, you’re making them work to process your email. And if it looks clunky, they’re bouncing.

### The Solution: Immersive Email Design

To create a **seamless, engaging** email experience, follow this **one simple rule**:

**Extend your hero image throughout the entire email.**

✔ **Match the background color** to your hero image
✔ **Use complementary fonts and text styles** throughout
✔ **Blend product images naturally** into the theme
✔ **Keep elements consistent** so nothing looks “off”

When you do this, your email stops feeling like an email. It feels like a beautifully designed landing page.

### How to Apply This to Your Emails (Step-by-Step)

**1. Pick a Strong Hero Image**

- Your hero image sets the tone for your entire email.

- Choose an image that represents the **main theme or product** you’re promoting.

**2. Use the Same Color Palette**

- Identify the **main colors** in your hero image (use a tool like Coolors or Adobe Color).

- Set your email background, section dividers, and CTA buttons in these colors.

**3. Keep the Typography Consistent**

- If your hero image has a bold, modern font, don’t suddenly switch to a script font in the body.

- Stick with **1-2 complementary fonts** throughout the email.

**4. Extend the Background**

- Instead of a white or grey email background, **extend the hero image colors throughout**.

- Example: If your hero image has a soft pastel blue sky, make your email background the same soft blue.

**5. Use Cohesive Product Imagery**

- If you’re featuring multiple products, edit them to blend with the theme.

- Avoid placing random images with different lighting or backgrounds—they’ll break the flow.

**6. Keep It Simple & Clean**

- Remove unnecessary dividers, blocks, and extra text.

- The email should **feel like one connected experience**, not separate sections.

### Why This Works

✅ Emails feel natural & effortless to read
✅ Your brand looks more premium & polished
✅ Higher engagement & click-through rates
✅ Better storytelling & visual impact

**Want to see this in action?**
I recorded a **5-minute video breakdown** showing how I transformed a basic email into a seamless, immersive experience.

**[📺 Watch it here → VIDEO WALKTHROUGH](https://www.loom.com/share/abe156ce20fd449a9b85750175316e9f?sid=d7b62190-db04-4e6c-a8ce-9c92cb12d78a&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-to-make-your-emails-look-professional)**

Let me know what you think!

entries.title: How to Use Psychology in Your Marketing
entries.summary: The best brands in the world don’t just sell… they brainwash you.
entries.body:
Hey, it’s Max from _The Inbox Newsletter_.

The best brands in the world don’t just sell… they brainwash you.

Not actually.

But today I want to break down **five insanely powerful psychology tricks** that brands use to make you buy.

Plus how you can use them in your own marketing to drive more conversions.

## 1. Labelling: Make Your Customer Live Up to Their Identity

People feel a deep need to align with the labels they’re given. If someone calls you “a great leader,” you’re more likely to step up in leadership situations to maintain that reputation.

✅ **How Brands Use It:**
A sustainable clothing brand might say:
_"As an environmentally conscious person, you probably choose products made with recycled materials."_

A supplement company might write:
_"As someone who treats their body like a temple, you only give it the best ingredients."_

The customer reads it and thinks, _"That’s me. I want to live up to that!"_—and just like that, they’re hooked.

💡 **How to Use This in Your Emails & Copy:**

- Assign your customers a positive trait that aligns with your product.

- Reinforce their self-image through your messaging.

- Watch them take action to stay consistent with that identity.

## 2. Negativity Bias: Sell by Avoiding Losses

People **fear losses more than they desire gains**. If given the choice between **losing $20** or **gaining $20**, they’d rather avoid the loss. Brands leverage this bias to make products feel _essential_.

✅ **How Brands Use It:**
A gym supplement company doesn’t just say, _"Our product helps you build muscle."_ They say:
_"You put in 5 hours a week at the gym… don't let it go to waste by skipping this post-workout complex."_

I saw that ad and thought, _"Wait—am I actually wasting my workouts?"_ Boom. I bought it.

💡 **How to Use This in Your Emails & Copy:**

- Identify the biggest pain points or fears of your audience.

- Position your product as the solution that _prevents_ that loss.

- Test framing your messaging around _what they might lose_ instead of _what they might gain_.

## 3. The Pratfall Effect: Turn Weaknesses into Strengths

People trust brands that **admit imperfections**. It makes them seem _more human_ and _honest_.

✅ **How Brands Use It:**
Instead of hiding their high price, a premium supplement brand might say:
_"Our creatine isn’t cheap. If you want a cheap option, go elsewhere. But if you choose the cheap option, you lose out on the benefits that ours provides."_

By acknowledging the “flaw” (high price), they increase _trust_ and _credibility_, while reinforcing their product’s value.

💡 **How to Use This in Your Emails & Copy:**

- Instead of hiding your product’s weaknesses, **own them**—but tie them to a strength.

- Example: _"We’re not the cheapest on the market, but we are the highest quality."_

- This builds **trust** and makes your brand feel **authentic**.

## 4. Curiosity: The Click Driver

When people feel **curious**, they _have_ to know the answer. It’s a psychological itch they _need_ to scratch.

✅ **How Brands Use It:**
Instead of saying, _"Here’s 10% off,"_ some brands say:
_"Reveal your mystery discount at checkout!"_

Or instead of saying, _"Our product will make your skin glow,"_ they might say:
_"There’s one thing dermatologists swear by for glowing skin… and it’s NOT what you think."_

Guess what happens? People **click** just to find out.

💡 **How to Use This in Your Emails & Copy:**

- Use _teasers_ to build intrigue and increase engagement.

- Try subject lines like: _“Most people make this mistake when choosing skincare (are you?)”_

- _“Open to reveal your exclusive mystery gift”_

- Drive clicks by making people **curious** about what’s inside.

## 5. Commitment Bias: Get Customers to Say "Yes" Early

Once someone starts a process, they’re more likely to follow through.

✅ **How Brands Use It:**
Ever seen a pop-up that says, _"Do you want $10 off?"_ with a **YES** or **NO** button?
Once someone clicks “YES,” they’re mentally committed—so entering their email feels _natural_.

💡 **How to Use This in Your Emails & Copy:**

- Instead of just asking people to sign up, frame it as an **exclusive commitment**: _"Be a part of our VIP community."_

- _"Claim your spot below."_

- _“Click to get automatically added to an exclusive list with early access”_

- These small tweaks can lead to **huge** conversion increases.

## Recap: 5 Psychology Tricks You Can Use Today

1️⃣ **Labelling** – Assign your customers traits that align with your brand.
2️⃣ **Negativity Bias** – Focus on what they might _lose_ instead of what they might _gain_.
3️⃣ **The Pratfall Effect** – Admit a “weakness” and turn it into a strength.
4️⃣ **Curiosity** – Create mystery to increase clicks and engagement.
5️⃣ **Commitment Bias** – Get small “yeses” early to boost conversions.

entries.title: The One Email You Should Send Today (From You, Not Your Brand)
entries.summary: You’re about to learn the simplest email strategy that will turn your leads into customers
entries.body:
Hey, it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

You’re about to learn the simplest email strategy that will turn your leads into customers

You can use this template to make money TODAY.

Let’s get into it.

#### Founder-Based Emails

Most emails today are over-designed and impersonal. They’re trying too hard to impress.

But people don’t buy necessarily because of sexy branding.

They buy from people they trust.

That’s where founder-driven emails come in:

- **They feel like a personal note.** A text-based email looks like it’s straight from your inbox, not a marketing team.

- **They build trust.** When people feel like the founder of a brand cares enough to reach out personally, they’re more likely to engage.

- **They’re distraction-free.** No flashy designs, just clear, to-the-point messaging.

The key to success with this approach is keeping it simple and conversational.

#### Use This Template to Send This Email Today

This email is meant for the people on your list who haven’t yet made a purchase. They’re interested in your brand (they signed up, after all) but need a little more context to trust you enough to buy.

Here’s exactly how you can do it:

**Sender Name:** “Founder First Name | Brand Name”

**Subject Line:** “Hey, quick thought…”

**Body:**

Hi there,

It’s [Founder Name], the founder of [Brand Name}.

I wanted to personally reach out and say thanks for checking out [Brand Name].

A lot of people come across us because they’re looking for [specific problem your product solves]—and I totally get it. That’s why I started [Brand Name] in the first place. [Brief 1-2 sentence personal story about the brand’s origin or mission.]

If you’re on the fence, no pressure. I just want to share a little about why customers love us:

- [Unique Selling Point #1]

- [Unique Selling Point #2]

- [Unique Selling Point #3]

And - I just reactivated your welcome discount for 10% OFF. Just use code [Discount Code] at checkout.

Whenever you’re ready, I’d love for you to give us a try. Here’s a link to check out our bestsellers: Shop Bestsellers »

Thanks for being here—it means a lot.

[Founder Name]

P.S. If you have any questions or want a recommendation, just hit reply. I actually read these myself :)

#### Why This Email Works:

- **It’s personal:** The email feels like it’s from a real person—not a corporate entity.

- **It educates:** Instead of pushing for a sale, it offers genuine insights about the brand and why it’s valuable.

- **It builds connection:** Inviting replies opens the door for real conversations, which fosters trust and long-term loyalty.

### Action Steps:

- **Write your email like a personal note.** Use the template above as a starting point.

- **Send it to your non-buyer segment.** These are the people most likely to respond to this approach.

- **Add it to your welcome flow.** Automating this email ensures every new lead gets the same warm welcome

entries.title: How to Fail At Email Marketing
entries.summary: You reading this may be failing. Today we’re going to talk about what failing looks like.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

What does it look like to fail at email marketing?

You reading this may be failing. Today we’re going to talk about what failing looks like.

### How to Fail at Email Marketing Like a Pro

Most brands screw this up.

They think they’re doing email marketing, but what they’re really doing is lighting money on fire.

If you want to fail, do what everyone else does.

**Here’s the exact playbook for losing revenue, alienating customers, and wasting time.**

#### 1. Ignore Pop-Ups Entirely

You are literally shooting yourself in the foot if you aren’t optimizing your pop-up forms.

Pop-ups allow you to capture email addresses from website visitors who are already interested in your brand.

Without them, you’re losing potential customers who will likely never come back.

**In many cases we can double or triple a client’s pop-up conversion rate… thus doubling or tripling their list growth AND their email revenue.**

What happens:

- Your email list grows slowly, if at all.

- You lose out on revenue from missed opportunities.

**What to do:**
Use optimized pop-up forms that convert visitors. Test offers, timing, and messaging to improve performance. (Tutorial [here](https://youtu.be/Zw7qW6cp4Kk?si=yjsmLZyhPFRsCvei&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-to-fail-at-email-marketing)).

#### 2. Blast Emails to Your Whole List

Sending emails to your entire list without segmentation reduces deliverability and engagement.

Most of your list isn’t engaged, and inbox providers will penalize you for low engagement.

What happens:

- Open and click rates drop.

- Inbox providers stop trusting you

- Emails end up in spam.

**What to do:**
Segment your list based on engagement levels. Only send to active subscribers—those who have opened or clicked in the past 30-90 days. (Guide [here](https://youtu.be/WYjfFNTWccw?si=r8jHhvEE8iAyjxOg&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-to-fail-at-email-marketing)).

#### 3. Only Send One Email Per Week

Sending only one email a week reduces visibility and just leaves a ton of revenue on the table.

Customers are distracted with messages from other brands, and infrequent emails make it harder for them to recognize or remember you.

What happens:

- Your brand gets forgotten.

- Engagement drops due to lack of consistent communication.

**What to do:**
Send at least 2-3 emails per week. Use a variety of content, like product highlights, educational tips, and offers, to maintain interest and engagement.

#### 4. Skip Monthly Reviews

Without reviewing your email performance regularly, you miss insights. W

hat works today might not work tomorrow, and ignoring metrics leads to wasted efforts.

What happens:

- Poorly performing campaigns keep running.

- High-performing strategies go unnoticed and unscaled.

**What to do:**
Analyze key metrics like open rates, click-through rates, and revenue monthly. Use this data to adjust and improve your strategies for next month.

#### 5. Neglect Conversion Rate Optimized Email Copy / Design

If your emails aren’t designed to drive conversions, you’re wasting sends.

Overly complicated designs and unclear CTAs reduce the likelihood of customers taking action.

Using a lot of copy and unclear value propositions distract the customer from clicking.

What happens:

- Click-through rates are lower than they should be.

- Customers get distracted or confused and leave without converting.

**What to do:**
Focus on clear, simple designs. Use bold CTAs, social proof, and compelling copy to guide readers to take action. (Guide [here](https://youtu.be/YzhXs9diyzU?si=pl3e43loelbfDzEZ&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-to-fail-at-email-marketing)).

#### 6. Set It and Forget It with Email Flows

Email flows can’t be left untouched for months.

Customer behavior and preferences change, and flows need to be updated regularly to stay relevant and effective.

What happens:

- Flows become outdated and ineffective.

- Customers disengage due to irrelevant messaging.

**What to do:**
Review and refresh your flows every quarter. Update subject lines, offers, and messaging to reflect current trends and customer behavior.

Stop failing at email marketing.

Email is your most important channel in 2025 if you care at all about profit.

If you’re struggling with time, watch this [4 hour per week email marketing system video I posted.](https://youtu.be/YRMrXB5TSE4?si=A8KTGd2ZNB5lHCUD&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=how-to-fail-at-email-marketing)

entries.title: Email Welcome Flow Strategies That SELL
entries.summary: I want to get a point across that you may not understand yet…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I want to get a point across that you may not understand yet…

Every strategy is different! Even for your Welcome Flow.

### Finding The Right Welcome Flow For You.

The truth about email marketing is that everything works…

It depends on the brand on what is the most optimal strategy.

I will be helping you find the optimal welcome flow strategy for your Welcome Flow.

Some brands need more education, which will entail a longer email welcome flow.

Others need fast impulse purchases, where a shorter email welcome flow with more urgency may be more optimal.

I have used all types of welcome flows, but my most used ones are the below:

### Option 1: The 3-Email Welcome Flow (Minimal Effort, Maximum ROI)

This is perfect for brands that need a lean, straightforward introduction to their audience w/ heavier urgency and impulse purchases.

**Email 1: The Welcome + Incentive Delivery**

- _Purpose:_ Deliver your promised discount or incentive while introducing your brand.

- _Content Highlights:_ Clearly state the discount or offer.

- Showcase 2-4 bestsellers.

- Briefly introduce your unique selling proposition.

**Email 2: The Brand Story**

- _Purpose:_ Build trust by telling your story.

- _Content Highlights:_ Share how your brand was founded and its mission.

- Add a personal touch (e.g., a founder’s photo).

- Include a subtle reminder of the incentive.

**Email 3: Urgency + Conversion**

- _Purpose:_ Push those on-the-fence subscribers to take action.

- _Content Highlights:_ Introduce urgency with a deadline for the incentive.

- Add social proof (testimonials or reviews).

- Include a clear, direct call-to-action (CTA).

### Option 2: The 5-Email Welcome Flow (Balanced Approach)

For brands with more resources, this flow goes deeper into building trust and conversion potential down the line.

**Email 1 & Email 2:** Same as above.

**Email 3: Product Highlight**

- _Purpose:_ Showcase your standout products.

- _Content Highlights:_ Highlight a single product category or bestseller.

- Focus on benefits and use cases.

**Email 4: Social Proof + Value**

- _Purpose:_ Reinforce credibility.

- _Content Highlights:_ Include glowing testimonials or user-generated content.

- Mention any media coverage or awards.

**Email 5: Last Chance Urgency**

- _Purpose:_ Create FOMO.

- _Content Highlights:_ Emphasize the deadline for their discount.

- Use bold visuals or a countdown timer.

- Provide an easy path to shop now.

### Option 3: The 8-Email Welcome Flow (High-Impact Nurture)

Designed for brands wanting to leave no stone unturned.

This flow ensures every customer touchpoint is covered while also introducing enough urgency at the back of the flow.

**Email 1–Email 5:** Same as in Option 2.

**Email 6: Competitor Comparison**

- _Purpose:_ Highlight why your brand is the better choice.

- _Content Highlights:_ Create a direct but subtle “us vs. them” comparison.

- Focus on your unique advantages, such as sustainability, pricing, or quality.

**Email 7: Community & Brand Love**

- _Purpose:_ Build emotional connection.

- _Content Highlights:_ Share details about your community or customer support initiatives.

- Highlight your social media or loyalty programs.

**Email 8: Personal Touch Follow-Up**

- _Purpose:_ Reach out one last time with a personal tone.

- _Content Highlights:_ A text-based email from the founder thanking the subscriber.

- Reiterate the discount (if still available).

- Offer a direct line for questions or concerns.

The choice of strategy depends on your resources and goals.

Whether you go for the simplicity of three emails or the comprehensive nature of eight, the key is testing and iteration.

Try all variations if you have the time!

entries.title: Nobody Talks About This Email Marketing Hack
entries.summary: Ever opened an email that looked like it was from a person and it turned out to be a brand?
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Ever opened an email that looked like it was from a person and it turned out to be a brand?

That’s the magic of using characters in your marketing.

Whether it’s the founder, an intern, or a customer service rep, these personas add a human touch that radically improves conversions.

### Why Using PEOPLE Work in Email Marketing

PEOPLE WANT TO BUY FROM PEOPLE - THEY DON’T WANT TO BUY FROM CORPORATIONS…

Just look at Mr. Beast and Feastables…

People buy his chocolate because of him. Not for Feastables.

We’re noticing this even more going into 2025… and it’s why we see some of the top brands sending emails from actual people.

Adding a face or personality to your emails does two important things:

- **Builds Trust:** Customers trust people more than faceless brands. A relatable persona makes your emails feel personal, not automated.

- **Drives Engagement:** Emails that feel like they’re from a real person often get higher open and click rates.

People relate to stories and personalities.

When your email is “from” someone specific it feels like a conversation, not a sales pitch.

**People love to buy, but they don’t want to be sold to.**

### Examples of Characters You Can Use

**The Founder**

- A message from the founder adds credibility and authenticity.

- Example: “Hi, I’m Max, founder of [Brand Name]. When I started this company, I wanted to solve [customer problem]. I’m so excited you’re here.”

**The Intern**

- Great for humor and casual engagement.

- Example: “Hey, it’s Emma, the intern. I might’ve accidentally sent this email early, but check out this awesome deal!”

**The Customer Service Rep**

- Perfect for follow-ups and support.

- Example: “Hi, I’m Sarah from Customer Happiness. I noticed you left something in your cart—need help deciding?”

**The Marketing Manager**

- Ideal for updates or new launches.

- Example: “Hey, I’m James. I’ve got the inside scoop on this week’s bestsellers—check them out before they’re gone!”

The Success Coach

This expert offers tips, advice, and insider knowledge, building trust and showcasing your brand’s authority in the niche.

- **Example:** “Hi, I’m Olivia, your personal success coach at [Brand Name]. Struggling to stay consistent? Here’s a simple 3-step plan to help you get back on track.”

**The Product Designer**

A behind-the-scenes character who shares insights about product development, fostering transparency and intrigue.

- **Example:** “Hi, I’m Leo, the product designer here at [Brand Name]. I wanted to give you an insider look at how we create our bestsellers—starting with the fabric everyone’s raving about.”

**The Expert in the Field**

This could be a nutritionist, stylist, or other specialist, depending on your niche. They add authority and value by providing niche-specific advice.

- **Example:** “Hi, I’m Ellie, a nutritionist working with [Brand Name]. Did you know most people don’t get enough protein? Here’s how our products can help you meet your daily goals.”

**The Enthusiastic Customer**

A fictionalized loyal customer who shares relatable testimonials and recommendations.

- **Example:** “Hi, I’m Lisa, a long-time fan of [Brand Name]. I just had to share how much I love the new [product]! It’s been a total game-changer for me.”

### How to Use Characters Effectively

- **Be Consistent:** Each character should have a distinct tone that aligns with your brand. The CEO might be serious and inspiring, while the intern could be quirky and fun.

- **Match the Message to the Character:** Use the founder for heartfelt notes, the rep for follow-ups, and the intern for lighthearted announcements.

- **Include a Visual:** Add a photo or illustration to make the character feel real and relatable. BONUS - Add a signature.

- **Segment Your Audience:** Pair characters with specific campaigns or customer actions. For example, the founder’s note could welcome new subscribers, while the marketing manager shares sale updates with loyal customers.

entries.title: I Reviewed a $400k/mo Ecom Brand and This is What They Were Missing
entries.summary: So I released my most valuable YouTube video I’ve ever released the other day.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

So I released my most valuable YouTube video I’ve ever released the other day.

In the video I spent an hour with a brand marketing lead doing $400k/mo, breaking down their email account and where they can improve.

No one has ever made a video like this on YouTube ([video here](https://youtu.be/mBGBmnRHMyI?si=E9-PoKM_nW4ueUSp&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=i-reviewed-a-400k-mo-ecom-brand-and-this-is-what-they-were-missing)).

It’s so valuable that I want to give you a summary of it all here so we can all learn from **how I’d add $50,000 - $100,000 PER MONTH to this brand with email…**

### Introduction to the Brand & Opportunity

The featured brand, [Happiest Hour](http://happiesthour.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=i-reviewed-a-400k-mo-ecom-brand-and-this-is-what-they-were-missing), sells wellness shots similar to Magic Mind, catering to specific needs like energy, calmness, and sleep.

Despite doing $400,000/month in revenue, their email channel only contributes 10%—a massive opportunity for growth.

TikTok Shop accounts for 70% of their revenue, but over-reliance on the platform poses risks due to potential U.S. bans and platform volatility.

Email is the only channel you truly own yourself, and it has the highest ROI so the brand wants to make it a focus in Q1 2025.

### Funnel Audit: Pop-ups & Welcome Flow

The pop-up form captures emails with a 13.6% opt-in rate, which is strong, but the **subscription-to-purchase conversion rate of 7.2% needs improvement (target: 10-15%).**

Suggested improvements:

- Add intermediary steps to collect email addresses BEFORE showcasing bundle options.

- Make discount codes look custom (e.g., “TY23GH”) to boost perceived exclusivity and conversion rates.

- Ensure every email in the welcome flow reminds users of the discount and includes buttons for easy navigation.

- Buttons in emails should be above the fold (top of the email) for maximum visibility and engagement.

### Flows Audit: The Missing Opportunities

Missing flows: site abandonment, browse abandonment, and cart abandonment. Adding these flows can _significantly_ increase revenue by recovering otherwise lost sales.

Post-purchase flows were nonexistent. Recommendations include:

- **Immediate Thank You:** Personalize from the founder, with a subtle PS upsell.

- **Upsell/Cross-sell:** One to two days post-purchase.

- **How to Use/Pair Products:** Educate users to maximize product value.

- **Check-in Email:** Send three weeks later to reinforce customer satisfaction and engagement.

For replenishment reminders, split flows based on product pack size (e.g., 5-pack vs. 12-pack) with appropriate timing (e.g., 14 vs. 30 days).

Win-back flows should fire at 2x-3x the replenishment period to re-engage inactive customers with urgency and tailored offers.

### Campaign Strategy: Building Consistency

Current campaigns are sparse, focused on product launches, restocks, and Black Friday.

This leaves significant untapped potential.

**Suggested approach:**

- Send 3-4 campaigns per week to a 90-day engaged list.

- Mix text-based, value-driven emails (e.g., founder stories, brain teasers) with visually engaging promotional emails.

- Incorporate educational content about product benefits and use cases to build trust and interest.

- Inspiration: Magic Mind’s email strategy combines clean designs, personal tones, and consistent value delivery.

### Segmentation Simplified

Campaign segmentation should be kept simple—cast a wide net with a 90-day engaged list for consistency and impact.

Over-segmentation in campaigns can cause inefficiencies without significantly improving ROI.

Use splits and customizations just in your email flows for personalization (e.g., product purchased, AOV, frequency of purchase).

### Metrics & Quick Wins

- Current email revenue contribution (10%) is below the benchmark for TikTok-native brands (20-30%). With improvements, the brand could achieve 25-30% in 60 days.

- Quick wins: Add missing abandonment flows and improve the welcome flow.

- Prioritize buttons, urgency, and discount reminders in all flows.

- Test campaign formats inspired by Magic Mind to increase engagement and retention.

- A strong email strategy will complement upcoming ad campaigns, driving profitability and long-term customer retention.

### Why This Matters

Owning customer data through email reduces reliance on platforms like TikTok and ensures the brand can adapt to market changes.

Tik Tok looks like it’s going to get banned… which will destroy a lot of brands.

You know what channel I can guarantee will never get banned? Email!

entries.title: Grow Your Email List on Autopilot
entries.summary: These can literally double your list growth and your email revenue with just a few simple tweaks.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Pop-up forms.

These can literally double your list growth and your email revenue with just a few simple tweaks.

I don’t want to waste any time because this is too important.

### The Case for High-Converting Pop-Ups

Without an effective pop-up form, most of your ad-driven traffic visits your site, browses, and leaves without buying.

That’s wasted opportunity and wasted ad spend.

When optimized, pop-up forms let you:

- **Capture leads** from visitors who aren’t ready to buy yet.

- **Nurture and convert them** through email marketing.

- **Lower your cost per acquisition** by maximizing the ROI of your traffic.

Real example:

One of our brands increased its pop-up conversion rate from 2.5% to 8.75%. This simple tweak turned 750 monthly email signups into 2,625.

And their Welcome Flow revenue jumped from **$7,000 to $25,000 per month!**

### How to Optimize Your Pop-Up Forms

#### 1. Nail the Offer

The offer is the most important element of your pop-up. Ask yourself: _Would I give my email for this?_

- **Under $100 AOV?** Offer a percentage off (e.g., 10% off).

- **Over $100 AOV?** Offer a dollar discount (e.g., $25 off).

- Test unique incentives like free shipping, exclusive access, or a giveaway.

- Try a “Mystery Discount” to see if it improves opt-in rates

#### 2. Design for Impact

Your pop-up needs to grab attention without overwhelming users:

- **Big and Bold:** Cover at least 75% of the screen.

- **Less Is More:** Use under 10 words of copy, and make your offer the focal point.

- **Avoid Clutter:** Too many colors, images, or text will confuse users.

#### 3. Optimize Timing

Your pop-up should appear neither too soon nor too late.

- **Ideal Delay:** 4–12 seconds after a visitor lands on your site.

- **Exit-Intent Pop-Ups:** Don’t use them… they have firing issues which can hurt the customer experience.

#### 4. Simplify the Process

The fewer steps, the better.

- **Ask for One Input:** Start with just the email address. You can ask for more info (like SMS) after they’ve signed up.

- **Instant Loading:** Avoid slow-loading pop-ups by compressing large images.

#### 5. Test and Iterate

You’ll never get it perfect on the first try, but that’s okay. Regular testing helps you inch closer to higher conversion rates.

- **A/B Test Ideas:** Time delays (e.g., 4 seconds vs. 8 seconds).

- Offer types (e.g., percentage vs. dollar discounts).

- Form design and layout.

Follow this guide for exact step-by-steps and examples:

entries.title: Email Marketing Myths vs Facts
entries.summary: Email marketing is one of the most misunderstood channels in ecommerce.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Email marketing is one of the most misunderstood channels in ecommerce.

Over the years, a handful of myths have popped up that can seriously limit how much revenue you’re driving through email.

Today, we’re setting the record straight on six of the biggest myths…

And replacing them with actionable facts that will hopefully bring you more clarity AND make you more money.

## Myth 1: You Can't Send Emails with Many Images

**Fact:** You absolutely can—just add **invisible text in your footer**.

Here’s the truth: inbox providers look for HTML content to verify your email isn’t spam.

If your email is all images and no text, yes… you might get flagged.

But you don’t have to ditch image-heavy designs.

Simply add 250-500 words of “invisible text” in your footer (a tiny strip of text with the same color as your background).

Then, you’ll pass the spam test while keeping your design intact.

### Myth 2: Your Open Rates Are Determined by Your Subject Line and Preview Text

**Fact:** Quality emails are what keep your audience opening.

Sure, a great subject line can grab attention, but if your actual content doesn’t deliver, people will stop opening.

True fans open every email because they know it’s worth their time.

Focus on crafting emails that provide value, inspire action, or entertain.

The goal is to **get people to open emails off of your Brand Name**, not your SL and PT.

Imrpvoe content, and watch your open rates improve consistently.

### Myth 3: Email Marketing Can’t Make More Than 20% of Store Revenue

**Fact:** Our client average is 41%.

Most ecommerce brands cap their email marketing potential because they don’t have proper systems in place.

With optimized flows, engaging campaigns, and a high-converting strategy, email marketing can become a backbone of your revenue.

We are actively proving this to be true for over 40 ecom brands.

### Myth 4: You Should Only Send Emails Once a Week

**Fact:** The sweet spot is 3–4 emails per week.

Sending just once a week isn’t enough to stay top of mind.

Consumers are on average hit with over 200 ecommerce brands every single day through social media ads and email marketing.

If you’re not showing up consistently with valuable, eye-catching emails, they’ll forget about you.

With quality content and intentional designs, 3–4 emails per week is the sweetspot to skyrocket your engagement and sales.

### Myth 5: The More Segmented, the Better

**Fact:** Over-segmentation can backfire.

While segmentation is important, overdoing it can waste time and resources.

Instead of trying to hyper-target tiny groups, focus on larger high-leverage segments like engaged users and recent purchasers.

These segments deliver great ROI without unnecessary complexity.

Would you rather send a targeted email to 1,000 people or a slightly less targeted email to 10,000 people?

### Myth 6: Unsubscribes Are Bad

**Fact:** Unsubscribes help clean your list and improve deliverability.

Don’t fear unsubscribes—they’re actually a good thing.

They actually don’t impact deliverability.

They help maintain a healthy, engaged email list and improve your sender reputation.

It’s better to focus on the users who genuinely want to hear from you.

Clean lists mean better open rates, more clicks, and higher deliverability.

Watch my new YouTube video explaining **how to operate a high-level ecom email list in only 4 hours per week!**

Link: [https://youtu.be/YRMrXB5TSE4?si=s2GuKcdF4M5LIeYZ](https://youtu.be/YRMrXB5TSE4?si=s2GuKcdF4M5LIeYZ&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=email-marketing-myths-vs-facts)
