entries.title: Email Design Conversion Principles
entries.summary: So today, I wanted to talk about the SECOND most important section…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

The hero section of your email is the most important.

And a lot of people talk about it…

So today, I wanted to talk about the SECOND most important section…

**The Product Section.**

## Email Product Section

Your product section is exactly as it sounds.

It's the part of the email that is going to specifically feature and highlight a product or products.

Products can even be categories, not necessarily specific products.

**It seems simple, but it’s very easy to mess it up.**

In fact, most brands I review mess it up…

Let’s talk about a few things you must have to maximize conversions.

## Product Section Layout

We don’t want to overcomplicate our product sections.

But for each product, we need 3 things:

- Image of the product (show the product)

- Name of the product (in case customer is going to search for it on your site)

- Clear button (will talk more about this below)

The simplest product section layout is a grid.

I recommend using only 2 products per row rather than 3 so that the products are bigger for the customer to see.

## Individual Calls To Action

It's important if you're showing products to make it **clear** that the customer can click it and go to that product page.

This removes friction for the buyer so they don't have to go to the general site and find the product.

**Make it clear by giving individual buttons or underlines under product titles.**

![](https://cdn.gamma.app/r08uk0sismotnn6/b5c4e65b294849a9a80a70a3cd4251f9/original/Screenshot-2024-05-09-at-9.51.19-AM.png)

Individual Product Buttons

## End With A General CTA

After you give individual products, it's important to always have a general CTA below.

Maybe the customer is interested, but didn't like any of the products in the email.

By leaving out a general CTA below, you lose out on all these customers.

We've noticed 25% boosts in clicks by including this.

Absolutely necessary for ALL product sections.

![](https://cdn.gamma.app/r08uk0sismotnn6/38b0a31f607946719db77975181ff61e/original/Screenshot-2024-05-09-at-9.49.37-AM.png)

General Shop Now Button

It’s so simple…

Individual buttons and end with a general CTA.

These alone will skyrocket your clicks and conversions…

That’s it.

entries.title: Send This Email ASAP
entries.summary: As 2024 winds down, your email list is primed for one last touchpoint…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

As 2024 winds down, your email list is primed for one last touchpoint…

Here’s an email I would recommend sending out this week.

### '2024 in Summary' Email

After a year of campaigns, your customers will appreciate a message that acknowledges their journey with you. This email reinforces the relationship and sets the stage for retention.

Also… it’s just cool to see everything accomplished by the brand over a years’ time.

It makes the customer feel like they are involved in something.

Use this email also to tease upcoming launches, trends, or really anything with the brand happening in 2025.

This gives your audience a peek at what’s next and keeps them engaged on the list so they don’t unsubscribe.

**Try to humanize your brand.** Customers love seeing the faces, stories, and efforts behind the products they buy. A heartfelt summary adds a personal touch to your brand.

### What to Include in Your Email

#### 1. Reflect on 2024

Share key moments of the year. Highlight milestones, awards, or new products your brand relaased.

Include interesting stats or achievements that your audience made possible, such as:

- “We shipped over 25,000 products to happy customers this year!”

- “Thanks to your support, we donated $10,000 to [cause] in 2024.”

#### 2. Thank Your Customers

Express genuine gratitude. Let them know how much they mean to your brand.

Use heartfelt language and let them know that they are what makes your business possible: “Your support fuels our passion and helps us grow every day.”

#### 3. Tease What’s Coming in 2025

Drop hints about upcoming launches, new products, or improvements to your services.

Example: “We’ve been cooking up something BIG for 2024… stay tuned for January!”

#### 4. Offer a CTA (Call-to-Action)

Add a subtle nudge so you can get clicks and revenue.

You can go for sales or social media engagement:

- A New Year-themed CTA: “Ring in 2025 with [xyz product"”

- An invite to stay engaged: “Follow us on Instagram to see behind-the-scenes magic heading into 2025.”

### Design Tips for the Campaign

- **Use Clean, On-Brand Visuals:** Keep the design simple but celebratory. Incorporate brand colors and a touch of New Year-themed elements like confetti or fireworks.

- **Incorporate Personalization:** Use first names if you can by using the Klaviyo formula 'there' “Emma, here’s what we accomplished together this year!”

- **Add a Timeline or Infographic:** Create a quick recap of your brand’s 2024 highlights with a timeline or stats bar—easy to skim and visually engaging.

### Subject Line Inspiration

- “Here’s to an Incredible 2024 (& What’s Next!)”

- “Our Journey Together: 2024 in Review 🎉”

- “2025 Is Almost Here… Let’s Reflect!”

### 2024 In Review Email Inspiration Examples

Check out 3 great examples I found of this email concept below:

[https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1TT1P6Sm8Tr_iSa7v6GhBkLF5r0vQzwOv?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1TT1P6Sm8Tr_iSa7v6GhBkLF5r0vQzwOv?usp=sharing&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=send-this-email-asap)

entries.title: January Email Strategy Planning
entries.summary: Let’s clear out some winter inventory and set the tone for the year ahead with a banger email campaign strategy.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

New year, new opportunities.

Let’s clear out some winter inventory and set the tone for the year ahead with a banger email campaign strategy.

## Email Campaign Calendars

A well put together email campaign calendar ensures your audience stays engaged while driving consistent revenue.

A strategic email calendar will:

Keep your list engaged without overwhelming them…

Provide a balanced mix of value, promotion, and storytelling…

Help build momentum for upcoming product launches and events…

### Setting Goals and Strategy

Let’s run through the example of Hydroflask and how I might want to plan their calendar.

There are 4 main goals we want to achieve:

- **Engagement:** Reconnect with the audience after the holidays.

- **Revenue:** Clear out inventory with promotions.

- **Education:** Position Hydro Flask as the go-to brand for style and hydration in the new year.

- **Brand Building:** Share user-generated content / highlight eco-friendly goals.

### Types of Emails to Send in January

- **Welcome Back Emails (2 emails)** Kickstart the month with personal messages.

- Example: “New Year, New Hydration Goals!” Include tips on staying hydrated and showcase your bestsellers.

- **Promotional Emails (5 emails)** Push sales for winter items or bundle deals.

- Example: “Winter Clearance – Save Up to 30% on Select Bottles!”

- **Educational Content (3 emails)** Focus on hydration tips, fitness resolutions, or sustainability.

- Example: “5 Tips to Stay Hydrated and Crush Your Fitness Goals in 2025.”

- **Social Proof/User-Generated Content (2 emails)** Build trust by sharing reviews or stories from real customers.

- Example: “Why Thousands Swear by Hydro Flask for Every Adventure.”

- **Product Highlights/New Arrivals (2 emails)** Spotlight your bestsellers or introduce new products for 2024.

- Example: “The Ultimate Travel Companion: Check Out Our New Tumbler!”

- **Reactivation Campaigns (1-2 emails)** Target inactive subscribers with exclusive offers.

- Example: “We Miss You! Here’s 20% Off to Get You Back on Track.”

- **Last-Minute Flash Sale (1 email)** Create urgency with a one-day-only deal to close out the month.

- Example: “One Day Only: 25% Off All Insulated Bottles!”

### Example Minimal January Email Calendar for Hydro Flask

**Date**

**Email Theme**

**Email Type**

**Key Focus**

**Jan 2**

New Year Goals: Hydration Matters

Welcome Back

Give health New Years resolutions.

**Jan 5**

Winter Clearance Sale

Promotional

Drive sales with discounts.

**Jan 8**

Hydration 101: Benefits for Winter Hikes

Educational

Highlight hydration tips for outdoor folk.

**Jan 11**

Customer Story: Adventures with Hydro

Social Proof/UGC

Share a relatable user story.

**Jan 15**

Top Picks for 2025

Product Highlights

Showcase popular and new arrivals.

**Jan 18**

Limited-Time Offer: Bundle & Save

Promotional

Push bundles with an exclusive deal.

**Jan 21**

Why Insulation Matters Year-Round

Educational

Educate on Hydro Flask’s Insulation with storytelling

**Jan 24**

We Miss You: Special Offer Inside

Reactivation

Engage dormant subscribers.

**Jan 27**

Final Days: Winter Clearance Ends Soon

Promotional

Create urgency with a sale reminder.

**Jan 30**

Last Chance: Flash Sale

Flash Sale

Wrap up the month with a strong CTA.

### Tips for Execution

- **Balance Frequency:** Send ~2-3 emails per week minimum to keep engagement high without fatigue.

- **Segment Your List:** Only send emails to active email subscribers, avoid sending to people who haven’t opened in months.

- **A/B Test:** Experiment with subject lines, CTAs, and imagery to optimize engagement.

- **Measure and Adjust:** Use click rates and revenue data to refine your February calendar.

entries.summary: If you think email marketing has to be flashy, packed with product images, or screaming “SALE,” think again.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

If you think email marketing has to be flashy, packed with product images, or screaming “SALE,” think again.

[_We’re Not Really Strangers_](https://www.werenotreallystrangers.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=unique-email-marketing-inspiration) (WNRS) is proof that you don’t…

I’ve been _**obsessed**_ with this brand recently and wanted to share some examples of their work.

Let’s break down some of their emails and why they work so well.

### What Makes WNRS Different?

WNRS doesn’t do email like anyone else:

- **Minimalist Design**: Simple black text on a white background. No distractions.

- **Emotional Resonance**: Their copy feels personal, exactly like a text from a friend.

- **Subtle CTAs**: They _sell softly_… emotional impact first, promo second.

The result is emails that grab attention, spark introspection, but still drive sales.

Yes, you can spam sales and discounts and make a lot of money quickly.

But WNRS understands the long game.

Lower unsubscribes over time = more revenue over time.

Let’s break down some examples

### Example 1: Thought-Provoking Questions

**Subject:** _“Are they good for you?”_

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/4f0edbaa-9571-4a38-aa53-a6788bf0b830/screencapture-milled-werenotreallystrangers-com-are-they-good-for-you-lODpQR4iCDKfsJDf-2024-12-20-05_20_45-edit.png?t=1734701264)

Email

**Why It Works:**

- It reads like a journal prompt, not a sales pitch.

- It builds trust and emotional connection, positioning WNRS as more than just a brand, they’re part of your personal growth.

- It’s not like ANY other emails you may receive from someone.

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8a07b85c-000d-4f98-b126-569099fcecab/Screenshot_2024-12-19_at_5.41.39_AM.png?t=1734701269)

### Example 2: Relatable Problem, Easy Fix

**Subject:** _“I’m tired of doomscrolling too.”_
**Body:**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/ec275f10-8a49-4bc5-b6e5-feaab58391ab/screencapture-milled-werenotreallystrangers-com-im-tired-of-doomscrolling-too-zCFmZACBAS2GIS3A-2024-12-20-05_20_15-edit.png?t=1734701251)

**Why It Works:**

- Relatable hook (doomscrolling) → Valuable content → Soft CTA.

- WNRS sells by helping you feel understood, not pressured.

- People like to BUY, but they don’t like to be sold to

### Example 3: Emotional Affirmation

**Subject:** _“there’s something you need to hear”_
**Body:**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/dbe98be8-74cb-4741-8604-17de5e44a039/screencapture-milled-werenotreallystrangers-com-theres-something-u-need-to-hear-hh5AgH2CIig3b97u-2024-12-20-05_21_52-edit.png?t=1734701257)

**Why It Works:**

- The bold statement immediately connects with readers’ emotions.

- Only 1-2 sentences

- It frames the discount as self-care, not consumerism.

### Key Takeaways

- **You DON’T need to follow what everybody else is doing.**

- **Create your own style, and experiment with the possibilities of your email marketing**

- **Simplicity cuts through the noise.**

- **Emotions sell better than discounts alone.**

- **Soft CTAs resonate better when paired with meaningful messaging**

entries.title: How to Execute Email Marketing in 4 Hours Per Week
entries.summary: If you’re running an eCommerce store and feel like you “don’t have time” for email marketing, this one’s for you.
entries.body:
Hey, it’s Max from _The Inbox Newsletter_.

If you’re running an eCommerce store and feel like you “don’t have time” for email marketing, this one’s for you.

Here’s the truth:
You _don’t need 20 hours a week_. You can drive serious revenue with just **4 focused hours**.

Here’s how to make every minute count.

## Hour 0-0.5: Plan Your Campaigns

**Why It Matters:**
Most people waste time figuring out what to send at the last minute. The strategy / idea behind your emails is what drives the most revenue, so you can’t rush this…

Plan once, and execution becomes easy.

**What to Do:**

- Go through your past emails from the past 30-90 days and take note of what emails and angles produced the most clicks and revenue

- Look around [reallygoodemails.com](http://reallygoodemails.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-execute-email-marketing-in-4-hours-per-week) and [milled.com](http://milled.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-execute-email-marketing-in-4-hours-per-week) for inspiration

- **Use a Simple Recurring Framework:** Plan 3 campaigns per week with a regular schedule: **Mondays: Product Highlight:** Showcase a product’s benefits and features.

- **Wednesdays: Customer Story/Testimonial:** Build trust and social proof.

- **Saturdays: Educational Content:** Share tips related to your products (e.g., “5 Ways to Style Your New Sneakers”).

- **OPTIONAL:** Add urgency or offer within those emails if you are running a sale.

Use a basic spreadsheet or tool like Airtable to map out your campaigns for the week.

By the end of Hour 1, you know **what** you’re sending and **when**.

## Hour 0.5-1.5: Write 3 Emails

**Why It Matters:**
Writing doesn’t have to take hours if you stick to proven formats and use ChatGPT.

We don’t need to write essays in our emails (customers don’t want to read that)… just short, quick, punchy copy.

**What to Do:**

- **Pick One Goal Per Email:** Don’t overwhelm readers with too much info.

- **Use a Plug-and-Play Structure:****Headline:** “John, don’t miss this [product/offer].”

- **Hook:** State a benefit or address a pain point in 1–2 sentences.

- **CTA:** (e.g., “Shop Now,” “Learn More”).

- **Body:** Keep it short, visually clear, and focused on one message.

- **CTA:** End with ONE clear call-to-action (e.g., “Shop Now,” “Learn More”).

- **Templates Are Your Friend:** Write a basic template for product highlights, urgency emails, or content updates.

- Reuse and tweak it each week for efficiency.

Write once, reuse often. Keep it simple.

## Hour 1.5-3: Design & Schedule

**Why It Matters:**
Designing and scheduling all your campaigns at once saves mental energy and time.

**What to Do:**

- Look around [reallygoodemails.com](http://reallygoodemails.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-execute-email-marketing-in-4-hours-per-week) and [milled.com](http://milled.com/?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-execute-email-marketing-in-4-hours-per-week) for inspiration

- Find an email you like to replicate,

- **Use Simple Tools:** Use tools like **Klaviyo**, or Figma for clean, consistent designs. Keep it light: Clean header, product image, and a CTA button.

- Stick to your brand fonts and colors (no overthinking).

- **Batch Your Scheduling:** Schedule all 3–4 campaigns for the week in Klaviyo.

- Send at least **1-2 morning campaigns** (8–10 AM) and test a mid-day send (5–7 PM).

PS - My [email design templates](https://blog.wellcopy.net/email-templates?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-execute-email-marketing-in-4-hours-per-week) will make this process A LOT faster…

### Hour 3-4: Analyze & Optimize

**Why It Matters:**
You don’t improve what you don’t measure. Having 30-60 minutes ACTUALLY set aside will force you to do it.

Look BEYOND campaigns… click around your flows, pop-up form, etc

See what you can find.

I still set time aside every week to just aimlessly click around Klaviyo to see what insights I can find… you’ll be shocked with how much you can learn.

**What to Do:**

- **Review the Week’s Results:****Open Rate:** Above 40%? If not, tweak segmentation and subject lines.

- **Click Rate:** Above 1%? If not, simplify your CTA.

- **Revenue:** Which email generated the most sales?

- **Make Adjustments:** Test a different subject line style next week (e.g., curiosity vs. urgency).

- If clicks are low, simplify the email design and CTA.

- **Take Notes:** Write down what worked (and what didn’t) so you can adjust in future weeks.

I have a video coming out in the next couple weeks going more in-depth on this process, so be on the lookout!

entries.title: How to Boost Your Email Open Rates in 60 Days (Without Burning Your List)
entries.summary: If your open rates are dipping below 40%, you’ve got a deliverability problem. Inbox providers are punishing you.
entries.body:
Hey, it’s Max from _The Inbox Newsletter_.

If your open rates are dipping below 40%, you’ve got a deliverability problem. Inbox providers are punishing you.

Low opens = emails landing in spam or promotions = wasted money.

The good news? **You can turn it around in just 60 days**.

Here’s how.

### Step 1: Clean Your List (Week 1)

**The Problem:**
You’re probably sending emails to disengaged subscribers who haven’t opened your emails in months. This tanks your sender reputation.

**The Fix:**

- Create engaged segments in Klaviyo: **14-Day Engaged:** Opened/clicked an email in the past 14 days.

- **30-Day Engaged:** Opened/clicked in the last 30 days.

- **60-Day Engaged:** Opened/clicked in the last 60 days.

**Action:**
For the next 2 weeks, ONLY send campaigns to your **14-day engaged list**.
This will immediately boost open rates and signal to inbox providers that people like your emails.

### Step 2: Send Better Emails (Weeks 1–4)

**The Problem:**
Your emails might not be compelling enough to open. Harsh, but true.

**The Fix:**

- **Subject Lines That Pop**: Ask questions: “Still looking for the perfect [product]?”

- Add urgency: “Last Chance – Your 10% Off Ends Tonight.”

- Personalize: “John, Don’t Miss This Secret Sale.”

- **Keep It Clean**: Avoid spammy words like _free_, _act now_, or too many emojis (e.g., 🔥🔥🔥).

- Stick to a clean sender name like _[Your Brand] or The Team at [Your Brand]_.

- **Text-Based Emails:** Use plain-text emails to mimic personal messages – they often outperform flashy designs.

### Step 3: Optimize Campaign Timing (Weeks 2–6)

**The Problem:**
You’re sending emails when your audience isn’t active.

**The Fix:**

- Test send times: Start with mornings (8–10 AM) or atfernoons (1-3 PM).

- Use Klaviyo’s **Smart Send Time** feature to find the best time for your list.

- Segment by time zones for international audiences.

### Step 4: Warm Up Your Sending Volume (Weeks 3–8)

**The Problem:**
If you’ve been sending to your entire list with low engagement, inbox providers have flagged you as spammy.

**The Fix:**

- Gradually expand your audience: Weeks 1–2: Send to the **14-day engaged list**.

- Weeks 3–4: Expand to the **30-day engaged list**.

- Weeks 5–6: Include the **60-day engaged list** if open rates are stable above 40%.

**Why It Works:**
You’re rebuilding trust with inbox providers by showing that recipients are opening and engaging with your emails.

### Step 5: Stay Consistent (Weeks 4–8)

**The Problem:**
Inconsistent sending trains inbox providers to distrust your emails.

**The Fix:**

- Send **3 campaigns per week** to your engaged segments.

- Focus on value-driven content: Product benefits

- Customer stories

- Educational tips

- Sneak peeks or exclusives

**The 60-Day Outcome:**
Follow this process, and you’ll:

- Rebuild your sender reputation.

- Land in inboxes instead of spam.

- Consistently hit open rates of **40-50%+**.

Want a full breakdown of email deliverability hacks?

Check out my **"**[**Get Out of Spam Guide**](https://gamma.app/docs/Get-Out-of-Spam-ASAP-o2qc6ges1re9r0s?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-boost-your-email-open-rates-in-60-days-without-burning-your-list)**"**, I share the exact strategy we used to hit 50% open rates for a fresh Klaviyo account in just 6 weeks.

Let’s get those emails opened. 🚀

entries.title: Non-Discount Email Campaign Topics
entries.summary: Anybody can make money with email marketing by throwing around crazy discounts.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s talk about generating email revenue WITHOUT discounts.

… AND Big news in this newsletter if you scroll down 👀

## Non-Discount Email Marketing

Anybody can make money with email marketing by throwing around crazy discounts.

Not everybody can make money with email marketing without sending discounts…

And there’s a fine balance and methodology to doing it correctly.

There are a couple main factors that go in to making non-discount email marketing actually work.

First, we need to find and create topics that our customers actually care about and would be interested in reading.

Second, we need to tie in our topics to our products and try to position our brand as a solution to some problem.

And third, we need to use engaging copy and high-converting design.

Today, I’m going to be sharing with you how to solve the first two factors…

## 50 Non-Discount Email Campaign Topics

Save this list so you can use it next time you’re creating a campaign calendar!

- One Benefit Feature: Pick one benefit from your product and make a whole email just talking about that one thing.

- One Feature: Pick one feature about your product and focus the entire email on it.

- FAQ: Address a frequently asked question in depth to educate and reassure customers.

- What’s Inside: Outline exactly what the customer is getting (e.g., ingredients, materials, add-ons).

- How It’s Made: Share how your product is made to build trust and intrigue.

- How to Use: Show customers how to use the product effectively with tips and instructions.

- Back in Stock: Announce the return of a popular product to create urgency.

- Trending: Highlight products currently performing well.

- Testimonials: Showcase reviews to boost credibility and social proof.

- Us vs Them: Compare your product to alternatives and emphasize your advantages.

- Myths vs Facts: Address misconceptions in your niche and position your product as the solution.

- Blog Promo: Drive traffic to a blog post that provides value or ties into your product.

- Research Study Highlight: Use research to validate the effectiveness of your product.

- Holiday Email: Tie your product to a holiday, real or fun.

- Progress Update: Share recent company milestones or achievements.

- Customer Transformation: Highlight real-life stories of customers who benefited from your product.

- Before vs After: Showcase before-and-after comparisons to demonstrate your product’s value.

- Puzzles/Riddles: Engage customers with brain teasers or fun challenges.

- Note From the Founder: Share personal insights or updates directly from the founder/CEO.

- Gift Guide: Curate a list of products for gifting occasions.

- Treat Yourself: Promote self-care with products designed to pamper or reward the customer.

- Media Publications: Highlight media coverage and press mentions.

- Behind the Scenes: Offer a look at your company processes or team.

- Tips and Tricks: Provide hacks or advice for getting the most out of your product.

- UGC Content: Feature user-generated content like customer photos or reviews.

- Sneak Peek: Tease upcoming products or features to build anticipation.

- Flashback Friday/Throwback Thursday: Share nostalgic content from your brand’s past.

- Staff Picks: Highlight products or tools recommended by your team.

- Brand Values: Reinforce your core values and mission to build trust with customers.

- Customer of the Month: Feature a standout customer and their story.

- “Why We Exist” Story: Share why the brand was created and the problem it solves.

- From Prototype to Product: Show the evolution of your product, from idea to reality.

- Day in the Life: Show how your product fits into a customer’s daily routine.

- Real-Life Scenarios: Highlight specific ways your product solves real, relatable problems.

- User Journeys: Showcase how customers use your product in unique ways.

- Ingredient Spotlight: Highlight a single ingredient or material and its benefits.

- Sustainability in Action: Share specific examples of how your brand is environmentally conscious.

- What’s the Science?: Break down the science behind how your product works.

- Lifestyle Pairing: Offer suggestions on pairing your product with other habits.

- Product Care Tips: Educate customers on maintaining your product for longevity.

- Step-by-Step Guides: Provide actionable, step-by-step instructions for specific uses.

- Beyond the Product: Offer niche-related tips that add value beyond the product itself.

- Style Quiz or Calculator: Help customers find the perfect product fit with an interactive quiz.

- Seasonal Checklist: Provide a seasonal prep checklist with relevant tips.

- Customer Challenges: Encourage customers to complete a 7-day or 30-day challenge.

- Vote on This!: Let your audience vote on upcoming features, names, or designs.

- Interactive True or False: Debunk myths with an engaging quiz format.

- Most Loved Features: Highlight top features your customers rave about.

- Customer Milestone Celebration: Celebrate achievements like “50,000 happy customers.”

- Meet the Makers: Introduce the people behind your product, from artisans to designers.

entries.title: Quicks Tips for Holiday Email Marketing
entries.summary: Even though Black Friday is over, people are still going to be buying as we rush into the Christmas gifting season.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s talk about holiday emails 🎄

## December Email Marketing

It’s December - and that means it’s almost Christmas time.

Even though Black Friday is over, people are still going to be buying as we rush into the Christmas gifting season.

There are a few angles I’ve seen work exceptionally well in this time, so I want to outline a few of them here so you can make the most out of the season.

## Gift Guide Emails

People are going to be shopping mainly for their loved ones in this time period.

We want to speak directly to that and talk about our products from a gifting point of view.

Send emails that call out certain types of people that would enjoy your product.

“Perfect for a busy mother”

“Your girlfriend will adore you for this”

“Not sure what to get your little brother? We got you”

Statements like this will hit home with people looking for gifts.

## Gift Yourself Emails

Who says you can’t get yourself Christmas gifts?

Emails that tell people to shop for themself actually do pretty well.

At the very least you can mention something like “Send this to your loved ones so they know what to get you for Christmas” so the customers will send your store to other people.

## Use Urgency - Shipping by Christmas

We don’t have the best deals of the year on our side like we do for Black Friday, but we do have shipping urgency.

Christmas is on December 25th, meaning most people should order by December 18th if they want their product in time by Christmas.

Use this to your advantage in your messaging.

Use phrases like:

- Guaranteed shipping by Christmas

- Don’t put off your gifting to the last minute

- Get ahead of the Christmas shipping delays

## Use The New Year to Your Advantage

2025 is around the corner and that means people will be getting New Year’s Resolutions.

Especially if you’re in the health industry, use this to your advantage.

Encourage people to start the new year off right, build their resolutions, and buy our products to accomplish them!

entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

It’s Black Friday…

## Quick tips for Black Friday

Happy Black Friday!

It’s going to be a crazy day / couple of days.

You’re busy… I’m busy… here are a couple quick tips.

**Tip #1: Some Shit Will Go Wrong… Keep Your Cool**

If there’s one thing I’ve learned from my past experience… it’s that nothing goes to plan. A code will stop working, the site will malfunction, an email will have an error in it, etc

It’s bound to happen in this crazy period.

Just keep your cool. One mistake doesn’t make or break your BFCM.

Accept that something will go wrong so it’s not a shocker when it does happen.

**Tip #2: Resend Emails After 4 Hours**

If you didn’t have time to make a ton of unique emails for this period, just do more resends.

You want at least 2 touch points per day over the next few days.

Customers really won’t notice if you just resend the same email but with a different Subject Line and Preview Text.

Feel free to resend the same email multiple times if you have to… over BFCM I’d rather oversend than undersend.

**Tip #3: Don’t Worry About Deliverability**

If you’re worried about BFCM segmentation… don’t be.

This is the one time of year you can let loose and go crazy.

Sending a couple of emails to larger lists won’t do lasting damage to your reputation and put you in the spam folder permanently.

Go crazy this week… then get strict with segmentation over the next 1-2 months to clean up any reputation issues you may have gained over BFCM.

You have my permission!

entries.title: This Email Myth is a Lie
entries.summary: Today we’re talking about the biggest myth in email marketing, why it exists, and why it’s BS (kinda).
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Today we’re talking about the biggest myth in email marketing, why it exists, and why it’s BS (kinda).

### The Biggest Myth in Email Marketing

I was asked about this topic the other day and it’s pretty insane how big of a misconception it is.

**It’s the idea that you** **_need_****HTML sections weaved in your emails.**

If you don’t know what I mean by HTML sections, they are essentially just the native Klaviyo text or blocks.

So, rather than just uploading images completely in your emails, HTML sections are made purely in Klaviyo or whatever email platform you’re using.

Essentially people say you need to weave text boxes in your image emails.

This notion is just false… to an extent.

**Why Does This Myth Exist?**

Everybody will say that HTML sections will help your deliverability because including only images in your emails will look “spammy”.

Most people who say this have never actually tested it (I have, there’s no difference as long as you do it right)

That statement does have some merit. It’s true… to an extent.

If you only attach massive image files in your emails and have absolutely zero HTML, in your email then you could end up with a higher spam folder rate.

But there’s a simple way to overcome it, which we’ll talk about shortly

**Why This Myth Is Harmful**

Interweaving images with HTML (text) sections brings a ton of issues.

For one, HTML sections will get altered at a very high frequency by inbox providers.

**Light vs Dark mode on iPhone for example is a major problem for HTML sections.**

Some people have light mode on their device and some have dark mode.

Based on what a user has, your HTML sections will be altered and unreadable at times.

I see it way too often, dark blue text in an HTML section whose background gets turned black because of dark mode… then you’re completely unable to read the message.

**Also, your sizing will get all messed up based on a user’s settings.**

Old folk with bad eyesight often have phone settings that enlarge text for them.

This will completely throw off the proportions and spacing of your HTML sections.

It’s very difficult to work around these issues and doing it adds way too much complexity to your processes.

More complexity leads to a higher probability of error.

**How To Overcome This Partially True Myth**

As we discussed, this myth does have some merit.

If you only use massive image files in your email you could look spammy.

**But an easy way to overcome this is just by having HTML in the footer of your email.**

Use native text to give your company location, list out some features of the brand, and your unsubscribe section.

This alone can be enough HTML to bring you out of “spammy” territory.

An extra bonus is to add “invisible text” to your footer.

Use a black background with size 2 black text with 500+ words from the website copy and pasted.

This will be a tiny little sliver in your email that isn’t readable, but has a ton of HTML data from an inbox provider’s POV.

It’s an easy way to ensure you have enough HTML and land in the inbox.

As far as the rest of your email, design on Figma and just upload images!

entries.title: Abandoned Cart Flow Hacks
entries.summary: I want to pack a couple quick tips in your abandoned cart / abandoned checkout flows to make you some more money…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I want to pack a couple quick tips in your abandoned cart / abandoned checkout flows to make you some more money…

Let’s do it.

## Hack #1: Include Your Welcome Offer for Non-Buyers

Most stores offer 10% OFF or something similar for first time buyers.

If someone hasn’t bought before and abandoned their cart, why not remind them of their welcome offer?

This will help with conversions immensely.

Add a conditional split at the top of your flow logic and split based on if someone has bought before or not.

For those who have bought from you before, send them regular abandoned cart emails.

For those who haven’t bought from you before, include a simple line of text in all of your emails that reminds them of the first order discount.

## Hack #2: Let People Know If They Have Free Shipping

Most stores offer free shipping on orders over a threshold, such as $100.

You can add a trigger split in Klaviyo for the value of someone’s cart.

For people who have a value over $100, you can just simply let them know that they have free shipping.

For those below the threshold, let them know where the threshold is and how they can unlock free shipping.

BONUS - You can even stack the first two hacks together… if someone has never bought before AND their cart value is over $100, you can tell them about the welcome discount and that they have free shipping.

## Hack #3: Only Offer Discounts To Non-Buyers

If you’re tight on margins, you don’t need to give everybody a discount on their cart.

I recommend only offering discounts towards the end of your flow to save on margins. Rather than offering a discount email 1, offer it on email 3 or later.

This way you can try to convert someone without a discount.

You can take it a step further and only offer the discount to specific people, like people who haven’t purchased before.

Simply add a conditional split (just like Hack #1) and split based on if someone has bought before.

Then create your emails with discounts and without based on if they have bought before.

This isn’t necessary, but it will help you save on margins.

If you want more info, here’s an **[83 page Cart Abandon Email Flow Guide »](https://gamma.app/docs/Abandoned-Cart-83-Page-Guide-5nnqionb8jhd6z6?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=abandoned-cart-flow-hacks)**

inspiration.note:
Something important to keep in mind with your emails is that you need to put your offer way up high at the top of the email.

This way the customer doesn’t have to scroll on the email… right in their face is the offer which can get them to purchase.

Use this email as an outline!

entries.title: Black Friday Email Tips
entries.summary: I want to make sure you make the absolute most out of the season…
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

BLACK FRIDAY IS 16 DAYS AWAY.

I want to make sure you make the absolute most out of the season…

So I’m going to rapid fire answer some of the frequently asked questions I get around the BFCM season…

### How Should My Black Friday Emails Look?

Don’t overthink it…

You don’t need to do anything special. In fact, **you should try to keep things as minimal and simple as possible.**

The goal of our emails is to get the click onto the site which will give the info needed to make a purchase.

Keep your emails simple and to the point.

If you want to take them up a notch design-wise, you can use a darker theme to make it branded for BFCM.

Here’s an example of a great, simple BFCM email:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/a84f6a42-6525-4a28-a55f-f828f21064a3/screencapture-milled-kaged-muscle-us-get-25-off-everything-w-code-bfcm-EmtUOznlSiVfii4e-2024-11-13-05_53_59-edit.png?t=1731506263)

Kaged Email

### How Many Emails Should I Send?

Depends on your brand size and goals.

Everybody no matter the brand size should be sending at least 1 email every day from Early Access, through Black Friday and until the end of Cyber Monday.

Ideally 2 emails a day is what we want.

No, you won’t bother your customers too much. They’re getting hit with a crazy amount from other brands… if you aren’t sending multiple your emails will get buried.

Shoot for 2 a day.

### When Should I Start Sending Emails?

I like to start with an Early Access offer that begins on Monday the week of BFCM.

The offer is a bit lower than the BF offer, but you focus your messaging on limited stock, priority shipping, etc.

Then run that through the following Tuesday or Wednesday after Cyber Monday.

### Should I Use Text Based Emails?

YES!

Text-based emails are going to be your best friend.

They stand out in the graphic-heavy inbox, they seem personaly for the customer, and they convert like crazy.

The best part… they take no time to create!

### What Do I Do With My Flows During BFCM?

Well, for our clients we create custom BFCM flows with the offer and tighter time frames.

If you’re strapped on time, I would just add a text box or a bar under the logo in each flow email that says “Black Friday Live XX% OFF: Shop Now »”

Then you can just keep your current flows live.

If you can update flows… make them branded to BFCM, very urgency focused, break down the offer in each email, and change the time frames to be 6 hours between emails!

Have more questions? Watch this [BFCM tips video »](https://youtu.be/JkAaIqhC_JY?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=black-friday-email-tips)

These emails will crush for you and save you so much time on design.

entries.title: The Perfect Black Friday Email Schedule
entries.summary: Black Friday is just a couple weeks away… You may already have started your sales, hope it’s going well.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Black Friday is just a couple weeks away… You may already have started your sales, hope it’s going well.

I want to talk about what some days in BFCM should look like.

## Black Friday / Cyber Monday Schedules

BFCM is the one part of the year where brands who haven’t sent emails in ages decide to pop back in and bombard their subscribers.

It’s going to be a CRAZY time in the email inbox…

I’m talking 50+ emails an hour being received by some people lol.

For this reason, we need to attack with frequency so our emails don’t get lost.

If we send an email at 9am, that email will be unfindable at 11am as other emails drown it out.

**FREQUENCY IS WHAT WINS IN BFCM.**

I’m going to give you a few daily send schedules for you to choose from based on your level of availability.

## Level 1: One Email + Resend

This is for the extremely busy individuals.

**9AM:** Send email 1

**4pm:** Resend email 1 with different SL and PT

## Level 2: Two Emails + Resend

Okay… now we’re starting to add a bit more volume and get fancy with segmentation. This would be my recommended send schedule for most busy founders to get some juice out of the holiday but not do too much.

**9AM:** Send email 1

**12pm:** Send email 2 (can be text based)

**4pm:** Resend email 1 with different SL and PT to people who haven’t opened an email today.

## Level 3: Two Emails + 2 Resends

**8AM:** Send email 1

**12pm:** Resend email 1 with different SL and PT to people who didn’t open the email.

**3pm**: Send email 2

**7pm:** Resend email 2 with different SL and PT to people who didn’t open email 2.

## Level 4: Three Emails + 1 Resend

3 unique emails straight up… delivered to everybody. Then a resend to clean up anybody who haven’t bought. This is going to be my team and mine’s most used layout

**8AM:** Send email 1

**12pm:** Send email 2

**4pm:** Send email 3

**7pm:** Resend any email with different SL and PT to everyone.

The more frequency you send with, the better.

This is the one time of the year you can really spam your list and get away with it lol.

Don’t worry about deliverability, we can spend the next few months being very careful. We want to be sure we make the most of the BFCM season.

**[Here’s a 25 doc with more hacks and tips for crushing your BFCM season »](https://gamma.app/docs/2024-Ecommerce-Black-Friday-Cyber-Monday-Plan-60ks5pzgafty2ul?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=the-perfect-black-friday-email-schedule)**

entries.title: High Levers in Your Email Flows
entries.summary: Let’s talk about THE most important part of email marketing… Flows.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Let’s talk about THE most important part of email marketing… **Flows.**

(Flows are your automated emails that fire after somebody completes a specific action, such as abandoning a cart).

PS - Here’s a free 40+ page guide breaking down all flows with examples that have made my clients and I $15M+ document: [Here »](https://gamma.app/docs/Email-Marketing-Flows-rfbgyj0cpy26gkx?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=high-levers-in-your-email-flows)

## Don’t Get Carried Away With Email Flows

KYFSS (Keep your flows simple, stupid)

When you have advanced, hyper segmented emails with all sorts of splits, it becomes very difficult for you to make changes and try to even understand what is going on.

**What’s simple can be optimized.**

We only want bases in place and focus on the 80/20 rule.

What are the high levers in your flows that you should focus on that will drive the majority of the results?

**The first high lever is having at least 1 email in every flow live (don’t mess this one up)**

Let’s break them down one by one with the highest levers.

### Welcome Flow

**Flow Purpose:** Brand intro emails set up for when somebody joins your email list to educate them on your brand.

**High Levers:**

- Nail the first email. Deliver the discount / incentive at the top of the email and give brief background.

- Adding urgency emails about the discount expiring.

- Minimum 3 emails.

### Site Abandon Flow

**Flow Purpose:** Email(s) set up for when someone visits your site but doesn't click any products or go any further down the funnel.

**High Levers:**

- 1 email minimum

- Nail the time delay… test 1 hour vs 4 hours to start

- Showcase your bestsellers, ideally as many as possible

- Offer support if they have questions

### Browse Abandon Flow

**Flow Purpose:** Email(s) set up for when somebody views a product but doesn't go further down the funnel. We want them to buy!

**High Levers:**

- Find your winning time delay for the first email (typically 30-60 mins after event)

- Minimum 3 emails

- Keep emails simple

- Show the exact product the customer left behind

### Cart Abandon Flow

**Flow Purpose:** Emails set up for when somebody abandons a product in their cart.

**High Levers:**

- Make sure you have this flow (most only have checkout abandon)

- Utilize text-based emails

- Feature buttons at the top of every email

- Minimum 3 emails

- Introduce discount at the end of the flow

### Checkout Abandon Flow

**Flow Purpose:** Emails set up for when somebody abandons checkout, meaning they got to entering their card info (farther down funnel than adding to cart)

**High Levers:**

- Strategically overcome objections

- Utilize text-based emails

- Feature buttons at the top of every email

- Minimum 3 emails

- Introduce discount at the end of the flow

### Post Purchase Flow

**Flow Purpose:** Emails set up after someone makes a purchase thanking them and potentially getting upsells.

**High Levers:**

- Have an immediate thank you email from the founder

- Subtly upsell your products

- Promote your community / social media

### Winback Flow

**Flow Purpose:** Email(s) set up for someone months after their last purchase encouraging them to come back.

**High Levers:**

- Address them directly that it’s been awhile since their last purchase

- Give them specific product recommendations based off their last purchase

- Set up a discount with urgency

There’s A LOT that goes into flows… but it’s important to at least get the basics.

Watch this in-depth video of me breaking down each core flow above: [https://youtu.be/H4jF8sr-e88?si=B496OfRqp5PU2d92](https://youtu.be/H4jF8sr-e88?si=B496OfRqp5PU2d92&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=high-levers-in-your-email-flows)

entries.title: Black Friday Cyber Monday Tips
entries.summary: Many brands will be promoting offers starting the beginning of November.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Black Friday is ALMOST here…

Let’s make sure we make the most of it.

Here are some Black Friday / Cyber Monday Tips…

## Tip #1: Utilize 3 Different Events

Black Friday is now more than just “Friday”.

Many brands will be promoting offers starting the beginning of November.

I would recommend doing something similar, but not to that extent.

My go-to layout is:

- Early Access 1 week before Black Friday which lasts 7 days

- Black Friday which lasts 3-4 days

- Cyber Monday which last 3-4 days

You want to make sure you have different offers for each.

This will keep your list engaged and not feeling like they are seeing the same thing over and over again.

## Tip #2: Use Different Types of Offers

Mix and match your offers for the different events, rather than doing one all the way through.

This will keep your list engaged throughout and encourage more than one purchase.

### Discount Offers

- **Sitewide Discounts**: Offer a flat percentage discount on all products (e.g., 20% off everything).

- **Product Specific Discounts:** Frame as "up to XX% OFF" and have different deals to encourage browsing.

- **Tiered Discounts**: Increase the discount based on the amount spent (e.g., 10% off $50, 20% off $100, 30% off $200).

- **Alternating Flash Sales**: Limited-time discounts on select products or categories, changing every few hours.

### Bundle Deals

- **Buy One, Get One Free (BOGO)**: Offer a free item with the purchase of another.

- **Product Bundles**: Create special bundles at a discounted price (e.g., a skincare set, tech bundle).

## Tip #3: Send Multiple Emails in One Day

So many people will be sending emails…

If you send an email at 9am it may be lost in the users inbox by 12pm.

Send emails in the morning, afternoon, and night so you are always in the customers face.

Black Friday you get an exception for being spammy… everybody will be looking to buy and they want to see your offers.

EXTRA POINTS - Resend emails to non-openers same day. If someone didn’t open your 9am email, resend it to them at 3pm!

## Tip #4: Update Your Flows

You’re going to want to update your flows to have tighter time frames and be specific to your offer.

This has a HUGE effect on conversions.

Just use 3-4 emails per abandonment flow and welcome flow and have them separated by a few hours with extreme urgency.

Don’t worry about being spammy… Black Friday is the only time of year you can get away with being scammy lol

## Tip #5: Update Your Pop-Ups

Same as flows, we want to update our pop-ups.

Simply put your Black Friday offer in your pop-up and you’ll get a sh*t ton of sign-ups.

The customer doesn’t need to sign up to get the offer but many people still do.

This will add a ton of members into your newsletter.

## Tip #6: Use Text-Based Emails

Text based emails absolutely crush it for conversions.

They're so simple, personal, and help you stand out while everybody else is focused on design.

This will also take strain off of your design team and allow you to send 2x-3x a day no problem.

Bonus points if you make the email come from the founder, the personal touch goes a long ways during this salesy time period.

If you want more tips on destroying BFCM watch this video: _**[BFCM Guide](https://youtu.be/JkAaIqhC_JY?si=FQsRpJwkxxAzPpve&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=black-friday-cyber-monday-tips)**_

If you are able to create different sections on your site with different price levels like the example, I would highly recommend it.

No need to go crazy on design, keep it simple like this example.

entries.title: Email Design Conversion Tip
entries.summary: I don’t see anybody talking about this… but it makes our clients a lot of money.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I don’t see anybody talking about this… but it makes our clients a lot of money.

## The Problem With Many Emails

Okay… so a lot of the emails that we send are very specific about certain products, collections, etc

But what if somebody doesn’t want the specific product your highlighting?

Or what if they already have it?

What if you show 4 products in your email but the customer already has all 4?

**Well, then you’re just sending them to a dead end.**

Another point…

You probably hear me also talking about how we want to provide value to our list.

We want to give our subscribers tips, tricks, and hacks that they can use in their every day life.

But… how do you make money off of these emails? Without having a dead-end email?

## Convert Customers on Autopilot

The secret to overcoming these issues is probably not what you’re expecting.

It’s actually just by utilizing a part of your email that you’re probably overlooking.

Your footer!

Footers are incredibly important because they are the only part of your emails that are repeated in every email.

Your footer shouldn't just be slapped together…

Take time putting together an on-brand, clean footer.

And more importantly,

**We've found it to be extremely effective to put Shop Now or Shop By Category buttons in your footer.**

Example:

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/68ee93a1-e068-48a7-ae38-641dae71d424/Screenshot_2024-11-01_at_9.26.47_AM.png?t=1730478414)

Footer Example

## Why Use Footer Buttons?

Think of footer navigation buttons as the nav buttons you probably have in the header of your website.

This allows people to shop on your site no matter what your email is!

Somebody can go through your product highlight email, or your value-based email, get to the bottom, and click buttons and go shop on the site.

Having buttons in your footer lets your engaged readers who made it to the bottom of your email to continue shopping based on what they may be looking for.

*Important - don't use these buttons in the top of your email, we've seen this hurt conversions as it overwhelms the hero section of your email.

**Often times, we see footer buttons on campaigns generate MORE clicks than the actual body of the email.**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/bdc5b6e4-4d4b-432f-9d6f-ea8b6ecedf33/GIKAhdFXcAARFBU__1_.jpeg?t=1730478581)

Clicks in Footer

**In summary, add buttons to your footer and you will make more money.**

inspiration.note:

A clean hero section that doesn’’t try to do too much, and then a strong informational bridge section.

The use of icons and subheadlines allows the reader to skim the email and understand it’s points without too much effort.

entries.title: Text-Based Emai Marketing
entries.summary: I want to talk today about text-based emails… as they are frequently our best performing emails for our clients.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I want to talk today about text-based emails… as they are frequently our best performing emails for our clients.

But why?

And how do you make them convert?

Let’s get into it.

## The Problem

The customer has a fried attention span.

They aren’t going to read or want to open boatloads of information in any email.

They get overwhelmed. And they don’t read any of it.

Plus, writing a sales letter with 100+ words can increase sales resistance.

**When someone opens an email full of blocks upon blocks of text they KNOW you are trying to sell them.**

By going overboard, you make it seem like the only way you CAN make sales is by spending forever trying to justify why the customer should buy.

Rather than just simply stating it.

A similar principle can be applied to email design.

If you’re way over the top, you’ll be distracting the customer from your true CTAs and selling points.

The simpler your design is, generally the better your emails perform.

## The Solution

Luckily, there is a way to overcome these issues in your email marketing.

Remove all friction and get straight to the point.

It’s with **Text-Based Emails.**

You’ve probably heard of them, but they genuinely don’t get enough praise.

Text-based emails are precisely how they sound - no pictures, just words.

And the emails show up in the customer’s native inbox provider’s email format, so when they open it it will look like it’s coming from a friend.

Personal touch + simplicity + transparency = 💸 💸

The best part is that the text based emails will stand out in the inbox.

While everybody is going crazy with designs, colors, etc…

You stand alone.

Not many ecom brands utilize these enough

**Here’s an example from Magic Mind I received the other day:**

![](https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8c1a0a74-068b-41a6-8fbe-fd3e9290fce0/Screenshot_2024-10-28_at_5.56.05_AM.png?t=1730122982)

Tet Based Example

## Tips for High-Converting Text-Based Emails

- Keep it under 100 words

- Use the font “Arial” to make sure it looks as native to email platform as possible

- Only use 1-2 main CTAs

- Instead of a faceless brand, make it from the founder so it’s more personal Make sure to use the founder’s name in the Sender Name section when you send the email

- Add a “PS” section with a “My personal recommendation”

Watch this video of me upgrading a text based email from a popular shoe brand.

_**[4 minute video training »](https://youtu.be/LtncHYckaZc?si=Fk7Vfv9IckviXLx6&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=text-based-emai-marketing)**_

Simple. personal, and to the point.

entries.summary: I have a very important Public Service Announcement I need to make clear about email marketing.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

I have a very important Public Service Announcement I need to make clear about email marketing.

This will hopefully make your life easier and a lot less stressful.

## Stop focusing on the extra sh*t!

I have a private email marketing community of 641 members where anyone can ask questions or send email reviews and I respond every weekday morning to all questions.

I get a lot of questions about some crazy stuff… advanced email strategies and tactics I haven’t even heard of… from people just starting with email marketing.

Now, I've worked inside over 100 different 7-8 figure brands.

After working in that many accounts you start to notice what the winners are doing and what the losers are doing.

Let’s start with the losers… What are the losers doing?

The losers are the ones asking about what advanced cross-sell or extra flow they need to add to their 27 different flows they have live right now.

What are the winners doing?

They’re focusing on the basics. Dialing in their core flows. Staying consistent with email campaigns. Delivering high-quality content. And continuing to provide excellent customer service and product fulfillment.

**The basics genuinely carry 80%-90% of the results.**

**You have NO BUSINESS asking or trying to nail a strategy for advanced segmentation or advanced flows if you don't have the basics dialed.**

## What Are the Basics?

- Sending 2-3 email campaigns per week minimum (no crazy segmentation, just the general 90 day engaged list)

- Good pop-up form converting 6%+ of site traffic into subscribers

- Core flows Welcome flow (minimum 3 emails)

- Site abandon flow (1 email)

- Browse abandon flow (minimum 3 emails)

- Cart AND checkout abandon flows (minimum 3 emails)

- Post purchase flow (minimum 1 email thank you message)

That's it.

This is your sign to stop stressing about the extra shit.

Your results SUFFER every day you are wasting your time and mental effort coming up with advanced strategies. Stop it.

**Nail the basics, then build off of the basics.**

I share my screen and talk about what are the high levers they need to change to ad $50k/mo in email revenue.

entries.title: How to Write Email Copy That Converts
entries.summary: Email marketing copywriting is both very simple but very nuanced.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

Email marketing copywriting is both very simple but very nuanced.

I’m going to break it all down here for you.

Here’s how to write email marketing copy that actually sells.

## The 2024-2025 Customer Is Different

We need to understand this.

People aren’t taking in content like they used to.

Tik Tok, Instagram, etc have completely changed the game and **customers’ attention spans are getting cut by the day.**

People aren’t reading emails like they used to.

In fact, they aren’t reading them at all.

The modern customer is **skimming** emails, and in reality, you only have **3-4 seconds of your customer’s attention.**

As a result, you have to be extremely intentional with the copy you do use in your emails.

There are 3 main principles I like to follow…

## Core Copy Principle #1: Skimmable

The customer isn’t reading, they are skimming. We need to optimize our copy for this.

We want our customer to be able to glance at out email for 3 seconds and understand the gyst of our email.

Create skimmable copy by doing the following:

- Avoid blocks of text… these scare off customers

- Bold your main points… this will guide the customers on where their eyes should be going.

- Utilize subheadlines… notice what I’ve done in this email 😉

## Core Copy Principle #2: Clear and Concise

The customer's IQ drops by about 50% the second they open their email inbox. They're in zombie brain mode.

If we aren't clear with what we're giving them, they won't understand. If we aren't concise, they won't bother giving you the time.

- Short and sweet… you should have less than 100 words in your emails in most cases

- One takeaway per email… try not to throw too much at the customer. Ask yourself what the one takeaway is you want the customer to get from this email and only focus on that

## Core Copy Principle #3: Engaging

The customer is craving dopamine, we need to give it to them. We want our emails to be engaging enough to trigger dopamine in the customer’s brain. That will lead to a positive association with our brand and result in future opens and sales.

Again, we don’t have much of our customers’ time. We have to make the best use of it.

- Punchy… make your emails pack a punch by using powerful words and dense information.

- Informational… people love learning, if you are giving people value they will continue to engage

- Entertaining… no one wants a bland brand, give the customer something they can have fun with.

## Infographics!!!!

Less copy, more infographics.

Infographics blend images with text and are much more effective than blocks of copy.

Follow this copywriting guide for more info on the 9 types of infographics you should be using in your emails: _**[Email Copywriting Guide](https://gamma.app/docs/Ecommerce-Email-Marketing-Copywriting-That-Actually-Sells-j5oevb6i2mxjdtc?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=how-to-write-email-copy-that-converts)**_

I’d likely recommend putting the answer to the teaser at the bottom of the email so people can see if they’re right, not many people will rep;y like they prompted.

Great

entries.title: The Perfect Email Welcome Flow
entries.summary: The email Welcome Flow is THE most important set of emails for your brand.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

The email Welcome Flow is THE most important set of emails for your brand.

It is what will get customers to trust you enough to purchase either now or down the line.

If you screw it up, you botch your chance to make a sale.

## Welcome Flow Purpose

The Welcome Come is going to be a sequence of emails sent towards people who join the email list over a duration of 7-14 days.

A dialed in Welcome Flow allows you to **automate and predictably convert customers in the pre-purchase decision journey.**

The Welcome Flow is going to leave us with one of two outcomes…

A) Convert customers who were just curious and otherwise would have left your site.

B) Prime future customers for purchases now that all objections have been addressed.

Either way, we need a dialed email welcome flow to establish a positive and profitable relationship with the customer.

## Email 1 - Welcome

We want to really keep things brief in this email.

People are really only here for the discount and maybe get a quick summary of what your brand has to offer before they continue shopping.

We want the design to simple, clean, and easy to follow.

The goal is simply to get people to click.

**Content:**

- Deliver incentive

- Introduce brand-unique selling propositions

- Social proof

- Show bestseller

## Email 2 - Brand Story

People haven't purchased yet probably because you are a faceless brand that they randomly stumbled across in an ad.

We want to slowly get them to believe you are a real brand with a real mission.

Earn trust points and remind them of their discount.

This email will make sales, but the real purpose is to **prime them for a purchase down the line**

**Content:**

- Founding story

- Mission statement

- Show a face if possible (put a face to the name —> personal feel)

- Reminder of discount

## Email 3 - Brand Unique Selling Propositions

The customer now has a bit of trust from us, let's get them thinking we're awesome.

We want to lay out our benefits on a silver platter.

Give them all the info they need about your brand in an organized fashion.

**Content:**

- Highlight mission statement

- Explain why you stand out

- Remind of discount

## Email 4 - Discount Reminder

Now the customer knows a bit about your brand and believes you are legit.

We want to introduce some urgency and get them to cross the line that they haven't crossed.

Add some social proof and risk reversals and this email will crush.

**Content:**

- Add urgency to offer

- Risk reversals

- Give testimonials for trust

## Email 5 - Us vs Them

The elephant in the room at this point is your competitors.

Why should someone go with you vs someone else?

People love to see the pros and cons and they love to make a decision themself.

That's what we are providing them within this email.

**Content:**

- Address competitors vs you

- Outline brand USPs

- Distinguish your brand from others

## Email 6 - Testimonials

We want to make sure the customer KNOWS your product and brand are great.

Maybe they don't have a strong need for the product right now, that's fine.

They need to know that our product **will fulfill that need once the time comes.**

By creating a whole email out of this it will also prove we are confident in our product and will stand by it, which says a lot.

**Content:**

- Brand testimonials

- Media features

- Any content that proves your brand is legit.

## Email 7 - Last Chance

At this point, the customer has pretty much all the info they would need to make a purchase.

Most of your audience probably would buy from you but are waiting for the right time to do it.

By going hard on urgency here we force their hand.

**Content:**

- Time or urgency-based graphic

- Your discount is expiring

- Keep it simple

## Email 8 - Everything Okay?

So the customer didn't purchase right off the bat.

That's okay, most won't.

But we may be able to get a few more over the line with a nice personal touch text based email.

This will also prime the customer for future purchases, knowing that the brand owner is willing to reach out.

They may have further questions so we also want to let them know they can reply to the email.

**Content:**

- Text based email

- Remind of discount code

- Offer resources

entries.title: Automate Revenue With These Email Marketing Flows
entries.summary: The #1 best part of email marketing is your ability to create email automation that generates revenue for you on autopilot.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

The #1 best part of email marketing is your ability to create email automation that generates revenue for you on autopilot.

I’ve generated $15M with email flows and I’m going to breakdown everything you need to know in the most concise way possible.

**Let’s talk automated revenue** 🚀

## Email Marketing Flows

Flows are the automated emails that you set up once and they’ll start firing automatically based on a customer’s action, such as abandoning a cart.

Why should you use email flows?

Well, more money. We have some clients that we generate $500k/mo+ just with automated emails.

Flows also contribute to the customer experience via **personalization.**

Different customers at different parts of the customer journey need different information.

Set up once and **orders will automatically be coming in every day.**

Any email platform you use will have the ability to set up automations using triggers that fire on your Shopify.

**Here are all the flows you need and their purposes.**

#### Welcome Flow

This flow is 4-10 emails set up for when somebody joins your email list. This is debatably the most important flow since it is the customer’s first touchpoint with your brand.

One of two things should occur as a result of this flow. Option A is the customer makes their first purchase with your brand. Option B is the customer at least gets all the information they need and objections overcame so that they are primed to buy in the future.

Flow Content:

- Deliver the welcome discount

- Educate them on the brand

- Showcase your products

#### Site Abandon Flow

This is just 1 email set up for when someone visits your site but doesn't click any products. There are two reasons someone will enter this flow… they didn’t find a product they liked or they got distracted while browsing your site.

Either way, we want to be sure to remind them and nudge them to go back to browsing.

Flow Content:

- Offer a helping hand

- Bring them down the funnel (get them to view a product)

#### Browse Abandon Flow

This flow of 3-8 emails fires when someone views a product but doesn't end up adding to cart, going to checkout, or buying. There are a number of reasons why, but in most cases it's because they weren't fully bought in on the brand or the product.

Our purpose of this flow is to get someone farther down the funnel. Get them to go back to the item or find a different product they like more.

Flow Content:

- Remind them of the abandonment

- Intrigue them on the product.

- Give social proof.

#### Cart AND Checkout Abandon Flow

You've probably heard of these flows and for good reason.

By not having these properly setup and optimized you are quite literally leaving money on the table from people who were in the process of purchasing.

However, 90% of the brands I audit don't have a proper Cart Abandon Flow. Most brands only have a Checkout Abandon flow… (go check your trigger and see if it says ‘Checkout Started’ or ‘Added to Cart’)

Flow Content:

- Remind them of their abandonment

- Show them how awesome the product is

- Give social proof

- Reverse risk

#### Post Purchase Flow

This flow will fire right after someone makes a purchase. There are many different directions you can go with this flow… You could focus on community building, upselling / cross selling, getting the customer excited for the order, pushing for a review, etc

I like to keep it simple. Improve the customer experience with a heartfelt thank you, build the community, and then inform them on how to get the most out of their product.

Flow Content:

- Thank them sincerely

- Remove buyer's remorse and get them excited

- Light nudge to add to their order

- Get a review

#### Winback Flow

This flow is pretty straightforward, we just want to encourage another purchase from past customers. Your customers here are still receiving email campaigns, sales, and whatever else you're blasting to your list.

We recommend 3-4 email campaigns a week… so 99% of your retention and repeat purchases will come from your campaigns. For this reason, we keep the Winback Flow nice and simple. This is more for customer experience and to at least automated part of the customer journey.

Flow Content:

- Encourage repeat purchases to increase LTV

- Remind them to replenish

- Give recommendations

## Want ALL Of These Flows and Their Emails Completely Templatized And Optimized?

I actually just released my QuickFlow Email Templates which have ALL of these flows and their emails templatized with the exact strategy we use for over 50 7-8 figure ecommerce brands (and have generated $15M in automated revenue for).

These templates on average generate 20% of total ecommerce store revenue for our clients.

entries.title: Re: What email metrics should I be hitting?
entries.summary: This is a very important topic, and I have sent similar emails but I want to point these numbers out to you again.
entries.body:
Hey it’s Max from The Inbox Newsletter.

This is a very important topic, and I have sent similar emails but I want to point these numbers out to you again.

**Email Marketing Metrics to Shoot For.**

## Total Email Revenue

Metric: 40% of total revenue

In general, you want to be around the 40% mark for Klaviyo attributed revenue.

If you’re above 55%, you may want to consider funneling more profits into ads and new acquisition / conversion channels.

If you’re below 35% you likely are leaving email revenue on the table.

Clean up common mistakes that are high leveraged in returns with [this guide.](https://gamma.app/docs/5-Most-Expensive-Klaviyo-Mistakes-Youre-Probably-Making-and-how-t-3z9wti6uoijw7et?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=re-what-email-metrics-should-i-be-hitting)

## Campaign / Flow Revenue

Campaigns: 40-60% of total email revenue

Flows: 40-60% of total email revenue

Comparing your campaign vs your flow revenue is a great way to see where your lowest-hanging fruit is.

If you’re pulling 70% of revenue from campaigns, your flows likely need work and vise versa.

If you need help with campaigns, [follow this guide.](https://gamma.app/docs/7fbdn728kmpo91c?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=re-what-email-metrics-should-i-be-hitting)

If you need help with flows, [follow this guide.](https://gamma.app/docs/33moitfx8e2mdtz?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=re-what-email-metrics-should-i-be-hitting)

## Open Rates

Metric: 45%

If you’re open rates in your flows and campagin engaged lists are below this, you likely have deliverability issues.

The best fix is to immediately tighten your email list and ONLY send to a segment of people who have opened an email in the past 30 days.

Usually, our base segment for clients is a 90-120 day engaged list.

If you’re having open rate issues, [follow this guide on how we got to over 50% opens from a fresh Klaviyo account in only a few weeks.](https://youtu.be/JS7RD9ZMwWs?si=hDA3f_NvIBYeRim6&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=re-what-email-metrics-should-i-be-hitting)

## Click Rates

Metric: 1%

Click rates will depend on the email, but for campaigns we want to be above the 1% mark.

If you’re below this, you have a content problem.

Either your design isn’t optimized or your copy isn’t good enough.

Follow [this guide for optimizing copywriting for email marketing.](https://gamma.app/docs/Ecommerce-Email-Marketing-Copywriting-That-Actually-Sells-j5oevb6i2mxjdtc?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=re-what-email-metrics-should-i-be-hitting)

Use this guide for insight on design optimization follow [this quick guide](https://youtu.be/ewcl6RKuC0Y?si=Mo1cdt09lAqHZc_t&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=re-what-email-metrics-should-i-be-hitting) and [this quick guide.](https://youtu.be/HtU9h3nJ2CM?si=p2Bo-66xVINUZVO5&utm_source=www.inboxnewsletter.com&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=re-what-email-metrics-should-i-be-hitting)

If you want a full course on email design you can [follow the course in this guide.](https://gamma.app/docs/Steal-My-Highest-Converting-Email-Design-Templates-That-Have-Gene-r0yqurwvpwzc9y5?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=re-what-email-metrics-should-i-be-hitting)

## Pop-Up Form Conversion Rates

Metric: Above 6-8% CTR

Pop-up forms are so key, but most brands are below 4%.

Take 4%-8% and your list doubles in growth and revenue.

If you have a low pop-up conversion rate, follow [this guide.](https://gamma.app/docs/Double-Your-List-Growth-Revenue-Pop-Up-Form-Training-bvf3tdaoibnpn2d?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=re-what-email-metrics-should-i-be-hitting)

## Abandoned Cart / Checkout Recovery

Metric: 10% Recovery

Abandonments are free money waiting to be recovered.

By having an unoptimized system in place you’re letting money walk away.

If you want higher recovery and more revenue, [follow this guide.](https://gamma.app/docs/Abandoned-Cart-83-Page-Guide-5nnqionb8jhd6z6?amp%3Butm_medium=referral&amp%3Butm_campaign=re-what-email-metrics-should-i-be-hitting)

Let me know what other metrics you guys are looking for!
